# WM 941415 ADJUSTING HEADLIGHT MOUNTING (ALL MODELS) > ADJUSTINGHEADLIGHT MOUNTING > CHECKING ADJUSTING ELEMENTS

Information

To restore the original installation position, thereby minimizing the amount of adjustment work required, the following steps must be carried out prior to removal:

Mark the position of the headlight mounting with respect to fastening screws.

Measure and take note of the height of the headlight mounting with respect to the body.

1. Check adjusting elements.

1. 1.1. Check adjusting elements -1- for damage and make sure they are seated securely. If an adjusting element -1- is damaged, it must be replaced. Check that the adjusting elements -1- are fitted correctly in the body.

2. 1.2. Measure the height -A- of the adjusting elements -1- using a calliper gauge and write it down so that you can set the original adjustment height again after the next test step.

3.1.3. Check that the adjusting rings -2-  are not stiff. Important: Left thread! It must be possible to turn adjusting ring -2- without resistance over the entire thread length, otherwise replace adjusting element -1- .

4.1.4. Set original height -A- of the adjusting elements -1- again.

![](images/9aa82f8ef2bff59a36166c181322534b142191ac404fe7a857105a550633a272.webp)  
Fig 1: Checking Adjusting Elements

# WM 941415 ADJUSTING HEADLIGHT MOUNTING (ALL MODELS) > ADJUSTINGHEADLIGHT MOUNTING > INSTALLING HEADLIGHT MOUNTING

If work is carried out on the headlight or retainer plate, the installed fastening screws must be replaced by microencapsulated fastening screws .

Micro-encapsulated fastening screws must be tightened only once to the specified torque.

Micro-encapsulated fastening screws must be replaced after loosening them.

# Left headlight mounting:

1. Clip antenna line holder -1- into the headlight mounting -2- .

2. Clip holders for electric plug connections -3- and headlight cleaning system hose -4- into the headlight mounting -2- .

# Headlight mounting at the left and right:

3. Position headlight mounting -2- on the adjusting elements.

Fig 1: Clipping Holders And Electric Plug Connections

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Fit fastening screws -1-

1.4.1. Press fastening screw -1- into adjusting element.   
2.4.2. Press headlight mounting -2- in the adjusting element area down -arrow F- and screw fastening screw -1- into adjusting element.   
3. 4.3. Align markings on the headlight mounting -2- - if markings were made - with the washers, press headlight mounting -2- down in the adjusting element area -arrow Fand tighten fastening screws -1- .

![](images/ed4e608d152c0064711422bd404987423450d3322ec0da811042672073f902b5.webp)  
Fig 2: Screwing Fastening Screws

# WM 941415 ADJUSTING HEADLIGHT MOUNTING (ALL MODELS) > ADJUSTINGHEADLIGHT MOUNTING > ADJUSTING HEADLIGHT MOUNTING TOWARDS Z-AXISAND X-AXIS

Do not adjust gap dimensions between the headlight mounting and front lid until you have adjusted the gap dimensions of the front lid with respect to all other add-on parts.

Adjust gap dimensions between the headlights and front lid in accordance with the specified

dimensions.

The specified gap dimensions are guidelines and are relevant for repair work and assembly work.

The gaps must not taper off or become narrow in places.

Use star gauge Nr.127-1 Pos.1 and star gauge Nr.127-1 Pos.2 to check the gap dimensions.

The gap dimensions and offset positions of the headlights are adjusted by moving the headlight mountings and by screwing the adjusting elements in and out.

1. Insert headlight into the mounting.

2. Close the front lid and check the gap dimensions between the headlight and front lid. → 5X00IN41 GAP DIMENSIONS

![](images/f41bdec3b124a5af47b13286ce1b1b62bfbfac5e4a1885d32a66e081c0786ce3.webp)

3. Remove headlight.

4. Loosen fastening screws -1- .

1.4.1. Press headlight mounting -2- in the adjusting element area down -arrow F- to ensure that the position of the adjusting element cannot be changed.

![](images/135dc117c9529accfa4ba4402046dd6420efa986eba2dde8239dc7a965d07dde.webp)  
Fig 1: Loosening Fastening Screws

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Move headlight mounting -2- in the required direction -X, Z- .

A scale is visible close to the fastening screws on the headlight mounting. The scale serves as a guide when the headlight is removed and makes adjustments easier.

6 Tighten fastening screws -1- .

1. 6.1. Press headlight mounting -2- in the adjusting element area down to ensure that the position of the adjusting element cannot be changed.

![](images/7fb1f140e5f16a63b57060063e31231ade7781d93c04c0508f9f97516e5c5e33.webp)  
Fig 2: Positioning Headlight Mounting

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Insert headlight into the mounting.

8. Close the front lid and check the gap dimensions between the headlight and front lid.

9. Repeat the adjustment procedure if necessary.

# WM 941415 ADJUSTING HEADLIGHT MOUNTING (ALL MODELS) > ADJUSTINGHEADLIGHT MOUNTING > ADJUSTING HEADLIGHT MOUNTING TOWARDS Y-AXIS

If work is carried out on the headlight or retainer plate, the installed fastening screws must be replaced by microencapsulated fastening screws .

Micro-encapsulated fastening screws must be tightened only once to the specified torque.

Micro-encapsulated fastening screws must be replaced after loosening them.

1. Insert headlight into the mounting.   
2. Close the front lid and check the gap dimensions between the headlight and front lid. → 5X00IN41 GAP DIMENSIONS

3. Remove headlight.

# Procedure for lowering the headlight:

4. Loosen fastening screws -1- .

1.4.1. Press headlight mounting -2- in the adjusting element area down -arrow F- to ensure that the position of the adjusting element cannot be changed.

![](images/49dd27f97e306b2a1652c8b1b14a9e7af52bbc9e66a603cd92f6d310d6a04de4.webp)  
Fig 2: Loosening Fastening Screws   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Screw in the adjusting ring -3- on the adjusting element to lower the headlight mounting -2- .

# Information

Read the operating instructions for the headlight aiming device and observe the following test and adjustment conditions:

•Vehicle and headlight aiming device positioned on a horizontal, clean surface.   
Vehicle parked safely and ready to drive, empty, including al fluids and fuel.   
All doors and rear lid closed.   
Tyre pressure corresponds to the specified values.   
Driver's seat occupied by one person or a weight of 75 kg.   
Steering in straight-ahead position.   
•For vehicles with air suspension: Vehicle level in center position.   
•Vehicle and chassis have been bounced. 1. Align the headlight aiming device -1- at a 90° angle to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle and position it at a distance of -a- in front of the left headlight. 2.Set the tilt angle of the light/dark limit of the dipped beam headlight on the headlight aiming device and align the collecting box with the center axis -b- of the dipped beam headlight.

# WM 941516 HEADLIGHTS - BASIC SETTING IN THE BODY (ALL MODELS) > ADJUSTING HEADLIGHTS (BASIC SETTING IN THE BODY)

The headlights are fitted into the body at the factory!   
The headights must only be re-adjusted during accident repairs or if the headlights are being replaced!

# Information

If work is carried out on the headlight or retainer plate, the installed fastening screws must be replacec by microencapsulated fastening screws .

Micro-encapsulated fastening screws must be tightened only once to the specified torque.

Micro-encapsulated fastening screws must be replaced after loosening them.

# Information

• Set gap dimensions on lid and accessories in accordance with the gap specifications.   
Given a clearance in the opening that is too great or too small the accessories must be centered with respect to the body.   
Ensure that the gaps do not run in a wedge-shaped fashion or do not narrow at local points. The given values are guidelines, which should be observed as far as possible.   
The guidelines apply to repair and assembly work.   
Use star gauges to check the gap dimensions. Star gauges for body gap dimensions NR.127-1

The headlight is aligned in the body by adjusting the headlight mounting points. → 941415 ADJUSTING HEADLIGHT MOUNTING

# WM 9415IN CONVERTING HEADLIGHTS FOR LEFT/RIGHT-HAND DRIVING (ALLMODELS) > CONVERTING HEADLIGHTS FOR LEFT/RIGHT-HAND DRIVING >INFORMATION

For driving in countries in which vehicles drive on the other side of the road, it is important to adapt the headlights as soon as you cross the border. The dipped beam headlight then lights symmetrically so that oncoming traffic is not dazzled.

Headlights with dynamic cornering light must be adapted in the multi-function display. The message "Headlights adapted for LHD/RHD" appears in the multi-function display every time the ignition is switched on. Don't forget to reset the headlights for the return journey.

# WM 941625 PROGRAMMING (CENTRAL) HEADLIGHT CONTROL UNIT (ALL MODELS) > PROGRAMMING (CENTRAL) HEADLIGHT CONTROL UNIT

NOTE: Voltage drop

•Risk of irreparable damage to control unit   
Risk of damage to control unit   
Fault entries in the control unit   
•Coding in the control unit is aborted   
• Malfunctions in control unit, even during programming

→ Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch offignition and remove ignition key.

→ Ensure that the power supply is not interrupted during programming.

→ Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least — Nominal value: 40 A to the vehicle battery.

# Information

The PIwis Tester Il9818 instructions take precedence since the description may be different with later Tester releases.

The procedure described here has been structured in general terms. Different text or additional information may appear in PIWis Tester Il 9818 .

1. PIWis Tester  9818 must be connected to the vehicle and ignition switched on.   
2. Start the diagnostic application and select the required vehicle type.   
3. Select the central headlight control unit in the overview .   
4. Extended identification must now be selected.   
5. Enter the vehicle identification number and press [Enter].   
6. Maintenance/repairs must then be selected.   
7. Control unit replacement must now be selected. Then press [F12].   
8. Select Write data, press [F12] and then press [F8] to start. The data is now loaded.   
9. The Tester displays the message Data has been written. Press [F12] to continue.   
10. Maintenance/repairs must now be selected.   
11. Select Headlight start-up and press [F12] to continue.   
12. Read the preconditions for start-up and press [F12] to continue.   
13. Headlight start-up can now be started by pressing [F8].   
14. Wait for confirmation that coding was completed successfully. Then press [F12] to   
continue.   
15. Wait for confirmation that start-up was completed successfully.  Press [F12] to continue.   
16. Read out the fault memory and erase it if necessary.   
17. Perform a function test on the control unit.

# WM 944955 REPLACING CONTROL UNIT FOR FRONT-END ELECTRONICS (ALL MODELS) > REPLACING CONTROL UNIT FOR FRONT-END ELECTRONICS

Information

All remote controls (keys) are required for teaching a DME, front-end electronics (front BCM), rear-end electronics (rear BCM), electronic steering lock (ELV) control unit or remote controls (keys) for example.

Remote controls (keys) that are not taught during this teaching procedure wil no longer be recognized by the vehicle.

NOTE: Voltage drop

Risk of irreparable damage to control unit   
Risk of damage to control unit   
Fault entries in the control unit   
•Coding in the control unit is aborted   
•Malfunctions in control unit, even during programming

→ Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch offignition and remove ignition key.

→ Ensure that the power supply is not interrupted during programming.

→ Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least — Nominal value: 40 A to the vehicle battery.

# Information

The PIwis Tester Il9818 instructions take precedence since the description may be different with later Tester releases.

The procedure described here has been structured in general terms; different text or additions may appear in PIWis Tester Il 9818.

1. PIWis Tester Il 9818 must be connected to the vehicle before starting the Tester. Switch on ignition.   
2. Select the vehicle type and start the diagnostic application.   
3. Select Front-end electronics.   
4. Extended identification must now be selected.   
5. Enter the vehicle identification number and press [Enter] to confirm your entry.   
6. Maintenance/repairs  must then be selected.   
7. Control unit replacement must now be selected. Then press [F12] to continue.   
8. Select Write values and press [F12] to continue.   
. Press [F8] to start writing values.   
10. When a message appears confirming that the values were written and coded successfully, press [F12] to continue.

11. Go back to the Start page on the Tester.   
12. To activate the control units, switch on the hazard warning lights.   
13. Select the menu Diagnostics -> Online teaching function --> Engine immobilizer on the   
Start page.   
14. Vehicle must now be selected. Then press [F12] to continue. Vehicle data will be read out.   
15. Follow the instructions on the Tester.   
16. The vehicle identification number (VIN) is displayed. Change the vehicle identification number if   
necessary.   
17. Enter the repair order number and press [F12] to continue.   
18. Enter the PPN user name and password and press [F12] to continue.   
19. Login is performed.   
20. The Tester displays the message Login successful . Press [F12] to continue.   
21. Follow the instructions on the Tester to select the required menu.   
22. Once the teaching process is completed successfully, the Tester shows the following status,   
for example:

2 keys taught

Front BCM: taught

ELV: taught

Rear BCM: taught

DME: taught

Overall vehicle status: taught. Press [F12] to continue.

23. Press [ESC] to exit the Online teaching function and select the vehicle type on the Starl page.

24. Read out the fault memory and erase it if necessary.

25. Function test: Lock, open and start the vehicle using all remote controls (hand-held transmitters).

Fig 1: Masking Rear Spoiler   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

1. 1.1. Mask the right-hand side of the rear spoiler underneath the additional brake light as shown — Masking rear spoiler  using fabric adhesive tape.

# Information

To prevent damage to the additional brake light, always observe the following installation sequence and never use a plastic wedge or slotted screwdriver to lever the additional brake light out of the rear spoiler.

You will find a video clip showing how to remove the additional brake light as a PDF file in the PIWiS information system in the "Workshop Manual" information medium under ==> "947019 Removing additional brake light - video clip".

2. 1.2. Carefully insert a plastic wedge at a horizontal position between the rear spoiler and additional brake light -arrow A- until there is a gap of approx. X = 3 mm between the lower edge of the additional brake light and rear spoiler.

![](images/f20be60e27e5093d365a136f102421f2e589e916de70e16535571a13f4518397.webp)  
Fig 2: Removing Additional Brake Light   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# Information

When removing the additional brake light, always use a small slotted screwdriver to move the locking lug to the left and unlock it through the widened gap.

Only release the additional brake light when part of the locking lug is visible through

the gap. Use a hand lamp to check this if necessary.

3. 1.3. Insert a narrow screwdriver in the marked area of the gap and push the additional brake light locking lug lying behind it to the left to unlock it -arrow A- until the additional brake light pops out slightly.

![](images/7c2124fedde142b04cb46a535e127e8c3e633939a0fb650079251f43c9efae18.webp)  
Fig 3: Removing Additional Brake Light

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. 1.4. Carefully pull the plastic wedge and additional brake light out of the rear spoiler -arrow- and leave the additional brake light hanging on the wire harness at the left.

5.1.5. Remove the fabric tape you affixed to the rear spoiler earlier.

# CONSOLE

NOTE: Voltage drop

•Risk of irreparable damage to control unit   
Risk of damage to control unit   
•Fault entries in the control unit   
•Coding in the control unit is aborted   
Malfunctions in control unit, even during programming

→ Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch off ignition and remove ignition key.

— Ensure that the power suppy is not interrupted during programming.

→ Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least — Nominal value: 40 A to the vehicle battery.

# Information

The PIWis Tester Il9818 instructions take precedence since the description may be different with later Tester releases.

The procedure described here has been structured in general terms. Different text or additional information may appear in PIWis Tester Il 9818 .

1. Connect the PIWis Tester to the vehicle and start the diagnostic application. Switch   
ignition.   
2. Select vehicle type.   
3. Select the Air conditioning control unit in the overview .   
4. Codings/adaptations must now be selected.   
5. Automatic coding must then be selected and press [F12] to start coding.   
6. The Tester displays the message Coding completed successfully.   
7. Select the Drive links/checks menu.   
8. Select General group and press [F12].

# Information

1.The Compressor run-in function can only be carried out when the engine is running. . Prerequisites for compressor run-in can be displayed in the Porsche System Tester by pressing the [F1] Help button for the air-conditioning system control unit. 3. Specifications in the Porsche System Tester have priority and take precedence over the specifications in the description.

4. If the Compressor run-in function cannot be activated, then the Reset compressor run-in function must be carried out first.   
5. Then start the Compressor run-in function again.

9. Start the engine.

10. Select the Reset compressor run-in function by pressing [F12] and then press [F8] to start the reset process.

1. 10.1. A compressor run-in remaining time of 150 s must be set.

11. Select the Compressor run-in function, press [F12] and then [F8] to start.

12. Read out the fault memory and erase it if necessary.

13. Check the function of the switch console during a test drive and read out the fault memory.

# WM 9638K2 CALIBRATING FRONT CAMERA (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION

When does the front camera need to be calibrated?

The front camera must be re-calibrated in the following situations:

When removing and instaling the front camera • When removing and instllin the windscreen When changing the height of the chassis When adjusting the chassis

# WM 9638K2 CALIBRATING FRONT CAMERA (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK

The exact position of the front camera with respect to the vehicle coordinate system is determined by calibrating the front camera.

The setting device Setting device with reflector WE 1362 , the calibration board Calibration board for lane departure warning WE 1540 and a wheel alignment computer are required for the calibration process.

# Information

Calibration must only be performed on a levelled wheel alignment platform or on level ground.

On vehicles with air suspension, switch on ignition, close the doors and set the air suspension to Normal.

# Information

The vehicle must be empty and all doors must be closed.

1. If work was carried out on the chassis, basic initial alignment must be carried out before calibrating the front camera. → 449503 SUSPENSION ALIGNMENT, COMPLETE

2. The level must be set to Normal for vehicles with air suspension .

Fig 1: Parking Vehicle On Wheel Alignment Platform (Shown On Cayenne)

![](images/225a3dcc1fe7bbea0d543f5ecb7e50050f0eab669f1f5dcaeeface4c0de55882.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

Park the vehicle on a levelled wheel alignment platform or on a level surface and set up the calibration unit Setting device with reflector WE 1362 in front of the vehicle in accordance with the instructions on the wheel alignment computer and PiWiS Tester.

→ Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch offignition and remove ignition key.

# Information

The PIWis Tester Il9818 instructions take precedence since the description may be different with later Tester releases.

The procedure described here has been structured in general terms. Different text or additional information may appear in PIWis Tester Il 9818 .

![](images/042966215249567a43b642ba76b8001ff86ba2cf7590e0a37d54918c45512b77.webp)  
Fig 1: Parking Vehicle On Wheel Alignment Platform (Shown On Cayenne)

1. The following tools are required:

1. 1.1. Setting device Setting device with reflector WE 1362

2. 1.2. Calibration board Lane departure warning calibration board WE 1540

3.1.3. Wheel alignment computer

2. Select the relevant vehicle in the wheel alignment computer.

3. Select quick function Calibrate front camera.

4. Align the calibration board. Follow the steps and instructions on the wheel alignment computer.

5. The surface of the board must be clean and free of objects.

# Information

The required height of the calibration board and the distance of the calibration board from the vehicle will not be displayed on the wheel alignment computer. These values are stored under Front camera calibration in the Tester.

6. Set the distance from the calibration unit to the vehicle as shown on the Tester. The distance -A- must always be between 1, 000 mm and 3, 000 mm from the center of the wheel hub to the calibration unit. The difference between the right and left side must be < 5 mm.

Fig 2: Checking Distance From Vehicle To Calibration Unit (Shown On Cayenne)

![](images/dd995cc116b1ec6b133af0677c73cda435682362988aa426cf353788450b75db.webp)

7. Secure measured-value pickup mounting to the rear wheels of the vehicle.

8. Fit the relevant measured-value pickups on the measured-value pickup mounting and the calibration board.

9 The height of the calibration board must be 1, 400 mm . Make sure that the measuring stick is touching the floor. If the vehicle is on a wheel alignment platform, the height of the calibration board must be adjusted to include the height of the wheel alignment platform.

10. Before starting the calibration process, write down the height of the four wheel housing edges. These must be measured from the floor (vehicle standing level) to the highest point of each wheel housing edge and must be specified in mm.

11. The wheel alignment computer is no longer needed for the rest of the calibration process. Do not move the vehicle or calibration board from this point onwards!

# Information

Once all adjustment procedures are complete in the wheel alignment computer, start the calibration process in the PIWiS Tester.

12. Connect the PIWiS Tester to the vehicle and start the PIWiS Tester. Switch on ignition and press [F12] to continue.

13. Select the vehicle type and start the diagnostic application.

14. Select the Front camera control unit in the overview .

15. Select Maintenance/repairs.

16. Select Calibrate front camera and press [F12]

17. Read the warnings displayed on the Tester and follow the instructions.

18. Enter the values Wheel housing edge height and Distance to calibration board. Press [F12] to continue.

19. Start the calibration process by pressing [F8]. The vehicle must not be moved.

20. The Tester confirms that calibration was completed successfully .

# Information

If the calibration process could not be completed successfully, one or more of the calibration values are outside of the required range. There can be a number of different reasons for this.

1.The calibration board is not at the correct height.   
2The vehicle and calibration board are not aligned correctly.

21. Switch ignition off and then on again.

22. Check the function of the front camera.

23. Read out the fault memory.

All remote controls (keys) are required for teaching a DME, front-end electronics (front BCM), rear-end electronics (rear BCM), electronic steering lock (ELV) control unit or remote controls (keys) for example.

Remote controls (keys) that are not taught during this teaching procedure wil no longer be recognized by the vehicle.

→ Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch offignition and remove ignition key.

# Information

The PlWis Tester Il9818 instructions take precedence since the description may be different with later Tester releases.

The procedure described here has been structured in general terms. Different text or additional information may appear in PIWis Tester Il 9818 .

1. Connect the PIWiS Tester to the vehicle and start the PIWis Tester. Switch on ignition.   
2. Select the menu Diagnostics -> Online teaching function -> Engine immobilizer on the Start page.   
3. The relevant vehicle must now be selected. Then press [F12] to \continue.   
4. Follow the instructions on the Tester and press [F12] to continue.   
5. The vehicle identification number (VIN) is displayed. Change the vehicle identification number if necessary.   
6. Enter the repair order number and press [F12] to continue.   
7. Enter the PPN user name and password and press [F12] to continue.   
8. Login is performed.   
9. The Tester displays the message Login successful . Press [F12] to continue.   
10. Follow the instructions on the Tester to select the required menu.   
11. Once the teaching process is completed successfully the Tester shows the following status, for example:

2 keys taught Front BCM: taught ELV: taught Rear BCM: taught

DME: taught

Overall vehicle status: taught. Press [F12] to continue.

12. Press [ESC] to end the Online teaching function and select the vehicle type on the Start page.

13. Function test: Lock, open and start the vehicle using all remote controls (hand-held transmitters).

14. Read al fault memories and erase if necessary.

# Information

Original remote controls for garage door system cannot be taught to operate with the HomeLink in the vehicle. OR: The teaching process was confirmed, but HomeLink will not work or only works sporadically.

Check that the battery in the original remote control for the garage door opener is new. If in doubt, change the battery and repeat the teaching process.

The programmable HomeLink replaces up to three original remote controls for operating various equipment (e.g. garage door, gate to property, alarm system).

The buttons I, I and Ill can each be programmed with one frequency of an original remote control.

Prerequisites for operating and programming the HomeLink:

oThe ignition is switched on.   
The hazard warning lights are switched off.

# WM 967955 REPLACING CONTROL UNIT FOR GARAGE DOOR OPENER(ALL MODELS) > DIAGNOSTICS

Original remote controls for garage door system cannot be taught to operate with the HomeLink in the vehicle. OR: The teaching process was confirmed, but HomeLink will not work or only works sporadically.

Check that the battery in the original remote control for the garage door opener is new. If in doubt, change the battery and repeat the teaching process.

If after carefull observing the operating instructions and following the procedures described, teaching of the garage door opener control unit is not possible, further information can be obtained from a Hotline facility. A basic requirement is to obtain the diagnostic information beforehand as follows.

# Software version

1. Press button I or Ill (not both) and hold for 50 seconds. The LED stops flashing and goes out completely. Continue to hold the button down. A few seconds later the LED flashes several times. The number of flashes corresponds to the software version.

![](images/8e5e637326f1d58c271fc2a594f38d36087276ade04220129d059bc71bb0c212.webp)

# Regional code status

2. Press button Il on the roof console and hold for approx. 50 seconds until the LED goes out and stays off. Continue to hold down button Il. After a few seconds the LED flashes several times. The number of flashes indicates the programmed region.

![](images/2adf24b8315d1fd6950b8e7a3e4532be0c6781b7f3829c38572f2487e149d604.webp)

# Information

3. Provide the following additional information about the vehicle and the original remote control:

1. Dealer, make, model and model year of the vehicle.   
2. Make, model, age and operating frequency of the original remote control.

# WM 0710IN GENERAL (ALL MODELS) > GENERAL INFORMATION ON "PORSCHE DYNAMIC REPAIR"

The term "Porsche Dynamic Repair" refers to cost-effective minor repairs, which are preferred over part replacement.

These repair methods can be used to rectify small areas of damage and signs of use with little effort or cost. This usually eliminates the need for replacement parts and the removal and installation of components.

However, a cost-effective repair may have quality implications. To achieve the best repair result, always use the tool recommended by Porsche and attend the special training courses run by the tool and system suppliers. The quality of the repair also depends on a number of factors, which are listed under the relevant repair descriptions.

The individual repair methods are:

Glass repairs   
Dent repairs   
•Interior cosmetic repairs   
Paint repairs   
Alloy wheel reconditioning   
•PCM repairs (process description in the Technical Sales Information)

Repairs can only be carried out independently after successfully completing a course, or should be contracted out to specialist providers. In either case, always comply with the instructions and repair restrictions for the individual repair methods.

WM 0720IN GLASS REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > TOOLS   
![](images/39fd618f73d7e043d9754309d35f9db8f61a2a25b0683c96ef478517dab4ec1f.webp)

NOTE: Stress from a stone chip on the inside of the window

Crack in the windscreen

→ Do not press against the stone chips in the window from the inside.

# Information

This repair method is a cost-effective repair that may have quality implications. To achieve the best repair result, always use the tool recommended by Porsche and attend the special training courses run by the tool/system suppliers.

Laminated glass in windscreens can only be repaired under the following conditions:

Damage in the driver's field of vision (30 cm wide in the wiper area -X- ) and at the edge of the windscreen (10 cm -Y- ) must not be repaired. → Driver's field of vision

![](images/bed2afcec057bb55a006d1c7c79d6b4fe059eb5b645c077c2403f10141fcf7bc.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Driver's Vision Field

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

Only damage to the outside of the windscreen may be repaired. There must be no damage to the inner pane or plastic film.   
Repairs must be carried out as soon as possible after the damage occurs. There must be no moisture or dirt that has visibly penetrated into the damaged area.   
The crater of the point of impact must not be more than 5 mm in diameter.   
Cracks extending radiall from the point of impact must not be longer than 50 mm. → Stone chip with crack

![](images/ab3ada60b8f69b25c9902c08aa486ca7babcf92dd6dd7cfa0a022fa606c0742b.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Stone Chip With Crack   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

A visible spot of around 1 - 2 mm in diameter willremain following repairs. → Repair result

![](images/b5d9fe6a03ea476c94b857e9ff9fed41fa61b3d68ad7636a6f4916bd8b7046c2.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Glass Repair Area   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

The following damage can be satisfactorily repaired economically using this repair method:

Bull's eye: restoration of appearance 90-99%

![](images/c883cfc89fc13f9faed51954cc8a7440b6864e9c589cc90d08ebc8a5a20f4932.webp)  
Fig 4: Identifying Glass Repair Area (Bull's Eye)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

Bee wings: restoration of appearance 90-99%

![](images/708e62ea2a3dd569edd34e788221d642a02bd22152b0da74bbb276995df70a2f.webp)  
Fig 5: Identifying Glass Repair Area (Bee Wings)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

• Star break: restoration of appearance 80-90%

![](images/6ed8fe71e3dd8b22728a3203d3ac072ab1bf719c62b9506e9bf4fbd47de4ab70.webp)  
Fig 6: Identifying Glass Repair Area (Star Break)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

• Shattered break: restoration of appearance 70-80%

![](images/4016a76ae6313d928d4c16ca54b2252f364ef72ba7fa247d15831bd7ead03d9d.webp)

# WM 0720IN GLASS REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > PREPARATION

1. Clean the damaged area.

1. 1.1. Use a dry cloth (without any window cleaner) to clean the windscreen around the area of damage, but do not wipe across the area of impact itself.

2. 1.2. Remove loose splinters of glass from the chipped area using the hard metal stylus, but do not enlarge the impact crater unnecessarily. → Exposing stone chip i IMPORTANT: The more glass missing from the chipped surface, the more obvious the blemish following repairs.

![](images/abbbb2f950f90f3b8d44c7e3febd2048f107c9a89ce717f9dc756c0530a7c633.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Stone Chip   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Secure the mirror.

Apply gel to the suction areas of the inspection mirror and attach the mirror to the inside of the windscreen so that the procedure can be monitored from outside. → Securing mirror

![](images/f770f294015d23fb135d8dda19096559ab854dcb34080da4c224a8f7eff29577.webp)  
Fig 2: Securing Mirror

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Drill out

If necessary, use a drillto mill glass splinters and dirt out of the impact hole to a depth of approx. 1 mm.

0 IMPORTANT: Always hold the dril firmly with both hands! This is the only way to ensure that the drill is positioned securely.

![](images/35d03649509366fe23a6e59a1beea7d61dd2874a2772a0e7e4c09fe4ff289d05.webp)  
Fig 3: Drilling Stone Chip   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Secure the bridge.

1.4.1. Rub gel into the suction area on the bridge. This allows the tool to be repositioned after it has been secured in place.   
2.4.2. Press the bridge -1- firmly onto the windscreen so that the threaded hole is directly above the point of impact.   
3.4.3. Stick the bridge firmly onto windscreen by operating the vacuum pump until the red marking -2- is no longer visible.

i IMPORTANT: The bridge must remain firmly seated on the windscreen for the duration of the repair work. Operate the pump again if the red mark becomes visible.

4.4.4. Align the bridge directly over the point of impact with respect to the windscreen and secure it in place using the central screw -3- .

5.4.5. Adjust the bridge so that it is parallel to the windscreen using the screws at the rear -4-.

![](images/2861f6f87a07d297a7bc15ca0b47cb3e7914fa20b53eaeec8c2262f3240e03ef.webp)  
Fig 4: Securing Bridge

# WM 0720IN GLASS REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > REPAIR PROCEDURE

1. Fit the bridge.

1.1.1. Screw injector with seal -5- into the bridge until the seal is touching the glass. Then press the injector against the window by completing one more turn.

![](images/3faead4463d1eee4417bdb13c0438b12d3578c8312110a7ce230ebd917e22839.webp)  
Fig 1: Turning Injector Seal   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2.1.2. Attach needle to the syringe and fil with approx. 0.15 ml of resin. → Filling syringe

![](images/11b44d6004cb767502774ea46dfc47780344293e1ecbb04433dc78ab531ad736.webp)  
Fig 2: Filling Syringe   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3.1.3. Inject resin into the injector. → Filing injector

![](images/9ffb0dbcc03017fb94981b622d3a5e7edeac41ab259df4368af26f6e0e050115.webp)  
Fig 3: Filling Injector

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# 2. Pressurizing phase

1.2.1. Slowly screw the plunger -6- into the injector -5- until resistance is felt and the shape of the seal changes → Seal under pressure . Keep a firm hold on the injector barrel while doing this.   
2. 2.2. Leave the plunger pressed down at this position for around 5 min., in which time the plunger will automatically build up pressure.

![](images/d942f10a449e3056b45fa1ed7d6e36e2bd52edf4411561c34fc45297ab0cf7ec.webp)  
Fig 4: Installing Plunger Into Injector

![](images/2dc0f394a94035a955e67d710115901d8576f8cff3518eaec29c2c55f8454f15.webp)  
Fig 5: Identifying Pressure Seal   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# 3. Vacuum phase

1. 3.1. Pull up the plunger -6- with one hand -A- and secure it in position by turning it 90° clockwise -B- . This allows any air to escape out of the damaged area.

2.3.2. Release the plunger so that pressure can build up again.

3. 3.3. Repeat steps → 3.1. and → 3.2. about 5-10 times until there is no more air in the damaged area.

![](images/f2df52ea8f3a169e173b28e78418928eb124b31223a1d238964515bfa5900712.webp)  
Fig 6: Pulling Plunger

![](images/b119080b45bbddf3165b20907f42b1de6472e459ec47f01db22ccc0c27dd8988.webp)  
Fig 7: Identifying Vacuum Seal   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Heating

If the damage is more severe, the removal of trapped air can be speeded up by heating the area gently. To do this, use a lighter to heat the area of damage from the inside for 3-5 seconds.

0 IMPORTANT: Heat during the vacuum phase only, otherwise the expanding air would cause excessive pressure in the damaged area.

5. Remove the bridge.

1.5.1. Release the plunger a litte (do not create a vacuum) and unscrew the injector.

2. 5.2. Remove the bridge from the windscreen. 6. Apply finishing resin.

1.6.1. Add a drop of finishing resin directly onto the impact point.

2.6.2. Slide film across the windscreen.

![](images/ca7f241fd3298fc6de8af69c55d48b1a465bbe4b69e64fa9035bbee092a90971.webp)  
Fig 8: Applying Resin   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Curing under a UV lamp

1.7.1. Place a UV lamp over the damaged area from the outside and switch it on. → Curing under a UV lamp

2.7.2. Curing takes around 10 minutes, depending on the size of the stone chip.

![](images/5194570b075d5f379a2d319b72809a2e0c4d56df2b08a995aa38bcee29852781.webp)  
Fig 9: Identifying UV Lamp

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

Scrape off repair resin.

1.8.1. Remove film and scrape of excess resin using a razor blade held at a 90 degree angle to the windscreen. → Scraping off resin

0 IMPORTANT: Risk of damage to the windscreen. Use only blades that are in perfect condition, otherwise they could damage the windscreen.

2.8.2. If there is an indentation at the point of repair, steps → 6. → 7. and → 8.1. will need to be repeated to obtain a perfect finish.

![](images/5021e5899cae4ce30f7429aba7778f0472251e35486ce6338c93b0638473a6b7.webp)  
Fig 10: Removing Resin

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# . Polishing

Polish the repair area with polish and a soft cloth.

i IMPORTANT: Do not polish for too long as this can wear down the repair resin and the surface will no longer be flat.

![](images/57897ab8747fd267f68d4b05c352ec74a79498638cfa7a950d35a19870e5f2cb.webp)  
Fig 11: Applying Polish On Glass   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# 10. Cleaning tools

After completing repairs, clean the tools using a dry, lint-free cloth. Otherwise, the resin will damage the seals.

# WM 0730IN DENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > TOOLS

![](images/2861cd46e23becff5c6825eb219c183831f51568472e4d893d50194857245aa4.webp)

![](images/ddaba6df95342d3cc4c77302a8a8f130a50f94950a25dd35f84b64920c912224.webp)

# WM 0730IN DENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > DENT REPAIRS

This repair method is a cost-effective repair that may have quality implications. To achieve the best repair result, always use the tool recommended by Porsche and attend the special training courses run by the tool/system suppliers.

# Information

Some damage cannot be worked back into shape using this method because of reinforced or bonded body parts. Each area of damage must be assessed individually.

Dents in sheet steel and aluminum panels caused by hail, bumps when parking (knocks against edge of door), chestnuts, etc. can be corrected by carrying out dent repairs using the reshaping method. With this method, dents are pressed out point-by-point from behind the metal panel using special dent removal tools and then polished.

Dent removal sets: Dent removal lever set VAS 6332 XL professional dent removal set WE 1358, Dent removal lever set VAS 6333 WE 1359, Dent removal lever set VAS 6334 WE 1360

![](images/2c3f1efcd68636f20fd36ec03dd2f718837911f2b072e871642c777c06e05964.webp)  
Fig 1: Removing Dent Removal Sets

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

The progress of the repair work is assessed using the reflected lines of a neon lamp on the upper side of the panel. → Before and after

![](images/b5bfda016c2db4989efc0f84ef0410762836a999436009674d29e5074f708dc5.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Neon Lamp Reflected Lines

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

Small dents that are not accessible from the rear can be "pulled out" using bonding techniques Dent remover VAs 6364 WE 1361 if the strength of the adhesive bond and the adhesion of the paintwork allow this. To this end, adhesive adapters are stuck to the center of the dent using special adhesive. The dent is pulled out carefully in a controlled manner using a slide hammer puller.

# NM 0730IN DENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > DENT REPAIRS > PREREQUISITES

The dent must not have any cracks in the paintwork. Examine the damaged area using an illuminated magnifier or reflected-light microscope.   
Measure thickness of paint layer around the damaged area. Paint layers up to approx. 450 μm thick are straightforward. With thicker layers of paint there is a danger that the paint will crack.   
High level of workmanship and skill   
Intensive training   
Continuous practice   
Use of recommended tools

# WM 0730IN DENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > DENT REPAIRS > SUCCESS FACTORS

The factors below affect the outcome of the repair work considerably:

The location of the damage   
The extent of the damage   
The shape of the damage   
The condition of the paintwork   
Skills and experience of the technician   
Color (dark colors are trickier than light colors)   
With silver colors, sharp-edged and pointed dents may cause slight changes to the color pigments (dark sports).   
Condition of tools

# WM 0730IN DENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > DENT REPAIRS > TECHNICAL RESTRICTIONS FOR CARRYING OUT REPAIRS

No/poor accessibility (for safety reasons, holes must never be drilled in order to make an area more accessible.)   
Workmanship skills, lack of practice.   
• Dents with paint defects/cracks cannot be repaired.   
Damage to folded edges or reinforcements usually cannot be repaired.   
Dents with crumpled edges usually cannot be corrected.   
It may not be possible to correct creased or pointed dents. With the bonding technique it is usually only possible to repair flat or minor dents.   
The maximum size of the dent should not exceed a diameter of 50 mm.

# WM 0730IN DENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > PROCEDURE > GENERAL PROCEDURE

1. Clean the surface to be treated to obtain good light reflection.

2. Mark the dent using the wax chalk.

3. Assess accessibility of the dent.

4. Try to find the best access, even if this is difficult for some areas.

5. Remove body parts in accordance with the Service information. When doing so, always be careful with safety-critical components, such as airbags, seat-belt pretensioners, electronic components, cables, etc.

6. Locate the dent using a locating lamp and find the tool tip on the metal panel.

7. Work according to the clock method described below.

8. Work calmly and patiently.

9. When working on bumps or bulges, it is much better to tap the metal gently and repeatedly rather than using one heavy strike.

10. Be very careful when using knife tools and cutter tools as these tools can easily cause the panel to buckle.

11. Sand down rough areas and high points with a sanding block (P2000 - 4000) and then polish them.

12. After removing the dent, seal the repair area with wax or cavity protection.

# NM 0730IN DENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > PROCEDURE > CLOCK METHOD

With the clock method, the lines of force running through the center of the dent are removed, with the result that the material stress is reduced and the panel is flat again.

The dent should be envisaged as a dial with "12" being the furthest away. In other words, the person performing the work is standing at 6 o'clock.

Start at the edge of the dent -A- at 9 o'clock and work clockwise through 12 o'clock to 3 o'clock. When doing this, always remember to press the panel at as many points as possible and as close together as possible. From 3 o'clock, move further inwards and carry on through 12 o'clock to 9 o'clock. Carry out the remaining steps in this same way.

![](images/d5c109cf319af5fc9807ff03340d09291f80b0721dec906535b7478e9f836377.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Dent Repair Clock Method   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

With a dent of approx. 2 cm in diameter, it will be necessary to press the panel at around 100 - 150 points. Any point that is pressed too hard must be pushed back again before continuing. Strain can be created in the panel as a result of too many high points, with the result that the metal sheet can no longer spread out evenly.

# WM 0730IN DENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > PROCEDURE > DENT MASSAGE (FOR LARGER DENTS)

With this method, the lines of force are removed not by pressing at numerous points but instead by short movements.

For this process, first draw a boundary circle -B- at the center of the dent using wax chalk. This circle is to prevent the tool from being pulled too far into the center. This could cause the dent to break up into numerous tiny dents and make any further work more difficult.

Use the large ball tool with the large round plastic attachment. Place the tool at the edge of the dent -Afirst at 12 o'clock and using gentle pressure approach the boundary circle with gradually increasing

pressure. Continue working from 11 o'clock to 1 o'clock, from 10 o'clock to 2 o'clock, etc. from the outer edge of the dent right up to the boundary circle. The pressure must not be too great as this could cause ridges. Once the dent has been shrunk back to the boundary circle, continue using the point-by-point clock method -c- .

![](images/ed25b89d3457fb4beee9f03c10a0e1521f4a5ef1d9dfb0df9ae9cc5c45493a94.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Dent Massage Method For Larger Dents   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

The various dent repair methods can only be learned through intensive training and continuous practice.

# WM 0740IN INTERIOR COSMETIC REPAIRS (EXCEPT MACAN) > TOOLS

![](images/8f3eef74f02c180e85c051693c9fa515900c53ebaae74026b033823fef738680.webp)

WM 0740IN INTERIOR COSMETIC REPAIRS (EXCEPT MACAN) > TECHNICAL   
![](images/c97843a12a268b795fbf24b072fc00cc5ea889619bc3f2c1c19bf52e33367f87.webp)

# VALUES

![](images/0e398e99f379afb18d2746e9643a7f4e258ed67483af10ad2e42bd297771c499.webp)

# WM 0740IN INTERIOR COSMETIC REPAIRS (EXCEPT MACAN) > GENERAL INFORMATION

WARNING: Toxic substances

Danger of poisoning or suffocation

• Danger of burns to the eyes and skin

→ Ventilate the work area well.

→ Never ingest or inhale.

→ Read specific information on the Hazard Sheet.

→ Do not smoke, eat or drink in the work area.

# Information

This repair method is a cost-effective repair that may have quality implications. To achieve the best repair result, always use the tool recommended by Porsche and attend the special training courses run by the tool/system suppliers.

With interior cosmetic repairs, it is possible to repair grazes, tears, scratches and burn holes in plastic and leather components in the interior. Example: → Before and after

![](images/8f5c52a7eea7b9cb4fb2b371a9b904f264b64589304af8424ced87a86fade3ff.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Interior Cosmetic Area (Before And After)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

With this repair method, the damage is filled with special adhesives and resins and the surface structure is restored by means of a pattern imprint. The damaged area is painted over in the last step.

# WM 0740IN INTERIOR COSMETIC REPAIRS (EXCEPT MACAN) > GENERAL INFORMATION > REPAIR RESTRICTIONS

Tears and cuts in low-stressed components (e.g. dashboard, trim panels) up to around 50 mm long can be repaired.   
Tears and cuts in more heavily stressed components (e.g. seats) up to around 20 mm long can be repaired.   
•Holes in low-stressed components (e.g. dashboard, trim panels) up to around 20 mm in diameter can be repaired.   
• Holes in more heavily stressed components (e.g. seats) up to around 10 mm in diameter can be repaired.   
Damage in the area of a seam cannot be repaired.   
Alcantara leather cannot be repaired.   
Here too, the skils and experience of the worker are crucial for a good repair result.

# WM 0740IN INTERIOR COSMETIC REPAIRS (EXCEPT MACAN) > CREATING PATTERN IMPRINT

Toolbox: Interior repairs system B1 WE 1355

1. Clean surface of the structural area to be copied using "Plastcleaner" and dry with warm air (approx. 60 °C).

![](images/052e4fcf27dfd02080115fa6eeab8b4c1022a37ecf7e1c4da93d265e219cefa4.webp)  
Fig 1: Cleaning Interior Cosmetic Surface

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Evenly apply the "Moldmaker" two-component material to the surface using the mixing tube and mixing gun.

3. Spread out the compound into a thin layer (approx. 2 - 3 mm) using a spatula.

![](images/87d95064a6f389177ca07c19a6de4990e64900307d95848848984cfa42624e5a.webp)  
Fig 2: Applying Paint On Interior Cosmetic

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Leave pattern imprint to cure for 10 - 15 min.

5. Carefully remove pattern imprint and clean the surface using "Plastcleaner".

![](images/33bb74ca6790b49b3c466af2c6effc26a8c39111269f0e7cd78b99df95b1fdc5.webp)  
Fig 3: Removing Pattern Imprint

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

The pattern imprint can be re-used numerous times.

The pattern imprint wil not leave behind any undesirable marks and can therefore be used anywhere.

# WM 0740IN INTERIOR COSMETIC REPAIRS (EXCEPT MACAN) > VINYL REPAIRS

1. Thoroughly clean the area to be repaired using "Plastcleaner" and dry with warm air (approx. 60 °C).

![](images/f97d54bcf3a65ccf80e8b3a891c2fb1e4cab6f2da45c9ccdf56bffc9e171aa90.webp)  
Fig 1: Cleaning Interior Cosmetic Surface

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

. Fill the damaged area with "Compound" adhesive filler right up to the upper level.

# Information

Always test the thermal sensitivity of the vinyl in a concealed area first.

If the damage is deep, apply the material in several layers, removing any excess compound at the edge immediately and curing between layers using an iron (→ Temperature: 160°C ).

![](images/93ac811d61423f72f7d3697f7ac0120cb7c56fbc439cfdb6466a8364dada5093.webp)  
Fig 2: Filling Material Damage Area

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. With larger areas of damage, such as tears or holes, insert a piece of nylon fabric under the area to be repaired for reinforcement.

1. 3.1. Cut a suitable piece of nylon fabric material to size and push it under the damaged area using the small spatula.

2.3.2. Rub adhesive filler into the nylon fabric and cure using the iron.

4. Lay the pattern imprint onto the top layer of adhesive fillr to restore the pattern, gently press on with the heated iron for 5 - 10 seconds and wait for a few seconds before continuing.

![](images/34940bacca7ef979f3aeba6c796b241f43518b37f6abbeefdb7a384d197382f1.webp)  
Fig 3: Heating Adhesive Filler

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Cool down and fix the transferred pattern using a cooling block.

![](images/980bc7d760845ab182db616aa8b5e03e4414d362a1e1efe34abebbfd21a806b7.webp)  
Fig 4: Cooling Adhesive Filler

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. Carefully remove pattern imprint.

![](images/1921c6012000b2c460647d2ca2ae50434ddc6032ae887b39f67672abffaef8ff.webp)  
Fig 5: Removing Pattern Imprint

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. The adhesive filler has cured when it becomes slightly transparent. If the adhesive filler still looks milky, repeat steps → 4. to → 6.

8Thoroughly clean the area to be painted using "Plastcleaner" and dry with warm air (approx. 60 C), as "Plastcleaner" is partly water-soluble.

Then paint the repaired area. → Painting and dyeing

![](images/e34509a107798a64bb70ee38dc352f5a93d5298bcab7109b4926d2d3700c9b2d.webp)  
Fig 6: Applying Paint In Repaired Area

# WM 0740IN INTERIOR COSMETIC REPAIRS (EXCEPT MACAN) > LEATHER REPAIRS

1. Thoroughly clean the area to be repaired a number of times using "Plastcleaner" and dry with warm air (approx. 60 °C).

![](images/2672b3ae9e6ef46c0ab393beafac65c4faf5d0e1fd2275e7e6eeaf8585c3bfa6.webp)  
Fig 1: Cleaning Interior Cosmetic Surface

# WM 0740IN INTERIOR COSMETIC REPAIRS (EXCEPT MACAN) > LEATHER REPAIRS > REPAIRING SCRATCHES AND CREASES

1. Fillscratches or creases with "Leather Crack Filler" and allow to dry for around 1 - 2 hours before continuing with step → 7.

If the damage is deep, apply in several layers and dry with warm air (approx. 60 C); the "Leather Crack Filler" shrinks by up to 30% as it dries.

![](images/97c67462f1e930ee8cb465d9abe62355d5a341f5d8cf3ed32f404be9f6056733.webp)  
Fig 1: Filling Scratches

# WM 0740IN INTERIOR COSMETIC REPAIRS (EXCEPT MACAN) > LEATHER REPAIRS > REPAIRING TEARS AND HOLES

1. Fillthe damaged area with "Compound" adhesive filler right up to the upper level.

# Information

Always test the thermal sensitivity of the leather in a concealed area first.

If the damage is deep, apply the material in several layers, removing any excess compound at the edge immediately and curing between layers using the iron (→ Temperature: 160°C ).

![](images/c19e2b7005fe4a9565a3feb2b85ab0359aaa53caae8b9f4f953e11a304bb3e84.webp)  
Fig 1: Filling Material Damage Area

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. With larger areas of damage, such as tears or holes, insert a piece of nylon fabric under the area to be repaired for reinforcement.

1.2.1. Cut a suitable piece of nylon fabric material to size and push it under the damaged area using the small spatula. 2.2.2 Rub adhesive filer into the nylon fabric and cure using the iron.

3. Lay the pattern imprint onto the top layer of adhesive filer to restore the pattern, gently press on with the heated iron for 5 - 10 seconds and wait for a few seconds before continuing.

![](images/39461111bc9de5124edb8e6821fd1fd43dcffb59a8f8aede5da10fa712b4d18a.webp)  
Fig 2: Heating Adhesive Filler

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Cool down and fix the transferred pattern using a cooling block.

![](images/3fa1a5fc0606d2ea7ffc187af23f3c13c44f0a9ca4674a84b0491e63666312b1.webp)  
Fig 3: Cooling Adhesive Filler

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Carefully remove pattern imprint.

![](images/b195277592e75c36bf87c5fa200e6ca6276a118fd63a93005eef92086e1e8eee.webp)  
Fig 4: Removing Pattern Imprint

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6The adhesive filler has cured when it becomes slightly transparent. If the adhesive filler still looks milky, repeat steps → 3. to → 5.

# Information

Leather is a natural product which must be treated individually.

The leather must be thoroughly cleaned a number of times prior to painting as leather becomes greasy from the inside and it is not possible to rule out any previous treatment with siliconcontaining products. Impregnation can also impair the adhesion of the paint.

7. Thoroughly clean leather a number of times with "Plastcleaner". Allow the leather to air dry for approx. 5 min. after cleaning. Clean the leather again if it is very dirty or if there is still a greasy residue.

8. Sand the damaged area with an abrasive pad or sandpaper (P400).

![](images/dc0122cb0e1e0525a1bdb10c9b75f42f4b7bb17b46b6e5de7bf504b633093fd1.webp)  
Fig 5: Cleaning Leather

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

Then paint the repaired area. → Painting and dyeing

# WM 0740IN INTERIOR COSMETIC REPAIRS (EXCEPT MACAN) > PAINTING AND DYEING

WARNING: Toxic substances Danger of poisoning or suffocation • Danger of burns to the eyes and skin

→ Ventilate the work area well.   
→ Never ingest or inhale.   
→ Read specific information on the Hazard Sheet.   
→ Do not smoke, eat or drink in the work area.   
1. From the color samples choose the color that most closely matches the original.   
. Shake paint container thoroughly before mixing.   
3. Mix paint on the paint scales interior repair scales, small(0.01g scale) WE 1357 in accordance with the formulary.   
4. Mix paints thoroughly and compare the color obtained with the original. To do this, dab or spray some of the paint onto the original part. Critically examine the color match of the paint when dry. It is often necessary to adapt the color mixture and sometimes this may take several attempts.   
5. If necessary, match the sheen and color intensity using the additive "Opacante A". The amount of this additive that can be added to the paint must not exceed 25%.   
6.Check adhesion of paint by gently scratching the dry paint.   
7. If the color is correct, apply paint to the damaged area using paint-spraying gun - Sata-Minijet WE 1146 or an airbrush gun.

For small areas of damage, the paint can also be applied using a clean, lint-free cloth. In this case, apply the paint in several layers using a circular motion.

![](images/4c81ab7a87481d697d951402f9485d698838fbcf2e8b3c240101e5f18b4f3827.webp)  
Fig 1: Applying Paint In Repaired Area

8. Leave paint to dry at a temperature of no less than 16 C for approx. 90 min. It may take less time to dry at warmer temperatures.

The drying time should be increased if the paint was applied in several layers.

. Match the lustre, if necessary:

1. "Matt fix scan" provides a matt finish.

2. "Gloss fix scan" provides a gloss finish.

3. A satin finish is achieved by mixing the two gloss regulators.

1.9.1. Shake gloss regulators thoroughly and filter through a paper filter.

2. 9.2. Mix "Mat fix scan" and "Gloss fix scan" thoroughly in the desired ratio.

3. 9.3. Test gloss regulator in a concealed area.

4.9.4. Check the lustre when dry and adapt if necessary.

5.9.5. Apply the gloss regulator using paint-spraying gun - Sata-Minijet WE 1146 or an airbrush gun.

For small areas of damage, the gloss regulator can also be applied using a clean, lint-free cloth. Apply it using a circular motion.

10. Leave the paint to dry overnight before applying any load.

# WM 0750IN PAINT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > GENERAL INFORMATION AND REPAIR AREAS

This repair method is a cost-effective repair that may have quality implications. To achieve the best repair result, always use the tool recommended by Porsche and attend the special training courses run by the tool/system suppliers.

Paint repairs (also known as spot coating) can be used for small areas of paint damage. In this case, the damage is repaired over a smallarea by touching up the base and clear lacquer. The transition point from the old to the new clear lacquer is polished to achieve a match.

IMPORTANT: There is a danger of creating trailing edges at the transition point when olishing the area.

# Areas of application:

•Paint repairs are possible on plastic and sheet metal.

Single-layer, double-layer and metallic paint finishes can be painted in this way.

This painting method can be used to its full extent in areas with low light reflection (e.g. bumpers, door sills, edges of parts). -green area

Paint repairs to components with larger surfaces are only possible to a limited extent -yellow area- . In these areas, only small areas of damage with a diameter of up to 35 mm or a length of up to 100 mm should be repaired.

•Damage to large surface areas cannot be corrected using paint repair methods. -red area

# WM 0760IN ALLOY WHEEL RECONDITIONING (ALL MODELS) > REPAIR

NOTE: Thermal stripping of alloy wheels

•Reduced rigidity of aluminum alloy Risk of breaks and irreparable damage to the rim

→ Do not use thermal stripping procedures or heat treatment on alloy wheels

NOTE: Incorrect repair of alloy wheels

Reduced endurance strength • Alloy wheel breaks

→ Only repairs to the surface paint finish on alloy wheel are permitted

The alloy wheel is a highly stressed vehicle component which may be subjected to extreme loads during operation. The repair restrictions must be strictly observed in order to ensure safe operation and prevent any potential hazards.

# Information

This repair method is a cost-effective repair that may have quality implications. To achieve the best repair result, always use the tool recommended by Porsche and attend the special training courses run by the tool/system suppliers.

The repair method combines paint repair methods and conventional painting methods.

When reconditioning alloy wheels, only repairs to damaged paintwork are permitted. Example: → Permissible damage , → Permissible damage

It is stil imperative to avoid sanding down areas through to the base material.

Repairs that affect the base material of the wheel (deposit-welding, filing and metal-cutting machining) → Prohibited machining operations are not permitted.

There must be no signs of corrosion on the alloy wheel.

6. Tighten top fastening screws securing transverse strut to body to the specified torque. Tightening torque 9.7 Nm (7.5 ftlb.)

7. Tighten side fastening screws securing transverse strut to body to the specified torque. Tightening torque 10 Nm (7.5 ftlb.)

Tighten side fastening screws on the front retaining strips to the specified torque. Tightening torque 9.7 Nm (7.5 ftlb.)   
9. Tighten fastening screws securing headlight mounting to body to the specified torque. Tightening torque 9 Nm (6.5 ftlb.)   
10.Tighten screw-type clamp securing throttle-housing cover to pressure pipe to the specified torque. Tightening torque 5.5 Nm (4 ftlb.)

# WM 503955 REPLACING SPRING STRUT MOUNT (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK > SUBSEQUENT WORK FOR BODY REPAIRS

1. Release and remove vehicle from the straightening system.

2. Clean joint areas and sheetmetal flanges with a wire brush.

3. Prime joint areas and sheetmetal flanges with 2K primer.

4. Restore standard seal with body sealant → 5X00IN42 SEAM SEALING .

Also seal the repair area carefully.

5. Paint repair area and adjacent surfaces, if necessary.   
6. Restore standard underbody protection with underbody sealant → 5X00IN43 UNDERBODY PROTECTION .

8. Install removed accessories in the repair area.

# WM 507955 REPLACING FRONT SIDE MEMBER (ALL MODELS) > PREPARING CONNECTION AREAS OF THE BODY FOR INSTALLATION

1. Align the sealing surface and connections of the body.

2. De-burr connection points and prepare them for welding.

# Information

1. Before final assembly, make sure you fully understand all the work steps involved and carry out a trial assembly without applying adhesive.

2. The bonding process can only be carried out reliably when a smooth and swift sequence of operations is guaranteed.   
3. Do not begin bonding work until all materials and tools necessary for later repair work are available.

3. Prepare marked areas for welding, bonding and blind riveting. → 5X00IN21 WORKING WITH BODY STRUCTURAL ADHESIVE .

# WM 507955 REPLACING FRONT SIDE MEMBER (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK > SUBSEQUENT WORK FOR BODY REPAIRS

1. Release and remove vehicle from the straightening system.   
2. Clean joint areas and sheetmetal flanges with a wire brush.   
3. Prime joint areas and sheetmetal flanges with 2K primer.   
4. Restore standard seal with body sealant → 5X00IN42 SEAM SEALING .   
Also seal the repair area carefully.   
5. Paint repair area and adjacent surfaces, if necessary.

6. Restore standard underbody protection with underbody sealant → 5X00IN43 UNDERBODY PROTECTION .   
7. Apply standard cavity preservation → 5XOOIN44 CAVITY PRESERVATION . Also carefully apply cavity preservation to the repair area.   
8. Install removed accessories in the repair area.

# WM 510555 REPLACING ROOF PILLAR (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Remove B-pillar reinforcement. → 514255 REPLACING B-PILLAR REINFORCEMENT

2. Remove A-pillar. → 511255 REPLACING A-PILLAR

3. Remove roof pillar. → 510555 REPLACING OUTER ROOF PILLAR PANEL

# WM 510555 REPLACING ROOF PILLAR (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK > SUBSEQUENT WORK FOR BODY REPAIRS

1. Release and remove vehicle from the straightening system.

2. Clean joint areas and sheetmetal flanges with a wire brush.

3. Prime joint areas and sheetmetal flanges with 2K primer.

4. Restore standard seal with body sealant → 5X00IN42 SEAM SEALING .

Also seal the repair area carefully.

5. Paint repair area and adjacent surfaces, if necessary.   
6. Restore standard underbody protection with underbody sealant → 5X00IN43 UNDERBODY PROTECTION .   
7. Apply standard cavity preservation → 5X00IN44 CAVITY PRESERVATION . Also carefully apply cavity preservation to the repair area.   
8. Install removed accessories in the repair area.

# WM 511355 REPLACING A-PILLAR REINFORCEMENT (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK > SUBSEQUENT WORK FOR BODY REPAIRS (WITHOUT STRAIGHTENING SYSTEM)

1. Clean joint areas and sheetmetal flanges with a wire brush.

2. Prime joint areas and sheetmetal flanges with 2K primer.

3. Restore standard seal with body sealant → 5X00IN42 SEAM SEALING . Also seal the repair area carefully.

4. Paint repair area and adjacent surfaces, if necessary.

5. Restore standard underbody protection with underbody sealant → 5X00IN43 UNDERBODY PROTECTION .   
6. Apply standard cavity preservation — 5X00IN44 CAVITY PRESERVATION . Also apply cavity preservation to the repair area.   
7. Install removed accessories in the repair area.

# WM 514155 REPLACING B-PILLAR (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK > PRELIMINARY WORK FOR BODY REPAIRS (WITHOUT STRAIGHTENING BENCH)

If it can be ensured there has been no deformation of the vehicle structure, the following repair can be carried out without the need of a straightening bench. In this case, the vehicle must not be raised when welding the component; it must stand on its wheels on an even surface.

1. Remove accessories in the repair area.

1.1.1. Remove accessories in the repair area according to the extent of damage to the vehicle.

2. Cover the accessories adjacent to the repair area on the vehicle.

1. 2.1. Cover all accessories remaining on the vehicle and adjacent areas with fire-proof protective covers.

3. Reshape connection area of the sheetmetal parts to be replaced.

4. Expose joint areas.

1.4.1. Remove underbody protection, paint, etc. from the joint areas of the body.

# WM 514255 REPLACING B-PILLAR REINFORCEMENT (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK > SUBSEQUENT WORK FOR BODY REPAIRS

1. Release and remove vehicle from the straightening system.

5. Paint repair area and adjacent surfaces, if necessary.   
6. Restore standard underbody protection with underbody sealant → 5X00IN43 UNDERBODY PROTECTION .   
7. Apply standard cavity preservation → 5XO0IN44 CAVITY PRESERVATION . Also carefully apply cavity preservation to the repair area.   
8. Install removed accessories in the repair area.

# Information

1. Before final assembly, make sure you fully understand all the work steps involved and carry out a trial assembly without applying adhesive.

2. The bonding process can only be carried out reliably when a smooth and swift sequence

of operations is guaranteed.

3. Do not begin bonding work until all materials and tools necessary for later repair work are available.

# WM 514855 REPLACING CENTRE SIDE MEMBER (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK > SUBSEQUENT WORK FOR BODY REPAIRS (WITHOUT STRAIGHTENING SYSTEM)

1. Clean joint areas and sheetmetal flanges with a wire brush.

2. Prime joint areas and sheetmetal flanges with 2K primer.

3. Restore standard seal with body sealant → 5X00IN42 SEAM SEALING . Also seal the repair area carefully.

4. Paint repair area and adjacent surfaces, if necessary.

5. Restore standard underbody protection with underbody sealant → 5X00IN43 UNDERBODY PROTECTION .

6. Apply standard cavity preservation → 5X00IN44 CAVITY PRESERVATION . Also apply cavity preservation to the repair area.

7. Install removed accessories in the repair area.

# WM 514955 REPLACING SIDE MEMBER REINFORCEMENT (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK > PRELIMINARY WORK FOR BODY REPAIRS (WITH STRAIGHTENING SYSTEM)

1. Remove accessories in the repair area.

1. 1.1. Remove accessories in the repair area according to the extent of damage on the vehicle.

2. Set up straightening bench with straightening system.

3. Set vehicle on straightening bench.

4. Cover accessories adjacent to the repair area on the vehicle.

1. 4.1. Cover all accessories remaining on the vehicle and adjacent areas with fire-proof protective covers.

5. Reshape connection area of the sheetmetal parts to be replaced.

6. Expose joint areas.

1.6.1. Remove underbody protection, paint, etc. from the joint areas of the body using a hot-air gun or rotary brush.

5. Paint repair area and adjacent surfaces, if necessary.   
6. Restore standard underbody protection with underbody sealant → 5X00IN43 UNDERBODY PROTECTION .   
7. Apply standard cavity preservation — 5X00IN44 CAVITY PRESERVATION . Also carefully apply cavity preservation to the repair area.   
8. Install removed accessories in the repair area.

# WM 516819 REMOVING AND INSTALLING DASHBOARD SUPPORT (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING DASHBOARD SUPPORT

The number of fastening screws, fixing clips, plug connections, holders and trim panels can vary depending on equipment.

The ilustrations for removing and installing the drive mechanism are shown only on one equipment variant and may differ from the actual equipment variant.

Some steps must be carried out automatically

Some of the repair ilustrations show only one side of the vehicle.

1. Cover center console with protective mat.

2. Remove Kessy antenna on dashboard with the bracket. → 966719 REMOVING AND INSTALLING KESSY ANTENNA

3. Unclip air guide -1- at the air conditioner and remove it.

4. Unclip air guide -2- at the air conditioner and remove it.

5. Unclip electric line -3- at bracket for passenger's airbag unit and remove bracket -4- .

6 Unscrew fastening screw -5- for the right air guide at the support.

![](images/93f706325b8557ffdad2a5aaea9c51e160615c6dae7e79b4bf7283aaaca48ea3.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Air Guides   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Unscrew fastening screws -1- on the support.

8. Unscrew fastening screws -2- and remove holder -3- .

![](images/e84696ce844242d1a66091eeb7478c6c51174805d4cb608c890c72e0af5e274c.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Dashboard Support Brackets   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

9. Unscrew fastening screws -1, 2, 3- on the air conditioner.

![](images/fd26d73e2155b8506c03de748f10667b88cc0b8354ac7a4846ab2382bba0cf80.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Air Conditioning Unit

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

10. Carry out all steps required for loosening the dashboard wire harness from the support. → WM 970819 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WIRE HARNESS FOR DASHBOARD

11. Unscrew fastening screws -1- .

12. Unscrew fastening screw -2- .

13. Unscrew fastening nuts -3- .

14. Unscrew fastening screw -4- .

![](images/bb7e9f377924330b0b7f85f909f96ef97ff27a73f9201fa7dbbb3bf64a3eeb08.webp)  
Fig 4: Identifying Dashboard Support Screws And Nuts

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# The help of another person is required for steps 15 to 18.

15. Press air conditioner -1- in direction of arrow -arrow- using a suitable tool and guide retaining lug -2- out of the bracket -3- .

16. Carefully pull support -4- forward until the support -4- is removed fully at the studs -5- .

17. Pad the strut -6- with foam to prevent damage to the windscreen.

18. Carefully lift up the support -4- and remove it.

![](images/a3a81e4ba95c8f59e67c359e4c96d7753633ac755e159c5a49974f4def28c15f.webp)  
Fig 5: Identifying Dashboard Support

# WM 516819 REMOVING AND INSTALLING DASHBOARD SUPPORT (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING DASHBOARD SUPPORT

Check that al fixing clis are positioned ful and correctly.

Check that the fixing clips are not bent or broken.

Replace damaged or missing clips with new ones.

Installation is performed in reverse order. Pay particular attention to the following:

1. When installing the support, check that the lines -1, 2- are routed correctly.

![](images/486f0583af079055ca348523ae9f04b9eab288f073ae3f743d550c114f57d6c0.webp)  
Fig 1: Installing Dashboard Support

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

Tighten fastening nuts on the support at the A-pilar to the specified torque. Tightening torque 20 Nm (15 ftlb.)

3. Tighten fastening screw on the support at the A-pillr to the specified torque. Tightening torque 20 Nm (15 ftlb.)

4. Tighten fastening screws securing support to cardan tunnel to the specified torque. Tightening torque 20 Nm (15 ftlb.)

5. Tighten fastening screw securing support to body to the specified torque. Tightening torque 20 Nm (15 ftlb.)

6. Tighten fastening screws securing support to air conditioner to the specified torque.

7. Tighten fastening screws securing brackets to support to the specified torque. Tightening torque 9 Nm (6.5 ftlb.)

Tighten fastening screw securing air guide to support to the specified torque. Tightening torque 1.5 Nm (1 ftlb.)

The bonding process can only be carried out reliably when a smooth and swift sequence of operations is guaranteed.   
•Do not begin bonding work until all materials and tools necessary for later repair work are available.

# Information

Adhesive must not be applied to areas to be plug-welded or fully welded using inert gas.

1. Install outer B-pillar and check that it fits perfectly. Check gap dimensions. → 5X00IN DIAGRAM - BODY GAP DIMENSIONS

Make sure that all openings and gaps between the body and C-pillar reinforcement are closed off with the sealing compound.

# WM 532955 REPLACING C-PILLAR REINFORCEMENT (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK > SUBSEQUENT WORK FOR BODY REPAIRS (WITHOUT STRAIGHTENING SYSTEM)

1. Clean joint areas and sheetmetal flanges with a wire brush.   
2. Prime joint areas and sheetmetal flanges with 2K primer.

Also seal the repair area carefully.   
4. Paint repair area and adjacent surfaces, if necessary.

7. Install removed accessories in the repair area.

# WM 534855 REPLACING REAR SIDE MEMBER (SECTION) (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK > SUBSEQUENT WORK FOR BODY REPAIRS

1. Release and remove vehicle from the straightening system.   
2. Clean joint areas and sheetmetal flanges with a wire brush.   
3. Prime joint areas and sheetmetal flanges with 2K primer.   
4. Restore standard seal with body sealant → 5X00IN42 SEAM SEALING Also seal the repair area carefully.   
5. Paint repair area and adjacent surfaces, if necessary.   
6. Restore standard underbody protection with underbody sealant → 5X00IN43 UNDERBODY PROTECTION   
7. Apply standard cavity preservation → 5X00IN44 CAVITY PRESERVATION . Also carefully apply cavity preservation to the repair area.   
8. Install removed accessories in the repair area.

# WM 536855 REPLACING (INNER) REAR WHEEL HOUSING (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK > SUBSEQUENT WORK FOR BODY REPAIRS

1. Release and remove vehicle from the straightening system.   
2. Clean joint areas and sheetmetal flanges with a wire brush.   
3. Prime joint areas and sheetmetal flanges with 2K primer.   
4. Restore standard seal with body sealant → 5X00IN42 SEAM SEALING - section on "Information". Also seal the repair area carefully.   
5. Paint repair area and adjacent surfaces, if necessary.   
6. Restore standard underbody protection with underbody sealant → 5X00IN43 UNDERBODY PROTECTION - section on "Information".   
7. Apply standard cavity preservation → 5X00IN44 CAVITY PRESERVATION - section on "Information". Also carefully apply cavity preservation to the repair area.   
8. Install removed accessories in the repair area.

Some steps must be carried out automatically.   
Some of the repair illustrations show only one side of the vehicle. 1. Remove pressure pipe. (Only if fitted) → 214119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING PRESSURE PIPE 2. Unscrew fastening screws -1- securing lower part of lid lock -2- to lock carrier. 3. Remove lower part of lid lock -2- by puling it up.

The self-locking nuts must always be replaced. 1. Adjust upper part of lock with respect to the lid according to the noted position (impression made at the factory). 2. Fit fastening nuts so that the upper part of the lock can still be moved. 3. Lower the lid slowly until the clip for the upper part of the lock -1- is touching the lower part of the lock. The clip must be centered flush with the slit in the lower part of the lock -2- .

# WM 552215 ADJUSTING FRONT LID (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > ADJUSTING FRONT LID > ADJUSTING FRONT GAP DIMENSIONS

Set gap dimensions on lid and accessories in accordance with the gap specifications.   
Given a clearance in the opening that is too great or too small the accessories must be centered with respect to the body.   
Ensure that the gaps do not run in a wedge-shaped fashion or do not narrow at local points. The given values are guidelines, which should be observed as far as possible.   
The guidelines apply to repair and assembly work.   
• Use star gauges to check the gap dimensions. Star gauges for body gap dimensions NR.127-1

# WM 552215 ADJUSTING FRONT LID (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CHECKING FRONT LID LOCK

The lid lock does not have an emergency release.

When working close to the front apron and on the various parts of the lock, carry out the following function test before closing the lid:

1. Check that the release cable is clipped fully into the bracket provided.   
2. Lock lower part of lid lock using a screwdriver.   
3. Release the lid lock using the lever in the passenger compartment.   
4. Perform a visual inspection to check that the lock releases correctly.

4. Install cover for alarm siren. → INSTALLING ALARM SIREN

5. Install cowl panel cover. → INSTALLING COWL PANEL COVER

# WM 553119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT PNEUMATIC SPRING (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING FRONT PNEUMATIC SPRING

CAUTION: Incorrect handling of gas-filled shock absorbers

Gas-filled shock absorbers can burst   
Risk of eye injuries   
Risk of bruising

→ Gas-filled shock absorbers must be in idle state before removal.

→ Open the lid.

→ Secure the lid to prevent it from closing accidentally following removal of the gas-filled shock absorbers.

→ Do not use force to open the gas-filled shock absorbers because of their high internal pressure.

![](images/05feeccde170744b599c4f1581d863afca7a6979610f1c55cc55a27383c67875.webp)  
Fig 1: Locating Pneumatic Spring Position

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

1. Disengage pneumatic spring at the lid and body.

![](images/d800cfa930f886b098e1b6673d0f1017f04d68d38325c2fb112a9be06dd476b5.webp)  
Fig 2: Disengaging Pneumatic Spring (Lid)

![](images/f36a82be2d176f6c2250bf0f05eccefa7b700590839009413cd665177147d911.webp)  
Fig 3: Disengaging Pneumatic Spring (Body)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

1.1.1. Get a second person to secure the front lid to prevent it from closing accidentally.   
2.1.2. Insert a screwdriver -2- between the head of the pneumatic spring and the safety clip -3- (-A-) .   
3.1.3. Loosen the safety clip -3- by levering the screwdriver -2- up and down -B  
4.1.4. The safety clip remains in the head of the pneumatic spring.   
5.1.5. Pull pneumatic spring -1- off the ball joints -C- .   
6.1.6. Remove screwdriver.

2. Remove pneumatic spring.
