# Information

Always comply with the regulations for handling ESD-sensitive components!

Assembly work may only be carried out if the mechanic is wearing the working clothes and shoes approved by Porsche.   
The new part must only be removed from the ESD (electrostatic discharge) protective packaging   
just before installation and at the position at which the part is to be installed.   
Never touch the electric pins and plug contacts. 1. Switch off ignition and pull remote control out of ignition lock. 2. Release clip -a- (-1-) , swivel it aside -b- and remove electric plug connection from rear lid control unit -2- . 3. Release electric plug connections -3- (-c-) and disconnect them from the rear lid control unit.

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# WM 556855 REPLACING CONTROL UNIT FOR REAR LID (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CODING AND CALIBRATING CONTROL UNIT

NOTE: Voltage drop

Risk of irreparable damage to control unit   
Risk of damage to control unit   
Fault entries in the control unit   
Coding in the control unit is aborted   
Malfunctions in control unit, even during programming

→ Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch off ignition and remove ignition key.

→ Ensure that the power supply is not interrupted during programming.

→ Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least → Nominal value: 40 A to the vehicle battery.

# Information

The PlWis Tester Il9818 instructions take precedence since the description may be different with later Tester releases.

The procedure described here has been structured in general terms. Different text or additional information may appear in PIWis Tester Il 9818 .

1. Connect the Porsche System Tester to the vehicle and start the System Tester. Switch on   
ignition and press [F12] to continue.   
2. Select the vehicle type. The diagnostic application starts.   
3. Select the required control unit, e.g. Rear lid in the overview and press [F12] to continue.   
4. Extended identification must now be selected.   
5. Enter the vehicle identification number and press Enter.   
6. Maintenance/repairs must then be selected.   
7. Control unit replacement must now be selected. Then press [F12] to continue.   
8. Select Write data, press [F12] and then press [F8] to start. Data is installed.   
9. The System Tester displays the message Data has been written. Press [F12] to continue.   
10. Codings/adaptations must now be selected.   
11. Automatic coding must now be selected. Then press [F12] to continue.   
12. If the message Coding was completed successfully appears, press [F12] to continue.

CAUTION: When you start the calibration/teaching process, the tailgate moves to its limit stops. Mechanical force limitation is not guaranteed during this process.

1. Danger of pinching and squashing body parts.

2. Incorrect values for the control unit, resulting in malfunctions.

→ Take precautions to ensure that no body parts and objects can get caught in the tailgate.

13. Select Calibration in the Maintenance/repairs menu and press [F12] to continue.

14. Read the warnings, press [F12] to continue and then press [F8] to start the calibration process.

15. Read the instructions on the Tester and perform the calibration process as instructed.

16. Once the teaching process has been completed successfully, an acoustic signal will be issued.

17. Fault memory must be selected and erased if necessary.

# WM 557319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING ACTUATING CYLINDER FOR REAR LID (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > PRELIMINARY WORK

CAUTION: Incorrect handling of actuating cylinders

•Actuating cylinders can burst Risk of eye injuries Risk of bruising

→ The actuating cylinders must be in idle state in order to remove them.

→ Open the lid.

→ Secure the lid after removing the actuating cylinders to prevent it from closing accidentally.

→ Do not use force when opening the actuating cylinders due to the high internal pressure.

The illustrations for removing and installing the drive mechanism are shown only on one equipment variant and may differ from the actual equipment variant.

Some of the repair illustrations show only one side of the vehicle.

# WM 559015 ADJUSTING REAR LID (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > ADJUSTING REAR LID

• Set gap dimensions on lid and accessories in accordance with the gap specifications.   
Given a clearance in the opening that is too great or too small, the accessories must be centered with respect to the body.   
Ensure that the gaps do not run in a wedge-shaped fashion or do not narrow at local points. The given values are guidelines, which should be observed as far as possible.   
The guidelines apply to repair and assembly work.   
• Use star gauges to check the gap dimensions. Star gauges for body gap dimensions NR.127-1

![](images/29c7e5e5df17e2af65d6006e5ac76bd599932d612c0b3f93a7ab067fc661091b.webp)  
Fig 1: Adjusting Rear Lid

![](images/c06f1f008939b6a958334e66062f5e71d6c13984739d3312cbc511675bcc8d86.webp)

![](images/345d2b651846e5e03891e85dbff594e419e7df26b799dca252befd50f977caf3.webp)

# WM 559015 ADJUSTING REAR LID (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CHECKING REAR LID LOCK > FUNCTION TEST ON REAR LID LOCK

1. Check the function of the rear lid lock.

1. 1.1. Lock the lid lock using a screwdriver and then unlock it again using the lid release. The lock must swivel out freely.

2.1.2. Check that the rear lid stays open automatically in the upper positions.

3. 1.3. From the middle position, the rear lid must fall nto the lock automatically and lock fully. (with gas-filled shock absorbers)

4.1.4. Perform a visual inspection to check that the lock releases again correctly.

2. Check electric operation of rear lid lock.

1. 2.1. Open the lock using the electric release or remote control.

3. Check electric tailgate drive mechanism.

1. 3.1. Check opening and closing function using the outer handle on the rear lid, the remote control and the switch in the driver's door.

2. 3.2. It must be possible to stop rear lid operation at any time using all actuators.

3. 3.3. Check the obstacle detection function.

Simulate an obstacle while opening and closing by holding the rear lid firmly.

# WM 559019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR LID (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING REAR LID

CAUTION: Incorrect handling of gas-filled shock absorbers

Gas-filled shock absorbers can burst   
Risk of eye injuries   
Risk of bruising

→ Gas-filled shock absorbers must be in idle state before removal.

→ Open the lid.

→ Secure the lid to prevent it from closing accidentally following removal of the gas-filled shock absorbers.

→ Do not use force to open the gas-filled shock absorbers because of their high internal pressure.

# Information

Only remove the wiring harness from the rear lid as far as the lid hinge.

# Information

Use a marking pen to mark the position of accessories with respect to each other before removal in order to reduce the amount of adjustment work required for gaps and joints.

э

1. A second person should hold the rear lid to prevent it from closing accidentally.

Only for vehicles with Power Lift Tailgate

2. Remove actuating cylinder for rear lid at the top of the rear lid. → 557319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING ACTUATING CYLINDER FOR REAR LID .

Only for vehicles without Power Lift Tailgate

3. Remove gas-filled shock absorber for rear lid at the top of the rear lid. → 559319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR PNEUMATIC SPRING .

4. Unscrew fastening screws securing rear lid to lid hinges.

2. Tighten fastening screws to the specified tightening torque Tightening torque 10 Nm (7.5 ftlb.)until secure.

# WM 559319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR PNEUMATIC SPRING (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING REAR PNEUMATIC SPRING

CAUTION: Incorrect handling of gas-filled shock absorbers

Gas-filled shock absorbers can burst   
Risk of eye injuries   
Risk of bruising

→ Gas-filled shock absorbers must be in idle state before removal.

→ Open the lid.

→ Secure the lid to prevent it from closing accidentally following removal of the gas-filled shock absorbers.

→ Do not use force to open the gas-filled shock absorbers because of their high internal pressure.

# Information

The number of fastening screws, fixing clips, plug connections, holders and trim panels can vary depending on equipment.   
The ilustrations for removing and installing the drive mechanism are shown only on one equipment variant and may differ from the actual equipment variant.   
Some steps must be carried out automatically   
Some of the repair illustrations show only one side of the vehicle. 1. Open the rear lid. . Loosen the pneumatic spring.

![](images/01dc7976274f7ac88b1469d543780a4c95429346f6dccfe5b2ae8e39268268db.webp)  
Fig 1: Removing Pneumatic Spring   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

1. 2.1. A second person should hold the rear lid to prevent it from closing accidentally.

2.2.2. Insert a screwdriver between the head of the pneumatic spring -1- and the safety clip.

3.2.3. Lift up the safety clip by levering the screwdriver towards the rear -A- . The safety clip remains on the head of the pneumatic spring -1- .

4.2.4. Pull the pneumatic spring off the ball joint -B- .

5.2.5. Remove the screwdriver.

# WM 559319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR PNEUMATIC SPRING (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > INSTALLING REAR PNEUMATIC SPRING

1. Installation is performed in reverse order to removal.   
2. Check that the safety clips have engaged correctly. The safety clip must be directly on the head of the pneumatic spring.

# WM 559319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR PNEUMATIC SPRING (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > FUNCTION TEST ON REAR PNEUMATIC SPRING

1. Close and open the lid several times to check that the pneumatic springs are working properly and were fitted correctly.

2. Open the lid fully. The two fitted pneumatic springs must hold the lid open.

3. Close the lid.

# WM 572615 ADJUSTING LOCK PEG (ALL MODELS) > ADJUSTING LOCK PEG

The striker pin can be adjusted by changing the plasticity of the adjusting element in the B-pillar.   
The setting is retained when the striker pin is removed.

# WM 575115 ADJUSTING FRONT DOOR (ALL MODELS) > ADJUSTING FRONT DOOR

WARNING: Incorrect handling of safety bolts

Danger of injury

Loss of torque

→ Always use new fastening screws and nuts following removal.

→ Observe specified tightening torques.

→ Carry out a visual inspection of allre-used parts.

# Information

Only tighten the fastening screws on the door hinges hand-tight from the inside until the doors are set correctly.

# Information

Set gap dimensions on the lids, doors and covers, or accessories in accordance with the gap specifications.   
Given a clearance in the openings that is too great or too small the movable body parts or the accessories must be centred accordingly.   
Ensure that the gaps do not run in a wedge-shaped fashion or do not narrow at local points. You can use star gauges for body gap dimensions NR.127-1 for this.   
The given values are guidelines which should be observed as far as possible.   
The guidelines apply to repair and assembly work.

# Information

The door hinge must be aligned after installing the door.   
Loosen fastening screws for door hinge at the door and fastening screws for door hinge at the A-pillar so that the threaded connections can be moved.

# Information

The number of fastening screws, fixing clips, plug connections, holders and trim panels can vary depending on equipment.   
The illstrations for removing and instaling the drive mechanism are shown only on one equipment variant and may differ from the actual equipment variant.   
•Some steps must be carried out automatically.   
Some of the repair illustrations show only one side of the vehicle. 1. Adjust front door with door hinge at the door.

![](images/0b6d1563be062a5392b2a93b4c5d6cf4ead05c1239ff8aaffbf5475841764119.webp)

![](images/51e5ebe38b85afd9319a2b42f0e3114eeb434472028c67d4a172d711a54c4ce1.webp)

![](images/4cff38eaa427d47c40ed4b91912c219cf3556cde71de4329204be3b02d4a4b24.webp)

# WM 575119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT DOOR (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING FRONT DOOR

1. Slide the locking mechanism -1- up using a suitable tool and disconnect plug connection -2- .

![](images/caeec5f2df5ffff2fd663c3c2c9ae3e09f7655fcadf7004227838178ad1dad5c.webp)  
Fig 1: Disconnecting Electric Plug Connection

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Unscrew and remove fastening screw on the door arrester -4- at the vehicle door.

![](images/e60e42b5bd52387307323fc9f25d1ffeb7cf82d4c0d60daa2d06d06030e2ef20.webp)  
Fig 2: Removing Screw On Door Arrester

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Pull plastic caps -3- off the hinge screws at the top and bottom hinge joints -6- .

![](images/04143088161693a52dc5aeff2b4577e3e98c566fab3ce67c9edaf4b99ce8d4e4.webp)  
Fig 3: Pulling Off Caps On Hinge Screws

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Loosen fastening screws -5- on the top and bottom hinge joint -6- .

![](images/c3315453abfa80f039d4e0a19569d6a04ccf569ffa9d84d96aad1249ff5ef458.webp)  
Fig 4: Loosening Hinge Joint

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Get another person to hold the vehicle door.

6. Lift the vehicle door up slightly until the hinge bolts come out of the hinge halves on the door side.

![](images/ef541d428e9291179724871b262ea1a8f15b505096106813dfcc9e2127ce6b3d.webp)  
Fig 5: Lifting Vehicle Door   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Remove vehicle door.

# WM 575119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT DOOR (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING FRONT DOOR

1. Installation is performed in reverse order to removal.   
2. Tighten fastening screw on door hinge to Tightening torque 27 Nm (20 ftlb.) +/-3.5 Nm (+/-2.5 ftib.) .   
3. Tighten fastening screw for door arrester to Tightening torque 33 Nm (24 ftlb.) .

# WM 575155 REPLACING FRONT DOOR (ALL MODELS) > REPLACING FRONT DOOR

•The scope of work to be carried out can vary depending on equipment variant.

Some steps must be carried out automatically.   
Missing or damaged components and fastening parts must be replaced with new ones. 1. Remove rear-view mirror. → Removing rear-view mirror 2. Remove window channel seal. → REMOVING FRONT WINDOW GUIDE 3. Remove window guide. → Removing front window guide 4. Remove cover for door. → Removing cover for front door 5. Remove corner window pane. → Removing front corner window pane 6. Remove door handle. → Removing Door Handle 7. Remove door lock. → Removing Door Lock 8. Remove inner door release. → Removing Inner Door Release 9. Remove door arrester. → Removing Front Door Arrester 10. Remove door control unit. → WM 577355 REPLACING DOOR CONTROL UNIT 11. Remove rubber seal for front door. → Removing Lower Rubber Seal For Front Door 12. Remove power window regulator. → Removing front power windows 13. Remove wire harness for door. → Removing wire harness for door in front door panel 14. Remove door. → Removing Front Door 15. Install new door. → Installing Front Door 16. Fit blind rivet nut (top fastening point for the corner window pane).

Further assembly is carried out in reverse order.

![](images/f778b5eb36edf3f7bb2606e20f2e47efe3cd3d491a88cfc5afd7451fd8309a76.webp)

# WM 577355 REPLACING DOOR CONTROL UNIT (ALL MODELS) > REPLACING DOOR CONTROL UNIT

NOTE: Voltage drop

Risk of irreparable damage to control unit   
Risk of damage to control unit   
Fault entries in the control unit   
•Coding in the control unit is aborted   
Malfunctions in control unit, even during programming → Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch offignition and remove ignition key.   
→ Ensure that the power supply is not interrupted during programming.

→ Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least — Nominal value: 40 A to the vehicle battery.

# Information

The PIWis Tester Il9818 instructions take precedence since the description may be different with later Tester releases.

The procedure described here has been structured in general terms. Different text or additional information may appear in PIWis Tester Il 9818 .

1. Switch ofignition and replace control unit. → Replacing Door Control Unit   
2. Connect the PIWis Tester to the vehicle and start the Tester. Switch on ignition.   
3. Select the vehicle type and start the diagnostic application.   
4. Select the required control unit, e.g. Driver's door in the overview .   
5. Extended identification must now be selected.   
6. Enter the vehicle identification number and press Enter.   
7. Maintenance/repairs must then be selected.   
8. Control unit replacement must now be selected. Then press [F12].   
9. Select Write data, press [F12] and then press [F8] to start. The data is now loaded.   
10. The Tester displays the message Data has been written. Press [F12] to continue.   
11. Codings/adaptations must now be selected.   
12. Automatic coding must now be selected. Then press [F12] to continue.   
13. When the message Coding has been completed successfully appears, press [F12] to   
continue.   
14. Read out the fault memory and erase it if necessary.   
15. Check the function of the door control unit.

# WM 578919 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CONTROL UNIT FOR REAR-END ELECTRONICS (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING CONTROL UNIT FOR REAR-END ELECTRONICS

NOTE: Voltage peaks

Risk of damage to load or to the control unit

→ Remove the ignition key and switch off load before disconnecting or removing load.

# Information

Always comply with the regulations for handling ESD-sensitive components!

Assembly work may only be carred out if the mechanic is wearing the working clothes and shoes approved by Porsche.   
The new part must only be removed from the ESD (electrostatic discharge) protective packaging just before installation and at the position at which the part is to be installed.   
Never touch the electric pins and plug contacts. 1. Unclip control unit for rear-end electronics -1- from the holder -2- (-a-) and swivel it out -b- .

![](images/8d6da359c78b14f9efb1926870a99ab847c924abf30d7c7b9fffc58e4712057b.webp)  
Fig 1: Removing Control Unit For Rear-End Electronics   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Release electric plug connections -1- (-arrows-) and disconnect them from the rear-end electronics control unit -2- .

![](images/4b7024035c5b752ae346edf69afe993fed23e93692713914e02b4a635fdf576a.webp)  
Fig 2: Disconnecting Electric Plug Connections

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Release the swivel bar -1- (-arrows-) , swivel it up and disconnect electric plug connections -2- from the rear-end electronics control unit -3- .

![](images/64bba9a0f570a9978b5400db5fb358aabcef0f7ecfa8c6d5e1499dc9294c9b9b.webp)  
Fig 3: Disconnecting Electric Plug Connections

Always comply with the regulations for handling ESD-sensitive components!

Assembly work may only be carried out if the mechanic is wearing the working clothes and shoes approved by Porsche.   
The new part must only be removed from the ESD (electrostatic discharge) protective packaging   
just before installation and at the position at which the part is to be installed.   
Never touch the electric pins and plug contacts. 1. Installation is performed in reverse order to removal.

# WM 578955 REPLACING CONTROL UNIT FOR REAR-END ELECTRONICS (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Switch off ignition and replace control unit. → 578919 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CONTROL UNIT FOR REAR-END ELECTRONICS

# WM 578955 REPLACING CONTROL UNIT FOR REAR-END ELECTRONICS (ALL MODELS) > TEACHING CONTROL UNIT FOR REAR-END ELECTRONICS > TEACHING

All remote controls (keys) are required for teaching a DME, front-end electronics (front BCM), rear-end electronics (rear BCM), electronic steering lock (ELV) control unit or remote controls (keys) for example.

Remote controls (keys) that are not taught during this teaching procedure wil no longer be recognized by the vehicle.

NOTE: Voltage drop

•Risk of irreparable damage to control unit   
Risk of damage to control unit   
• Fault entries in the control unit   
Coding in the control unit is aborted   
• Malfunctions in control unit, even during programming

→ Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch offignition and remove ignition key.

— Ensure that the power suppy is not interrupted during programming.

→ Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least — Nominal value: 40 A to the vehicle battery.

# Information

The Plwis Tester Il9818 instructions take precedence since the description may be different with later Tester releases.

The procedure described here has been structured in general terms. Different text or additional information may appear in PIWis Tester Il 9818 .

1. Connect the PIWis Tester to the vehicle and start the Tester. Switch on ignition.   
2. Select the vehicle type and start the diagnostic application.   
3. Select the Rear-end electronics control unit in the overview.   
4. Codings/adaptations  must now be selected.   
5. Automatic coding must be selected and then press [F12].   
6. The Tester displays the message Coding completed successfull. Press [F12] to end the   
process.   
7. To activate the control units, switch on the hazard warning lights.   
8. Return to the Start page.   
9. Select the Online teaching function menu on the Diagnostics tab .

10. Select the Engine immobilizer sub-menu.

11. Vehicle must now be selected. Then press [F12] to continue. Vehicle data will be read out.

12. Follow the instructions on the Tester and press [F12] to continue.

13. Once the teaching process is completed successfully, the Tester shows the following status, for example:

2 keys taught Front BCM: taught ELV: taught

Rear BCM: taught

DME: taught

Overall vehicle status: taught. Continue with [F12]

14. Press ESC to exit the Online teaching function and return to the diagnostic application.

15. Erase the fault memory.

16. Function test: Lock, open and start the vehicle using al remote controls (hand-held transmitters).

17. Read out the fault memory.

# WM 585115 ADJUSTING REAR DOOR (ALL MODELS) > ADJUSTING REAR DOOR

WARNING: Incorrect handling of safety bolts

• Danger of injury

Loss of torque

→ Always use new fastening screws and nuts following removal.

→ Observe specified tightening torques.

→ Carry out a visual inspection of all re-used parts.

# Information

Only tighten the fastening screws on the door hinges hand-tight from the inside until the doors are set correctly.

# Information

Set gap dimensions on the lids, doors and covers, or accessories in accordance with the gap specifications.   
Given a clearance in the openings that is too great or too small the movable body parts or the accessories must be centered accordingly.   
Ensure that the gaps do not run in a wedge-shaped fashion or do not narrow at local points. You can use star gauges for body gap dimensions NR.127-1 for this.   
The given values are guidelines which should be observed as far as possible.   
The guidelines apply to repair and assembly work.

# Information

The door hinge must be aligned after installing the door.   
Loosen fastening screws for door hinge at the door and fastening screws for door hinge at the B-pillar so that the threaded connections can be moved.

# Information

The number of fastening screws, fixing clips, plug connections, holders and trim panels can vary depending on equipment.   
The illustrations for removing and installing the drive mechanism are shown only on one equipment variant and may differ from the actual equipment variant.

![](images/d96d472c46ff7d215526aaedc179c091080cb1f87ae0de0c9cfaa11acefa09f5.webp)

# WM 587355 REPLACING REAR DOOR CONTROL UNIT (ALL MODELS) > REPLACING REAR DOOR CONTROL UNIT

NOTE: Voltage drop

Risk of irreparable damage to control unit   
Risk of damage to control unit   
Fault entries in the control unit   
•Coding in the control unit is aborted   
• Malfunctions in control unit, even during programming

→ Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch offignition and remove ignition key.

→ Ensure that the power supply is not interrupted during programming.

→ Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least → Nominal value: 40 A to the vehicle battery.

# Information

The PIWis Tester Il 9818 instructions take precedence since the description may be different with later Tester releases.

The procedure described here has been structured in general terms. Different text or additional information may appear in PIWis Tester Il 9818 .

1. Switch off ignition and replace control unit. → 587355 REPLACING REAR DOOR CONTROL   
UNIT   
2. Connect the PIWis Tester to the vehicle and start the Tester. Switch on ignition.   
3. Select the vehicle type and start the diagnostic application.   
4. Select the required control unit, e.g. Rear left door in the overview.   
5. Extended identification must now be selected.   
6. Enter the vehicle identification number and press Enter.   
7. Maintenance/repairs must then be selected.   
8. Control unit replacement must now be selected. Then press [F12].   
9. Select Write data , press [F12] and then press [F8] to start. The data is now loaded.   
10. The Tester displays the message Data has been written. Press [F12] to continue.   
11. Codings/adaptations must now be selected.   
12. Automatic coding must now be selected. Then press [F12] to continue.   
13. When the message Coding has been completed successfully  appears, press [F12] to   
continue.   
14. Read out the fault memory and erase it if necessary.   
15. Check the function of the door control unit.

# Service Manual: 5X - BODY - GENERAL - (95B) - MACAN WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS) > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR RAISING VEHICLES > DANGER OF INJURY WHEN RAISING VEHICLES

WARNING: Vehicle can fall down

Risk of squashing or crushing Risk of damage to the vehicle

→ Do not place any solid objects under the raised vehicle.   
→ Ensure that the lifting platform is prevented from lowering.   
→ Remove solid objects before lowering the vehicle.   
→ Raise the vehicle only at the jacking points provided.   
→ The outer jacking points should be used primarily.

# WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS) > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR RAISING VEHICLES > DAMAGE WHEN RAISING VEHICLES

WARNING: Vehicle can fall down

Risk of squashing or crushing Risk of damage to the vehicle

→ Do not place any solid objects under the raised vehicle.   
→ Ensure that the lifting platform is prevented from lowering.   
→ Remove solid objects before lowering the vehicle.   
→ Raise the vehicle only at the jacking points provided.   
→ The outer jacking points should be used primarily.

# WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS) > GENERAL WARNING NOTES > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR GRINDING WORK

WARNiNG: Excessively high dust concentration during grinding work

Risk of explosion

→ Remove any grinding dust using the relevant vacuum cleaner approved for use on the material.

→ Remove dust in the work area regularly.

→ Do not use compressed air to blow away dust deposits.

→ Always separate the dust from different materials (separate aluminum, steel and carbon fibrereinforced plastic).

→ Clean the extraction system at regular intervals.   
→ Never weld and grind in the same room at the same time.   
→ Only use pneumatic grinders if possible.

# WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS)  GENERAL WARNING NOTES > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR FUEL TANK

WARNING: Grinding and welding work

Danger of fire or explosion

→ Avoid working in an area with highly inflammable or explosive materials.

→ Cover highly inflammable or explosive areas.

→ Remove highly inflammable or explosive parts.

# WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS) > GENERAL WARNING NOTES > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR AIR CONDITIONING

CAUTION: Danger of injury! Bursting of the filled air-conditioning system during welding and brazing work!

Danger of injury due to the filled air-conditioning system bursting during welding and brazing work.

→ No welding, brazing or hot-air heating may be performed on parts of the filled air-conditioning system!

→ While drying after painting work, the temperature burden on the vehicle must not exceed two hours at a maximum temperature of 80 °C!

→ Make sure that parts of the air-conditioning system do not heat up during welding or brazing work on the vehicle!

→ In the case of extreme heating of filled air-conditioning systems, a very strong overpressure may be caused in the system which may lead to an explosion.

# WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS) > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR ADHESIVE BONDING > DANGER OF POISONING AND INJURY WHEN USING ADHESIVE

WARNING: Toxic substances

• Danger of poisoning or suffocation Danger of burns to the eyes and skin

→ Ventilate the work area well.

→ Never ingest or inhale.

→ Read specific information on the Hazard Sheet.

→ Do not smoke, eat or drink in the work area.

# WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS) > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR ADHESIVE BONDING > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR TEROMIX-6700 TWO-COMPONENT ADHESIVE

NOTE: Non-observance of setting time for adhesive

Risk of damage to side panel

→ Weld in the new part within 30 minutes.

# WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS) > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR INSTALLATION WORK > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR AIRBAG SYSTEM

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag units

Triggering of airbag unit.   
System faults can occur.

→ Switch off ignition and remove ignition key or remote control (hand-held transmitter).

→ A power supply (e.g. battery charger) must not be connected to the external power supply/jump-lead starting terminals.

→ Disconnect the battery and insulate the ground strap so that all contact with a ground carrier is avoided.

→ Wait 1 minute after disconnecting the battery.

→ Only pull off connector on the triggering unit after the waiting time has elapsed.

→ Make sure that no foreign objects are located in front of the airbag unit during installation.

→ Replace damaged parts during removal.

→ Always position airbag units so that the blow-out opening is facing upwards, e.g. crest on driver's airbag.

→ Do not position anything on the airbag units.

→ If removed for an extended period, the airbag units must be stored in a safe place.

— Airbag units must not come into contact with grease, oil, detergents, liquids, or similar substances.

→ Do not expose airbag units to temperatures above 90°.

→ Do not remove the short-circuit spring on the plug-in contacts.

→ Ignition and preparations may only be carried out by skilled staff, supervised by a second responsible person.

→ Before disposal, the airbag unit must be rendered harmless by electrical ignition performed in accordance with all precautionary measures, thereby preventing it from being used incorrectly.

WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS) > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR CORROSION PROTECTION > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR STOPPER LOCATION PLAN (BODY)

NOTE: Removing stoppers

Risk of corrosion •Uncontrolled water leakage

→ Body apertures that are sealed with stoppers at the factory must be re-sealed with the stoppers

# WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS) > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR CORROSION PROTECTION SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR WATER DRAINS (BODY)

NOTE: Water drain hoses not cleaned correctly

Water drain hoses are pushed out or pressed into the body.

→ When cleaning water drain hoses, only blow the hoses out with light compressed-air pressure.   
→ The water hoses should only be blown out when the slide/tit roof is closed.

# WM 5XOOIN CORROSION PROTECTION MEASURES DURING REPAIR WORK (ALL MODELS) > MEASURES FOR MAINTAINING LONG-TERM BODY PROTECTION

Following repair work, the standard corrosion protection should only be restored using the corrosion protection agents approved by the manufacturer. The following points must be observed during body repairs.   
Always apply welding primer to both sides of the welding flange when resistance spot welding.   
Prime repair areas from outside. Prime on both sides in the accessible areas.   
Seal all sheetmetal overlaps, sheetmetal edges, butt joints, weld seams etc. with body sealant.   
Only apply body sealant to primed sheetmetal parts.   
Apply top coat paint to the inside of the outer panelling before welding. See "Paint build-up": → "Paint Manual"   
Build up paint on bare sheetmetal panels according to the painting methods described in the → "Paint Manual".   
Repair or create standard underbody protection by applying long-life undersealing material.   
Preserve cavities in the repair area with cavity preservative after applying a top coat paint.   
Check that the standard water drains (stoppers) are working correctly and clean them after the cavity preservation material has dried.

# WM 5XOOIN CORROSION PROTECTION MEASURES DURING REPAIR WORK (ALL MODELS) > PREREQUISITE FOR ENSURING VALIDITY OF THE LONG-LIFE GUARANTEE

All body repairs must be carried out correctly and according to the specific Porsche instructions for sheetmetal, paint and corrosion protection/preservation work.   
To avoid jeopardising the long-life guarantee, a paint condition report wil be drawn up two years after delivery of the vehicle. This condition report must be drafted annually by every Official Porsche Centre.

# WM 5XOOIN BODY PARTS OF VARIOUS SHEET-STEEL STRENGTHS (ALL MODELS) > LIST OF MATERIALS

![](images/6a2219f157ee5683372d90781aa97b66f6dc8d87054ca8509375e3f08f273fff.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Materials

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

A - Sheet steel B- High-strength steel C, E - Very-high-strength steel D- Ultra-high-strength steel

![](images/7c6eb109bea14b512ae9b08f04d70c03084d347c20c664ecbc07f09c4a89a0fe.webp)

![](images/865fca08bf2290c5a45a895a11ef300edeab38919e5efa085512a22226b988a6.webp)

# WM 5XOOIN BODY PARTS OF VARIOUS SHEET-STEEL STRENGTHS (ALL MODELS) > HIGH-STRENGTH STEEL

Only "Genuine Porsche spare parts" must be used for repair work.

Body parts of high-strength steel contribute to better protection of the passenger compartment and thus increase protection of the passengers. In addition to improved crash safety, these parts also have a positive influence on fatigue strength. In terms of crash behavior, body parts made from high-strength sheet steel are characterized by their higher energy absorption. But this also means that higher reshaping force must be applied in reshaping work.

# WM 5XOOIN BODY PARTS OF VARIOUS SHEET-STEEL STRENGTHS (ALL MODELS) > VERY-HIGH-STRENGTH STEEL

Only "Genuine Porsche spare parts" must be used for repair work.

Damaged or deformed body parts can impair torsional rigidity, flexional resistance and crash safety. Body parts can no longer be reshaped. Straightening and reshaping is not permitted. If a body part is damaged or deformed, it must be replaced.

# WM 5XOOIN BODY PARTS OF VARIOUS SHEET-STEEL STRENGTHS (ALL MODELS) > ULTRA-HIGH-STRENGTH STEEL

Only "Genuine Porsche spare parts" must be used for repair work.

# Information

Ultra-high-strength steel panels are extremely strong and rigid. These body parts are recast warm during manufacturing and are press-hardened in cooled recast tools. Damaged or deformed body parts can impair torsional rigidity, flexional resistance and crash safety.

# Information on ultra-high-strength steel:

• Ultra-high-strength body parts must only be replaced as a complete unit.   
Ultra-high-strength body parts can no longer be reshaped.   
Straightening and reshaping is not permitted.   
• Use special drill bits for drilling ultra-high-strength steel.   
•Resistance spot-welding can only be carried out using the inverter welders currently approved by Porsche AG.   
•Plug spot-welding ultra-high-strength steel does not produce suficiently strong joints. If holes need to be welded, additional welding seams must be applied.   
For butt, overlap and reinforcement welding, the individual spot welds and welded seams must be at least 30 mm long.   
Resistance spotwelds can also be replaced by blind rivets and adhesive. The number of rivets must be increased for ultra-high-strength steel panels.

During repairs, always read the specific instructions in the relevant Service information.

# SEPARATION POINTS

Separation points that influence the strength of the body, and thus also the vehicle's operating and traffic safety, must be determined according to the specifications in the relevant Service Information!

Body reinforcements can be separated or joined together only if this is specified in the method descriptions. Otherwise, a damaged reinforcement must always be replaced with a new one!

# WM 5XOOIN BODY PARTS OF VARIOUS SHEET-STEEL STRENGTHS (ALL MODELS) > WELDING WORK

The oxyacetylene welding process must not be used for welding body parts made of high-strength, very-high-strength and ultra-high-strength steel!

Carry out test-welding before starting resistance spot-welding!

All specified steel panels can be welded using the approved resistance spot-welders.

The MIG welding process can only be used on ultra-high-strength steel in exceptional cases! Details of where this process can be used can be found in the relevant repair instructions. The MIG welding process can be used without restriction on all other specified steel panels.

# WM 5XOOIN GENERAL INFORMATION AND NOTES ON QUALITY (ALL MODELS) > BATTERY TRICKLE CHARGING > BATTERY TRICKLE CHARGE

In Order To Prevent The Vehicle Battery From Discharging When Visiting The Workshop, A Battery Charging Unit With A Rated Current Of At Least 40 A Must Be Connected As Soon As The Vehicle

Is Unlocked.

Refer To → 270619 Removing And Installing Battery For More Instructions About Connecting The Battery Charger.

# WM 5XOOIN GENERAL INFORMATION AND NOTES ON QUALITY (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION ON ELECTRONIC CONTROL UNITS

If electronic components, e.g. ABS control module, have been removed for repair work and are then reused, they must undergo a functional check after fitting in accordance with existing specifications.

# WM 5XOOIN GENERAL INFORMATION AND NOTES ON QUALITY (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION ON ELECTRONIC CONTROL UNITS > PROTECTION AGAINST OVERVOLTAGE WHEN PERFORMING WELDING WORK

To protect electronic control units from overvoltage during electric arc welding, the follwing work regulations must be observed:

When performing welding work: Remove plug connections on the engine, transmission and airbag control units.   
Remove clamp from negative terminal of battery and cover the battery.   
When welding work is extensive, electronic control units in the immediate vicinity of the welding point must be removed.   
Connect the ground connection of the electric arc welding equipment as near as possible to the welding point on the part to be welded. Ensure that there are no electrically insulated parts between the ground connection and the welding point.   
•Do not touch electronic control units or electric cables with the ground connection or the welding electrode.

# WM 5XOOIN GENERAL INFORMATION AND NOTES ON QUALITY (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION ON ELECTRONIC CONTROL UNITS > REPLACING CONTROL UNITS

The replacement of electronic control units after an accident is necessary if at least one of the following conditions is met:

The housing is noticeably deformed or damaged.

The sealing surface or console is deformed (the unit shows no external damage).

The plug connection is damaged or corroded by moisture.

Functional checks or on-board diagnosis of the unit indicate the fault "Control unit faulty".

# WM 5XOOIN GENERAL INFORMATION AND NOTES ON QUALITY (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION ON MAINTAINING LONG-LIFE CORROSION PROTECTION

Following repair work, the standard corrosion protection should only be restored using the corrosion protection agents provided and approved by the manufacturer. The following points must be observed for body repairs.   
Always apply welding primer to both sides of the welding flange when resistance spot welding.   
Prime repair areas from outside. Prime on both sides in the accessible areas.   
Seal all sheetmetal overlaps, sheetmetal edges, butt joints, weld seams etc. with body sealant.   
When replacing structurally bonded body parts, proceed according to the information in the respective repair instructions.   
Only apply body sealant to primed sheetmetal parts.   
Apply top coat paint to the inside of the outer panelling before welding. See "Paint build-up": → "Paint Manual"   
Build up paint on bare sheetmetal panels according to the painting methods described in the → "Paint Manual".   
•Repair or create standard undersealing by applying long-life undersealing material.   
Preserve cavities in the repair area with cavity preservative after applying a top coat paint.   
Check that the standard water drains (stoppers) function correctly and clean them after the cavity preservation material has dried.

# WM 5XOOIN GENERAL INFORMATION AND NOTES ON QUALITY (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION ON MAINTAINING LONG-LIFE CORROSION PROTECTION > PREREQUISITE FOR MAINTAINING THE LONG-LIFE GUARANTEE

All body repairs must be performed properly and according to the specific instructions defined by Porsche for sheetmetal, painting and corrosion inhibition/preservation work. To avoid jeopardising the longlife guarantee, a paint condition report wil be drawn up two years after delivery of the vehicle. This condition report must be updated every two years by every Official Porsche Centre.

# WM 5XOOIN WORKING WITH BODY STRUCTURAL FOAM (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH BODY STRUCTURAL FOAM > PRODUCT DESCRIPTION

Processing time is approx. 60 - 90 minutes. The structural foam is hardened after 8 - 24 hours. The

hardening time depends on temperature, area of application, amount of foam used and exposed surface.   
The hardening process can be speeded up by heating the components to up to 50 °C.

# WM 5XOOIN WORKING WITH BODY STRUCTURAL FOAM (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH BODY STRUCTURAL FOAM > APPLICATIONS

The body structural foam is ideal for increasing the rigidity, strength and fatigue endurance limit of cavities, plates and structural parts , e.g. pillars, door sills and frame sections.

# WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION ON THE USE OF STRUCTURAL ADHESIVES IN VEHICLE CONSTRUCTION > GENERAL

Structural bonding in the bodyshell means that the adhesive assumes functions of stiffness, crash strength and endurance strength, whereby the characteristics of the bodyshellare positively influenced in a significant way.

A high-strength, heat-hardening single-component epoxy resin adhesive, which hardens fully in the cathodic immersion paint drying oven, is used for the conventional steel bodyshell.

In the event of repairs, this adhesive is replaced by a cold-hardening two-component epoxy resin adhesive, since the hardening temperatures necessary for the single-component epoxy resin adhesive cannot be used on an assembled vehicle.

# WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION ON THE USE OF STRUCTURAL ADHESIVES IN VEHICLE CONSTRUCTION > COMBINED JOINING PROCESSES

Combined joining processes are regularly used both in standard production and during repairs.

In the case of resistance-spot welding, al bonding surfaces and spot welds are replaced during repairs.

In this case, the unhardened adhesive must be displaced from the joint area by observing an appropriate holdback time before actually starting resistance-spot welding.

In the case of two-component adhesives, the hardening reaction starts immediately after mixing and application; this increases the viscosity and so there is only a certain time window in which spot-weld bonding can be performed if the process is to be reliable.

For this reason, alltime-intensive preliminary work (drilling, cutting to size, fixing etc.) on the parts to be joined must be performed before application of adhesive and joining.

This also applies to mechanical joining processes where the adhesive has to be displaced from the joint area, e.g. riveting.

# WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION ON THE USE OF STRUCTURAL ADHESIVES IN VEHICLE

In the case of 3-layer spot-welded panel joints with a hardened bonded layer in which only the outer panel needs to be replaced, drill the outer panel in the area of the spotwelds sufficiently without damaging the spotweld and bonded joint in the second component layer.

![](images/4269789c334f574a0eed0e8a7ec8c95bc903084e03bb6acd6ada50b6cdd2cbab.webp)

In the case of 3-layer spot-welded panel joints with a hardened bonded layer on the outer panel, drilthe outer panel in the area of the spotwelds suficiently without damaging the spotweld in the second component layer.

![](images/c7ff82a0fab8833530bd314186e8cbafebceb9f30014bd5f31a39810eeebacf0.webp)  
Fig 2: Separating Bonded Body Components

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

After removing the loosened body part, old adhesive must be removed and any uneven spots must be sanded down.

The flange area must then be pre-treated for bonding.

# WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION ON THE USE OF STRUCTURAL ADHESIVES IN VEHICLE CONSTRUCTION > WELDING IN BODY COMPONENTS

Once the spare parts have been secured, repair spotwelds must be placed on the old spotwelds because there is no current flow possible in areas with a hardened bonded layer.

![](images/f787a58e446b0b063473ac777cc2eb55b65af0b566fe519d0bdea82402c85007.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Spot-Welding Body Components

![](images/ee4122badfa0c0ff530eb5cb8373cb2be22b446ac5de24403def9368c06bee9b.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Spot-Welding Body Components

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# Information

In areas in which bonded flanges are spot-welded in an unhardened state, suction devices must be used due to combustion products.   
Areas that can only be accessed from one side must be joined with MAG plug-welds or MAG welded seams. In these cases, no adhesive can be used in the vicinity of the welded seam because this would burn and would have a negative effect on the joint.   
The areas without adhesive must be protected using appropriate anti-corrosion and sealing measures.

Welding procedures other than resistance spot-welding are not permitted since the thermal effect would destroy the bonded joint over a wide area.

# WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > GENERAL INFORMATION

WARNING: Toxic substances

Danger of poisoning or suffocation

Danger of burns to the eyes and skin

→ Ventilate the work area well.

— Never ingest or inhale.

→ Read specific information on the Hazard Sheet.

→ Do not smoke, eat or drink in the work area.

# Information

The vehicle, components and adhesives must be brought to processing temperature (acclimatised) before getting started. Processing temperature must be maintained for approx. 30 minutes before starting to work on the bonding surfaces.   
Bonding surfaces must be free from oil, old adhesive, dirt, moisture, and layers of paint and oxide.   
Body structural adhesive and primer must only be used on bare metal parts.   
•Only use abrasive products based on pure silicon carbide (SIC) for sanding/grinding down the bonding area until bare.   
Always wear clean gloves when touching the cleaned surfaces to ensure that no sweat from your hands or dirt is transferred onto the bonding surface.   
Apply primer within 5 minutes on bare surfaces, particularly on aluminum components. Work in sections on large components and carry out intermediate sanding.   
The jointing operation must take place directly after application of the adhesive in order to guarantee a high quality and reliable bond. Otherwise the adhesive bead must be removed, with pre-treatment of the surface and application of the adhesive being repeated.   
After adhesive has hardened, carefully prime accessible bonding areas and seal with body sealant. Protect bonding areas in cavities against corrosion using cavity preservation.

# Information

To check that the substance is completely mixed, apply a 30-mm long bead of fresh adhesive to a piece of cardboard before processing.   
Process the adhesive within the processing time. The adhesive must be applied and the body part must be joined within this time period. Any resistance welding or mechanical joining procedures (e.g. riveting, screwing) to be carried out in the bonding area must also be performed within this time period.   
Do not put pressure on bonded parts until hardening is complete!   
If the contents of the cartridge is not used up completely, the processing nozle must be left on the cartridge until the adhesive hardens. If you intend to use the adhesive again later, a new processing nozzle must be used.

# Information

During cold periods, overnight or in cold countries, appropriate steps must be taken to ensure that the minimum hardening temperature is reached.

Optimize heating system settings, e.g. deactivate night-time lowering of temperature.   
Keep doors and windows closed; avoid droughts.   
Install uxiliary heaters in the body repair area.

# Information

In addition to this information, observe the relevant job descriptions for body repairs!

# Information

frared heaters only heat smallsections of the body and are therefore only suitable for minor repairs.

• Only use devices with temperature control, automatic distance measurement and measuring poin display, e.g. infrared heater WE xxxx or infrared heater WE xxxx.

# WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > PREPARING BONDING SURFACES > CLEAN

Sticky, solid layers such as dirt, rust, layers of paint (cathodic-dip layers), etc. must be removed using 100 to 150 grain sandpaper in order to improve the strength of a bonding area.

# WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > PREPARING BONDING SURFACES > DEGREASE

To prevent possible grease residue from spreading onto the surface when grinding down the surface unti bare at a later stage, the bonding surfaces must be cleaned using a lint-free cloth soaked in acetone.

H 7

# WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > PREPARING BONDING SURFACES > SAND/GRIND UNTIL BARE

To improve adhesion, it is important to sand the bonding surfaces until bare using 150 to 180 grain sandpaper. The sanding effect can be improved by cross-sanding.

Only use abrasive products based on pure silicon carbide (SIC) for sanding/grinding down the bonding surface until bare.

Leave cleaned surfaces to dry ofor approx. 5 - 10 minutes; bonding surfaces must be completely dry.

# WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > PROCESSING CONDITIONS

During processing, the ambient and material temperature must be at least — Minimum temperature: 15°C and must not exceed → Maximum temperature: 35°C.

The optimal processing temperature is → Minimum temperature: 18°C to → Maximum temperature: 23°C.

Higher processing temperatures reduce processing time.

→ Processing time at 15 °C: 75 min → Processing time at 18 °C: 70 min → Processing time at 20 °C: 65 min → Processing time at 23 °C: 60 min → Processing time at 25 °C: 55 min → Processing time at 30 °C: 45 min → Processing time at 35 °C: 35 min

# WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > HARDENING

The body structural adhesives used harden at temperatures of between → Minimum temperature: 18°C and — Maximum temperature: 80°C.

# Information

nfrared heaters only heat small sections of the body and are therefore only suitable for minor repairs.

• Only use devices with temperature control, automatic distance measurement and measuring point display, e.g. infrared heater WE xxxx or infrared heater WE xxxx.

Hardening can be accelerated by heat (e.g. using an infrared heater or in a painting booth).

Do not put pressure on bonded parts until the required assembly strength is reached.

# WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > ASSEMBLY STRENGTH

The object temperature must be above the minimum hardening temperature for the entire specified time period.

If the minimum hardening temperature could not be reached within the specified time period, the standing time must be increased or additional heat must be applied to the bonded joint.

If the hardening temperature is significantly less than the minimum hardening temperature (approx. 10 C), this can cause irreversible damage to the bonded joint. This can have a negative effect on the strength of the bonded joint.

# Information

Once the required assembly strength is reached, the vehicle must be removed from the straightening system. Assembly work can then be performed.

The vehicle must not be moved and no further work must be carred out on the vehicle following repair bonding for at least → Hardening time at 18 °C: 12 h (leave to harden overnight).

The standing time can be shortened by applying heat. E.g. → Hardening time at 60 °C: 35 min.

# WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > CORROSION PROTECTION

After adhesive has hardened, carefully prime accessible bonding areas and seal with body sealant.

Protect bonding areas in cavities against corrosion using cavity preservation.

WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) >

# WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > DISPOSAL

Small amounts remaining after mixing and complete hardening may be disposed of as industrial waste.

Dispose of used acetone-soaked cleaning cloths as special-category waste.

# WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > ENDURANCE STRENGTH

The object temperature must be above the minimum hardening temperature for the entire specified time period.

If the minimum hardening temperature could not be reached within the specified time period, the standing time must be increased or additional heat must be applied to the bonded joint.

If the hardening temperature is significantly less than the minimum hardening temperature (approx. 10 C), this can cause irreversible damage to the bonded joint. This can have a negative effect on the strength of the bonded joint.

# Information

After this time, the vehicle meets the crash requirements and may be driven on public roads.

The vehicle can be handed over to the customer.

The time between joining the repaired components and starting to use them must be at least → Standing time at 18 °C: 96 h.

# WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > HANDLING PRIMER > GENERAL

Primers improve the long-term durability of the bonded area

Primers reveal the actual condition of the surface to be bonded.

Primers protect the bonding surface from environmental influences, thereby increasing corrosion protection.

To achieve a better effect, apply primer only very lightly.

Primer prevents oxidation of the surface. This is particularly important when bonding aluminum.

# WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > HANDLING PRIMER > 2-COMPONENT SIP

Information

Use the primer within 8 hours. Apply a thin, even coat to the bonded flanges and remove excess primer. Protect surfaces you have already primed from dirt and soiling. Otherwise, the bonded joint may be defective.

# Information

Primed surfaces can be exposed for up to 3 days before undergoing further processing. Make sure that the surfaces are not contaminated by environmental influences. If the primer is left exposed for more than 3 days, it must be removed and re-applied. Fig 9: Identifying Primer Bonded Flange (Incorrect)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

9. Dry primer.

1.9.1. Allow primer to flash off; it must be dust-dry before any adhesive is applied.

![](images/a9b44b47df2bf677ec574d7828e68572281c5b66b962c6d9d99e17587f28c159.webp)

10. Process adhesive.

# WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > HANDLING PROCESSING DEVICES > APPLICATOR GUN

1. Open holder.

1.1.1. Release holder -arrow- and fold up.

![](images/2665050c7e5eb6c7ce2c6d4d7911b4bfb8b606120b421209a21c807a071ce754.webp)  
Fig 1: Releasing Holder   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# 2. Press sliding lock upwards

1.2.1. Press sliding lock upwards in direction of arrow -arrow- .

![](images/c18ec0c42b6e45f2ce9dbefff8978a1cec7d6f2c7c6b5a68362bb18f3b98cf27.webp)  
Fig 2: Pressing Sliding Lock   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Insert piston rod.

1.3.1. Hold sliding lock pressed and insert piston rod -B1- completely into the gun grip -B1- .

![](images/6989f8f9e39958458764533c0b22cbc54b2f68f340db44aec2937127646baf4d.webp)  
Fig 3: Inserting Piston Rod   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Insert mixing cartridge.

1.4.1. Insert double cartridge -c1- into the gun -B- from above. Insert the cartridge until the muzzle of the gun engages in the groove of the cartridge.

![](images/2be535e44d481e033df54fd8c5b18056edba12cd01d1e859eb3860066c025a06.webp)  
Fig 4: Inserting Cartridge   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# 5. Engage holder.

1.5.1. Swivel holder downward and engage on handle of gun.

![](images/914c8659b3c34655b2c51b926d21699d50b2290ab236bb4b3a01f7d479331500.webp)  
Fig 5: Engaging Holder

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# 6. Open cartridge.

1.6.1. Turn screw cap 90 ° counter-clockwise and remove.

![](images/3c87609237110465caf5cac0fe06040ff986124fe165e72b8c357ce9b5edefd2.webp)  
Fig 6: Opening Cartridge   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Squeeze adhesive to the front.

1. 7.1. Press the gun grip to allow the piston rod to move out slowly until an equal amount of both components emerges.

2.7.2. Wipe off any adhesive that emerges.

8. Fit processing nozzle.

1. 8.1. Before fitting the processing nozzle, make sure that the muzzle -A- and the mixing ducts are aligned; turn the bayonet locking mechanism on the processing nozzle by 90° if necessary.

2. 8.2. Position processing nozzle -C2- and turn clockwise 90°.

![](images/fd284ba86c78fee9edbfcb8334f8df97f6771417d2a99046a793ef7ead66a7e7.webp)  
Fig 7: Fitting Nozzle   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

9. Mix adhesive components.

1.9.1. Press the gun grip to allow the piston rod to move out slowly until the adhesive is visible in the processing pipe.

10. Bond the body part within the specified processing time.

![](images/87d4f9a32770972154ad7a97798c18b5884dc1c23f258df5bbbd7e4082f1f4f0.webp)  
Fig 8: Identifying Working Time Of Structural Adhesive

# WM 5XOOIN WORKING WITH BODY FOAM FILLER (ALL MODELS) > PRODUCT DESCRIPTION

The processing time is approx. 15-18 minutes. Processing can be interrupted briefly for up to approx. 5 minutes. The chemical reaction is essentially complete after approx. 30 minutes. The hardened foam does not swell or shrink.

# WM 5XOOIN WORKING WITH BODY FOAM FILLER (ALL MODELS) > APPLICATIONS

The foam filler is ideal for filling, insulating and sealing cavities, e.g. on pillars, door sils and frame sections.

WM 5XOOIN WORKING WITH BODY FOAM FILLER (ALL MODELS) > PROCESSING Information

Always observe the relevant work safety regulations when working with the foam filler.

WARNING: Toxic substances

Danger of poisoning or suffocation • Danger of burns to the eyes and skin

→ Ventilate the work area well   
→ Never ingest or inhale.   
→ Read specific information on the Hazard Sheet. → Do not smoke, eat or drink in the work area.

# Information

The work area must be free of dust and grease.   
Remove loose parts.   
Do not wet the area beforehand.

# Observe temperature limits:

Can and ambient temperature: 10-35°C •Optimal temperature: 18-23°C

# Information

Apply sparingly since the volume of the foam filer will expand by approx. 50-100% in open areas and by approx. 100-200% in cavities. Approx. 0.25 liters of foam volume is produced per second of foam time (free-foaming). The foam filer is silver-grey. Remove fresh foam residues immediately with PU cleaner. Hardened foam residues can only be removed mechanicall afterwards. Always remove foam from the can following activation.

# Activation process:

1. Break open the seal on the activation lid.   
2.Use a piece of wire to pull the activation lid out as far as it will go (approx. 11 cm up to the notch).   
. Break off the wire at the required rupture point (notch) over the valve.   
0 4. Screw plastic adapter into the valve.   
05. Shake can vigorously up and down (approx. 20 times).   
06. Release foam downwards out of the can with the valve.

# Subsequent work:

The hardened foam filler can be processed further by sanding, cutting or sawing. It can be painted

or varnished.

1. Align and secure body parts.   
. Drill body parts using a small drill it (-X- mm).

# WM 5XOOIN REPLACING THREADED BOLTS (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Remove add-on parts in the repair area.

# WM 5XOOIN REPLACING THREADED BOLTS (ALL MODELS) > REPLACING THREADED BOLTS

Fig 1: Identifying Threaded Bolts Installation Position

![](images/467f5f8a91ae3624445ef522b934a05d3d3d1969aeaf0ad39aff25a7d32cd5c8.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# Information

Defective or broken threaded bolts can be replaced with repair bolts.

The following bolts are available:

• Threaded bolt, M6: → BOLT N.105.954.01

1. Grip defective threaded bolts on the complete vehicle (e.g. bolts with damaged threads) using a pliers and screw them out. Grind down during body repairs if necessary.   
2. Remove dirt from the sealing surface area of the repair bolt.   
3. Drill a hole.

1.3.1. Drill a hole in the center of the broken bolt -1- (-arrow- ). → Diameter: 4.0 mm

![](images/08bcaf5e57d357f40f2cdcbb8425ac88320e5dd60e4a5c1a262ce08ee1a1c00f.webp)  
Fig 2: Locating Drill Hole   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# 2.3.2. Drill out the hole.

For M6 threaded bolts → Diameter: 9.0 mm

![](images/525dd27ff22726a7a52ee71366a98760e44911b9d38da4af36256a33a14f09b7.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Threaded Bolts Hole   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Prime rivet area.

5. Prepare threaded bolt for installation.

1. 5.1. On the back of the bolt -1- , apply sealing compound → SEALING MATERIAL 000.043.204.38 as a continuous bead of sealant -2- .

![](images/fcc44b3d908e64737cee27fd80b91a3c1964861d38c36710ba8d141af2e0a393.webp)  
Fig 4: Applying Sealing Compound   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. Rivet in threaded bolt.

1.6.1. Insert threaded bolt into the bore.   
2.6.2. Rivet in threaded bolt using the riveting tool pop rivet nut pliers WE 1476.

![](images/dd58ebf39c59a413565a3c445606a15b70fb110f3d8267e82a1865f2ab325f18.webp)  
Fig 5: Identifying Riveted Threaded Bolt   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Remove any sealing compound that has oozed out.

WM 5XOOIN REPLACING THREADED BOLTS (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Apply primer to the repair area.   
2. Seal the joint for the threaded bolt.   
3. Install add-on parts in the repair area.   
4. Apply cavity protection to the repair area. → 5X00IN44 CAVITY PRESERVATION

# WM 5XOOIN WORK SEQUENCE FOR ACCIDENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > WORK SEQUENCE FOR ACCIDENT REPAIRS > PROCEDURE FOR ACCIDENT REPAIRS

1.Determine scope of damage

2. Expose the area to be repaired

3. Make an economic or technical decision: Should parts be repaired or replaced?

4. Determine the scope of replacement parts and order the parts

See "REPAIRS " below. See "REPLACEMENT " below. 5. If necessary, prime and seal the seam areas 6. If necessary, renew the stone impact protection 7. Paint the repaired area If necessary, touch up the undersealing 9. Seal cavities 10. Fit accessories

# WM 5XOOIN WORK SEQUENCE FOR ACCIDENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > WORK SEQUENCE FOR ACCIDENT REPAIRS > REPAIR

1. Cover undamaged areas of the vehicle . Reshape damaged areas 3. Fill or apply body solder to reshaped areas 4. Apply fine filler on repair areas

# WM 5XOOIN WORK SEQUENCE FOR ACCIDENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > WORK SEQUENCE FOR ACCIDENT REPAIRS > REPLACEMENT

1. Cover undamaged areas of the vehicle so that they are protected against fire   
2. Disconnect battery   
3. Pre-paint new parts from the inside   
4. Roughly cut out damaged areas   
5. Cut out remaining pieces   
6. Fit new parts in, then check the gap dimensions with the accessories fitted   
7. Protect panel flanges against corrosion   
8. Weld in new parts   
9.Grind visible weld seams flat; if necessary apply body solder or filler

# WM 5XOOIN PROCEDURE FOR DAMAGE DIAGNOSIS (ALL MODELS) > INSTRUCTIONS

• Porsche AG recommends that you perform damage diagnosis using an electronic measuring system (e.g. Measuring unit, professional WE 1397 ).

# Information

A body is constructed so that it has deformation zones in the front and rear areas. These deformation zones enable absorption of impact energy through their special design. The bearing structure in these areas is adapted to provide optimum energy reduction in the event of a crash.   
Due to the vehicle dimensions in the side area of the body, deformation zones cannot be provided for absorbing energy. The impact energy can only be absorbed to a lesser extent here through the deformation of doors and pillars. This is also the case for the roof area where only the roof skin can absorb impact energy to a very small extent. In these areas, occupant protection is guaranteed by a rigid design of the passenger cell.   
The aim of this design is to absorb the impact energy in defined areas to keep the passenger cell as free of damage as possible in the event of a crash. If the passenger cell has been deformed as a result of a crash, the damage in this case can often only be repaired by replacing body parts.   
In general, an impact occurs diagonally or offset to the vehicle axle so that mixed forms are usually the result of a front and side impact or a rear and side impact. The deformation is not always restricted to the impact area. Due to inertia forces of masses, such as the chassis, drive line, occupants of the vehicle and load or the body itself, deformation can also occur in the opposite areas.   
The following work sequence is designed to help you to correctly determine the scope of damage to vehicles damaged in an accident.

# WM 5XOOIN PROCEDURE FOR DAMAGE DIAGNOSIS (ALL MODELS) > PROCEDURE FOR DAMAGE DIAGNOSIS

1. Identify impact points on the exterior panelling or wheels.

. Remove accessories that restrict the view of the impact area.

3. Check unit mounts, chassis parts and steering parts for deformation and cracks.

Determine the scope of damage to the body. See: IDENTIFIABLE DEFORMATIONS ON THE BODY STRUCTURE

5. Repair vehicle, if necessary.

# WM 5XOOIN PROCEDURE FOR DAMAGE DIAGNOSIS (ALL MODELS) > IDENTIFIABLE DEFORMATIONS ON THE BODY STRUCTURE

1. Visual inspection of the structural parts for creasing and bending, starting from the point of impact toward the center of the vehicle

2. Visual inspection of the structural parts at the joints for gaping panel joints (e.g. entry area at the side member under the rubber seal of the door)

3. Check the body structure using an electronic measuring system or a straightening bench system.

4. Decide whether the vehicle is technically repairable

5. Decide whether the vehicle is economicall repairable Repair vehicle, if necessary.

# WM 5XOOIN PROCEDURE FOR DAMAGE DIAGNOSIS (ALL MODELS) > NO IDENTIFIABLE DEFORMATIONS ON THE BODY STRUCTURE

1. Check seam joining line on the accessories → WM 5X00IN GAP DIMENSIONS

2. Check accessories for paint abrasion (accessories that were impacted during the crash)

3. Drive the vehicle onto a lifting platform and raise it. Measure screw points using an electronic measuring system (e.g. Measuring unit, professional WE 1397 ) and compare with the required values.

4.Determine the extent of any damage to chassis components Measure the chassis electronicallyif necessary → 449503 SUSPENSION ALIGNMENT, COMPLETE

5. Decide whether the vehicle has to be repaired Repair the vehicle, if necessary.

# WM 600625 PROGRAMMING/TEACHING ROOF ASSEMBLY (PANORAMA ROOF) (ALL MODELS) > PROGRAMMING/TEACHING ROOF ASSEMBLY (PANORAMA ROOF) END POSITION

The end positions are lost and must be re-taught in the following situations:

After disconnecting or connecting the vehicle battery When the vehicle battery is completely flat or after jump-lead starting After emergency operation

After changing the electric fuse

After replacing the glass panel, motor, powered sunroof mechanism or sun blind

NOTE: Electrically moved components

Risk of damage to components

→ Move objects out of the range of movement.

The force limiters are not available when storing the end positions. The panorama roof and sun blind therefore close with full force!

1. Park the vehicle and start the engine.

# Information

When storing the end positions, always save the settings for the panorama roof and sun blind fully one after the other. If one of the processes is interrupted, it is not possible to start the process for the other drive mechanism.

2. Press the actuating button for the panorama roof forward towards Close and keep it pressed until the panorama roof is closed fully and has stopped moving. The process for storing the end position will start after approx. 10 seconds.

3. Press the actuating button for the sun blind forward towards Close and keep it pressed until the sun blind is closed full and has stopped moving. The process for storing the end position will start after approx. 10 seconds.

4. Check that the panorama roof and sun blind operate correctly.

Never touch the electric pins and plug contacts.

WM 605455 REPLACING SEALS FOR ROOF ASSEMBLY (ALL MODELS) >

# REPLACING SEAL FOR ROOF ASSEMBLY (BODY SIDE)

1. Pull outer seal -1- off the bonding surface -3- on the roof -2- .

![](images/a9e67b3e8d0fb98abda6374739697c9a4499402942057ba11ae0db13b2aff921.webp)  
Fig 1: Replacing Seal On Body Side

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Remove any adhesive residue from the roof using an erasing disc film eraser Nr.174 Pos.1

# Information

1. Immediately before sticking on, wash off the areas on which you intend to stick the seal using isopropanol to ensure that alltraces of silicone, grease and oil are completely

removed.

3. Clean bonding surface with isopropanol.   
4.Centre the new outer seal -1- with the gap -arrow- facing the middle of the rear roof cut-out.   
5. Pulloff protective film on the adhesive tape -3- and press the seal evenly onto the roof -2- .   
6. Press the outer seal firmly onto the roof by pressing it on evenly twice allthe way around using   
a press-on roller.

# WM 605455 REPLACING SEALS FOR ROOF ASSEMBLY (ALL MODELS) > REPLACING SEAL FOR ROOF ASSEMBLY (BODY SIDE) > REPLACING SEAL FOR REAR PANEL

1. Remove seal for rear panel.

1.1.1. Pulloff seal at the side -4- of the rear glass panel -2- sideways.

2.1.2. Puloff seal at the front -3- of the rear glass panel -2- in an upward direction.

![](images/35daee43594e740be927477ec9539bed6ac69b70529a9259f785834e9773f227.webp)  
Fig 1: Replacing Rear Panel Seal   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Install seal for rear panel.

# Information

To make installation easier, the area should be moistened with a soapy solution.

1. 2.1. Press seal at the front -3- into the front mounting from above and center it.

2.2.2. Press seal at the side -4- into the mounting on the glass panel.

# WM 605455 REPLACING SEALS FOR ROOF ASSEMBLY (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK > SUBSEQUENT WORK FOR REPLACING ROOF ASSEMBLY SEAL (BODY SIDE)

1. Install rear sliding-roof panel. → Installing Rear Sliding-Roof Panel   
2. Close the front lid.

# WM 605455 REPLACING SEALS FOR ROOF ASSEMBLY (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK > SUBSEQUENT WORK FOR REPLACING SEAL FOR REAR PANEL

1. Install rear lid. → Installing Roof Assembly Panels (Panorama Roof)

# WM 607019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING SUN BLIND (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING SUN BLIND

1. Installation is performed in reverse order to removal.   
Tighten fastening screw for sun blind to Tightening torque 2.5 Nm (2 ftlb.) until secure.

# WM 607019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING SUN BLIND (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

After installing the sun blind, check that it moves perfectly and smoothly. To do this, move the sun blind drive mechanism forwards and backwards at the motor by hand by actuating it manually using a commercially available hexagon wrench and check that the sun blind fabric folds and moves correctly.

1. Install rear panel. → Installing Rear Sliding-Roof Panel   
2. Install headliner. → Installing headliner   
3. Carry out standardization if necessary   
4. Switch on ignition.   
5. Reinitializes end positions of the sun blind. 1. 5.1. Press sun blind button forward and keep it pressed. 2. 5.2. The sun blind closes as far as its limit stop and then opens again. 3. 5.3. The sun blind button must remain pressed for the entire duration of the standardization run. 4.5.4. Release the sun blind when the standardization run is complete.

# WM 607219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING MOTOR FOR SUN BLIND (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING MOTOR FOR SUN BLIND

WARNING: Electrically moved components

•Danger of limbs being trapped or severed

→ Switch off electric power to drive motor.   
—→ Make sure it does not switch on again.   
→ Check that there is no electric charge.

# Information

Always comply with the regulations for handling ESD-sensitive components!

Assembly work may only be carried out if the mechanic is wearing the working clothes and shoes approved by Porsche.   
The new part must only be removed from the ESD (electrostatic discharge) protective packaging just before installation and at the position at which the part is to be installed.   
Never touch the electric pins and plug contacts.

# Information

The glass sliding roof motor is located on the glass sliding roof frame at the front.

The sun blind motor is located on the glass sliding roof frame at the rear.

The control units for the panorama roof system are installed in the glass sliding roof motor and sun blind motor.

1. Switch off ignition and pull remote control out of ignition lock.   
Pull out locking mechanism on electric plug connection -1- (-a-) , press release -b- and pul electric plug connection off the motor for the sunblind -2- .

Fig 1: Disconnecting Sun Blind Motor Electric Plug Connection (Glass Sliding Roof Motor)

![](images/251d2074fd484f64a63e5a04bea577e3877208c0d8f7c272b05af21eb1dd4c22.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# WM 631519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT APRON (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING FRONT APRON

Installation is performed in reverse order. Pay particular attention to the following:

1. Tighten fastening screws securing front apron to inner lock carrier to the specified tightening torque. Tightening torque: 8 Nm (6 ftlb.)   
.Tighten fastening screws securing front apron to retaining strip to the specified tightening torque. Tightening torque: 2 Nm (1.5 ftlb.)   
3. Tighten fastening screws securing front apron to outer lock carrier to the specified tightening torque. Tightening torque: 8 Nm (6 ftlb.)   
4.Tighten fastening screws securing front apron to lock carrier at the bottom to the specified tightening torque. Tightening torque: 2 Nm (1.5 ftlb.)   
5. Tighten fastening screws securing front apron to lock carrier at the sides to the specified tightening torque. Tightening torque: 2 Nm (1.5 ftlb.)   
6. Tighten fastening screws securing wheel housing liner to lock carrier to the specified tightening torque. Tightening torque: 2 Nm (1.5 ftlb.)

# WM 642949 REWORKING (COATING) FRONT CORNER WINDOW PANE (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK

The hydrophobic coating is extremely durable. If the hydrophobic characteristics are reduced, a new coating can be applied to the windows without any special measures. Check whether new coating needs to be applied by examining drops of water on the windows.

Spray on water using a water spray bottle with an atomiser and check the hydrophobic coating by examining the drops.

Drop size if hydrophobic coating is OK

# WM 642949 REWORKING (COATING) FRONT CORNER WINDOW PANE (ALL MODELS) > CHECKING WINDOW GLASS

Mixed hydrophobic coating agent must be used within 24 hours!

1. Pour the entire contents of the Component 2 bottle into the Component 1 bottle.   
2. Close the bottle tightly again and shake well immediately for at least three minutes.

# WM 642949 REWORKING (COATING) FRONT CORNER WINDOW PANE (ALL MODELS) > CHECKING WINDOW GLASS > CLEANING WINDOW SURFACES

Information

The window must be coated immediately after being polished.

1. Clean the window using commercially available glass cleaner.   
2. Shake the polish well before use.   
3. Dampen polishing cloths with water, apply polish and buff for several minutes.   
4.Allow the film of polish to dry and then wipe it off completely.

# WM 642949 REWORKING (COATING) FRONT CORNER WINDOW PANE (ALL MODELS) > APPLYING COATING

The hydrophobic coating must not come into contact with water or other fluids for at least 30 minutes after applying the coating.

1. Apply hydrophobic coating agent as a flat liquid film and rub immediately and uniformly with a paper towel.

2. A grey fog forms on the treated surface following application. Polish off this grey fog completely using a new, dry and clean paper towel.

3. The coating must not come into contact with water or other fluids for at least 30 minutes.

oDried-on coating agent can be softened by rubbing it with the cloth soaked in coating agent and then wiping it off with a clean paper towel.

3. Dampen polishing cloths with water, apply polish and buff for several minutes.   
4.Allow the film of polish to dry and then wipe it off completely.

# WM 644049 REWORKING (COATING) FRONT DOOR WINDOW (ALL MODELS) > APPLYING COATING

The hydrophobic coating must not come into contact with water or other fluids for at least 30 minutes after applying the coating.

1. Apply hydrophobic coating agent as a flat liquid film and rub immediately and uniformly with a paper towel.

2. A grey fog forms on the treated surface following application. Polish off this grey fog completely using a new, dry and clean paper towel.

3. The coating must not come into contact with water or other fluids for at least 30 minutes.

oDried-on coating agent can be softened by rubbing it with the cloth soaked in coating agent and then wiping it off with a clean paper towel.

Make sure not to damage the heated rear window connections when removing the glass with the cutting wire.   
Cut up to just before the connection.   
Slacken the cuting wire.   
Guide the cutting wire past the connection on the inside.

Continue separating the window glass. 1. Remove rubber sleeve from the wiper arm. 2. Release and disconnect electric plug connections for the antenna amplifier control unit.

→ Removing antenna control unit

3. Release and disconnect electric plug connections on antenna amplifier. → Removing antenna amplifier

5. Release and disconnect electric plug connections on actuating cylinders for the rear lid. → Removing actuating cylinder for rear lid

7. Affix adhesive tape -1- to the top right corner of the rear window at the rear lid.

# Information

Cover add-on parts and adjacent areas.

Protect components against scratching and damage.
