# WM 270619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING BATTERY

WARNING: Static battery charge

Battery can explode •Electrical discharges

→ Do not rub the battery with a dry cloth.

# Information

Switch off al loads and remove the ignition key.

Do not disconnect the battery while the engine is running.

Disconnect and reconnect battery with extreme caution.

Do not rub the battery with a dry cloth.

1. Installation is performed in reverse order to removal.

2.Tighten fastening screw for clamp support securing battery to the body. Tightening torque 23 Nm (17 ftlb.)

3. Tighten fastening nuts on terminal clamps. Tightening torque 5 Nm (3.5 ftlb.)

# WM 270619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK > VEHICLES WITH SOUND SYSTEM

1. Install subwoofer. → Installing subwoofer

2. If the battery was replaced, write new battery data into the gateway control unit using PIWIS Tester II 9818. → WM 270619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING BATTERY

3. Follow work instructions after disconnecting the battery. → 2X00IN WORK INSTRUCTIONS AFTER DISCONNECTING THE BATTERY

WM 2706IN EXTERNAL POWER CONNECTION, JUMP-LEAD STARTING (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > EXTERNAL POWER CONNECTION, JUMP-LEAD STARTING

WARNING: Live jump leads

Risk of electric shock Risk of short circuit

→ Route the jump leads so that they do not become entangled in moving parts in the engine compartment.

→ There must be no contact between the vehicles.

NOTE: Using charging cables/jump leads directly on the vehicle battery.

Risk of damage to battery sensors.

→ Always connect charging cables/jump leads to the external power supply for jump-lead starting.

# Information

If the battery is flat, jump leads can be used together with the battery of another vehicle to start the

car or to supply external power to the vehicle.

# Information

Both batteries must be 12 V batteries.

The capacity (AH) of the donor battery must not be significantly lower than that of the flat battery.

The flat battery must be properly connected to the vehicle electrical system.

1. Open protective cover on the positive terminal for jump-lead starting -+- (-arrow- ).   
.Connect the positive cable to the positive terminal for jump-lead starting -+- , then to the positive terminal of the donor battery.   
3. First, connect the negative cable to the negative terminal of the donor battery, then to the ground point for jump-lead starting - .

![](images/167b9be2d68578df76cd54947fb0f3fe0b94710cbeff2481207d78a2a9d6f53a.webp)  
Fig 1: Connecting Battery To Vehicle Electrical System

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Leave the engine of the vehicle supplying the power running at higher revs.

5. Start the engine. Do not spend longer than 15 seconds trying to start the vehicle with the jump leads, then wait for at least one minute before trying again.

6. Disconnect the two jump leads in reverse order when the engine is running.

7. Close protective cover.

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > TOOLS

![](images/b317debe2d85438a236189526ec30523313195b4ada0bf7d92b43a5e515e6e94.webp)

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > TECHNICAL VALUES

![](images/3af6188353345eef7747ba033d9087a3eebff112eb371687d7f5b871f6707541.webp)

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION

NOTE: A battery charger for providing an external power supply or for jump-lead starting connected directly to the battery in the vehicle.

Risk of damage to the battery sensor.

Battery sensor sends incorrect battery values to the vehicle electrical system.

→ Always connect a battery charger for providing an external power supply or for jump-lead starting to the defined connections in the engine compartment. → 2XOOIN BATTERY TRICKLE CHARGING

# Information

The AGM (A bsorbent G lass M at) battery is a maintenance-free, sealed battery.

This battery must not be opened. If the battery is opened, it must be replaced.

There is a serial number -A- and a part number -B- on the top right-hand side of the battery.

![](images/6d8e8ed15072569401d1da47a498ade72741410aa7e4894d5ff14199e442757c.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Battery Serial And Part Number

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

After replacing the battery, the serial number and part number as well as the battery size and manufacturer must be entered using the PIWiS Tester under: Gateway/Maintenance/repairs /Change battery.

The battery size and battery manufacturer must also be entered when changing the battery.

# Information

To prevent contact corrosion, only approved bolts, nuts, washers, etc. should be used. These elements have a special surface coating and must be stored separately.

The battery is one of the most important electrical components in the vehicle. Fault-free functioning of the battery contributes greatly to customer satisfaction. To guarantee long and eficient operation, the battery must be checked and maintained according to the instructions provided here.

Besides starting the vehicle, the battery also acts as a buffer and supplier of electrical power for the entire vehicle electrical system.

An AGM (A bsorbent G lass M at) battery is used as standard. The AGM battery offers the following advantages, for example:

Sealed, valve-controlled battery   
High-cycle battery   
High cold-start performance   
Cannot leak or tilt   
oTotally maintenance-free   
Shake-resistant   
No acid leakage if the housing is damaged   
oFlexible installation and safe to handle   
High load capacity and longer service life   
Ideal for Start/Stop function

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > INSTRUCTIONS FOR HANDLING BATTERIES

Battery terminals do not need to be greased.   
The battery terminal clamps should only be attached by hand - without excessive force - to prevent damage to the battery.   
The tightening torque for the battery terminals is → Torque: 5 Nm (3.5 ftlb.).   
If the battery is reconnected, proceed according to → 2X0000 WORK INSTRUCTIONS AFTER DISCONNECTING THE BATTERY .

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > WARNING NOTES AND SAFETY REGULATIONS FOR BATTERIES

1.-1- No fire, sparks, naked flames or smoking:

1. Avoid sparking when using cables and electrical devices.   
2. Avoid short circuits.   
3. On batteries with central venting, there is an increased concentration of oxyhydrogen gas at the hose opening. The vent hose should not be bent or blocked by dirt.

2.-2- Wear eye protection.

3. -3- Keep children away from acids and batteries.

4. -4- Risk of acid burns:

1. Battery acid is highly caustic, so wear protective gloves.

2. Do not tip battery; acid can emerge from the vent opening.

![](images/39beb6bd5396dabfe27260e31e366f46538d1deb3e774c1e50a6f75502b5717f.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Battery Symbols

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# Information

1. First aid: Rinse acid splashes in the eyes immediately with clean water for a few minutes. Consult a doctor immediately. Neutralize acid splashes on the skin or clothing immediately with soap suds and rinse again with plenty of water. If acid has been drunk unintentionally, consult a doctor immediately.

5. -5- Follow the instructions on the battery, in the Technical Information and in the Driver's Manual.

6.-6- Risk of explosion:

1. A highly explosive detonating gas mixture is formed when charging batteries.

7. -7- Disposal:

1. Hand in old batteries at a collection point.

8. -8- Never dispose of old batteries in domestic rubbish!

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > NOTES ON REMOVING AND INSTALLING THE BATTERY

NOTE: A battery charger for providing an external power supply or for jump-lead starting : connected directly to the battery in the vehicle.

Risk of damage to the battery sensor.

Battery sensor sends incorrect battery values to the vehicle electrical system.

→ Always connect a battery charger for providing an external power supply or for jump-lead starting to the defined connections in the engine compartment. → 2X0OIN BATTERY TRICKLE CHARGING

# Information

The battery is located in the luggage compartment under the loadspace floor.   
In order to avoid triggering the siren in vehicles with an additional alarm siren, the battery must be disconnected while the ignition is on!   
All oads must be switched off beforehand! Remove ignition key!   
Never disconnect battery with engine running!   
Never start engine without a securely connected battery!   
To prevent damage to the battery, the battery terminal clamps should only be attached by hand - without excessive force.   
Check that the battery is seated correctly after installation. A loose battery presents other dangers, such as: - Reduced service life due to vibration damage. - Noises. - Damage to the battery housing from mounting parts. - Inadequate crash safety.

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > NOTES ON REMOVING AND INSTALLING THE BATTERY > OPERATING PRINCIPLE OF CENTRAL VENTING

State-of-the-art batteries have central venting -A- .

In certain battery states, the gas produced during charging can emerge centrally through an opening on the upper cover side. Backfire protection is integrated at the same position and prevents the combustible gas in the battery from igniting.   
On batteries with a vent hose -A- , check that the vent hose is not disconnected or pinched. Only then can the battery be freely vented.

![](images/dabe4d1b87b52eef76ebd5dedab06c5e71945e7635c8b05d289a73735701df96.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Battery Vent Hose

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > VISUAL INSPECTION

A visual inspection of the battery must be performed before taking measurements, e.g. measuring the open-circuit voltage, or before carrying out the battery load test.

# This test can be used to determine:

Whether the battery housing is damaged. Leak-free operation and function of the battery cannot be guaranteed if the housing is damaged.   
Whether the battery terminals (battery line connections) are damaged. The line connections might not make contact if the battery terminals are damaged. This can cause the lines to catch fire and can result in malfunctions in the electrical system.

# NM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) >

Make sure that the vent hose -A- is not kinked or damaged. If in doubt, replace it.

The vent hose -A- must be inserted in the battery and in the battery box.

![](images/d672b4fe9ae21464d861b9f6ca2820ef40725af4b1c4e7f9ecb3385e6d7d26a8.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Vent Hose (Panamera)

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > OPEN-CIRCUIT VOLTAGE MEASUREMENT

Compared with the value from PIWis Tester II 9818, the battery voltage can be measured using a hand-held multimeter.   
Proceed as follows:

# Information

The open-circuit voltage measurement should be read out using PIwis Tester Il9818 in the Gateway control unit by selecting Energy management, Quick closed-circuit current measurement in the menu.

1. Switch off ignition and remove ignition key.   
2. Disconnect ground strap on the battery.

# Information

1. After charging and waiting for at least 2 hours, during which time the battery should neither be loaded nor charged:

3. Measure the battery voltage with a hand-held multimeter.

1. The battery open-circuit voltage should not fallbelow 12.5 V.   
2. If the hand-held multimeter shows 12.5 V or more, the battery voltage is OK.   
. f the hand-held multimeter shows a battery voltage below 12.5 V: Charge the battery.

WARNING: Highly inflammable or explosive materials

Danger of fire or explosion

→ Avoid contact with hot parts or sources of ignition.

→ Use suction to remove ignitable vapors.

→ Attach warning sign in a clearly visible position.

# Information

A battery charger is required.   
Read operating instructions for the charger.   
The battery must have a minimum temperature of 0 °C.   
If possible, do not rapid-charge batteries as this can damage them.   
If exhaustively discharged batteries are charged quickly, they wil not take up a charge current or they will be identified too early as full due to the so-called "surface charge".

NOTE: A battery charger for providing an external power supply or for jump-lead starting is connected directly to the battery in the vehicle.

Risk of damage to the battery sensor.   
Battery sensor sends incorrect battery values to the vehicle electrical system.

→ Always connect a battery charger for providing an external power supply or for jump-lead starting to the defined connections in the engine compartment. → 2XOOIN BATTERY TRICKLE CHARGING

1. Switch off the battery charger.   
. Switch off ignition and remove ignition key.   
3. Connect cables from the charger to the external power supply points.   
4. Set the charge current on the battery charger according to the battery capacity.   
Switch on the battery charger.

# Procedure for charging exhaustively discharged batteries:

Batteries that have not been used for a long time discharge automatically.

A battery is exhaustively discharged if the open-circuit voltage has dropped below 11.6 V, see OPEN-CIRCUIT VOLTAGE MEASUREMENT

In exhaustively discharged batteries, the battery acid (sulfuric acid and water mixture) consists of virtually only water, as the sulfuric acid proportion is considerably reduced.

Exhaustively discharged batteries sulphatise, i.e. the entire plate surfaces of the batteries harden.

If exhaustively discharged batteries are immediately recharged after an exhaustive discharge, the sulphatisation recedes again.

If these batteries are not recharged, the plates continue to harden and charge take-up ability is limited. This results in reduced battery performance.

Exhaustively discharged batteries must be charged using a low charge current as follows:

1. Set the charge current to maximum 10% of battery capacity, i.e. with a 95 AH battery, the charge current is max. 9.5 A.

Charge the battery.

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > BATTERY TRICKLE CHARGING

When working or carrying out tests on the vehicle or when the vehicle is in the workshop, a battery charger with a rated current of at least 40 A must be connected.

As soon as the vehicle is unlocked, e.g. the vehicle is in the workshop or salesroom, it must be trickle charged with a battery charging device.

1.Switch off the battery charger.   
2. Switch offignition and remove remote control (hand-held transmitter).   
3.Switch off all electrical loads(e.g. lights).

4. Open protective cover on the positive terminal for jump-lead starting.

5. First, connect the positive cable to the positive terminal for jump-lead starting, then to the positive terminal of the donor battery.   
6. First, connect the negative cable to the negative terminal of the donor battery, then to the ground point for jump-lead starting.   
7. Set the charge current on the battery charger according to the battery capacity.   
. Switch on the battery charger.

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > CONNECTING THE BATTERY FOR TRICKLE CHARGING

A charger with a current rating of at least 40 A must be connected to the external power supply points/jump-lead starting points.

Set the charger to maximum A (amps).

Switch off allunnecessary loads (e.g. lights).

When working on the vehicle for more than 15 minutes.

When running diagnostics using the Porsche System Tester.

When adjusting the headlights.

When working on or with the Infotainment system.

If the doors, bonnet and rear lid are open for a long period of time or if these components are actuated frequently.

# WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > TOOLS

![](images/44aff77720a992fd0d97cae1dd5e1dfb2d7ff68fa393492145e7879e2c534657.webp)

# WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK > WHEN DOES DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR CONTROL UNIT NEED TO BE ADJUSTED?

The distance measuring sensor control unit must be re-adjusted in the following situations:

1. Suspension was aligned and adjusted.   
2. Distance measuring sensor control unit or distance measuring sensor control unit holder was loosened or removed and installed.   
3. Bumper was loosened or removed and installed.   
4. The front end is damaged.   
5. Fault memory entry: ACC sensor incorrectly adjusted (Do0004).   
1.5.1. The misalignment angle is outside of the range -1.5° to +1.5°.

# WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK > REQUIREMENTS FOR TESTING AND ADJUSTMENT

1. Tyre tread depth of the tires of one axle must not deviate by more than 2 mm.   
2. Tyre inflation pressure in accordance with regulations ("Comfort" or "Normal" tire pressure).   
3. As with complete suspension alignment, make sure that there is no sliding base or turnplate at the end stop during alignment.   
1. 3.1. Take the track width and wheel base into consideration.   
4. Check that vehicle weight corresponds to empty weight. Weight of the vehicle ready for driving (completely full fuel tank, reducing agent tank and water reservoir for the windscreen washer/headlight cleaning system, spare wheel, tool kit, jack) without driver.   
5. Spare wheel, tool kit and jack must be located at the positions specified by the vehicle manufacturer.   
6. Vehicle aligned correctly, having been bounced multiple times.   
7. Wheel suspension, steering and steering linkage show no signs of play or damage.   
1.7.1. Check for play and damage and carry out repairs if necessary.   
8. Set vehicles with air suspension to normal level.   
1. 8.1. Switch off ignition, close and lock all doors.   
2. 8.2. Wait 15 seconds until vehicle has settled in normal level.   
3.8.3. Open door and leave it open during the measurement, switch on ignition.

# WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK > SETTING UP THE MEASURING SYSTEM

Check that there is suficient floor space between the vehicle and the adjustment device - the gap between the adjustment device and vehicle must be approx. 120 cm.

The vehicle can be reversed onto the axle alignment platform if there is not enough floor space in front of the measuring platform.

The vehicle must be positioned so that the front and rear axles are centered on turnplates/sliding plates.

# Information

The procedure described here is for the wheel alignment system ML 5000 Porsche WE 1272 and the axle alignment system with DSP508XF sensors WE 1328.

Deviations can occur with other alignment systems.

1. Select the relevant vehicle in the wheel alignment computer.   
2. Select quick function Calibrate distance measuring sensor .   
3. Fit instrument holders onto the wheels on the rear axle.   
4. Fit the rear sensors onto the rear axle using the spoiler adapter (Beissbarth only, this sets the sensors to a lower position).   
5. Align the rear sensors on the rear axle using the spirit level and clamp the instrument holders using the wing screws.

# Information

Once the vehicle and adjustment tool are aligned, the vehicle and adjustment tool must no longer be moved.

1. The vehicle is standing on turnplates/sliding plates that are released on one side , allowing the vehicle to be moved slightly.   
2. If the vehicle is moved while taking measurements on the turnplates, the measurement process must be repeated.   
3. If the adjustment tool is moved following alignment, the measurement process must be repeated.

.Attach the front sensors to the measuring mirror, align using the spirit level and clamp.

1.6.1. Centre the adjustment tool.   
2.6.2. Set distance of adjustment too and vehicle in accordance with the specifications provided by the measuring equipment manufacturer.   
3. 6.3. The distance between the left sensor and the vehicle -Bl- should be identical to the distance between the right sensor and the vehicle -Br- .

![](images/b4205cc2c77511406c8d04decdbb338782e2e9de2d2af8f74f4a5ff358664e84.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Right Sensor Dimension   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Switch on (initialize) the sensors.

# WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK > PREPARATION FOR ADJUSTING DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR

1. Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least 40 A to the external power feed points.

2. Read out the fault memory using Piwis Tester Il 9818 , create a vehicle analysis log if necessary → OXO3IN CREATING VEHICLE ANALYSIS LOG (VAL) and correct any faults.

3. Remove trim cover -1- from the distance measuring sensor control unit.

1.3.1. Push trim cover up -a-.

2. 3.2. Pull trim cover forward and remove it -b- .

Fig 1: Removing Trim Cover   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Clean distance measuring sensor control unit and trim cover using commercially available cleaning agent.   
5. Fit the front sensors onto the adjustment device, align using the spirit levels and clamp using the wing screws, and switch them on (initialize).   
6. Set the distance between the adjustment device with reflector VAS 6430/1 WE 1362 and the vehicle in accordance with the specifications provided by the measuring equipment manufacturer.   
1. 6.1. The distance between the left sensor and the vehicle -Bl- should be identical to the distance between the right spirit level and the vehicle -Br- .

![](images/91ab1665b063dd47b1c0eeb6ff218fe7c92f462579eaee0a9af95f71d7d4edc1.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Right Sensor Dimension   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. On the adjustment device, move the mirror into the position -2- in alignment with the marking (-A- the number 2 on the rotary knob must point towards the vehicle).

![](images/9d8164762c10fccb9c8cb989740f5dcbcd9ab52afe5b7d4bdf8f5aa5240a8785.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Adjustment Device Position   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# Information

Once the vehicle and adjustment tool are aligned, the vehicle and adjustment tool must no longer be moved.

1. The vehicle is standing on turnplates/sliding plates that are released on one side, allowing the vehicle to be moved.

2. If the vehicle is moved while taking measurements on the turnplates, the measurement process must be repeated.

3. If the adjustment tool is moved following alignment, the measurement process must be repeated.

8. Release turnplates/sliding plates on one side of the vehicle .

9. Start the menu for adjusting the distance measuring sensor control unit, see operating instructions for measuring platform .

10. Before starting the adjustment process, use the laser beam at the mirror -3- on the adjustment device (for switching on the laser beam, see operating instructions for adjustment device) to check that the laser beam strikes the sensor lens. Info:

1. 10.1. The adjustment device is positioned correctly if the laser beam still strikes the sensor lens even after the identical individual toe values have been set.

2. 10.2. If the laser beam does not strike the sensor lens, the alignment of the adjustment device must be repeated.

![](images/048d158840ad684dcaa9bf9f38edb33788e81433140268e0200e8d84481d7230.webp)  
Fig 4: Identifying Adjustment Device Position   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

11. Align adjustment device at the side:

1. 11.1. The laser beam of the adjustment device must strike the center of the sensor lens.

![](images/d1920a60c13286a319fc671881f3736c476f4dae0ccee88d05fdd8817ef70ad9.webp)  
Fig 5: Aligning Adjustment Device   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

12. Use the adjusting screws -1, 2, 3, 4, 5- on the adjustment device to level the mirror's spirit levels -A, B- horizontally.   
13. Use the crank -arrow- on the adjustment device to adjust the mirror so that the laser beam strikes the center of the sensor lens on the vertical line.

![](images/15b940e68de57dca744ed317cfcca22643eacf80d8a462f138140adadea174be.webp)  
Fig 6: Aligning Mirror's Spirit Levels   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR

1. Connect PiWis Tester Il 9818 to the vehicle and start it.

2. Switch on ignition.   
3. Select the required vehicle and the Adaptive cruise control control unit. Press [F12] to continue.   
4. Select the Maintenance/repairs sub-menu in the Adaptive cruise control menu. Press [F12] to continue.   
5. Follow the instructions on Piwis Tester Il 9818 and adjust the distance measuring sensor control unit -1- as required using adjustment tool T-socket wrench for ACC sensor VAS 6190/2 WE 1364 -2- by turning the relevant adjusting screw -3- according to specifications.

# WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Switch off ignition and pull remote control out of ignition lock.

2. PIWis Tester Il 9818 must now be disconnected from the vehicle.

3. Disconnect battery charger.

4. Remove sensors and instrument holders.

# Information

Before and after fitting the trim cover for the distance measuring sensor control unit, check the following points:

1. The holder for the distance measuring sensor control unit must not show any signs of deformation, which may have been caused, for example, by removing or installing the trim

cover for the distance measuring sensor control unit. If the holder for the distance measuring sensor control unit is deformed, carefully push it back into shape.

2. If the trim cover is damaged or cracked, replace the trim cover.

3. After fitting the trim cover, check that it is seated correctly and securely.

5. Installtrim cover -1- on the distance measuring sensor control unit.

1.5.1. Fit trim cover -a- .

2.5.2. Push trim cover down -b- until it engages securely.

# WM 2XOOIN BATTERY TRICKLE CHARGING (ALL MODELS) > BATTERY TRICKLE CHARGING > INFORMATION

→ "Workshop Equipment and Special Tools Information" Battery chargers.

# Information

When working or carrying out tests on the vehicle or when the vehicle is in the workshop, a battery charger with a rated current of at least 40 A must be connected.   
As soon as the vehicle is unlocked, e.g. the vehicle is in the workshop or salesroom, it must be trickle charged with a battery charging device.

NOTE: Using charging cables/jump leads directly on the vehicle battery.

Risk of damage to battery sensors.

→ Always connect charging cables/jump leads to the external power supply for jump-lead starting.

1. Open protective cover on the positive terminal for jump-lead starting.   
2. First, connect the positive cable from the charger to the positive terminal.   
3. Connect the negative cable from the charger to the ground point for jump-lead starting.   
4. Read the operating instructions for the charger.   
5. Switch off all electrical loads.   
6. Switch on the charger.

# WM 2XOOIN BATTERY TRICKLE CHARGING (ALL MODELS) > BATTERY TRICKLE CHARGING > CONNECTING THE BATTERY FOR TRICKLE CHARGING

A suitable battery charger must be connected to the vehicle electrical system when performing the following tasks. All unnecessary electrical loads must be switched off.

When working on the vehicle for more than 15 minutes.

When running diagnostics using the Porsche System Tester.

When adjusting the headlights.

When working on or with the Infotainment system.

If the doors, bonnet and rear lid are open for a long period of time or if these components are actuated frequently.

# WM 2XOOIN WORK INSTRUCTIONS AFTER DISCONNECTING THE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > EFFECT OF DISCONNECTION OR TOTAL DISCHARGE OF BATTERY ON ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS IN THE VEHICLE AND THE PRECAUTIONS TO BE TAKEN

Values and faults stored in the control units can be deleted if the batery is disconnected or completely discharged.

If possible, al fault memories should be checked and, if necessary, printed out before the battery is disconnected.

# Supply voltage fault entry

The entry "supply voltage" may be stored in various control units if the battery has been completely discharged.

Delete the "supply voltage" entry from the control units in question.

# Ready status

In some countries (presently the U.S.A. and Canada), after disconnecting the battery, it is necessary to reach the Ready status by a test drive and/or by using the Porsche System Tester DME control module menu). If in doubt about this, contact the relevant importer.

# 2470 DME control module

With all DME systems, the engine must run for several minutes before the engine control module can relearn the idle speed and mixture adaptation values!

After disconnection of the power supply, the idle speed might change or fluctuate briefly until the throttle valve adjusting unit has been readapted.

The mixture adaptation is also lost.

# After the battery is connected:

With the DME, it is necessary to carry out a learning and adaptation routine as described below:

Switch ignition on for 30 seconds without starting the engine.

• Do not actuate accelerator pedal.

This completes the adaptation of the throttle valve adjusting unit.

# Tyre pressure monitoring system

When the battery is disconnected and connected, the tire pressure is first displayed as "- - - ".

Once the battery has been disconnected and work is complete, the vehicle must be driven for a short distance.

The actual pressures will then be displayed again.

# 4560 Steering angle sensor

The steering angle sensor must be re-initialized when the battery is disconnected and connected.

Turn wheels to straight-ahead position.   
Switch ignition off and then on again twice.   
Start engine.   
From the straight-ahead position, turn steering wheel approx. 20° to the right, past the straight-ahead position.   
Drive the vehicle straight ahead for at least one second at a speed above 4 km/h (2.5 mp

The steering angle sensor segment is recognized again in this process.

Once the sensor has been successfull initialized, the fault code that is stored in the fault memory is documented using the fault deletion counter.

The fault memory erases itself automatically.

The PSM indicator light in the instrument cluster goes out.

# 6014 Motor for sunroof

The limit positions of the sunroof are deleted from the control unit when the battery is disconnected and connected.

Switch on ignition.   
Press the sunroof button for several seconds in direction of travel.   
After approx. 10 seconds, the sunroof performs an automatic standardization process anId resets all positions.   
Keep the button pressed during the standardization process.

Afterwards, the sunroof is standardized correctly.

# 6452 Power windows

The limit positions of the power windows are deleted from the control unit when the battery is disconnected and connected.

Perform the following procedure for all power windows:

Pull rocker switch and fully close window once.   
Pull rocker switch once more.

The upper end position of the window is stored.

Press rocker switch and fully open window once.   
Press rocker switch once more.

The lower end position of the window is stored.

# 4815 Electrical steering column adjustment (ELVS)

The electrical steering column adjustment end positions (ELVS) are deleted when the battery is disconnected and connected.

The following buttons must be pressed in sequence in order to re-initialize electrical steering column adjustment.

Press the extend button three times (extend towards the driver).   
Press the retract button once.   
Press the extend button once (towards the driver).   
Press the up button once.   
Press the down button once.

Once the buttons have been pressed correctly, the steering column automatically moves all axles and stops at the center position (only works when the vehicle is stationary).

1. Erase error messages from the control units.   
2. Perform the required initialization steps, depending on vehicle equipment.

# WM 2XOOIN WORK INSTRUCTIONS AFTER DISCONNECTING THE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > TEST DRIVE AFTER DISCONNECTING AND CONNECTING THE BATTERY

Depending on the vehicle equipment fitted, al these work steps are carried out during the test drive.

Read out the fault memories of all control units after the test drive.

If there is a fault present, check to see if the fault was caused by an undervoltage.   
If faults were caused by an undervoltage (or CAN timeout error), erase the fault memory, perform   
another test drive and read out the fault memory.   
If faults were not caused by an undervoltage, correct the faults in accordance with GFF (Guided Fault Finding). 1. Perform a test drive.

# WM 902555 REPLACING INSTRUMENT CLUSTER (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REPLACING INSTRUMENT CLUSTER

NOTE: Voltage drop

Risk of irreparable damage to control unit Risk of damage to control unit Fault entries in the control unit

Coding in the control unit is aborted •Malfunctions in control unit, even during programming

→ Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch offignition and remove ignition key.

→ Ensure that the power supply is not interrupted during programming.

→ Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least — Nominal value: 40 A to the vehicle battery.

# Information

The PlWis Tester Il9818 instructions take precedence since the description may be different with later Tester releases.

The procedure described here has been structured in general terms. Different text or additional information may appear in PIWis Tester Il 9818 .

1. Connect the PIWis Tester to the vehicle and start the Tester. Switch on ignition.   
2. Select the vehicle type and start the diagnostic application.   
3. Select the required control unit Instrument cluster in the overview .   
4. Maintenance/repairs must then be selected.   
5. Select the Set total mileage function and press [F12].   
6. Read the warning on the Tester and press [F12].   
7. Read off and take note of the total mileage.   
8. Switch off ignition and replace control unit. → 902519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING   
INSTRUMENT CLUSTER .   
9. Switch on ignition.   
10. Select the vehicle type and start the diagnostic application.   
11. Select the required control unit Instrument cluster in the overview .   
12. Extended identification must now be selected.   
13. Select the Vehicle identification number field.   
14. Enter the vehicle identification number and press "Enter" to confirm your entry.   
15. Maintenance/repairs must then be selected.   
16. Select the Set total mileage function and press [F12].   
17. Read the warning on the Tester and press [F12].   
1. Select Total mileage and enter the value that was read out in Step 7. Then press "Enter" to   
confirm your entry and press [F8] to write data.   
19. Coding/adaptations must then be selected.   
20. Select Automatic coding and press [F12].   
21. Wait until coding has been completed, then press [F12] to continue.   
22. Maintenance/repairs must then be selected.   
23. Select Fuel tank calibration and press [F12] to continue.   
24. Read the information displayed on the Tester, then start by pressing [F8].   
25. Read out the fault memory and erase it if necessary.   
26. Return to the control unit overview .   
27. Check the function of the instrument cluster and fuel level gauge during the test drive.

# WM 903555 REPLACING GATEWAY CONTROL UNIT (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REPLACING GATEWAY CONTROL UNIT > CODING THE GATEWAY CONTROL UNIT

NOTE: Voltage drop

Risk of irreparable damage to control unit Risk of damage to control unit •Fault entries in the control unit

Coding in the control unit is aborted Malfunctions in control unit, even during programming

→ Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch off ignition and remove ignition key.

→ Ensure that the power supply is not interrupted during programming.

→ Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least — Nominal value: 40 A to the vehicle battery.

# Information

The PIwis Tester Il9818 instructions take precedence since the description may be different with later Tester releases.

The procedure described here has been structured in general terms. Different text or additional information may appear in PIWis Tester Il 9818 .

1. Switch off ignition and replace control unit. → 903519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING   
GATEWAY CONTROL UNIT .   
2. Connect the PiWis Tester to the vehicle and start the Tester. Switch on ignition.   
3. Select the vehicle type and start the diagnostic application.   
4. Select the required control unit Gateway in the overview and press [F12] to continue.   
5. Extended identification must now be selected.   
6. Enter the vehicle identification number and press [Enter].   
7. Maintenance/repairs must then be selected.   
8. Control unit replacement must now be selected. Then press [F12] to continue.   
9. Select Write data , press [F12] and then press [F8] to start. Data is installed.   
10. As soon as the Tester confirms that data has been written , switch the ignition off and on   
again.   
11. Go back to the overview by pressing [F7].   
12. Select Maintenance of vehicle data and press [F12] to continue.   
13. Enter data in the required fields  and press [F12] to continue.   
14. Maintenance/repairs must then be selected.   
15. Required & Actual configuration must now be selected. Then press [F12] to continue.   
16. Check the list of components that are actually installed and accept it by pressing [F8].   
17. Codings/adaptations must now be selected. Then press [F12] to continue.   
18. Automatic coding must now be selected. Then press [F12] to continue.

19. The Tester displays the message Coding has been completed successfully . Press [F12] to continue.   
20. Read out the fault memory and erase it if necessary.

# WM 906425 ACTIVATING PCC/PVTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > TECHNICAL VALUES

![](images/3ff48f291a212c862fa4992164866b6c757acac31d991db73337783c6791eea3.webp)

# WM 906425 ACTIVATING PCC/PVTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > ACTIVATING PCC/PVTS

NOTE: Voltage drop

Risk of irreparable damage to control unit   
Risk of damage to control unit   
Fault entries in the control unit   
•Coding in the control unit is aborted   
•Malfunctions in control unit, even during programming

→ Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch offignition and remove ignition key.

→ Ensure that the power supply is not interrupted during programming.

→ Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least — Nominal value: 40 A to the vehicle battery.

# Information

The PlWis Tester Il9818 instructions take precedence since the description may be different with later Tester releases.

The procedure described here has been structured in general terms; different text or additions may

# appear in PIWis Tester Il 9818 .

PCC/PVTS should be activated just before vehicle hand over as the customer has access to the vehicle and the term of the PCC/PVTS contract begins following activation.

1. Get installation code from the customer.

# Information

If the installation code is not available, PCC/PVTS activation must be carried out during vehicle hand over.

2.Connect the PIWiS Tester to the vehicle and start the Tester. Switch on ignition.

3. Select the vehicle type and start the diagnostic application.

4. Check the chassis number and press [F12] to start.

5. Select Vehicle functions in the menu by pressing [F7].

6. Start the Tester sequence Activate PCC/PVTS by pressing [F12].

7. Follow the steps/instructions shown on the PIWIS Tester.

8. Log PCC/PVTS activation.

9. Switch off gnition.

10. Read out the fault memory and erase it if necessary.

11. Perform a function test if necessary.

Risk of damage to lines

Risk of damage to optical waveguide

NOTE: Incorrect handling of main wire harness

Risk of damage to lines

→ The main wire harness contains all airbag lines, antenna lines and optical waveguides.

→ The main wire harness must not be separated and is always replaced as a complete wire harness when carrying out extensive repairs.

→ If individual lines are damaged, shut off these lines and install new lines. Lay the new lines along the main wire harness and secure them to the main wire harness.

# Information

Always comply with the regulations for handling ESD-sensitive components!

Assembly work may only be carried out if the mechanic is wearing the working clothes and shoes approved by Porsche.   
The new part must only be removed from the ESD (electrostatic discharge) protective packaging just before installation and at the position at which the part is to be installed.   
Never touch the electric pins and plug contacts. 1. Release electric plug connections -1- , disconnect them and push them to the right out of the holders.

# WM 970909 LOOSENING AND SECURING MAIN WIRE HARNESS IN ENGINE COMPARTMENT (ALL MODELS) > SECURING MAIN WIRE HARNESS IN ENGINE COMPARTMENT AT THE RIGHT

NOTE: Incorrect handling of main wire harness

Risk of damage to lines

→ The main wire harness contains all airbag lines, antenna lines and optical waveguides.

→ The main wire harness must not be separated and is always replaced as a complete wire harness when carrying out extensive repairs.

→ If individual lines are damaged, shut off these lines and instal new lines. Lay the new lines along the main wire harness and secure them to the main wire harness.

# Information

Always comply with the regulations for handling ESD-sensitive components!

Assembly work may only be carried out if the mechanic is wearing the working clothes and shoes approved by Porsche.   
The new part must only be removed from the ESD (electrostatic discharge) protective packaging just before installation and at the position at which the part is to be installed.   
•Never touch the electric pins and plug contacts.

1. The main wire harness is secured in reverse order to the steps required for loosening it.

1.1.1. Make sure that the individual sub-parts of the wire harness in the engine compartment at the right are not twisted or entangled.   
2. 1.2. Check that the wire harness is routed correctly and without tension so that no chafing occurs.

Risk of damage to lines

→ The main wire harness must not be separated and is always replaced as a complete wire harness when carrying out extensive repairs.

→ If individual lines are damaged, shut off these lines and instal new lines. Lay the new lines along the main wire harness and secure them to the main wire harness.

Risk of damage to optical waveguide

→ Observe the requirements for working with and instaling optical waveguides.

# Information

Always comply with the regulations for handling ESD-sensitive components!

Assembly work may only be carried out if the mechanic is wearing the working clothes and shoes approved by Porsche. The new part must only be removed from the ESD (electrostatic discharge) protective packaging just before installation and at the position at which the part is to be installed. Never touch the electric pins and plug contacts.

NOTE: Incorrect handling of main wire harness

Risk of damage to lines

→ The main wire harness contains all airbag lines, antenna lines and optical waveguides.

→ The main wire harness must not be separated and is always replaced as a complete wire harness when carrying out extensive repairs.

→ If individual lines are damaged, shut off these lines and install new lines. Lay the new lines along the

main wire harness and secure them to the main wire harness.

NOTE: Incorrect handling of optical waveguides

Risk of damage to optical waveguide

→ Observe the requirements for working with and installing optical waveguides.

# Information

Always comply with the regulations for handling ESD-sensitive components!

Assembly work may only be carried out i the mechanic is wearing the working clothes and shoes approved by Porsche.   
The new part must only be removed from the ESD (electrostatic discharge) protective packaging just before installation and at the position at which the part is to be installed.

1. The main wire harness is secured in reverse order to the steps required for loosening it.

1.1.1. Make sure that the individual sub-parts of the wire harness in the passenger compartment at the left are not twisted or entangled.   
2. 1.2. Check that the wire harness is routed correctly and without tension so that no chafing occurs.   
3. 1.3. Clip all electric lines for the main wire harness in the passenger compartment at the left in securely at the designated positions.   
4.1.4. Connect allelectric plug connections until they engage securely.   
5.1.5. Lock all electric plug connections by hand using the manual slide lock.

2. Tighten fastening nut securing ground line to the body. Tightening torque 9 Nm (6.5 ftlb.)

# WM 973219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WIRE HARNESS FOR DOOR IN REAR DOOR SUB-FRAME (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING WIRE HARNESS FOR DOOR IN REAR DOOR SUB-FRAME

Always comply with the regulations for handling ESD-sensitive components!

Assembly work may only be carried out if the mechanic is wearing the working clothes and shoes   
approved by Porsche.   
The new part must only be removed from the ESD (electrostatic discharge) protective packaging just before installation and at the position at which the part is to be installed.   
Never touch the electric pins and plug contacts. 1. Installation is performed in reverse order to removal. 1.1.1. Make sure that the individual sections of the wire harness in the rear door sub-frame are not twisted or entangled.

2. 1.2. Check that the wire harness is routed correctly and without tension so that no chafing occurs.

3.1.3. Connect allelectric plug connections until they engage securely.

4. 1.4. Lock all electric plug connections by hand using the manual slide lock.

5. 1.5. Clip in allsections of the door wire harness in the rear door sub-frame securely at the relevant positions.

2. Make sure that the grommets -1, 2, 3- and the cover -4- are seated correctly in the rear door.

1.2.1. Align grommet -2- in such a way that the center bar -a- of the grommet is pointing towards the recess -b- in the door panel.

2. 2.2. Align grommet -3- in such a way that the grommet exit points in the door are pointing straight down.

![](images/312967fcb0e0a1b7102add72a84b6c946d1715d8526748a9a818ad5dcfda8d00.webp)  
Fig 1: Checking Grommets And Cover

# WM 974519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING BATTERY-STARTER WIRE HARNESS (FROM EXTERNAL POWER CONNECTION TO STARTER) (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING BATTERY-STARTER WIRE HARNESS (FROM EXTERNAL POWER CONNECTION TO STARTER)

1. Installation is performed in reverse order to removal.   
2. Tighten fastening nut securing B+ positive cable to the potential distributor on the longitudinal member. Tightening torque 20 Nm (15 ftlb.)   
3. Tighten fastening nut securing ground line to the longitudinal member. Tightening torque 20 Nm (15 ftlb.)   
4. Tighten fastening nut securing positive cable at the jump-start point. Tightening torque 7.5 Nm (5.5 ftlb.)   
5. Tighten connection terminal securing B+ positive cables to the jump-start point. Tightening torque 20 Nm (15 ftlb.)   
6. Tighten fastening nut securing positive cable to B+ positive cable. Tightening torque 7.5 Nm (5.5 ftlb.)

# WM 974619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CUTOFF RELAY (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING CUTOFF RELAY

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag units

Triggering of airbag unit.   
System faults can occur.

→ Switch off ignition and remove ignition key or remote control (hand-held transmitter).

→ A power supply (e.g. battery charger) must not be connected to the external power supply/jump-lead starting terminals.

→ Disconnect the battery and insulate the ground strap so that all contact with a ground carrier is avoided.

→ Wait 1 minute after disconnecting the battery.

→ Only pullof connector on the triggering unit after the waiting time has elapsed.

→ Make sure that no foreign objects are located in front of the airbag unit during installation.

→ Replace damaged parts during removal.

→ Always position airbag units so that the blow-out opening is facing upwards, e.g. crest on driver's airbag.

→ Do not position anything on the airbag units.

— If removed for an extended period, the airbag units must be stored in a safe place.

— Airbag units must not come into contact with grease, oil, detergents, liquids, or similar substances.

→ Do not expose airbag units to temperatures above 90°.

→ Do not remove the short-circuit spring on the plug-in contacts.

→ Ignition and preparations may only be carried out by skilled staff, supervised by a second responsible person.

→ Before disposal, the airbag unit must be rendered harmless by electrical ignition performed in accordance with all precautionary measures, thereby preventing it from being used incorrectly.

1. Screw off fastening nuts -1- .   
2. Removing cutoff relay -2- from the power distributor.

![](images/5ca7894695031083fa23368516ba26ca1ae3bc9f15e18588e95533bd6f68bd2e.webp)  
Fig 1: Removing Cutoff Relay

# WM 974619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CUTOFF RELAY (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING CUTOFF RELAY

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag units

Triggering of airbag unit.   
System faults can occur.

→ Switch offignition and remove ignition key or remote control (hand-held transmitter).

→ A power supply (e.g. battery charger) must not be connected to the external power supply/jump-lead starting terminals.

→ Disconnect the battery and insulate the ground strap so that al contact with a ground carrier is avoided.

→ Wait 1 minute after disconnecting the battery.

→ Only pull off connector on the triggering unit after the waiting time has elapsed.

→ Make sure that no foreign objects are located in front of the airbag unit during installation.

→ Replace damaged parts during removal.

→ Always position airbag units so that the blow-out opening is facing upwards, e.g. crest on driver's airbag.

→ Do not position anything on the airbag units.

→ If removed for an extended period, the airbag units must be stored in a safe place.

— Airbag units must not come into contact with grease, oil, detergents, liquids, or similar substances.

→ Do not expose airbag units to temperatures above 90°.

→ Do not remove the short-circuit spring on the plug-in contacts.

→ Ignition and preparations may only be carried out by skilled staff, supervised by a second responsible person.

→ Before disposal, the airbag unit must be rendered harmless by electrical ignition performed in accordance with all precautionary measures, thereby preventing it from being used incorrectly.

1. Installation is performed in reverse order to removal.   
2. Tighten fastening nuts used to secure cutoff relay on power distributor. Tightening torque 8 Nm (6 ftlb.)

# WM 975219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WIRE HARNESS FOR ENGINE (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Remove engine. → 100119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING ENGINE .

2. Loosen the generator and disconnect electric plug connections at generator. → 272219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING GENERATOR .

3. Disconnect oxygen sensors upstream of the catalytic converter at the left and right and unclip all holders for the lines. → 246919 REMOVING AND INSTALLING OXYGEN SENSOR UPSTREAM OF CATALYTIC CONVERTER .

4. Disconnect oxygen sensors downstream of the catalytic converter at the left and right and unclip all holders for the lines. → 247319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING OXYGEN SENSOR DOWNSTREAM OF CATALYTIC CONVERTER .

5. Remove vacuum reservoir with secondary air pump. → 245419 REMOVING AND INSTALLING VACUUM RESERVOIR .

# WM 975219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WIRE HARNESS FOR ENGINE (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > INSTALLING WIRE HARNESS FOR ENGINE

1. Installation is performed in reverse order to removal.

1.1.1. Make sure that the individual sub-parts of the engine wire harness are not twisted or entangled.   
2.1.2. Check that the wire harness is routed correctly and without tension so that no chafing occurs.   
3.1.3. Connect allelectric plug connections until they engage securely.   
4. 1.4. Lock all electric plug connections by hand using the manual slide lock.   
5.1.5. Clip in all sections of the engine wire harness securely at the relevant positions.

2. Tighten fastening screws for the wiring ducts at the left and right on the cylinder head.

3. Tighten fastening screws for the wiring ducts at the left and right on the valve cover.

4. Tighten fastening screws for the wiring ducts on the thermostat housing.

5. Tighten fastening screws for the wiring ducts on the crankcase.

6. Tighten fastening screw for the vent line on the cylinder head. Tightening torque 10 Nm (7.5 ftib.)   
7. Tighten fastening screw securing holder to left cylinder head.   
8. Tighten fastening nut used to secure the electric B+ line to the starter. Tightening torque 18 Nm (13 ftlb.)   
9. Tighten fastening nut used to secure the electric line for terminal 50 to the starter. Tightening torque 10 Nm (7.5 ftlb.)   
10. Tighten fastening screw securing wiring duct to the timing chain housing cover.   
11. Tighten fastening screws securing coolant line to the timing chain housing cover.

# WM 975219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WIRE HARNESS FOR ENGINE (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Install vacuum reservoir with secondary-air pump → INSTALLING VACUUM RESERVOIR .   
2. Connect oxygen sensors downstream of the catalytic converter at the left and right and clip in all holders for the lines → INSTALLING OXYGEN SENSOR DOWNSTREAM OF CATALYTIC CONVERTER .   
3. Connect oxygen sensors upstream of the catalytic converter at the left and right and clip in all holders for the lines → INSTALLING OXYGEN SENSOR UPSTREAM OF CATALYTIC CONVERTER .   
4. Install the generator → INSTALLING GENERATOR .   
5. Install engine → INSTALLING ENGINE .

# Information

Always comply with the regulations for handling ESD-sensitive components!

Assembly work may only be carried out if the mechanic is wearing the working clothes and shoes approved by Porsche.   
The new part must only be removed from the ESD (electrostatic discharge) protective packaging   
just before installation and at the position at which the part is to be installed.   
Never touch the electric pins and plug contacts.

# Information

Before routing a new optical waveguide:

Replace damaged parts if necessary. 1. Release electric plug connection -1- for optical waveguide at the compact connector -2- for the PCM display and operator control unit -B- and disconnect it.

Fig 2: Disconnecting Electric Plug Connection From TV Tuner Compact Connector

# WM 977223 INSTALLING OPTICAL WAVEGUIDE (PCM TO TV TUNER) (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING OPTICAL CONTACTS ON CONNECTOR SIDE

1. Open the secondary locking mechanism using press-out and unlocking tools for tab and round plug connectors of allsizes Nr.155. Insert the tool into the opening provided and lift the locking mechanism. The locking mechanism engages in the upper position.

![](images/c549cbb189dc3f9c4f70dd42755f88dd6cfe6773d8a063ef539be473e1d9958f.webp)  
Fig 1: Removing Secondary Locking Mechanism Of Optical Contacts (Connector Side)   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Press-out and unlocking tools for tab and round plug connectors of alsizes Nr.155 must be positioned on the primary locking mechanism. Then lift the locking mechanism.

A. Optical contact, grey B. Optical contact, black

![](images/bf170de950a1f14302bdc057a03593403a568f260b45449b985af76f683214c2.webp)  
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Carefully pull on the optical waveguides -A and B- in -direction of arrow- . If it is not possible to pull out the optical waveguide, check again that the secondary locking mechanism is completely released and that the primary locking mechanism is raised sufficiently.

Perform visual inspection of locking mechanisms, connector housings and contacts for possible damage, and exchange the damaged parts, if necessary.

![](images/456a92b372a8709a170918a5d9409baf6a90edadde7e56dcd88c11ff4ce3cef1.webp)

# Instaling optical waveguide (PCM to TV tuner)

The new lines willbe secured to the fastening points for the old lines.   
The old wire harness remains installed in the vehicle.   
The old wire harness will only be disconnected/unplugged directly at the connected components.

# Information

When installing the wire harness, make sure the insulation of the line is not damaged.

# Information

The range of spare parts available for optical waveguides depends on the vehicle equipment. Depending on the vehicle equipment, there is a specific set containing the individual optical waveguides.

Select the required optical waveguide and remove it from the set.

# Information

Before routing a new optical waveguide:

Visually check the locks, connector housing and contacts for damage.   
Replace damaged parts if necessary. 1. Cut off optical contacts of the damaged optical waveguide, isolate it and tie it to the main wire harness. 2. Route new optical waveguide along the main wire harness, guide it through the existing cable ducts and tie it to the main wire harness using tie-wraps. 3. Plug electric plug connection -1- for the optical waveguide into the compact connector -2- for the TV tuner -A- until the electric plug connection engages securely.

![](images/a64ee6e7e231d8a4e5c1c0805e8418fc50926195883916521c7c938250e8ff22.webp)  
Fig 3: Plugging Electric Plug Connection Into TV Tuner Compact Connector

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Plug electric plug connection -1- for the optical waveguide into the compact connector -2- for the PCM display and operator control unit -A- until the electric plug connection engages securely.

![](images/fe0cc006052f920e74d81fcb0e0b73e419927afb48659d173fcdbd5bfa63e0b5.webp)  
Fig 4: Plugging Electric Plug Connection Into PCM Compact Connector

# WM 978919 REMOVING AND INSTALLING POWER DISTRIBUTOR (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING POWER DISTRIBUTOR

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag units

Triggering of airbag unit.   
System faults can occur.

→ Switch off ignition and remove ignition key or remote control (hand-held transmitter).

→ A power supply (e.g. battery charger) must not be connected to the external power supply/jump-lead starting terminals.

→ Disconnect the battery and insulate the ground strap so that all contact with a ground carrier is avoided.

→ Wait 1 minute after disconnecting the battery.

→ Only pull off connector on the triggering unit after the waiting time has elapsed.

→ Make sure that no foreign objects are located in front of the airbag unit during installation.

→ Replace damaged parts during removal.

→ Always position airbag units so that the blow-out opening is facing upwards, e.g. crest on driver's airbag.

→ Do not position anything on the airbag units.

→ If removed for an extended period, the airbag units must be stored in a safe place.

→ Airbag units must not come into contact with grease, oil, detergents, liquids, or similar substances.

→ Do not expose airbag units to temperatures above 90°.

→ Do not remove the short-circuit spring on the plug-in contacts.

→ Ignition and preparations may only be carried out by skilled staff, supervised by a second responsible person.

→ Before disposal, the airbag unit must be rendered harmless by electrical ignition performed in accordance with all precautionary measures, thereby preventing it from being used incorrectly.

1. Open cover -1- on the positive terminal.

2. Loosen terminal clamp -2- for the power distributor from the battery terminal.

Fig 1: Loosening Terminal Clamp On Positive Terminal

![](images/1590531526474ec7984aebc08a2da9790872a8a840e2bd9ea226e7dcee98846d.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Release cover -1- (-a- ) and fold it up towards the rear.

![](images/88ae72484f78ca72fe3bd49d33dfeb39d76c480183c81523c6f4dada7ae2d8c2.webp)  
Fig 2: Opening Cover

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Unscrew fastening screw -1- and remove electric line.

5. Unscrew fastening nuts -2- and remove ground lines.

![](images/656200d0b1ebd7c56feeae7fee8d087ae10fbea7f8034fbdab374cf7f623cb77.webp)  
Fig 3: Disconnecting Electric Lines

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. Lift the power distributor and release and disconnect electric plug connection -1- on the cutoff relay -2- (-a- ).

![](images/a0c9f99962433150feb39e57ad0a3a6cf7125f1fb41057f9d3ecbcd30d301ca0.webp)  
Fig 4: Disconnecting Electric Plug Connection On Cutoff Relay

# WM 978919 REMOVING AND INSTALLING POWER DISTRIBUTOR (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING POWER DISTRIBUTOR

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag units

Triggering of airbag unit.   
System faults can occur.

→ Switch off ignition and remove ignition key or remote control (hand-held transmitter).

→ A power supply (e.g. battery charger) must not be connected to the external power supply/jump-lead starting terminals.

→ Disconnect the battery and insulate the ground strap so that al contact with a ground carrier is avoided.

→ Wait 1 minute after disconnecting the battery.

→ Only pull off connector on the triggering unit after the waiting time has elapsed.

→ Make sure that no foreign objects are located in front of the airbag unit during installation.

→ Replace damaged parts during removal.

→ Always position airbag units so that the blow-out opening is facing upwards, e.g. crest on driver's airbag.

→ Do not position anything on the airbag units.

→ If removed for an extended period, the airbag units must be stored in a safe place.

→ Airbag units must not come into contact with grease, oil, detergents, liquids, or similar substances.

→ Do not expose airbag units to temperatures above 90°.

→ Do not remove the short-circuit spring on the plug-in contacts.

→ Ignition and preparations may only be carried out by skilled staff, supervised by a second responsible person.

→ Before disposal, the airbag unit must be rendered harmless by electrical ignition performed in accordance with all precautionary measures, thereby preventing it from being used incorrectly.

1. Installation is performed in reverse order to removal.   
2. Tighten M6 fastening nuts used to secure electric lines to the power distributor. Tightening torque 7.5 Nm (5.5 ftlb.)   
3. Tighten M8 fastening nut used to secure electric line to the power distributor. Tightening torque 16 Nm (12 ftlb.)   
4. Tighten fastening screw used to secure electric line to the power distributor. Tightening torque 7.5 Nm (5.5 ftlb.)

# WM 9XOOIN BASIC INSTRUCTIONS AND PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE PIWIS TESTER (ALL MODELS) > TOOLS

![](images/acce784ffeb3bc0a61f7398ba4c35dbea315cfe4dc799c91cccc56979bc6646d.webp)

# WM 9XOOIN BASIC INSTRUCTIONS AND PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE PIWIS TESTER (ALL MODELS) > BASIC INFORMATION AND INSTRUCTIONS FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING > BASIC INFORMATION ON CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING

There are basically two different ways of carrying out control unit programming:

Using the "Programming" menu for the relevant control unit (e.g. for the DME and PDK control units).

# or

•Using the "Campaign" function in the Additional menu on the PIWis Tester by entering a specific programming code.

The type of control unit programming to be used is described in the relevant Service Information or in the relevant Technical Information.

# WM 9XOOIN BASIC INSTRUCTIONS AND PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE PIWIS TESTER (ALL MODELS) > BASIC INFORMATION AND INSTRUCTIONS FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING > BASIC INSTRUCTIONS FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING

NOTE: Fault entry in the fault memory and control unit programming aborted due to lervoltage.

Increased current draw during diagnosis or control unit programming can cause a drop in voltage, which can result in one or more fault entries and the abnormal termination of the programming process.

→ Before commencing work, connect a suitable battery charger with a current rating of at least 40 A to the jump-start terminals in the engine compartment.

NOTE: Control unit programming will be aborted if the WLAN connection is unstable.

•An unstable WLAN connection can interrupt communication between PIWIS Tester Il and the vehicle communication module (VCl). As a result, control unit programming may be aborted.

→ During control unit programming, always connect PIWis Tester II to the vehicle communication module (VCI) via the USB cable.

NOTE: Control unit programming will be aborted if the vehicle key is not recognized

If the vehicle key is not recognized in vehicles with Porsche Entry & Drive, programming cannot be started or will be interrupted.

→ Switch on the ignition using the original vehicle key. To do this, replace the control panel in the ignition lock with the original vehicle key if necessary.

# WM 9XOOIN BASIC INSTRUCTIONS AND PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE PIWIS TESTER (ALL MODELS) > GENERAL PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least 40 A (e.g. battery charger HFL 65 WE 1353) to the jump-start terminals in the engine compartment and switch it on.

.Switch on the ignition using the original driver's key.

On vehicles with "Porsche Entry & Drive", do this by replacing the control panel in the ignition lock with the original driver's key if necessary.

3. PIWis Tester Il 9818 must be connected to the vehicle communication module (VCl) via the USB cable. Then, connect the communication module to the vehicle and switch on the PIWIS Tester.

# WM 9XOOIN BASIC INSTRUCTIONS AND PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE PIWIS TESTER (ALL MODELS) > BASIC PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE PIWIS TESTER > INFORMATION ON THE PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING

There are basically two different ways of carrying out control unit programming using the PIWis Tester

• Using the "Programming" menu for the relevant control unit (e.g. for the DME and PDK control units) → Control unit programming using the "Programming" menu.

# or

Using the "Campaign" function in the Additional menu on the PIWis Tester by entering a specific programming code → Control unit programming using the "Campaign" function in the Additional menu on the PIWIS Tester.

The type of control unit programming to be used is described in the relevant Service Information or in the elevant Technical Information.

# WM 9XOOIN BASIC INSTRUCTIONS AND PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE PIWIS TESTER (ALL MODELS) > BASIC PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE PIWIS TESTER > CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE "PROGRAMMING" MENU

1. On the PIWiS Tester start screen, call up the ==> 'Diagnostics' menu and select the relevant vehicle type.

The diagnostic application is then started and the control unit selection screen is populated.

2. Select the control unit to be programmed in the control unit selection screen (==> "Overview" menu) and press [>] to confirm your selection → see Fig 1.

![](images/02d4a562fab1e55f9cea3a6d47f94aa487adb017d25a302b5508b3556ec924d3.webp)  
Fig 1: Screen Display - Control Unit Selection

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. When the question "Create Vehicle Analysis Log (VAL)?" appears, either press [F12] to create a VAL or press [F11] if you do not want to create a VAL.

4. Press [>] to acknowledge the message that may appear informing you that campaigns for the vehicle are stored in the PIWIS information system.

5. Once the control unit to be programmed has been found, select the ==> 'Programming' menu

6. Select the ==> 'Automatic programming'function and press [>>] to confirm your selection and start the guided programming sequence → see Fig 2.

![](images/3f42c2ead07221d67bcc57b8bdfc2cfdb78ff12229050f84e820444bb45e4b5d.webp)  
Fig 2: Screen Display - Automatic Programming

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Read and follow the information and instructions on the Plwis Tester during the guided programming sequence. Then press [>>] to continue.

During the programming sequence, the control unit is re-programmed and then re-coded automatically if necessary.

# Do not interrupt programming and coding.

Once control unit programming - and coding if necessary - is complete, you will be prompted to switch the ignition off and then back on again after a specified waiting time.

# Information

Once programming is completed successfully, the work described under ==> "General subsequent work"  must always be carried out.

If other specific subsequent work is required, this is described in the relevant Service Information or in the relevant Technical Information.

# Information

1. If an error message is displayed during programming (e.g. "Campaign does not exist", "No suitable programming rules found" or "Vehicle data could not be read", etc.), please read and follow the appropriate instructions provided under — Troubleshooting. 2. If programming is interrupted (e.g. due to a voltage drop or if communication is aborted, etc.) or if programming could not be carried out successfully (error message

"Programming unsuccessful"), programming must be repeated .

3. If coding is not carried out successfully during the guided programming sequence, the control unit must be re-coded again separately once the guided programming sequence is complete. To do this, select the relevant control unit in the control unit selection screen ("Overview" menu) and press [>>] to confirm your selection. Once the control unit has been found, select the "Codings/adaptations" menu and re-code the control unit using the 'Automatic coding' function.

# WM 9XOOIN BASIC INSTRUCTIONS AND PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE PIWIS TESTER (ALL MODELS) > BASIC PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE PIWIS TESTER > CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE "CAMPAIGN" FUNCTION IN THE ADDITIONAL MENU ON THE PIWIS TESTER

1. On the PlWis Tester start screen, call up the ==> 'Diagnostics' menu and select the relevant vehicle type.

The diagnostic application is then started and the control unit selection screen is populated.

2. In the control unit selection screen ("Overview" menu), press [F7] to callup the ==> 'Additional menu' (→ see Fig 1).

![](images/3226223f8a6cd70ffdcb7bf187c4a0c07433deaa8946eb5e7c022ad50da3e216.webp)  
Fig 1: Screen Display - Control Unit Selection

3. When the question "Create Vehicle Analysis Log (VAL)?" appears, either press [>] to create a

VAL or press [F11] if you do not want to create a VAL.

4. Press [>] to acknowledge the message that may appear informing you that campaigns for the vehicle are stored in the PIWiS information system.

5. Select the ==> 'Campaign' function and press [>>] to confirm your selection → see Fig 2. You are then prompted to enter a programming code.

![](images/6bd7eaa160e5df81b0f25f4c592d0b929400d4c10ca3bbc699b918927c71e4d6.webp)  
Fig 2: Screen Display - Additional Menu - Campaign

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. To enter the programming code, click in the relevant text box so that the cursor starts to flash → see Fig 3.

![](images/27d559ff2b518efc479bf6b41e1aef87c96a29fd9cfcc629c513c4ad69bb033d.webp)  
Fig 3: Screen Display - Programming Code Input Field

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Enter the programming code specified in the relevant description (Technical Information, Service Information) and press Enter to confirm your entry.

The text box turns blue.

8. Press [>>] to start the guided programming sequence.

Read and follow the information and instructions on the Piwis Tester during the guided programming sequence. Then press [>>] to continue.

During the programming sequence, the control unit is re-programmed and then re-coded automatically if necessary.

# Do not interrupt programming and coding.

Once control unit programming - and coding if necessary - is complete, you will be prompted to switch the ignition off and then back on again after a specified waiting time.

# Information

Once programming is completed successfully, the work described under ==> "General subsequent work"  must always be carried out.

If other specific subsequent work is required, this is described in the relevant Service Information or in the relevant Technical Information.

# Information

1. If an error message is displayed during programming (e.g. "Campaign does not exist", "No suitable programming rules found" or "Vehicle data could not be read", etc.), please read and follow the appropriate instructions provided under → Troubleshooting.

2. If programming is interrupted (e.g. due to a voltage drop or if communication is aborted, etc.) or if programming could not be carried out successfully (error message "Programming unsuccessful"), programming must be repeated by entering the programming code again (Additional menu > Campaign >> Enter campaign number). It is not possible to program the control units manually.

3. If coding is not carried out successfully during the guided programming sequence, the control unit must be re-coded again separately once the guided programming sequence is complete. To do this, select the relevant control unit in the control unit selection screen ("Overview" menu) and press [>>] to confirm your selection. Once the control unit has been found, select the "Codings/adaptations" menu and re-code the control unit using the 'Automatic coding' function.

# WM 9XOOIN BASIC INSTRUCTIONS AND PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE PIWIS TESTER (ALL MODELS) > GENERAL SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Read out and erase allfault memories.

1.1.1. In the control unit selection screen (==> 'Overview menu), press [F7] to callup the ==> 'Additional menu' (→ see Fig 1).

![](images/472e0b9866a6d7f75c581318cfe6d2958ea167e13f4f8b40a2f9761291bcfcf6.webp)  
Fig 1: Screen Display - Control Unit Selection

2. 1.2. Select the function ==> 'Read all fault memories and erase if required' and

press [>>] to confirm → see Fig 2.

The fault memories of the control units are read out.

![](images/42430194f4c2058497a14cbd4c240fcdb77a5294de04a47ccffeb76a0c687a63.webp)  
Fig 2: Screen Display - Erasing Fault Memories

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3.1.3. Once you have read out the fault memories, delete the fault memory entries by pressing [F8].

4. 1.4. Press [>>] ("Yes") in response to the question as to whether you really want to delete all fault memory entries.

The faults stored in the fault memories of the various control units are deleted.

# Information

If there are still fault memory entries in individual control units, start the engine briefly and then switch it off again. Wait for approx. 10 seconds before switching the ignition on again and re-establish the connection between the PIWiS Tester and the vehicle. Then read out and erase the fault memories of the affected control units again separately.

If the control units are found to have other faults, which cannot be erased and are not caused by control unit programming,these faults must be found and corrected.

1. Switch off ignition.

2. Disconnect the PIWIS Tester from the vehicle.

3. Switch off and disconnect the battery charger.

4. On vehicles with Porsche Entry & Drive, replace the original driver's key in the ignition lock with the control panel again.

# WM 9XOOIN BULB TABLE AND INSTALLATION INSTRUCTIONS (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > INSTALLATION INSTRUCTIONS

WARNING: Live components

Risk of electric shock → Remove electric charge from component.

— Make sure it does not switch on again. → Check that there is no electric charge → Cover adjacent live parts.

NOTE: Incorrect handling of bulbs

Risk of damage to bulbs and the bulb housing

→ Switch offignition and remove ignition key.   
→ Switch off the relevant loads when changing bulbs.   
→ Only use bulbs listed in the bulb table.   
→ Only install clean bulbs that are free of grease.   
→ Always use a cloth or soft paper when working with bulbs.   
→ Observe the safety instructions when changing a bulb in a Bi-Xenon headlight.   
→ In certain states, it is compulsory to carry spare light bulbs.
