# WM 9XOOIN ORDERING AND REPAIRING ELECTRIC PLUG CONNECTIONS (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > GENERAL INFORMATION ON ORDERING CONNECTOR HOUSINGS AND REPAIR LINES

Information

oSpare parts for repairing electric plug connections can be purchased in the TKR Automotive GmbH online shop. Link: www.tkr-connector.com   
oThe spare parts available there include: Connector housings, individualines with crimped-on contact, crimp connectors, cable seals and dummy plugs.   
Initially, only the electric plug connections installed in the Macan are available in the online shop.   
oOnly spare parts for repairing electric plug connections are available in the online shop. The tools that are available there must be purchased using the usual procurement process for tools.   
oOnly one account for ordering connectors should be set up for the online shop for every Porsche Centre, but the account can be used many times internally in the Porsche Centre.

![](images/f11e15d8b24ed09eb6ac028ed320bef10c2246a616b13002209acd0d7bc1d364.webp)  
Fig 1: Screen Display - Online Shop

# WM 9XOOIN ORDERING AND REPAIRING ELECTRIC PLUG CONNECTIONS (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > IDENTIFICATION OF REQUIRED ELECTRIC PLUG CONNECTION

oThe correct individual line is identified based on the relevant connector housing. oThe correct individual lines and the correct tool for loosening the primary and secondary locks on the connector are displayed for every connector housing. The following options are available for identifying the conector housing in the online shop oPerform a search in the search field using the part number shown on the connector .

IMPORTANT: Enter the part number without spaces or punctuation

oPerform a search based on the number and arrangement of the pins and comparison with colored photos   
oPerform a search based on the position of the connector in the vehicle and comparison with colored photos   
o Identify the part number using wiring diagrams — "Wiring Diagrams" in PIWis Tester II 9818 and perform a search in the search field based on the part number that is read out.

oThe correct crimp connectors are identified based on the color coding of the line diameters in the online shop. The color coding corresponds to the color of the crimp connector.

# WM 9XOOIN ORDERING AND REPAIRING ELECTRIC PLUG CONNECTIONS (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > REPAIRING ELECTRIC PLUG CONNECTION

NOTE: Risk of damage to connector contacts or locking lugs •Corrosion on connector contacts Contact problems

→ Only use the recommended press-out tool

1. Release secondary lock on electric plug connection using the specified press-out tool.

2. Release primary lock on electric plug connection using the specified press-out tool.

3. Cut offaulty line -1- using stripping pliers VAS 1978/3 -2- .

![](images/4608436c24d269c45d8da07e048b0052dbbd9fe4e2119ac7266ec61bb05c374d.webp)  
Fig 1: Cutting Line Using Stripping Pliers   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Cut repair line with crimped-on contacts on both sides to the required length.

5. Insert contact on the repair line into the connector housing until the contact engages securely.   
6.Guide a suitable line seal -2- onto the repair line -1- if necessary.

1.6.1. The wide end of the line seal is guided on first.   
2.6.2. The diameter of the line seal must be smaller than the diameter of the line to ensure that the line seal fits securely.   
3. 6.3. A suitable tool can be used as an aid for guiding on the line seal.   
4.6.4. Guide the line seal on as far as required until the line seal is fitted full and securely in the sealing chamber.

![](images/2732d93e887dd80563f98ac326ea8503f4aabe1e7402a38c6512af71ece05a6e.webp)  
Fig 2: Installing Seals   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Strip the repair line -1- and the line that was cut using stripping pliers VAS 1978/3 -2- .

![](images/3018d7e83c0c19bf1ece7591964dddace2d110561ceb5d84f13f8390664c1304.webp)  
Fig 3: Cutting Repair Line Using Stripping Pliers   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

8. Insert stripped part of the repair line -1- and stripped part of the line to be repaired -3- into a suitable crimp connector -2- .

![](images/da757414506c722a2ed49b1cea9ecacd48330a7302607ab1a48044dabc0c523d.webp)  
Fig 4: Inserting Repair Lines Into Crimp Connectors   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

9. Crimp on both repair lines using crimping pliers VAS 1978/1-1 .

1.9.1. Fit crimping pliers insert -1- according to the color marking -3- on the crimp connector -2- into the crimping pliers VAS 1978/1-1

2. 9.2. Crimp on the crimp connector -2- using crimping pliers VAS 1978/1-1 .

![](images/c721f1ebff2ad779690010f3914c087df525a93f8222d4d482a8b8d31fb30075.webp)  
Fig 5: Installing Repair Line   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

10. Seal shrink-fit hose on the crimp connection -1- using hot-air blowerVAs 1978/14A -2- .

![](images/9cb36badaed49af135214dd75ae430e920e6ef57c889c5059664dd32b1990c81.webp)  
Fig 6: Installing Seal Shrink-Fit Hose On Crimp Connection

# VM 100119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING ENGINE (MACAN) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Remove ignition key.   
2. Disconnect the battery. → 270619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING BATTERY   
3. Remove engine cover.   
4. LooSen drive belt. → 137819 REMOVING AND INSTALLING DRIVE BELT   
5. Remove cowI panel cover. → 508719 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COWL PANEL COVER   
6. Remove fillr neck from windscreen-washer reservoir. → 926019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WINDSCREEN-WASHER RESERVOIR   
7. RemOve front strut. → 408619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT STRUT   
8. Remove front wheels. — 440519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WHEEL   
9. Remove front wheel housing liner. → 505619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT WHEEL HOUSING LINER   
10. Remove cover for front underbody. → 519219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COVER FOR FRONT UNDERBODY   
11. Drain Coolant. → 193817 DRAINING AND FILLING COOLANT   
12. Remove croSs panel. → 508 119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CROSS PANEL (DISASSEMBLING PLENUM PANEL)   
13. Remove catalytic converter. → 267319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CATALYTIC CONVERTER

# WM 100119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING ENGINE (MACAN) > REMOVING ENGINE

WARNING: Danger of objects or loads falling down

Risk of squashing or crushing

→ Secure components to prevent them from falling down.

WARNING: Hot fluid

•Danger of scalding

→ Let the fluid cool down.   
→ Wear personal protective gear.

WARNING: Highly inflammable or explosive materials

Danger of fire or explosion

→ Avoid contact with hot parts or sources of ignition.

→ Use suction to remove ignitable vapors.

→ Attach warning sign in a clearly visible position.

CAUTION: Hot components

Risk of burns

→ Let hot components cool down.

→ Wear personal protective gear.

NOTE: Aggressive fluids

•Risk of damage to components and surfaces

→ Do not spill luids.   
→ In the event of contact, wash the component or surface with water.

→ Replace components that are already damaged.

# Information

Close of open connections and lines using suitable stoppers or caps.

# Information

Place a cloth underneath to catch escaping fuel.

# Information

The pictures shown in this document may differ from the original.

1. Loosen screw-type clamps and pull off pressure hose.

Fig 1: Locating Charge-Air Cooler/Throttle Valve Pressure Hose

Fig 3: Identifying Air Cleaner Housing Cover

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

1.4.1. Press fastening bolts -1- down slightly and turn 90° in -direction of arrow- .

2.4.2. Pull out loosened fastening bolt -2- .

Fig 5: Loosening Air Guide

1.6.1. Disconnect vacuum line -2- and loosen screw-type clamp -3- .

2. 6.2. Lift air box for air cleaner up and remove it.

![](images/fcd7a172564e74953ee214ff690a074b5ac473b8e40081e151c2948a24a7d856.webp)  
Fig 6: Identifying Air-Cleaner And Vacuum Line

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Disconnect fuel lines at the front.

1.7.1. Press unlocking ring -1- and disconnect fuel supply line.

2. 7.2. Loosen clamp -2- and pull hose off the carbon canister.

![](images/72dc4abc739cf4fd79af6b7211d6f32f0db5efa330715a204a0ba306a221272e.webp)

8. Disconnect coolant line at the radiator.

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

9. Disconnect lines on the coolant reservoir -1- .

2.9.2. Lift up retaining clip -arrow- and pull of coolant line -3- .

Fig 9: Locating Coolant Reservoir Lines

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2.10.2. Unscrew screws -3- .

3.10.3. Secure air-conditioning compressor using tie-wraps on the longitudinal member for example.

![](images/cdaa77106c3a3614f76f588388369551f91719cbbf343f5adde2e8f2d1e64c6d.webp)  
Fig 10: Identifying Air-Conditioning Compressor

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

11. Unscrew fastening screws -1, 2 and 4- and remove cover -3- on the fuse box.

![](images/30e4020eac74f42f734d21b221f050c7afc016819a2b5fcebc3188b16619b982.webp)  
Fig 11: Removing E-Box Cover

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

12. Unscrew fastening nut -1- , disconnect ground line -2- and set it aside.

![](images/c4dded98f42a2dca23b98fa661574e9f285825f277f7e86499c42bfe35b6437a.webp)  
Fig 12: Identifying Engine Ground Line

Fig 13: Identifying Engine Cover B+ Line

![](images/62270a90f869fbaeb1e6170aa5784e3f8390f4d9f46902a8f37baab5fea91bb7.webp)  
Fig 14: Identifying Engine B+ Line And Nut

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

15. Release electric plug connections -A- in direction of arrow and remove DME control unit in -direction of arrow B- .

Fig 15: Removing DME Control Unit

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

16. Loosen the fuse box.

1. 16.1. Disconnect electric plug connections -2- and -4- .

2.16.2. Unscrew fastening nut -3- .

3. 16.3. Press locking lug -arrow- and remove the fuse box by pulling it upwards.

![](images/e5b550fc91fcaaca2dbd49a0026b9aca369d7a7d58e3ce06e659fe2233d7dfa9.webp)  
Fig 16: Removing Relay And Fuse Box

1.17.1. Pull off rubber seal on the firewall.

2. 17.2. Carefully unclip clips -arrow A- .

3. 17.3. Remove cable bushing -1- in -direction of arrow B- .

Fig 17: Removing Cable Bushing

1.20.1. Unscrew screws -2... 5- .

21. Open locking lug -1- with a screwdriver, open housing cover -2- on the right longitudinal member and remove it.

Fig 21: Identifying Housing Cover

3.22.3. Disconnect electric plug connection -5- and pull it out of the clip.

23. Press in locking lugs -1- , pull out ground line -2- in -direction of arrow - and set it aside.

![](images/532362a71cff296963acfc8d469893dba1deb7b4b6c3b474e56f7376481eedf0.webp)  
Fig 23: Pulling Ground Line

![](images/2429a97239de8685cd26c9f67c17e95f608b402be2b4ddb22fe7ffad80153724.webp)

26. Disconnect electric lines.

1. 26.1. Disconnect electric connectors for the engine mount and expose line. — 975219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WIRE HARNESS FOR ENGINE

27. Disconnect coolant line at the bottom of the radiator.

1. 27.1. Lift up retaining clip -2- and pull off the coolant hose.

![](images/f919c438c296b8260501be79c105984c667cfbad2ba07339736f520013a4aa70.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

37. Support transmission on the body using support bracket 10-222 A .

1. 37.1. Secure 10-222 A to the adapters 10-222 A/8 using wing screws.

2. 37.2. Fit 10-222 A using adapters 10-222 A/8 to the spring strut domes at the left and right.

3. 37.3. Join transmission and spindle using gearbox support 3147 .

![](images/ab35c07f747a0d4438351dd2dd2f70fe4783280bd422d1b3eede6ae8707f52c6.webp)

# WM 101031 CONVERTING CRANKCASE (DOWEL SLEEVES) (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CONVERTING DOWEL SLEEVES

As of a certain engine number, longer dowel sleeves are installed in the crankcase and cannot be fitted on the old transmission.

The long dowel sleeves must be replaced with short dowel sleeves when installing new engines on the old transmission.

![](images/1ebfd8a61c6b6a7fb03afbc532f437d70441e663af32126ea78caa6e60d28bee.webp)

1. Convert dowel sleeves -arrows- on the crankcase

# WM 101802 PRESSURE LOSS TEST (MACAN) > TEST EVALUATION

тhe toot docs nor onow any тeanmgraгтeoun on a now сhgmo (r.o. оne hat пasm рoonтan n).

A difference in pressure loss between the individual cylinders of approx. 5% is not significant.   
If the test shows an excessive loss of pressure (> 30%), a few drops of oil can be sprayed into the combustion chamber. Repeat the test. If the loss in pressure is now significantly less, the seal between the piston and cylinder is damaged.   
The air that is escaping causes hissing noises, which provide information about the component that is causing the damage.

# If the limit values are exceeded, the engine must be started and the test repeated.

![](images/3ed103ffb239e2f415593be3dd2b6b161b033235e340989b3ace2b91f5a117fc.webp)

# WM 101802 PRESSURE LOSS TEST (MACAN) > TESTING PRESSURE LOSS ON THE ENGINE

WARNING: Rotating components

•Danger of limbs being trapped or severed

→ Do not reach into the danger area.

# Information

The check for loss of pressure can be used to assessthe mechanical condition of a combustion engine. A pressure loss test is more meaningful than the compression pressure check. The percentage leakage quantity can be used to establish whether the leaks in the combustion chamber in question are so large that the combustion chamber must be repaired. The worn components (e.g. piston rings) can be identified by the compressed air that is escaping.

# Information

The piston must be exactly at the upper return point when checking pressure loss. Do not touch any components of the belt drive and do not put any tools on the crankshaft pulley while performing the check.

# Information

Read the work steps and tips in the operating instructions for the Bosch tester before performing the pressure loss test. The described Bosch tester is used as an example for allsuitable pressure loss testers. Details of calibration and use can be found in the relevant operating instructions.

1. Get the tester ready. Pressure loss tester Bosch EFAW 210 A WE 1066 2. Screw the test hose into the spark plug thread of cylinder 1 by hand (compression TDC) and tighten hand-tight.

![](images/0d67bd40cf6669e1c89473c777fac4049931c9d89984e4890f294675866841fb.webp)  
Fig 1: Adjusting Test Hose

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Connect the pressure loss tester to the compressed air system.

4. Adjust the scale. To do this, insert the test nozzle at the front into the device.

![](images/6b49acd06c70fe269cdffe7897e146cfe01e49578b358fcd7dc8f6061f0a82a2.webp)  
Fig 2: Adjusting Scale

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Turn the adjusting wheel until the scale pointer is at the "cal." marking or "23%". The pressure is then equal in the two test chambers of the tool.

![](images/55c4491d9ba735c3ce5736fa0d7db717819e2fe9d404ea64eb21068d4828abbb.webp)  
Fig 3: Adjusting Wheel   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. Remove test nozzle and check that the pointer falls back. Then connect the test hose. The value that is displayed should not be greater than 25%. If the loss in pressure is greater, it is safe to assume that the engine needs an overhaul.

![](images/6c592769d2f774b16e7f6cab4073d0bd1f4324bbb0cf068e5efbca2331253ef1.webp)  
Fig 4: Checking Pressure Loss

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Interrupt the compressed air supply and unscrew the test hose.   
8. Check the next cylinder by turning the crankshaft through another 180° and check the next cylinder in the firing order following the instructions provided.

Firing order: 1 - 3 - 4- 2

# Information

1. If the piston pin is stiff, heat the piston to arround 60 °C (140°F).

5. Drive out piston pin using drift Ww 222 A.

# WM 131020 REMOVING AND INSTALLING PISTONS (MACAN) > INSTALLING PISTONS

1. Fit piston pin using drift Vw 222 A.   
. Fit new circlips in the piston pin eye.   
3. Install piston rings offset by 120° using piston ring pliers Nr.58.   
4. Insert bearing shels into the connecting rod and connecting-rod bearing cap. Do not mix up worn bearing shells. Dimension -a- must be the same at the left and right.

# WM 137801 CHECKING DRIVE BELT (MACAN) > CHECKING DRIVE BELT

NOTE: Drive belt removed incorrectly

Risk of damage to drive belt

→ Only remove the drive belt when it is cold.   
→ Replace damaged drive belt.

NOTE: Drive belt breaks and becomes jammed

Risk of damage to components (trim panels, electric cables, etc.) •Sealing ring on crankshaft vibration balancer can start to leak •Vibration balancer can overheat and lose its strength

→ Following belt breakage, check adjacent components and the interior of the engine compartment for damage, and repair or replace damaged parts if necessary.

→ Find out why the belt broke. Check deflection rollers or crankshaft vibration balancer for prior damage.   
→ If the drive belt is jammed, replace vibration balancer.

WARNING: Rotating components

•Danger of limbs being trapped or severed

→ Disconnect power supply to the drive motor of components or to the battery.

# Information

If spark plugs must be changed in the course of maintenance operations, the drive belt should be checked when the spark plugs are removed. The engine can then be cranked easier.

# Information

The following table indicates damage which necessitates replacement.

![](images/6e3b6539f6ff7ddd673bdeae92890a0acb09c903177d28c5c6b23cd48f0bff10.webp)

![](images/1f97311f85a6a21cb44b491403f768c2d90b7cc1c8a717bfdf069887a46a1497.webp)

1. Using chalk, mark the drive belt in the area around the tensioning roller.

2. Turn engine at the vibration damper in rolling direction using a socket wrench until the chalk mark is at the same place again. While turning at the crankshaft, check the drive belt for signs of damage.

# WM 150505 CHECKING AND ADJUSTING CAMSHAFTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CHECKING CAMSHAFTS

NOTE: Timing not set correctly

Risk of engine damage • Rough running engine Loss of engine power

→ Do not use force when fiting the staking tool.

→ Make sure that the gap is equal on both sides.

→ When inserting the staking tools, do not use force to turn the camshafts against any resistance.

—→ The engine must be exactly at top dead center.

→ The opposite cylinder must be at ignition TDC.

1. Remove engine cover (design cover).

2. Remove front underbody cover. → 519219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COVER FOR FRONT UNDERBODY

3. Remove upper timing-case cover. → 153319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING TIMING-CASE COVER

4. Use counter-hold tool T10355 to turn the crankshaft in direction of rotation of the engine until the markings -arrows- are at the top.

Markings on timing chain

![](images/b0e8d86a00e2b0a4cbc42d406f5d384c2a119a0c2e4fc0167c9a5b096045d0ad.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying TDC Position Of Cylinder 1

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Remove spark plug for cylinder 1. → 287020 REMOVING AND INSTALLING SPARK PLUGS

6. Set TDC position of cylinder 1.

1. 6.1. Dial gauge adapter T10170 A must be screwed as far as it wil go into the spark plug thread.

2. 6.2. Dial gauge Nr.136 Pos.1 with dial gauge adapter T10170 A must be inserted as far as it will go and secured with a clamping nut -arrow- .

# Information

If the crankshaft was turned beyond the TDC position, turn the pulley another two turns in direction of rotation of the engine.

Do not turn engine against the direction of rotation of the engine.

# Information

Use a ratchet with socket-wrench insert a/f 24 or counter-hold tool T10355 to turn the pulley.

3.6.3. Turn the crankshaft slowly in direction of rotation of the engine until maximum

pointer deflection (reversing point of the pointer) is reached.

4. 6.4. Once maximum pointer deflection is reached, the piston is at top dead center. Fig 2: Identifying TDC Position Of Cylinder 1

![](images/1ea968bb53427d202418393c6a7eb5ece985173922891e9ea8e2e75bc79a280f.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Check markings.

1.7.1. The notch on the pulley and the marking on the lower timing-case cover must be aligned. -arrow

2.7.2. The markings -1- on the camshaft sprockets must be facing upwards.

![](images/ebb2e3f1a8e8f022859e762ff1597fdb97bde0ea273946b958addad9c2f2cc63.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Top Dead Center Markings   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

8. Measure the distance from the edge -1- to the marking -2- on the outlet camshaft sprocket.

# Information

An offset from one tooth indicates a deviation from the setpoint value of approx. 6 mm.   
If an offset is detected, the timing chain must be re-fitted.

Nominal value: 74.… 77 mm.

![](images/637ee730f82e74b727a90a4b7b463fadb7dd3d8247eae784a8ae137aa3ba51dd.webp)  
Fig 4: Measuring Outlet Camshaft Distance

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

9. Once the nominal value is reached, measure the distance between the marking on the outlet camshaft sprocket -3- and the marking on the intake camshaft sprocket -4- .

# Information

An offset from one tooth indicates a deviation from the setpoint value of approx. 6 mm.   
If an offset is detected, the timing chain must be re-fitted.

# Nominal value: 124... 127 mm.

![](images/207e27a50539677d36d176329a9b054de0edabb2718c62e940e83547753db6ad.webp)  
Fig 5: Measuring Sprockets Markings Distance

# WM 150516 SETTING TIMING FOR CAMSHAFTS (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Remove cylinder head cover. → 158219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CYLINDER HEAD COVER

2. The spark plugs can be removed so that it will be easier to turn the crankshaft. → 287020 REMOVING AND INSTALLING SPARK PLUGS

# WM 150516 SETTING TIMING FOR CAMSHAFTS (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > SETTING TIMING FOR CAMSHAFTS

NOTE: Incorrect handling of crankshafts

Risk of damage to the timing system

→ Never turn the crankshaft against the rolling direction or when the chain tensioner is removed.

— Proceed carefully with your work.

→ Only turn the engine at the crankshaft.

— After working on the camshaft, re-set the valve timing.

→ Observe general warning notes and working regulations.

NOTE: Timing not set correctly

Risk of engine damage • Rough running engine Loss of engine power

→ Do not use force when fitting the staking tool.   
→ Make sure that the gap is equal on both sides.   
→ When inserting the staking tools, do not use force to turn the camshafts against any resistance. → The engine must be exactly at top dead center.   
→ The opposite cylinder must be at ignition TDC.

# Information

The adjustment of the oil pump with balance shaft with respect to the crankshaft must be correct.   
Correct adjustment of the balance shaft with respect to the crankshaft is a prerequisite for the valve timing of the camshafts.   
If the engine has vibrations in the crank drive, also check that the balance shaft is set correctly. For details of how to adjust the balance shaft , → 172019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING OIL PUMP .

1. Turn the crankshaft at the vibration balancer so that the vibration balancer's staking bore -2- is located approx. 45° degrees in front of the lower staking point on the timing-case cover -1- .

![](images/b9d98814f4ac0b73ef2db156b22a266950140b5d58d1748e6314c79e005a78f9.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Staking Bore Angle

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Loosen central screws on the four camshaft controllers.

3. Remove chain tensioner. → 153619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CHAIN TENSIONER

4. Auxiliary chain tensioner 9683/1 must be screwed in hand-tight. Connect 1 bar of compressed air and slowly increase to 5.0 up to 5.5 bar (prevents the assembly chain tensioner from "crashing" against the timing chain).

5. Turn the camshafts at the hexagon until the flat surfaces are pointing upwards.

Fig 2: Turning Hexagon Camshaft

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. Staking tool for valve timing 9861 must be fitted on the camshafts.

1.6.1. Tighten screws to 20 Nm (15 ftlb.) so that the camshafts are moved over the flat surfaces -arrows- into the exact position.

4 L

7. Secure the crankshaft.

1.7.1. Locating pins 9595/1 must be inserted into the staking bore on the vibration balancer -2- .   
2.7.2. Turn the crankshaft at the vibration balancer (approx. 45°) -3- so that the staking pin in the vibration balancer slips into the lower staking point on the timing-case cover -1- .   
3.7.3. At the same time, exert gentle pressure on the staking pin while turning.

![](images/2823f06a191a2a491c160dddbd11513480aaff6f71a5f5fd02ae476bc89820c6.webp)  
Fig 4: Identifying Vibration Balancer Bore

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# 8. If you accidentally turn the vibration balancer too far, do not try to turn it back again!

1. 8.1. The staking tools must be removed and the camshafts must be turned in such a way that there is only the slightest pressure on the valve springs.

2.8.2. Turn the crankshaft once and start the setting procedure again.

9. Camshafts and crankshaft are fixed correctly.

1. 9.1. Screwed-in assembly chain tensioner with approx. 5.0 to 5.5 bar pressure.

2.9.2. Two fixed staking tools on the camshafts.

3.9.3. Staking pin secures crankshaft in TDC of cylinder 1.

10. Tighten central screws on the four camshafts as instructed. To do this, counter at the hexagon on the camshaft controllers and observe the specified sequence!

1.10.1. Tightening torque: Initial tightening 30 Nm (22 ftlb.) Final tightening +40°

2. 10.2. Tightening sequence:

![](images/39ea4d8ec58fa5c10c9de1666be28c9ddb6ac852a8c3fb4fde902ad48359fe94.webp)

![](images/7ab93eae3e14da2e38253942f807180738d2bb019693a9645a535d2cd0324461.webp)

11. Remove tools.

12. Install chain tensioner.

13. Check by turning the engine twice.

# WM 153319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CHAIN HOUSING COVER (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > INSTALLING CHAIN HOUSING COVER > INSTALLING UPPER CHAIN HOUSING COVER

1. Remove sealant residue on the bearing saddle.

. Clean sealing faces to remove any oil and grease.

3. Cut off the nozze on the tube at the front marking. (The nozzle diameter is approx. 1.5 mm).

# Information

The chain housing cover must be installed within 5 minutes of applying the sealant.

4. Apply beads of sealant to the clean sealing rings -arrows- . Sealant bead thickness: 2 mm.

![](images/7ebc51a64eef4b9d4a67d8c64979579f5b76e8e793eb5e7d8d41e4767086d7bc.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Sealant Area   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Install chain housing cover.

1.5.1. Fit chain housing cover with new O-rings.

2.5.2. Fit and tighten fastening screws -1.….6- . Tightening torque 9 Nm (6.5 ftlb.) Observe tightening sequence -1…6- .

![](images/9cb6ce73ccfc142b5aec7d311664c3b2416dcc9f3ff7518c49b843079514d802.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Upper Chain Housing Cover Fastening Screws   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. Secure the coolant line.

1.6.1. Install guide tube for oil dipstick -4- with a new seal.

2.6.2. Fit and tighten fastening screw -1- . Tightening torque 9 Nm (6.5 ftlb.)

![](images/ceb7c402c6a15256f21b6ea0f80c055c986b7456ea407b75ab23006d09bbc487.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Coolant Hose And Guide Tube For Oil Dipstick   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Install actuators for camshaft.

1. 7.1. Position actuators for camshaft -2 and 4- .

2.7.2. Fit and tighten new fastening screws -arrows- . Step 1: Initial tightening 4 Nm (3 ftlb.) Step 2: Final tightening +45°

3.7.3. Connect electric plug connections -1 and 3- .

![](images/86fe7364b3494b09fd6381c3aa87b03ed1096bd6cd88ee16368ba3f5a90649f5.webp)  
Fig 4: Identifying Electric Plug Connections For Camshaft Actuators

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# WM 153319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CHAIN HOUSING COVER (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > INSTALLING CHAIN HOUSING COVER > INSTALLING LOWER CHAIN HOUSING COVER

The lower chain housing cover must be replaced.

1. Remove sealant residue on the cylinder block using a flat scraper.   
2. Clean sealing faces to remove any oil and grease.   
3. Check that dowel pins for centering -arrows- are available.

![](images/ce18653b6b0778de07eeb94dd9afc45d98b0e38a05645c2cf7d216a171e533e6.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Centering Chain Housing Cover Dowel Pins

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Cut off the nozzle on the sealant tube at the front marking. (The nozzle diameter is approx. 3 mm).

# Information

The chain housing cover must be installed within 5 minutes of applying the sealant.

![](images/2d45be0b21c10b1ce00901c3e4cc44c3c1457cf9a95188d4c77e4e37bf458e4e.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Sealant Applying Area   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. Install new chain housing cover.

1.6.1. Position chain housing cover and fit new fastening screws -1…15- .

2.6.2. Tighten fastening screws in the sequence -1…15- . Step 1: Initial tightening 8 Nm (6 ftlb.)

# Step 2: Final tightening +45°

![](images/ae58f584d323cde39c7f0ba843ff9064aca3dc6afb75f17b9f524d4d9f2aa06f.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Lower Chain Housing Cover   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Secure the coolant line.

1. 7.1. Install guide tube for oil dipstick -4- with a new seal.

2. 7.2. Fit and tighten fastening screw -1- . Tightening torque 9 Nm (6.5 ftlb.)

![](images/73a2afb64f8c10d6dce7f487d979aadb629adb7d9b4040f3cfae9ed515eb12e2.webp)  
Fig 4: Identifying Coolant Hose And Guide Tube For Oil Dipstick

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

8. Unscrew fastening screw for pulley and remove pressure piece T10368. → Pressure piece -T10368-

![](images/af75cb153631648a9daf35e5fd030fa8317f82fdc082c581611ccaed9debc0a6.webp)  
Fig 5: Identifying Pressure Piece - T10368

# WM 153519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING TIMING CHAIN (MACAN) > INSTALLING TIMING CHAIN

1. 1.1. The markings -arrows- for TDC position of the crankshaft must be aligned.

2. 1.2. Apply marking on the cylinder block -1- using a water-resistant marker.

. Position guide rail and fit and tighten guide pins -arrows- .

12. Installtiming chain. The colored chain links must be positioned at the markings on the sprockets. → Installing timing chain

1. 12.1. Position timing chain on the intake camshaft.

WM 153719 REMOVING AND INSTALLING SOLENOID/HYDRAULIC VALVE(ACTUATORS) FOR CAMSHAFT CONTROLLER (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) >REMOVING SOLENOID/HYDRAULIC VALVE (ACTUATORS) FOR CAMSHAFTCONTROLLER > REMOVING SOLENOID/HYDRAULIC VALVE FOR CAMSHAFTCONTROLLER

3. Pull hydraulic valve -6- forward and remove it.

# WM 155519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HYDRAULIC VALVE FOR VALVE LIFT SWITCHOVER (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > PRELIMINARY WORK

Guided Fault Finding using the PIWIS Tester as well as the DME short test "Valve lift" must be performed before replacing the hydraulic valve. This is essential in order to avoid replacing the hydraulic valve unnecessarily.

The hydraulic valves are on the rear side of the cylinder heads facing the plenum panel.

1. Remove croSs panel. → 508119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CROSS PANEL (DISASSEMBLING PLENUM PANEL) .

2. Cylinder bank 1 to 3: Remove Vacuum pump — 477619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING VACUUM PUMP .

3. Cylinder bank 4 to 6: Disconnect coolant pipe.

1. 3.1. Loosen coolant pipe holder.

# WM 155519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HYDRAULIC VALVE FOR VALVE LIFT SWITCHOVER (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVAL > REMOVING HYDRAULIC VALVE FOR VALVE LIFT SWITCHOVER

1. Disconnect electric plug connection on the hydraulic valve -3- .

. Loosen fastening screws -4- .

3. Pull hydraulic valve -3- out of the cylinder head.

1. 3.1. Make sure that the sealing ring is also removed.

WM 156355 REPLACING VALVE-STEM SEALS (MACAN) > PRELIMINARY WORK

# Information

The new valve stem seals have a plastic sleeve -3- .

# Information

Mark allocation of rocker arms and hydraulic compensating elements for re-installation.   
Rocker arms must be set aside in such a way that they cannot be mixed up.

Remove rocker arms together with the hydraulic compensating elements and set them down on a clean surface. 1. Remove spark plugs. → 287020 REMOVING AND INSTALLING SPARK PLUGS 2. Remove camshafts. → 150520 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CAMSHAFTS 3. Take hydraulic tappets and rocker arms out of the cylinder head.

# WM 156355 REPLACING VALVE-STEM SEALS (MACAN) > REMOVING VALVE-STEM SEALS

Set pistons of the respective cylinder to bottom dead center .

1. Screw guide plate -VAS 5161/19B- with the knurled screws -VAS 5161/12- on the cylinder head as shown.

![](images/8463b3cc6726eb493bcc0f08f36b9ae0a5c9ef1e1cab7413fbfe713a432979cb.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Guide Plate 1

2. Screw adapter -T40012- into the spark plug thread.

3. Connect compressed air of at least 6 bar overpressure.

4. Loosen any tight valve collets using the impact mandrel -vAs 5161/3- and a plastic hammer. Fig 2: Identifying Adapter

![](images/d14b07844da3f41b8a516b21478b21372511066df8dec8d7a351972f9a74ab35.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# For intake side

5. Screw retainer -VAS 5161/6- with attachment fork -VAS 5161/5- into the center thread of the guide plate -VAS 5161/19B- .

6. Fit assembly cartridge -VAS 5161/8- into the guide plate -VAS 5161/19B- .

7. Engage pressure fork -VAS 5161/2- on the retainer -VAS 5161/6- .

![](images/220fe8d5972f7f20dd85a0c367b19b09c586a2f8e5b4fa88219b351f694d3498.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Retainers

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# For outlet side

8. Screw retainer -VAS 5161/6- with attachment fork -VAS 5161/5- into the outer thread of the guide plate -VAS 5161/19B- .   
9. Press assembly cartridge -VAs 5161/8- down and turn the knurled screw for the assembly cartridge -VAs 5161/8- to the right at the same time until the tips engage in the valve collets.   
10. Move knurled screw back and forth slightly to press the valve collets apart and engage them in the assembly cartridge.   
11. Release pressure fork -VAS 5161/2- .   
12. Remove assembly cartridge -VAS 5161/8- .

![](images/abfc18a9acf48c97b9c5c4b6b0e3de65d53c3a5a97ef09264854c19869873347.webp)  
Fig 4: Identifying Assembly Cartridge

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

13. Pull off valve stem seals using valve-stem seal puller -3364- .

![](images/f43647b00ac244b00eae048ce85d65ef88d987016965a52583fb3eec20550f05.webp)  
Fig 5: Identifying Puller   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

14. If you cannot use the valve-stem seal puller -3364- due to lack of space, tap out the roll pin -arrow-  using a mandrel and remove the puller attachment.

![](images/f1f97456b12fc0814faa143e772483225a670b1d78b8af0afd3bc40b67dc0f0e.webp)  
Fig 6: Identifying Puller   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

15. Fit lower part of valve-stem seal puller -3364- on the valve stem seal.

16. Fit mandrel -1- into the bore in the lower part of puller.

17. Fit assembly lever on the puller and pull out the valve stem seal. -arrow

![](images/26b8377bb2151c19fee923fcb08681b0a99547ad15c74510195e4e11489c8ba3.webp)  
Fig 7: Pulling Valve Stem Seal

# WM 156355 REPLACING VALVE-STEM SEALS (MACAN) > INSTALLING VALVE STEM SEALS

Risk of damage when installing valve stem seals.

Place plastic sleeve -A- , included with the new valve stem seals -B- , onto the valve stem.

Lightly oil sealing lip of valve stem seal.   
Slide the valve stem seal -B- onto the plastic sleeve -A .

1. Carefully press valve stem seal onto the valve guide using valve-stem seal fiting tool -3365- .

2. Remove plastic sleeve.

3. Insert valve spring and valve-spring plate.

4. Set up removal and installation device -VAS 5161- .

Intake side

Fig 2: Identifying Retainer

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

Fig 3: Identifying Assembly Cartridge

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. If the valve collets were removed from the assembly cartridge -VAs 5161/8- , they must first be inserted into the insertion device -VAS 5161/18- .   
6. Press assembly cartridge -VAS 5161/8- onto the insertion device -VAS 5161/18- from above and pick up the valve collets.

![](images/146b83acc333af6dff863408a7f503a206c07a43b210234a226b9d61b3020bbd.webp)  
Fig 4: Identifying Insertion Device

![](images/0b32b1d004fbe644f43232d6537d4274916e9c3b10641fad03b85888f439ae09.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Press assembly cartridge -VAS 5161/8- down using the pressure fork -VAs 5161/2- and turn knurled screw on the assembly cartridge back and forth and pull upwards at the same time. . Reduce pressure on the pressure fork -VAs 5161/2- while pulling on the knurled screw. 9. Remove removal and installation device -VAs 5161- .

If the hydraulic tappets are to be re-used, they must be marked according to installation position using a water-resistant felt-tip pen and set aside in such a way that they cannot be mixed up!

# WM 156120 REMOVING AND INSTALLING VALVES (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING VALVES

Secure the cylinder head on a level surface, which allows easy access to the valves from underneath.

No valves should be hidden by the surface under the cylinder head.

The cylinder head fastening must not tip over when tools are used.

1. The spark plugs must be removed and the valve lock screwed in before the valves are removed → Screwing in tool . The valve lock prevents the valves from being opened while being pressed down. Alternatively, a rubber plate placed underneath helps if the cylinder head surface is smooth -2- .

![](images/2f9dce0e538ce45658833366c1eed5e42857ce5b40f3d39ca55893dcf1778265.webp)

![](images/aa6c22c6c695db753f0d67023a55ea79a33033070dbfafd34c104c6a3084475b.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Fit the tool on the cylinder head and adjust it.

1.2.1. Screw holder -1- with the appropriate thread into its matching thread on the cylinder head. The hook piece -2- is pre-fitted in the holder.

![](images/76dcbfd49e274e8e4eb8fbdc52fdf0b7a4d9ed7fb25e4feabcfcaf2f029986de.webp)  
Fig 3: Fitting Tool On Cylinder Head

Fig 4: Inserting Plastic Guide

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

![](images/427388b60ec127cfa395726f8cb2c9919acd511767040ec4eb646441aa03bcbb.webp)  
Fig 5: Inserting Cartridge Assembly

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. 2.4. Hook the lever (assembly bar) -1- into the hook and place correctly onto the assembly cartridge. Make sure that the tool and equipment can be used without tilting.

![](images/a12c1075281fa5788a2b1bf0b4085dc95fb4ecc65bbcf62efad1249905a1f29b.webp)  
Fig 6: Installing Assembly Bar

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# 3. Remove valve keys.

1. 3.1. Press assembly cartridge with the lever (assembly bar) against the force of the valve spring and keep it pressed → Tool fitted correctly . The knurled screw of the assembly cartridge pushes forward -1- .

![](images/335d1a2cb4ef9badab3808a9c7c643b97107f82223e87efc45054b7e13b1c265.webp)

# Information

The mechanic must practise for use of the assembly cartridge to be effective. Some repetitions must be made to ensure that the valve keys are correctly held in place.

2. 3.2. Turn the knurled screw back and forth -1- until the valve keys snap into place in the assembly cartridge -2- and are held there. The knurled screw retracts.

![](images/538306cb9e0872e0f7148dc5b104b53eb24b7cfb345ca57ef9917f98a35cb8d1.webp)

# WM 156120 REMOVING AND INSTALLING VALVES (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > INSTALLING VALVES

NOTE: Valve grinding paste not removed

Risk of damage to sealing face on intake valve

→ Remove al valve grinding paste fully after grinding.

# Information

•The valves cannot be touched up afterwards.   
The valves can be grinded using commercially available valve grinding paste. 1. Apply a small amount of valve grinding paste to the valve seat.

2. Oil the valve stem of a new valve and insert it into the valve guide from the combustion chamber. Push the valve in until it is seated securely in the valve seat of the cylinder head.

3. Grind the valve with a commercially available valve grinder (with rubber suction head) using rotating movements. To do this, hold the valve grinder between the palms of both hands and press against the valve seat with rotating movements → Grinding valve seat .

![](images/34c4f5a097d3e037aff413beea76867e773dbf7cf76e9ab8a90c1384f8156ce3.webp)  
Fig 1: Turning Valve Seat

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Carry out the grinding operation for each valve that is replaced. Check for leaks using some fuel and installed spark plugs. The fuel must not escape through the valve seat. Carefully

remove valve grinding paste.

. Fit valve lock. → Locking valves

![](images/c912015c161b298e3e1106badc88365f2a470c4375c0a8c6d5bce106351d3772.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Valves

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. Replace valve stem seals. For details, → 156355 REPLACING VALVE-STEM SEALS

7. Fit valve springs, concave washers and valve keys. To do this, place valve springs (there are two in the outlet valve in the turbo engine) on the bottom concave washer. Place top concave washer in position.

# Information

The mechanic must practise for use of the assembly cartridge to be effective. Some repetitions must be made to ensure that the valve keys are correctly held in place.

. Insert valve keys into the assembly cartridge.

1.8.1. Press the spring washer of the assembly fixture downwards -1- and insert the valve keys -2- with the narrow end pointing downwards.

![](images/e7454df1029c03c0b91191a2199f83341cb1cfed2a9b23fcbf49771b9e5d739b.webp)  
Fig 3: Installing Valve Keys In Assembly Fixture   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. 8.2. Ensure that the valve keys fit symmetrically and are inserted as far as they will go in the tool. The spring washer automatically locks the valve keys in place.

3. 8.3. Place the assembly cartridge -2- onto the center of the assembly fixture. Observe installation position of the valve keys -1- .

![](images/276c832f6949b3fba0d7517deb377f0313ed9a8a873c0014a1e927bdceb3934a.webp)  
Fig 4: Identifying Assembly Cartridge   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. 8.4. Press the assembly cartridge against the spring force onto the assembly fixture. The knurled screw moves forward. When doing so, turn the knurled screw back and forth until the valve keys snap into place. Repeat as required. → Assembly cartridge with valve keysFig 5

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

9. Place the valve key assembly cartridge onto the cylinder head (same as removal of valve) and position it on the top concave washer.   
10.Press assembly cartridge with the lever (assembly bar) against the force of the valve spring and keep it pressed. The knurled screw moves forward. When doing so, turn the knurled screw back and forth until the valve keys snap into place → Installing valve keysFig 7. Repeat as required.

# WM 157019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CYLINDER HEAD (MACAN) > INSTALLING CYLINDER HEAD

NOTE: Risk of damage if components are not cleaned and handled correctly when ng the cylinder head.

Risk of damage to sealing faces.   
Risk of damage to the crankcase.   
Risk of leaks at the cylinder-head gasket.   
Risk of damage to open valves.   
Risk of damage to valves and piston crowns after working on the valve drive.

→ Carefully remove any residual sealant from the cylinder head and crankcase. Make sure there are no long scores or scratches.

→ Carefully remove lubricating gel and sanding residues.

→ There must be no oil or coolant in the blind holes for the cylinder-head fastening screws in the crankcase.

To prevent damage to the silicone layer and seam area of the cylinder-head gasket, do not remove the new cylinder head-gasket from its packaging until just before installation and handle with extreme care.

→ If you are using a replacement head, do not remove the plastic socket used to protect the open valves until just before you install the cylinder head.

→ To prevent valve problems when starting the engine, careful turn the engine with your hand for at least two turns.

# Information

If you are installing a replacement cylinder head, the contact surfaces between the hydraulic compensating elements, rocker arms and running surfaces of cams must be oiled before installing the cylinder head cover.   
If you are replacing the cylinder head or cylinder-head gasket, change the coolant and engine oil.   
Replace screws that are tightened to an additional torque angle.   
Replace selflocking nuts as well as sealing rings, seals and O-rings.   
Note the different sealants for sealing surfaces and cylinder head screws .   
Secure all hose connections with standard hose clamps . 1. Fit cylinder head.   
1. 1.1. Fit new cylinder-head gasket. Check installation position of cylinder-head gasket .   
2. 1.2. Check centering pins -arrows- in the cylinder block.   
3.1.3. Fit cylinder head.

# WM 158219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CYLINDER HEAD COVER (MACAN) > INSTALL THE CYLINDER HEAD COVER

WARNING: Preloaded or pressurized components

Risk of eye injuries Risk of bruising

→ Wear personal protective gear.   
→ Secure components to prevent them from falling off suddenly.

NOTE: Dirt and contamination

Risk of damage to units or components

→ Protect components from dirt and contamination.

→ Clean or replace dirty components.

# Information

Sealing faces must be free of oil and grease.   
The rocker arms must rest properly on the valve stem ends.   
The crankshaft must not be at the TDC position.

If the crankshaft has been turned, the piston of the 1st cylinder must be set to the top dead center and the crankshaft must be turned back again slightly.

1. Remove any sealant residue on the cylinder block using a flat scraper.   
2. Remove any sealant residue from the groove on the cylinder head cover and from the sealing   
faces.   
3. Oil the running surfaces of the camshafts.   
4. When replacing the camshafts, transfer the markings -arrow- onto the new camshafts.

NM 170101 CHECKING ENGINE-OIL LEVEL (MACAN) > CHECKING ENGINE OIL

The vehicle must be horizontal.

The engine must be at operating temperature.

Always check that there is enough engine oil in the engine.

NOTE: Incorrect oil level

Risk of damage to engine or catalytic converter

→ Check the oil level regularly.

→ The oil level must not fall below the Minimum marking or rise above the Maximum marking.

→ Only use engine oil approved by Porsche.

# Information

The engine-oil level can be checked on the instrument cluster display or using PlWis Tester 2 9818 .

1. For details of checking the oil level using the instrument cluster, see Driver's Manual.

2. To check the engine-oil level using PIWis Tester II 9818 , select [DME], [Maintenance/repairs], [Oil filling]. Follow the instructions for oil fll measurement on the Tester. If the engine oil has not yet reached measuring temperature, it can be heated to operating temperature by leaving the vehicle running while stationary or test-driving the vehicle. Check the engine-oil level after the test drive using the Tester. The Tester shows the oil level as a percentage and recommends a top-up quantity in liters.

# WM 170117 DRAINING AND FILLING ENGINE OIL (MACAN) > PRELIMINARY WORK > DRAINING ENGINE OIL

When changing engine oil, drain the oil when it is hot because hot oil is more fluid than cold oil and all dirt particles and suspended matter can be cleaned out. Position the collecting container as close as possible to the drain outlet of the oil pan.

WARNING: Hot fluid

•Danger of scalding

→ Let the fluid cool down.

→ Wear personal protective gear.

1. Drain oil.

1.1.1. Position collection container under the stopper.

2. 1.2. Unscrew stopper and drain oil.

2. Insert stopper with a new O-ring and turn it as far as it will go. Coat new O-ring with engine oil.

1.2.1. Stopper engages at the lock.

# WM 170301 CHECKING OIL PRESSURE (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > PRELIMINARY WORK

If vehicles have fault entries relating to oil pressure, oil pump activation, oil pressure monitoring, etc. in the DME control unit (and a warning light comes "on" on the instrument cluster), proceed as follows:

Check the oil level.   
•Delete related faults.

Do not replace components, such as the oil pump, oil pressure sensor or oil pressure control valve if you suspect that they are faulty.

If the vehicle has not been driven for a long time (months), the control mechanism in the oil pump can become stiff ("stick").

Very short trips and a lot of loading/maneuvering can cause the oil to become very diluted => Oil pressure very low. For example, 20 cold starts in quick succession can reduce the viscosity of the engine oil by 30%.

Change the engine oil. Test-drive the vehicle.   
If error messages/warnings are displayed again, proceed in accordance with the instructions under Guided Fault Finding in the PIWiS Tester.

# Information

The oil pressure can be displayed and checked for any engine speeds using the PIWis Tester.   
The pressure readings can be shown graphicall in the data logger.   
If an oil-pressure gauge needs to be connected for further tests, proceed according to the instructions starting from "Preliminary Work".   
For details of measured values, see below. 1. Remove cover for front underbody. → 519219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COVER FOR FRONT UNDERBODY

WARNING: Toxic substances

• Danger of poisoning or suffocation

Danger of burns to the eyes and skin

→ Ventilate the work area well

→ Never ingest or inhale.

→ Read specific information on the Hazard Sheet.

→ Do not smoke, eat or drink in the work area.

• Danger of scalding

→ Let the fluid cool down.   
→ Wear personal protective gear.

WARNING: Highly inflammable or explosive materials

Danger of fire or explosion

→ Avoid contact with hot parts or sources of ignition.   
→ Use suction to remove ignitable vapors.   
→ Attach warning sign in a clearly visible position.

# The oil pressure may be too low for a number of reasons:

Oil is diluted (e.g. fuel gets into the oil due to too many cold starts without warming up the engine afterwards).   
Oil pump is faulty.   
•Too much bearing clearance (e.g. crankshaft bearing).   
• Oil level is too low.   
Oil pressure regulating valve is faulty.   
Oil pressure sensor is faulty.   
Incorrect oil has been used. Use only oil that has been approved by Porsche for the measurement.

# The oil pressure may be too high for a number of reasons:

•Oil has thickened or is very cold after a cold start and high engine speeds.   
Oil pump is faulty.   
Mechanical oil pump pressure relief valve is faulty (oil pump needs to be replaced).   
• Oil pressure regulating valve is faulty.   
Cable plug of oil pressure regulating valve has fallen off or open circuit between it and the control unit (oil pressure may be up to 11 bar, engine loses approximately 10 kW of engine power) • Oil pressure sensor is faulty.   
Incorrect oil has been used. Use only oil that has been approved by Porsche for the

2.4.2. Make sure that the oil-pressure gauge and hose are not touching any rotating components.

5. Complete the engine for taking measurements.

6. Check that there are no rotating components touching the measuring hose and that the pressure gauge is easy to read when positioned.

7. Connect the PIWIS Tester and battery charger.

1. Use the PIWiS Tester to display the actual values for oil pressure, engine temperature and engine speed in DME. The oil pressure displayed in the PIWIS Tester is always higher than that on the pressure gauge by the value of the ambient pressure (depending on the altitude, e.g. 1, 000 hPa).

2. The pressure display on the oil-pressure gauge must be the same as the value on the PIWIS Tester once adjusted by the ambient pressure value.

3. The pressure display on the oil-pressure gauge is much slower than that on the PIWIS Tester. The measured value on the PIWis Tester fluctuates rapidly. The trend between

the two measuring instruments is significant.

4. The measured oil pressure remains virtually constant over different rev ranges. The measurement using the oil-pressure gauge merely confirms that the oil pressure sensor's display is correct. 5. The pressure readings can be shown graphically in the data logger.

8Start the engine and leave it running until t reaches the measurement temperature. → Engine temperature: 90°C

Measured values (examples)

1. For a cold start (e.g. 24 °C), pressure immediately jumps to 8 bar briefly (oil-pressure gauge).   
2. Following a cold start, oil pressure drops briefly to 3 bar (oil-pressure gauge) - 4, 000 hPa (PIWIS Tester).   
3. During warm-up phase at idle speed, pressure drops from 3 bar to 1.8 bar (oil-pressure gauge) - 4, 000 hPa drops to 2, 800 hPa (PIWiS Tester).   
4. At engine temperature of 90 C at idle speed, pressure is 1.5 to 1.6 bar (oil-pressure gauge) - 2, 600 hPa (PIWIS Tester).   
5. At engine temperature of 90 °C at 1, 000 RPM, pressure is 2.8 bar (oil-pressure gauge) - 3, 800 hPa (PIWIS Tester).   
6. At engine temperature of 90 °C at between 2, 000 RPM and 4, 000 RPM, the oil pressure is almost constant at 3.0 bar (oil-pressure gauge) - 4, 000 hPa (PIWIS Tester). The value can fluctuate by 0.1 bar (100 hPa).

# WM 170419 REMOVING AND INSTALLING OIL-PRESSURE SENDER (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > PRELIMINARY WORK

If vehicles have fault entries relating to oil pressure, oil pump activation, oil pressure monitoring, etc. in the DME control unit (and a warning light comes "on" on the instrument cluster), proceed as follows:

Check the oil level.   
• Delete related faults.

Do not replace components, such as the oil pump, oil pressure sensor or oil pressure control valve if you suspect that they are faulty.

If the vehicle has not been driven for a long time (months), the control mechanism in the oil pump can become stiff ("stick").

Very short trips and a lot of loading/maneuvering can cause the oil to become very diluted => Oil pressure very low. For example, 20 cold starts in quick succession can reduce the viscosity of the engine oil by 30%.

Change the engine oil. Test-drive the vehicle.   
If error messages/warnings are displayed again, proceed in accordance with the instructions under Guided Fault Finding in the PIWIS Tester.

1. Remove cover for front underbody. → 519219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COVER FOR FRONT UNDERBODY

2. Remove lower pedestrian protection. → 697019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING PEDESTRIAN PROTECTION

# WM 170419 REMOVING AND INSTALLING OIL-PRESSURE SENDER (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING OIL-PRESSURE SENDER

WARNING: Hot fluid

Danger of scalding

→ Let the fluid cool down.

→ Wear personal protective gear.

WARNING: Highly inflammable or explosive materials

Danger of fire or explosion

— Avoid contact with hot parts or sources of ignition.

→ Use suction to remove ignitable vapors.

→ Attach warning sign in a clearly visible position.

# Information

Oil pressure may be too low for a number of reasons: Oil is diluted.

Oil pump is faulty.   
Bearing clearance is too large (e.g. crankshaft bearing)   
•Oil level is too low.   
• Oil pressure regulating valve is faulty.   
Incorrect oil has been used. Only use oil that has been approved by Porsche for the measurement.

# Information

When the oil-pressure sender is unscrewed, approx. 0.3 liters of engine oil will escape.

Collect emerging oil and dispose of it in accordance with the applicable national laws.

Engine cold.

•Vehicle horizontal.

1. Check coolant level at the reservoir.

1. 1.1. The ideal level must be between the -MAX- marking -1- and -MIN- marking -2- .

2. 1.2. If the level is under -MIN-, the level must be corrected.

3. 1.3. If the level is above -MAX-, some coolant must be extracted.

1. Check antifreeze content.

1. 1.1. Check antifreeze content using antifreeze tester -1- .

2.1.2. If it is below -35 °C, correct the antifreeze content by increasing the proportion

of pure coolant accordingly.

![](images/fb77036a5acf4db422a96f7bc6ba078acd1fdf0368196f6f28fe040ce2cc5659.webp)

![](images/7907aae3ac64988d4c8a8adad78455868ca78f3d886ba80fbbc625e25907186f.webp)

# WM 190101 CHECKING THE COOLING SYSTEM (MACAN) > CHECKING ENGINE COOLANT LEVEL > CHECKING THE COOLING SYSTEM FOR LEAKS

1. Check the engine coolant level. Top up to the maximum fill level if necessary. → CHECKING ENGINE COOLANT LEVEL .

2. Screw adapter K65 onto the coolant expansion tank. Then apply a test pressure of approx. 1.5 bar using the cooling system test device and check the hose connections, connection pieces, cooling system components for leaks. The pressure must not drop. There must be no drops of coolant.

# WM 190101 CHECKING THE COOLING SYSTEM (MACAN) > CHECKING ENGINE COOLANT LEVEL > CHECKING COOLING SYSTEM FOR DIRT

1. Check radiator for external dirt. The radiators should not be excessively dirty. They can be cleaned using a vacuum cleaner with a brush attachment if necessary.

2. Check charge air coolers for external dirt. The charge air coolers should not be excessively dirty. They can be cleaned using a vacuum cleaner with a brush attachment if necessary.

3. Check air guides to the radiators for external dirt and collected leaves. They can be cleaned using a vacuum cleaner with a brush attachment if necessary.

# WM 193817 DRAINING AND FILLING COOLANT (MACAN) > INFORMATION > COOLANT MIXTURE RATIO

![](images/98487f4afe2dc6d1ffed353bcfd8c517df37e69785f5e57916fa042c957429c3.webp)

# WM 193817 DRAINING AND FILLING COOLANT (MACAN) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Switch off gnition.   
2. Remove upper engine cover.   
3. Remove cover for front underbody. → 519219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COVER FOR FRONT UNDERBODY

Remove cowl panel cover. → 508719 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COWL PANEL COVER

WM 193817 DRAINING AND FILLING COOLANT (MACAN) > DRAINING COOLANT

WARNING: Hot fluid

Danger of scalding → Avoid contact with hot fluid.

→ Wear personal protective gear.

NOTE: Cooling circuit not filled correctly

Risk of damage to vehicle components — Do not start the engine after relieving the system pressure.

→ Fill he cooling system correctly and bleed it before starting the engine.

# Information

Cooling systems with thermal management (controlled thermostats or coolant valves for controlling engine temperature) must be vacuum-filled.   
The thermostat must not be activated or electric current must not be applied to the thermostat since this can cause irreparable damage to the thermoelectric couple.   
Filling with a watering can only does not always guarantee a complete fil (trapped air - overheating).   
Clamps on cooling system components should be examined carefully following refiling (check the coolant level while cold and top up several times as required).   
Clamps on cooling system components must also be vacuum-filed if significant amounts of coolant are drained. Drain at least two liters of coolant for vacuum-filling because otherwise the correct vacuum cannot be built up.

# Information

Note special features in the corresponding information for vehicles with auxiliary heater.

1. Slowly open the cap on the reservoir → Reservoir .

![](images/4f643bb9f5295559cc7e757247dd6e465a1b18365b805002e03cfc39f8d0668a.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Reservoir

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Place drip pan under the radiator.

3. Open drain plug -1- on the adapter and drain coolant.

![](images/9914b90190fcfd1fbd296db98cfe7de4202784a37a51505856e97e2c90c345c1.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Coolant Drain Plug

# WM 193817 DRAINING AND FILLING COOLANT (MACAN) > FILLING COOLANT

The amount of coolant available must be approx. 2 liters more than the amount to be filed in.

Because different quantities of coolant can drain away during different types of repairs, the filing capacity can vary greatly. Recommendation: To be on the safe side, fil the canister to 30 I, then bleed the cooling system. The difference after bleeding is the coolant quantity that is sucked in. Check the volume scale on the canister.

An antifreeze content of -35 C corresponds to a mixture of 50: 50 (antifreeze: water).

# Information

The filing process is completed more quickly if the canister is positioned at roughly the same height as the coolant reservoir.

# Information

•A hissing sound after connecting the compressed air supply is usual.

# Information

If no vacuum is generated (the pointer does not move to the green area), there is a leak in the cooling system.   
If a vacuum is still not established, there is a blockage in the tool. Clean the device, use clean compressed air.   
Deformation of the rubber hoses of the cooling system is normal.   
Pressure of between 6 and 10 bar must be present. The higher the pressure, the better the vacuum in the vehicle cooling system.   
When the pressure gauge pointer is in the green area of the display scale, a sufficient vacuum has been built up.   
After both shutoff valves on the vacuum pressure gauge have been closed and the compressed air supply has been disconnected, the vacuum must not drop. If the vacuum drops within approx. 30 seconds, there is a leak in the coolant circuit.

1. Tighten drain plug -1- on the adapter.

![](images/583255c956975f102a456e56ca5e418a2bf33bcacee07b980e18b425160ab052.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Coolant Drain Plug   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Set up and connect vacuum filing device.

1.2.1. Fill coolant reservoir -5- with at least 12 liters of pre-mixed coolant in the correct mixture ratio.

2. 2.2. Screw cap adapter K65 -6- for the coolant reservoir onto the reservoir.

3.2.3. Connect the flexible extension (FZ 100) to the cap.

4. 2.4. Connect the vacuum gauge -7- of the bleeder tool to the flexible extension and make sure that both shut-off valves -V1- and -V2- are closed.

# V1 and V2 are at a 90° angle to the flow direction

5.2.5. Connect the Venturi nozle to the vacuum gauge.

6. 2.6. Push the filler hose of the vacuum gauge onto the canister connection.

7. 2.7. Route the return line -1- from the Venturi nozzle to a second container -2- .

8.2.8. Connect the compressed air supply -4- to the filler hose -3- .

9. 2.9. Build up overpressure of 6 to 10 bar.

![](images/ad598e12e43292095c35fd62570f471654536cfd2242846ee86efeaf3053f658.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Vacuum-Filing Device Setup   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Open both shut-off valves on the vacuum gauge until the transparent filer hose has completely filled with coolant.

![](images/70e62cea094cd92188b315514e4fb4a7bba08845ac3fde1d74b66e631d0477d8.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Shut-Off Valve

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Close the left shutoff valve (V1) -arrow- on the vacuum gauge and allow a vacuum to build up in the coolant circuit.

![](images/c7879613c06345dbdd874e8a154deba63064e5322f2f16eeb1fbb23468a82b98.webp)  
Fig 4: Locating Shut-Off Valve On Filler Hose

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Allow a suficient vacuum to build in the cooling system (pointer is in the green area) —→ Vacuum built up (pointer in green area) .

![](images/c2798dfa790cbaa9c32b14dbec0eeafb6dc627475c29f72c4ac0f443979ac0a6.webp)  
Fig 5: Identifying Vacuum Built Up (Pointer In Green Area)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. Close the right shut-off valve (V) -arrow- and then disconnect the compressed air supply.

![](images/0bfdc3338c97458c3d93cb09c8079626606a228ab2b6be5afb269caa388032e5.webp)  
Fig 6: Locating Shut-Off Valve For Filler Hose

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Open the left shut-off valve (V1) -arrow- on the vacuum gauge again. The cooling system is now filled.

![](images/2ed212fdac395914f6a84108d17ee6b5d16f02210906ef59818e122487968374.webp)  
Fig 7: Locating Shut-Off Valve On Filler Hose

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

8. When there is no trace of vacuum present and no more coolant is being drawn from the canister, open the right shut-off valve (V2). → Opening right shut-off valve

![](images/b385053c04b9a7d64e782fef4bb23b069b6e8dcb65c1ed828a7297f859e1f445.webp)  
Fig 8: Identifying Right Shut-Off Valve

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

Then remove the complete filing tool (including the adapter K65).

10. Connect pipe, pipe for coolant cooling system tester WE 1387 to the adapter for the cooling system tester WE 1386 .

![](images/3eaf1eea5e9b446649bddfd0048d22b1fc3a73eaaa24a49687e3f56e8a84755f.webp)  
Fig 9: Identifying Cooling System Tester

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

11. Fill in coolant until the pipe for the coolant system tester is full.

# Can be topped up during the bleeding process if necessary.

12. Open the front bleeder screw -arrow- on the exhaust gas recirculation cooler until coolant emerges and then close it again.

# WM 200101 CHECKING FUEL SYSTEM (HIGH-PRESSURE SIDE) FOR LEAKS (EXCEPT MACAN) > PRELIMINARY WORK

WARNING: Toxic substances

•Danger of poisoning or suffocation

Danger of burns to the eyes and skin

→ Ventilate the work area well.

→ Never ingest or inhale.

→ Read specific information on the Hazard Sheet.

→ Do not smoke, eat or drink in the work area.

WARNING: Highly inflammable or explosive materials

Danger of fire or explosion

→ Avoid contact with hot parts or sources of ignition.

—→ Use suction to remove ignitable vapours.

— Attach warning sign in a clearly visible position.

NOTE: Dirt on injection system components

Material damage • Rough-running engine Bad exhaust emissions

→ Thoroughly clean connection points and adjacent areas before loosening them. If the engine is very dirty, wash it before starting disassembly work.

→ Lay removed parts on a clean surface and cover them. Do not use fibre-shedding cloths.

→ Carefully cover components or seal them if repair work will not be carried out immediately. Place rubber caps on connections. Seal intake openings with film or adhesive tape.

→ Only installclean parts. Do not take spare parts out of the packaging until just before installtion.   
→ Never use compressed air when the system is open. Do not move the vehicle.

WARNING: Leaking fuel supply lines

• Emerging fuel Risk of fire

→ Perform leak test.

# Information

Do not bend high-pressure lines. Always remove the high-pressure distributor pipe and other fuel-supply components in the high-pressure area completely. Check that the connection points are not damaged and are perfectly clean and make sure there is no thread damage. Fit union nuts on all connection points by hand before screwing in screws or bolts. Remove dirt on the conical/ball joints. Check connection points for leaks following fitting.

# Information

The ignition must be switched off when working on the fuel system.   
Absorb any escaping fuel using a suitable binding material or a cloth.   
Cloths which have absorbed fuel must be disposed of according to the applicable national laws.   
The fuel system must be depressurised before starting work on it.   
Only work on the fuel system in well-ventilated rooms.   
Any seals which have been removed must always be replaced.   
After disassembly work on the high-pressure injection system, fit the components to the prescribed torques.   
Visible threaded joints must be checked for leaks with the engine idling after a test drive.   
For the check to be performed correctly, the components to be checked must not contain any fuel. Remove fuel from the lines during disassembly work. 1. Remove rear engine compartment cover. → Removing front trim panel 2. Pull out fuse for the fuel pump in the central electrical system or disconnect the battery. This ensures that the fuel pump does not start up when a door is opened.

# WM 200101 CHECKING FUEL SYSTEM (HIGH-PRESSURE SIDE) FOR LEAKS (EXCEPT MACAN) > TOOLS AND MATERIALS

![](images/8316744b335bc36255f6428b262f592780da733317cd4dcca90311774017e832.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Leak Test Tools

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

1. The required pressure is set on the compressed gas bottle using the commercially available pressure gauge unit (pressure reducer). The commercially available compressed gas bottle must be filled only with approved leak-locating gases.

2. Air-spring strut filing unit VAS 6231 WE 1282 with air-spring filing unit; the connection is fitted between the pressure reducer and adapter. Perform the leak test using individual bursts of pressure.

3. K-Jetronic Tester WE 1291 adapter V.A.G 1318/11for fitting on the fuel supply line.

4. Commercially available leak-locating spray for detecting gas leaks.

Approved leak-locating gases (test media)

# WM 200101 CHECKING FUEL SYSTEM (HIGH-PRESSURE SIDE) FOR LEAKS (EXCEPT MACAN) > CHECKING FUEL SYSTEM FOR LEAKS

WARNING: Toxic substances

• Danger of poisoning or suffocation •Danger of burns to the eyes and skin

→ Ventilate the work area well.

→ Never ingest or inhale.

→ Read specific information on the Hazard Sheet.

→ Do not smoke, eat or drink in the work area.

WARNING: Highly inflammable or explosive materials

Danger of fire or explosion

→ Avoid contact with hot parts or sources of ignition.

—→ Use suction to remove ignitable vapours.

→ Attach warning sign in a clearly visible position.

WARNING: Leaking fuel supply lines

• Emerging fuel Risk of fire

→ Perform leak test.

1. Loosen hose clamp -2- and remove fuel supply line -1- from the fuel pipe -3- . Absorb escaping fuel.

Connection point for fuel supply line -1- is located close to the torque support.

Fuel supply line -1- must not be damaged, otherwise fuel supply line -1- must be replaced.

![](images/cf56a97962f9c6ad7eaa73d8aa03126968c2596dd9f79972daf73927103bf59c.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Low-Pressure Fuel Line

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# Information

1. Check that the tool fittings are clean before starting the leak test. .Blow out the tool fitings before assembly using gentle bursts of pressure to prevent dust and foreign bodies from getting into the high-pressure system during the leak test. 3. Ensure that the tools for the leak test remain clean and free of dirt when stored.

2. Fit adapter → Adapter VAG 1318/11 to the fuel supply line -1- . Tighten hose clamp -2- .

The fuel supply line -1- must not be damaged, otherwise the fuel supply line must be replaced.

![](images/0df6cbd9dde1a650808e2468736b570d93651fd73a544a6a63be23d71d3f1a57.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Adapter VAG 1318/11

![](images/dd86536859724fcc385102b829ab545a5c7d93fe48657dc3f664b66bdb8d5b3b.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Fuel Supply Line Adapter VAG 1318/11

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

NOTE: Test pressure is exceeded

1. Risk of damage to high-pressure pump

→ The test gas test pressure must be set to less than → Pressure: 10 bar on the pressure reducer on the test gas bottle.

WARNING: Working with compressed air

1. Risk of eye injuries

2. Risk of damaging and dirtying components → Wear protective goggles with side eye protection.

→ Protect the point at which the compressed air emerges with suitable material.

→ Place the point at which the compressed air emerges on suitable surfaces.

# Information

The use of unapproved test gases results in incorrect test results. Only approved test gases guarantee comparability with fuel high-pressure systems at pressures of up to 10 bar .

3. Fit test gas bottle with pressure reducer and air-spring strut filling unit VAS 6231 WE 1282 securely so that no gas can escape → Test equipment setup . Set pressure reducer to max. 10 bar pressure —→ Adjusting pressure reducer to between 7 and 9 bar of test gas pressure .

![](images/5342199e8ac9e94f3900e6bf9f06b30631b090f5ec2d119f2ab42ffc1dcb635b.webp)  
Fig 4: Identifying Air-Spring Strut Filing Unit VAS 6231

Fig 5: Identifying Test Equipment Setup

![](images/2f264d21f17fa0c4fad6f4c68f27a8d35008c92985a398469b26f1a1bcac517d.webp)  
Fig 6: Adjusting Pressure Reducer Tool

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Air-spring strut filling unit VAS 6231 WE 1282 must then be connected to the adapter 9759 (→ Connecting test equipment ). Tighten the connection -4- if necessary.

![](images/6d148fccac01d783a2ece2ee295c4f54a354bd2d115ca975493a831314d51a85.webp)  
Fig 7: Connecting Test Equipment

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Depending on the high-pressure connections that were loosened (removed fuel distributor pipe or removed high-pressure pump), complete the following steps => If the fuel distributor pipe (high-pressure rail) was removed =>   
6.Before screwing the fuel distributor pipe (high-pressure rail to the engine, quickly blow out residual fuel from the high-pressure pump and high-pressure line (intake) to the high-pressure rail.

1. 6.1. Apply a quick burst of pressure using the filling unit and blow residual fuel out of the high-pressure pump and high-pressure line. Absorb escaping fuel. → Blowing out high-pressure line

![](images/5289bb26959e35fd3b43b920549c521a647ce6499ccd733d1cc8734d4880711b.webp)  
Fig 8: Identifying High-Pressure Line

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2.6.2. Drain residual fuel from the high-pressure distributor pipe before fitting it. Absorb escaping fuel.

7. Fit high-pressure distributor pipe (high-pressure rail and tighten it to the correct tightening torques. → Installing fuel collection pipe

NOTE: Test pressure is exceeded

→ The test gas test pressure must be set to less than → Pressure: 10 bar on the pressure reducer on the test gas bottle.

8. Use air-spring strut filling device VAS 6231 WE 1282 to apply test gas pressure of between 7 and just under 10 bar to the completely fitted high-pressure system. The pressure is distributed slowly in the system and can increase slightly on the pressure gauge —→ Building up pressure . If there is a constant drop in pressure, there is a leak in the system.

![](images/f8eadcf6bb4e7ab39f65d19cee7f76be04008764eebe860bc9c74a8e09e5c7fb.webp)  
Fig 9: Testing Gas Pressure Using Tool

9. Spray all connection points in the high-pressure system with commercially available leak-locating spray. If the pressure drops even though the threaded joints are perfectly sealed, also spray the soldered joints and connecting pipes as well as the high-pressure pump and test equipment with leak-locating spray.

10. If there is a leak, gently sashaying, moving and growing air bubbles → Leaks wilemerge. These could be caused by a damaged seal, loose connections or incorrectly fitted union nuts, for example. The cause must be determined and corrected.

![](images/f36a855da94aa5d481a3da17cc3af0fb08c0864829b8703b9fd7cfb748737bef.webp)  
Fig 10: Locating Pressure Line Leaks

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

If the high-pressure pump was removed =>

11. Before screwing the high-pressure line (intake) to the high-pressure pump, residual fuel must be blown out of the high-pressure pump.

1. 11.1. Apply a quick burst of pressure using the filing unit and blow any fuel out of the high-pressure pump → Blowing out high-pressure pump . Absorb escaping fuel. → Blowing out high-pressure pump

![](images/7f8a49392666ca3ee14e648ce3abe9a8f60e23ae31e57c4f410ec6b353211303.webp)  
Fig 11: Applying Pressure Using Filling Unit

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

12. Screw high-pressure line correctly to the high-pressure pump. → Instaling high-pressure pump

NOTE: Test pressure is exceeded

1. Risk of damage to high-pressure pump

→ The test gas test pressure must be set to less than → Pressure: 10 bar on the pressure reducer on the test gas bottle.

13. Use air-spring strut filling device VAS 6231 WE 1282 to apply test gas pressure of between 7 and just under 10 bar to the fitted high-pressure pump. The pressure is distributed slowly in the system and can increase slightly on the pressure gauge → Building up pressure . If there is a constant drop in pressure, there is a leak in the system.

![](images/bdc13a6b8f36885590d0f25d3f899f8a3534e3a3c708dce19566745af3947db6.webp)  
Fig 12: Applying Pressure

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

14. Spray all connection points for the high-pressure pump with commercially available leak-locating spray. If the pressure drops even though the threaded joints are perfectly sealed, also spray other connection points as well as the high-pressure pump and test equipment with leak-locating spray.

15. If there is a leak, gently sashaying, moving and growing air bubbles will emerge (union nut on injector is shown) → Leaks . These could be caused by a damaged seal, loose connections or incorrectly fitted union nuts, for example. The cause must be determined and

corrected.

![](images/e02f29694470a55e0c314ab800322fee9410bb5b9cd98887e23e96d576a8367e.webp)  
Fig 13: Locating Pressure Line Leaks

# WM 200101 CHECKING FUEL SYSTEM (HIGH-PRESSURE SIDE) FOR LEAKS (EXCEPT MACAN) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Remove tool setup.   
Fit the fuel line.To do this, fit the fuel supplyline (low pressure) at the marking correctly. Counter while fitting. → Tightening torque: 35 Nm (26 ftlb.)   
3. Fit engine cover. For details, see → Installing front trim panel   
Fit the fuse or connect the battery.
