# WM 200201 CHECKING FUEL PRESSURE (EXCEPT MACAN) > TOOLS

![](images/f419aba45e624441363fb70012c9a69c08279ac98e7f48e358a2eaaf4886731b.webp)

![](images/28bad5d6c1ad513663bc6d56685089a312d9b4a47cce2574e1d8d0c4359152ca.webp)

# WM 200201 CHECKING FUEL PRESSURE (EXCEPT MACAN) > CHECKING FUEL PRESSURE (LOW PRESSURE) USING THE PIWIS TESTER (QUICK TEST)

Faults in the fuel high-pressure injection system can also be caused by defects in the pre-delivery system (fuel low pressure)   
In the event of problems in the fuel high-pressure injection system, the pre-delivery system should be checked first

# Information

A leak in the fuel high-pressure pump supplying the engine (mechanical drive) dilutes the oil. Check the engine oil and initiate appropriate remedial action if necessary.

# Information

The fuel delivery pressure (low pressure) cannot be measured during a test drive. When you drive the vehicle, only the measured value Fuel high pressure actual value can be read out with the PIWIS Tester in the DME control unit via the high-pressure sensor. There is no "low pressure" actual value

# Information

The fuel system contains a fuel pump, which is controlled according to demand by a control unit, and one

or two supply-driven sucking jet pumps, depending on model.

# Information

If you suspect that a pump in the fuel tank is defective (particularly if symptoms include a very low fuel level), always check the sucking jet pumps for dirt or blockages.

# Information

Checking the low-pressure area with the high-pressure sensor cannot be used as the sole reference. The high-pressure sensor has a certain percent inaccuracy in the low-pressure area. It is best to check the low-pressure area using both test methods (Tester and pressure gauge).

# General information on converting pressure =>

• 10000 hPa = 10 bar = 10000 mbar 1000 kPa = 10 bar = 10000 mbar • 1 MPa = 10 bar = 10, 000 mbar

1. Connect the Tester and get it ready. PiWis Tester Il 9818

1. 1.1. Connect a charger to the vehicle battery. The voltage should be approx. 12.5 V (no rapid charging allowed because the voltage is too high!).

2. 1.2. The fuel pump can be activated and deactivated as follows:

3.1.3. DME => Drive link test/checks => Drive links => Fuel pump 1

4. 1.4. 100% is displayed. The fuel pump starts to deliver fuel when you press Start .

5. 1.5. The fuel pump stops when the percentage value changes to 0%. Press Start again.

2. Callup the test value B070 Fuel high pressure actual value .

1. 2.1. DME => Actual values/input signals => B070 Fuel high-pressure actual value

Fuel pressure is approx. 5500.0 hPa to 5800.0 hPa when the pump is running.

![](images/014349c4461d95368516ab6e048d5061947f32088e4c70326129de23e004b2d1.webp)  
Fig 1: View Of Both Values One Under The Other On The PIWIS Tester (German illustration)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

1. Drive links/tests

2. Fuel pump status (0% when pump is off - 100% when pump is running). Always confirm by pressing Start .

3. Fuel pressure in hPa (figure shows holding pressure shortly after switching pump of).

# Information

The fuel holding pressure must only drop by max. 1 bar (1000 mbar) in one hour.

# 1. Step 2: Check the fuel system for leaks =>

1. 1.1 Read out the fuel high pressure actual value in the DME control unit using the PIWIS Tester.

1. Nominal pressure is approx. 5000 to 5500.0 hPa. Monitor the fuel pressure for about 5 to 10 minutes.

2. The pressure is not maintained. In other words: the fuel high-pressure actual value has dropped considerably. There is an internal or external leak in the fuel system.

3. The pressure is maintained. In other words: the fuel high-pressure

actual value has only dropped slightly.

WARNING: Toxic substances

Danger of poisoning or suffocation   
•Danger of burns to the eyes and skin   
oVentilate the work area well.   
Never ingest or inhale.   
oRead specific information on the Hazard Sheet. oDo not smoke, eat or drink in the work area.

# WARNING: Highly inflammable or explosive materials

Danger of fire or explosion oAvoid contact with hot parts or sources of ignition. Use suction to remove ignitable vapours. Attach warning sign in a clearly visible position.

1. Remove engine compartment trim panel at the front right. → REMOVING FRONT TRIM PANEL .Disconnect fuel low-pressure line -2- at the front left of the wheel housing.

1.2.1 Loosen clamp -1- and pull off line -2- .

2.2.2 Collect escaping fuel.

![](images/f5eb1891600f8bba3c448a9819ed7257a5d344ba4cc2e544f2475e9a4c301dba.webp)  
Fig 1: Fuel Supply Line

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# 3. Check fuel supply pressure (low-pressure) =>

1. 3.1 Connect test equipment and secure connections with a clamp -1- or screw-type clamp -2- .

2. 3.2 The tool setup must be fitted with sealing rings (copper, aluminium, or plastic, etc.) between the individual components. The setup must be full sealed.

3. 3.3. Start the engine and leave it running at idle speed. Read off the fuel pressure on the pressure gauge. The pressure gauge pointer can oscillate slightly at idle speed. With increased idle speed (accelerator pressed slightly), the pointer deflection calms down. The fuel low-pressure system operates at a fuel pressure of 5.5 to 5.8 bar . The pointer oscillates at around this value. Measurements under load can even generate values of below 5 bar (4.5 bar) briefly. This is not a sign of a defect.

![](images/f54690c6390dfa55d35b1839dff835c39b94e2f4fc3c23cfeddf023c82009052.webp)  
Fig 2: Connection For Measuring Pressure On The Vehicle

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# 4. Check fuel retaining pressure (low-pressure) =>

1. Engine cold

2. Workshop air-conditioned to normal temperature

3. Fluctuations may occur if the engine is warm or if the outside temperature is high

4. Fully sealed measuring tool setup

1. 6.1 Same tool setup and connection as for measuring the fuel delivery pressure (see above).

2.6.2. Allow engine to run for a few minutes. Switch off engine. Check the pressure drop. Drop in fuel pressure after "ignition is switched of" must not exceed 1 bar after 1 hour . Make sure that the tool setup itself does not have any leaks (even the slightest leak). The fuel retaining pressure will decrease extremely rapidly and falsify the measured result with even the tiniest leak.

→ Wear personal protective gear.

→ Ensure that there is good ventilation.

→ If you do come into contact, wash off immediately with plenty of warm water and contact a doctor if necessary.

# Information

Calibration of the fuel level sender is required after replacing the fuel tank, the fuel level sender or the instrument cluster. Calibrate the sender - after replacing the instrument cluster - only if the function Read out values cannot be performed!   
The fuel level sender does not have to be calibrated if the battery was disconnected or a plug connection on the instrument cluster or sender was disconnected. The values remain stored in the instrument cluster.   
A range on remaining fuel of less than 15 km (9 miles) is not displayed in the instrument cluster.

# WM 2015K2 CALIBRATING FUEL LEVEL SENDER (ALL MODELS) > CALIBRATING FUEL LEVEL SENDER > CALIBRATING FUEL LEVEL SENDER

1. Empty the fuel tank. → Emptying The Fuel Tank

2. Wait for a short time (approx. 1 minute) to allow the fuel-level sensor to settle at the current level.   
3. Connect the Porsche System Tester to the vehicle and start the System Tester. Switch on ignition. [>>] to continue.   
4. Select the vehicle type.   
5. Select Instrument cluster control unit, then press [>].   
6. Select the Maintenance/repairs menu and press [>>].   
7. Select Fuel tank calibration menu and press [F8] to start the calibration process.   
8. The message Fuel tank calibration completed successfully appears on the Tester screen.   
9. Press [F12] to exit.   
10. Fil the vehicle with fuel and check the fuel gauge in the instrument cluster. Wait a few minutes. Fuel gauge shows full.   
11. Change terminals.

1.11.1. Switch off ignition.   
2. 11.2. Wait approx. 30 seconds.   
3.11.3. Switch on ignition.

12. Check the fuel gauge in the instrument cluster again. Fuel gauge shows full.

1. Drain coolant.

2. Remove air cleaner housing. → 242519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING AIR CLEANER HOUSING

# WM 213019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING TURBOCHARGER (MACAN) > REMOVING TURBOCHARGER

Replace gaskets, sealing rings and O-rings.   
Hose adapters and hoses for the charge air system must be free of oil and grease before being fitted.   
Secure all hose connections with standard hose clamps.   
To fasten the charge air hoses securely to their adapters, spray the threaded parts of previously used screw-type clamps with anti-rust agent before installation.   
Refit all heat protection boots at the same position during installation.   
Leave the engine running at idle speed for about 1 minute and avoid revving the engine after

installing the turbocharger to ensure an adequate oil supply for the turbocharger.

# Information

Do not damage O-rings!

1. Open cap on reservoir.

2. Loosen spring band clamp -arrow- , pull off molded hose on the turbocharger and swivel it aside.

![](images/2bd17885534f36fddb2c22074b4b24fbd9c848d73de9332fcabb06cba6225e7b.webp)  
Fig 1: Locating Turbocharger Spring Band Clamp

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Loosen fastening screw -1- on support for turbocharger -2- .

![](images/670aa0fba0e60f9b22945b56166d597fdb02752141c8993fe94cb8d3d574ab11.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Turbocharger Support Screws

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Disconnect oil return line on the turbocharger.

# WM 213019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING TURBOCHARGER (MACAN) > INSTALLING TURBOCHARGER

Replace gaskets, sealing rings and O-rings.   
Hose adapters and hoses for the charge air system must be free of oil and grease before being fitted.   
Secure all hose connections with standard hose clamps.   
To fasten the charge air hoses securely to their adapters, spray the threaded parts of previously used screw-type clamps with anti-rust agent before installation.   
Refit all heat protection boots at the same position during installation.   
Leave the engine running at idle speed for about 1 minute and avoid revving the engine after installing the turbocharger to ensure an adequate oil supply for the turbocharger.

# Information

Do not damage O-rings!

1. Position the turbocharger.

1.1.1. Position the turbocharger and fit coolant supply pipe -2- with a new O-ring under the heat shield. Coat O-ring with coolant.   
2. 1.2. Fit and tighten fastening screw -1- over the heat shield.   
3.1.3. Fit new seal at the connection point between the turbocharger and exhaust manifold.   
4.1.4. Fit the turbocharger on the studs in the opposite direction to the -direction of arrow- .

![](images/de127210726106a2f1afa944e3707cf76b34ffeac46187bd0b89653d008ef6c3.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

1.2.1. Coat studs with high-temperature paste.

2.2.2. Fit and tighten new fastening nuts -arrows- .

3. 2.3. Fill the turbocharger with engine oil at the oil supply line adapter.

4. 2.4. Fit oil supply line with new O-ring  over the heat shield and press it into position. Coat O-ring with engine oil.

5.2.5. Fit and tighten fastening screw -2 - .

Tool recommendation: Special inserts Nr.170

6.2.6. Fit coolant return pipe with a new O-ring . Coat O-ring with coolant.

7.2.7. Fit and tighten fastening screw -1- . Tool recommendation: Special inserts Nr.170

8.2.8. Connect electric plug connection -3- at the electronic adjuster for the turbocharger.

• Emerging fuel Risk of fire → Perform leak test.

NOTE: Dirt on injection system components •Material damage • Rough-running engine Bad exhaust emissions

→ Thoroughly clean connection points and adjacent areas before loosening them. If the engine is very dirty, wash it before starting disassembly work.

→ Lay removed parts on a clean surface and cover them. Do not use fibre-shedding cloths.

→ Carefully cover components or seal them if repair work will not be carried out immediately. Place rubber caps on connections. Seal intake openings with film or adhesive tape.

→ Only install clean parts. Do not take spare parts out of the packaging until just before installtion.

→ Never use compressed air when the system is open. Do not move the vehicle.

# WM 243019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FUEL COLLECTION PIPE (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING FUEL COLLECTION PIPE

WARNING: Toxic substances

• Danger of poisoning or suffocation

Danger of burns to the eyes and skin

→ Ventilate the work area well

→ Never ingest or inhale.

→ Read specific information on the Hazard Sheet.

→ Do not smoke, eat or drink in the work area.

WARNING: Highly inflammable or explosive materials

Danger of fire or explosion

→ Avoid contact with hot parts or sources of ignition.

→ Use suction to remove ignitable vapors.

— Attach warning sign in a clearly visible position.

WARNING: Leaking fuel supply lines

• Emerging fuel Risk of fire

→ Perform leak test.

NOTE: Dirt on injection system components

Material damage • Rough-running engine Bad exhaust emissions

→ Thoroughly clean connection points and adjacent areas before loosening them. If the engine is very dirty, wash it before starting disassembly work.

→ Lay removed parts on a clean surface and cover them. Do not use fibre-shedding cloths.

→ Carefully cover components or seal them if repair work will not be carried out immediately. Place rubber caps on connections. Seal intake openings with film or adhesive tape.

→ Only install clean parts. Do not take spare parts out of the packaging until just before installation.

→ Never use compressed air when the system is open. Do not move the vehicle.

# Information

•Do not bend high-pressure lines. Check that the connection points are not damaged and are perfectly clean and make sure there is no thread damage. Fit union nuts on all connection points by hand before screwing in screws or bolts. Remove dirt on the conical/ball joints. Check connection points for leaks following fiting.

# Information

The ignition must be switched off when working on the fuel system.   
•Absorb any escaping fuel using a suitable binding material or a cloth.   
Cloths which have absorbed fuel must be disposed of according to the applicable national laws.   
The fuel system must be depressurized before starting work on it.   
Only work on the fuel system in well-ventilated rooms.   
Any seals which have been removed must always be replaced.

# WM 244019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FUEL INJECTOR (MACAN) > REMOVING FUEL INJECTORS > REMOVING FUEL INJECTORS FOR DIRECT FUEL INJECTION (DFI)

Close off open connections and lines using suitable stoppers or caps.

f fuel injectors remain in the cylinder head, the following procedure applies.

1. Push sleeve T10133/18 over the fuel injector.

![](images/9d7ac0155e03dd6a401b3acd943ff31cc30b783e3e5fec3376769637f6ce997d.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Sleeve T10133/18

2. Carefully tap several times on the sleeve around the fuel injector to loosen it.

![](images/e74d95afbf1f824f479f8446700c271ed4980c80c1fd6f57b2e99e2143c2cf96.webp)  
Fig 2: Tapping Fuel Injector Sleeve   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Loosen fuel injector.

1.3.1. Guide puller T10133/2A into the groove on the fuel injector.

2.3.2. Fit puller T10133/16A .

3.3.3. Adjust the torque wrench to 5 Nm (3.5 ftlb.) .

4.3.4. Turn the screw with the torque wrench and remove the fuel injector.

5. 3.5. If the torque limit of 5 Nm (3.5 ftlb.) is reached and the fuel injector is still not loosened, remove the extraction tool and loosen the fuel injector again using the sleeve.

Non-observance of the specified torque can cause irreparable damage to the fuel injector.

![](images/1b9a6a1ca09dd48d6f239e4462b44785067f8e79cfa462dbbce8afe135e186fa.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Puller T10133/2A And T10133/16A

# WM 244019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FUEL INJECTOR (MACAN) > REMOVING FUEL INJECTORS > REMOVING FUEL INJECTORS FOR INTAKE MANIFOLD INJECTION

WARNING: Highly inflammable or explosive materials

Danger of fire or explosion → Avoid contact with hot parts or sources of ignition.

→ Use suction to remove ignitable vapors.

— Attach warning sign in a clearly visible position.

WARNING: Toxic substances • Danger of poisoning or suffocation Danger of burns to the eyes and skin

→ Ventilate the work area well   
→ Never ingest or inhale.   
→ Read specific information on the Hazard Sheet. → Do not smoke, eat or drink in the work area.

# Information

•Absorb any escaping fuel using a suitable binding material or a cloth.   
Cloths which have absorbed fuel must be disposed of according to the applicable national laws.   
The fuel system must be depressurized before starting work on it.   
Only work on the fuel system in well-ventilated rooms.   
Any seals which have been removed must always be replaced.   
•Do not use any sealant containing silicone or silicone spray when the injection system is open.   
Traces of silicone drawn in by the engine are not combusted and damage the oxygen sensors.

# Information

Close off open connections and lines using suitable stoppers or caps.

1. Disconnect lines at the intake-air distributor.

1. 1.1. Disconnect vacuum line -1- and coolant vent line -2- on the intake-air distributor. 2. 1.2. Remove electric plug connection -3- from the bracket. 3.1.3. Release and disconnect electric connectors -4- and -5- .

![](images/781d77157bfd7c5b0b7032e34475ab36eca7d03e4dd1834348cae8624aa1ee05.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Intake-Air Distributor Lines

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Remove fuel collection pipe.

1.2.1. Expose wiring harness -1- from the fuel collection pipe.

2.2.2. Loosen clamp and pull off fuel supply line -2- .

3.2.3. Unscrew screws -arrows- .

![](images/80dd28d2bb1a1bf953c463f237ebf13bf7b9b0ddfb2685c6b8384886de67ba28.webp)  
Fig 2: Locating Intake Manifold Injection Fuel Collection Pipe

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Remove fuel injector.

1. 3.1. Carefully pull fuel collection pipe with fuel injectors up and remove them.

2. 3.2. Release and disconnect electric connectors on the fuel injector.

3. 3.3. Loosen retaining clip -3- and pul fuel injector carefully out of the fuel collection pipe.

![](images/9679ae185ae3715d6a24780001c8e8e791bce3b89488d55929bb7abd2462f503.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Intake Manifold Injection Fuel Injector

# WM 244019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FUEL INJECTOR (MACAN) > INSTALLING FUEL INJECTORS > INSTALLING FUEL INJECTORS FOR DIRECT FUEL INJECTION (DFI)

NOTE: Incorrect handling of sealing rings and covers

Leaks •Risk of damage to components

→ Use clean tools without burrs.

→ Make sure not to leave any scores or scratches when cleaning.

# Information

The combustion chamber sealing ring widens out as you slide it onto the fuel injector. It must therefore be closed in again in two steps after fitting.

1. The following work must be carried out before installing the fuel injector.

1.1.1. Replace intermediate ring -1- .

2.1.2. Replace mounting -2- .

3. 1.3. Carefull remove the combustion chamber seal -3- by cutting the seal with a knife or widening it with a small screwdriver and then pulling it forward. If the groove on the fuel injector is damaged, the fuel injector must be replaced!

4.1.4. Replace spacer ring -5- .

5.1.5. Replace O-ring -6- and coat with clean engine oil.

6.1.6. Replace support ring -7-

![](images/536e822c187926128801b428fea824d6ca2aaeff17a1c9c58bbdcf7f60fa494f.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Fuel Injector Components   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Clean the bore in the cylinder head using the nylon cylinder brush -T10133/4- .

![](images/576b9d175ee4bd17c4ed66500bb689575eef1dab2698474bf1879fc22686b1fa.webp)  
Fig 2: Cleaning Fuel Injector Bore

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Fit mounting code -T 10133/5- with the new combustion chamber sealing ring -1- from the repair kit onto the fuel injector -2- .

![](images/fe4a49a7fd789c1228a82bde0e230d19e729a8373506db313afa95752db23fe4.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Mounting Cone T 10133/5

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Slide combustion chamber seal with assembly sleeve -T 10133/6- onto assembly cone -T 10133/5- as far as it will go.

Turn the assembly sleeve -T 10133/6- around and slide the combustion chamber sealing ring into the sealing ring groove.

![](images/d9a103233683407a92237e50723ef4e8d9a470786ed81dafe15ea7059c139838.webp)  
Fig 4: Identifying Assembly Sleeve

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Press the calibrating nozzle -T10133/7- with a slight rotary movement (approx. 180°) as far as it will go onto the fuel injector.

Pull the calibrating sleeve off again by turning it in the opposite direction.

![](images/38d757b07b0c0bdb2b2e52d42c7752f5f1f05e6525c7f5d716450a57b01c607f.webp)  
Fig 5: Identifying Sleeve T10133/7

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. Press the calibrating nozzle -T10133/8- with a slight rotary movement (approx. 180°) as far as it will go onto the fuel injector.

Pull the calibrating sleeve off again by turning it in the opposite direction.

![](images/717b55d3b49b6312c1ab79984ae2d3844a5ccefe6d7a7e40c5866bfb0da437cb.webp)  
Fig 6: Identifying Sleeve T10133/8   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Install fuel injector.

# 1.7.1.

2.7.2. Press the fuel injector as far as it will go into the bore on the cylinder head with your hand. Make sure that the fuel injectors are positioned correctly in the cylinder head.

3.7.3. The lug -1- and the bore in the cylinder head must be aligned.

![](images/aab808edfd61b3bef8a6d209efa8bafab08aea6934544169420384b6e4933b05.webp)  
Fig 7: Locating Fuel Injector Position

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

8. If the fuel injector cannot be inserted by hand the following procedure must be performed.

1. 8.1. Use the puller T10133/2A -2- with impact hammer T10133/3 -2- to guide in the fuel injector.

6. Do not use any sealant containing silicone or silicone spray when the injection system is open. Traces of silicone drawn in by the engine are not combusted and damage the oxygen sensors.

# WM 246319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HIGH-PRESSURE PUMP (MACAN) > REMOVING HIGH-PRESSURE PUMP

WARNING: Highly inflammable or explosive materials

Danger of fire or explosion

→ Avoid contact with hot parts or sources of ignition.

→ Use suction to remove ignitable vapors.

→ Attach warning sign in a clearly visible position.

WARNING: Toxic substances

Danger of poisoning or suffocation

Danger of burns to the eyes and skin

→ Ventilate the work area well.

→ Never ingest or inhale.

→ Read specific information on the Hazard Sheet.

→ Do not smoke, eat or drink in the work area.

# Information

•Absorb any escaping fuel using a suitable binding material or a cloth.   
Cloths which have absorbed fuel must be disposed of according to the applicable national laws.   
The fuel system must be depressurized before starting work on it.   
Only work on the fuel system in well-ventilated rooms.   
Any seals which have been removed must always be replaced.   
Do not use any sealant containing silicone or silicone spray when the injection system is open. Traces of silicone drawn in by the engine are not combusted and damage the oxygen sensors.

# Information

Close of open connections and lines using suitable stoppers or caps.

1. Unscrew screw -arrow- and loosen holding clamp on fuel high-pressure line.

![](images/c36793a895d9fe08cd27333b6f3a05c9f0ce0a4727877acac155ef192543983e.webp)  
Fig 1: Locating High-Pressure Line Holding Clamp

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Remove high-pressure pump.

1.2.1. Release and disconnect electric connector -2- for the fuel pressure sensor.

2.2.2. Loosen clamps and pull off fuel lines -3- and -4- .

3.2.3. Unscrew union nut and loosen fuel high-pressure line -5- at the adapter. Replace adapter on the high-pressure pump.

4.2.4. Unscrew screws -arrows- and remove high-pressure pump. The roller tappet can remain in the vacuum pump.

![](images/4952da3634f95619196a962394cd222e8ce494b0bf7e50450c5d3ceca95f21e7.webp)  
Fig 2: Locating High-Pressure Pump Screws

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# WM 246319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HIGH-PRESSURE PUMP (MACAN) > INSTALLING HIGH-PRESSURE PUMP

An adaptation must be performed after replacing the high-pressure pump and/or the fuel pressure control valve. Use the vehicle diagnostic tester to do this.

1. Install high-pressure pump.

1.1.1. Replace O-ring on high-pressure pump.

2.1.2. Fit roller tappet into the vacuum pump.

3. 1.3. Turn the crankshaft until the roller tappet is set to the lowest point.

4.1.4. Replace adapter for high-pressure pump. Tightening torque 40 Nm (30 ftlb.)

5.1.5. Insert high-pressure pump into the vacuum pump and tighten screws hand-tight.

6.1.6. Tighten screws to the specified tightening torque. Tightening torque 20 Nm (15 ftlb.)

2. Install fuel high-pressure line.

1.2.1. Tighten union nut on high-pressure line hand-tight.

2.2.2. Secure holding clamp for high-pressure line.

3.2.3. Align high-pressure line without tension and tighten to the specified tightening torque. Tightening torque 20 Nm (15 ftlb.)

4.2.4. Tighten screw on the holding clamp.

3. Further installation is performed in reverse order.

1. Remove engine cover.

WM 247319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING OXYGEN SENSOR DOWNSTREAM OF CATALYTIC CONVERTER (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING OXYGEN SENSOR DOWNSTREAM OF CATALYTIC CONVERTER

NOTE: Incorrect handling of oxygen sensors

• Damage to oxygen sensors Different exhaust emission behavior

— Do not remove the plastic cap on the thread until just prior to fiting.

— Protect oxygen sensors from impact of any kind.

→ Do not kink or twist the cables when screwing in the sensors.

→ Do not re-use dirty or damaged components.

# Information

The procedure for removing and instaling is described for one side as an example. The procedure for the other side is practically identical.

1. Remove oxygen sensor.

1. 1.1. Release and disconnect electric connector -1- .

2.1.2. Loosen electric line -2- from the holder -3- .

3. 1.3. Unscrew oxygen sensor -4- using crow foot wrench Nr.189-1 or socket insert a/f 17 T10491 -5- .

# WM 249019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FUEL LINE (HIGH-PRESSURE) (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING FUEL LINE (HIGH-PRESSURE)

WARNING: Hot fuel and hot fuel lines.

Danger of scalding

→ Allow the fuel to cool down before opening line connections.   
→ Wear protective gloves.   
→ Wear protective goggles.

# Information

Always read the rules relating to cleanliness and instructions for working on the fuel system.   
These instructions must always be observed before and while working on the fuel system.

# Information

Close off open connections and lines using suitable stoppers or caps. 1. Unscrew fastening screws -2- for the high-pressure lines -1, 4 and 5- . 2. Loosen union nuts on high-pressure line -1- . 1.2.1. Remove high-pressure line -1- . 3. Loosen union nuts on high-pressure line -4- . 1.3.1. Remove high-pressure line -4- .

4. Loosen union nuts on high-pressure line -5- .

1.4.1. Remove high-pressure line -5- .

5. Place high-pressure lines -1, 4 and 5- on a clean surface.

Fig 1: Identifying High-Pressure Pump With High-Pressure Lines

![](images/f0a7a6d603d17fb011508004195e0ac689e6e7b0c73103aacf87ccaafdd47e4e.webp)

# WM 249019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FUEL LINE (HIGH-PRESSURE) (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > INSTALLING FUEL LINE (HIGH-PRESSURE)

Observe cylinder-specific markings if high-pressure lines are to be reused.

High-pressure lines can always be reused.   
Check the sealing cone of each high-pressure line for deformities and tears before installation.   
The line bore must not be deformed, narrowed or damaged. 1. Remove dirt from the sealing cone on the fuel collection pipe by suction. 2. Clean high-pressure lines and line heads with a cold-cleaning product and blow-dry with compressed air. 3. Coat the thread on the union nuts with fuel. 4. Install high-pressure lines. 1.4.1. Observe specified tightening sequence.

# WM 249019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FUEL LINE (HIGH-PRESSURE) (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

The high-pressure connections do not have to be opened in order to bleed the system. The fuel system is bled automatically.

If there is stillair in the fuel system, the engine can switch to emergency operation during the test drive. Switch off the engine and erase the fault memory. Then continue to test drive the vehicle.

1. Bleed the fuel system and perform a leak test.

1.1.1. Leave the engine running at idle speed for a few minutes without pressing the accelerator.   
2.1.2. Switch off the engine and turn off the ignition.   
3. 1.3. Carefully check the entire high-pressure area of the injection system.   
4. 1.4. Then perform a test drive for more than 20 km (12 miles) with at least one full-throttle acceleration. Then check the high-pressure area for leaks again.

. Install engine cover (design cover).

WM 2706IN EXTERNAL POWER CONNECTION, JUMP-LEAD STARTING (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > EXTERNAL POWER CONNECTION, JUMP-LEAD STARTING

WARNING: Live jump leads

Risk of electric shock Risk of short circuit

→ Route the jump leads so that they do not become entangled in moving parts in the engine compartment.

→ There must be no contact between the vehicles.

NOTE: Using charging cables/jump leads directly on the vehicle battery.

Risk of damage to battery sensors.

→ Always connect charging cables/jump leads to the external power supply for jump-lead starting.

# Information

If the battery is flat, jump leads can be used together with the battery of another vehicle to start the

car or to supply external power to the vehicle.

# Information

Both batteries must be 12 V batteries.

The capacity (AH) of the donor battery must not be significantly lower than that of the flat battery.

The flat battery must be properly connected to the vehicle electrical system.

1. Open protective cover on the positive terminal for jump-lead starting -+- (-arrow-).   
.Connect the positive cable to the positive terminal for jump-lead starting -+- , then to the positive terminal of the donor battery.   
3. First, connect the negative cable to the negative terminal of the donor battery, then to the ground point for jump-lead starting - .

![](images/42075b3ac031b8bdcff1e006bc59c11eeba3ecb35ae894d3dc60614b91f419b4.webp)  
Fig 1: Connecting Battery To Vehicle Electrical System

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Leave the engine of the vehicle supplying the power running at higher revs.

5. Start the engine. Do not spend longer than 15 seconds trying to start the vehicle with the jump leads, then wait for at least one minute before trying again.

6. Disconnect the two jump leads in reverse order when the engine is running.

7. Close protective cover.

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > TOOLS

![](images/ca4244a8ba62bce75f8c350f1f1be8af0f3561a4e84e51930716c5037d2ceff2.webp)

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > TECHNICAL VALUES

![](images/2d9545bebe33907ff4a34076e9bb2e3318aedea226d29de6cc5c8f63d52f252c.webp)

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION

NOTE: A battery charger for providing an external power supply or for jump-lead starting connected directly to the battery in the vehicle.

Risk of damage to the battery sensor.

Battery sensor sends incorrect battery values to the vehicle electrical system.

→ Always connect a battery charger for providing an external power supply or for jump-lead starting to the defined connections in the engine compartment. → 2XOOIN BATTERY TRICKLE CHARGING

# Information

The AGM (A bsorbent G lass M at) battery is a maintenance-free, sealed battery.

This battery must not be opened. If the battery is opened, it must be replaced.

There is a serial number -A- and a part number -B- on the top right-hand side of the battery.

![](images/6ae9e1e4c0a3130adff3966563f77de6f2a5fbbadccfc57bcd7c6e269d2449be.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Battery Serial And Part Number

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

After replacing the battery, the serial number and part number as well as the battery size and manufacturer must be entered using the PIWiS Tester under: Gateway/Maintenance/repairs /Change battery.

The battery size and battery manufacturer must also be entered when changing the battery.

# Information

To prevent contact corrosion, only approved bolts, nuts, washers, etc. should be used. These elements have a special surface coating and must be stored separately.

The battery is one of the most important electrical components in the vehicle. Fault-free functioning of the battery contributes greatly to customer satisfaction. To guarantee long and eficient operation, the battery must be checked and maintained according to the instructions provided here.

Besides starting the vehicle, the battery also acts as a buffer and supplier of electrical power for the entire vehicle electrical system.

An AGM (A bsorbent G lass M at) battery is used as standard. The AGM battery offers the following advantages, for example:

Sealed, valve-controlled battery   
High-cycle battery   
High cold-start performance   
Cannot leak or tilt   
oTotally maintenance-free   
Shake-resistant   
No acid leakage if the housing is damaged   
oFlexible installation and safe to handle   
High load capacity and longer service life   
Ideal for Start/Stop function

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > INSTRUCTIONS FOR HANDLING BATTERIES

Battery terminals do not need to be greased.   
The battery terminal clamps should only be attached by hand - without excessive force - to prevent damage to the battery.   
The tightening torque for the battery terminals is → Torque: 5 Nm (3.5 ftlb.).   
If the battery is reconnected, proceed according to → 2X0000 WORK INSTRUCTIONS AFTER DISCONNECTING THE BATTERY .

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > WARNING NOTES AND SAFETY REGULATIONS FOR BATTERIES

1.-1- No fire, sparks, naked flames or smoking:

1. Avoid sparking when using cables and electrical devices.   
2. Avoid short circuits.   
3. On batteries with central venting, there is an increased concentration of oxyhydrogen gas at the hose opening. The vent hose should not be bent or blocked by dirt.

2.-2- Wear eye protection.

3. -3- Keep children away from acids and batteries.

4. -4- Risk of acid burns:

1. Battery acid is highly caustic, so wear protective gloves.

2. Do not tip battery; acid can emerge from the vent opening.

![](images/72301f9ed6d3f0e7444f29d12aa1ee03ccd6fe098d2904aef5b9e7b4382c87c6.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Battery Symbols

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# Information

1. First aid: Rinse acid splashes in the eyes immediately with clean water for a few minutes. Consult a doctor immediately. Neutralize acid splashes on the skin or clothing immediately with soap suds and rinse again with plenty of water. If acid has been drunk unintentionally, consult a doctor immediately.

5. -5- Follow the instructions on the battery, in the Technical Information and in the Driver's Manual.

6.-6- Risk of explosion:

1. A highly explosive detonating gas mixture is formed when charging batteries.

7. -7- Disposal:

1. Hand in old batteries at a collection point.

8. -8- Never dispose of old batteries in domestic rubbish!

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > NOTES ON REMOVING AND INSTALLING THE BATTERY

NOTE: A battery charger for providing an external power supply or for jump-lead starting : connected directly to the battery in the vehicle.

Risk of damage to the battery sensor.

Battery sensor sends incorrect battery values to the vehicle electrical system.

→ Always connect a battery charger for providing an external power supply or for jump-lead starting to the defined connections in the engine compartment. → 2X0OIN BATTERY TRICKLE CHARGING

# Information

The battery is located in the luggage compartment under the loadspace floor.   
In order to avoid triggering the siren in vehicles with an additional alarm siren, the battery must be disconnected while the ignition is on!   
All oads must be switched off beforehand! Remove ignition key!   
Never disconnect battery with engine running!   
Never start engine without a securely connected battery!   
To prevent damage to the battery, the battery terminal clamps should only be attached by hand - without excessive force.   
Check that the battery is seated correctly after installation. A loose battery presents other dangers, such as: - Reduced service life due to vibration damage. - Noises. - Damage to the battery housing from mounting parts. - Inadequate crash safety.

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > NOTES ON REMOVING AND INSTALLING THE BATTERY > OPERATING PRINCIPLE OF CENTRAL VENTING

State-of-the-art batteries have central venting -A- .

In certain battery states, the gas produced during charging can emerge centrally through an opening on the upper cover side. Backfire protection is integrated at the same position and prevents the combustible gas in the battery from igniting.   
On batteries with a vent hose -A- , check that the vent hose is not disconnected or pinched. Only then can the battery be freely vented.

![](images/9abfa8b205c74e11bedc0322fafd87bdc635a1e8aba3799d3ac3a7fe4dcaab03.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Battery Vent Hose

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > VISUAL INSPECTION

A visual inspection of the battery must be performed before taking measurements, e.g. measuring the open-circuit voltage, or before carrying out the battery load test.

# This test can be used to determine:

Whether the battery housing is damaged. Leak-free operation and function of the battery cannot be guaranteed if the housing is damaged.   
Whether the battery terminals (battery line connections) are damaged. The line connections might not make contact if the battery terminals are damaged. This can cause the lines to catch fire and can result in malfunctions in the electrical system.

# NM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) >

Make sure that the vent hose -A- is not kinked or damaged. If in doubt, replace it.

The vent hose -A- must be inserted in the battery and in the battery box.

![](images/d3698391c8fbc43505a93c220d921b7583acad88e6fedfb9b1816cc80e70e630.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Vent Hose (Panamera)

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > OPEN-CIRCUIT VOLTAGE MEASUREMENT

Compared with the value from PIWis Tester II 9818, the battery voltage can be measured using a hand-held multimeter.   
Proceed as follows:

# Information

The open-circuit voltage measurement should be read out using Piwis Tester Il9818 in the Gateway control unit by selecting Energy management, Quick closed-circuit current measurement in the menu.

1. Switch off ignition and remove ignition key.   
2. Disconnect ground strap on the battery.

# Information

1. After charging and waiting for at least 2 hours, during which time the battery should neither be loaded nor charged:

3. Measure the battery voltage with a hand-held multimeter.

1. The battery open-circuit voltage should not fallbelow 12.5 V.   
2. If the hand-held multimeter shows 12.5 V or more, the battery voltage is OK.   
. f the hand-held multimeter shows a battery voltage below 12.5 V: Charge the battery.

WARNING: Highly inflammable or explosive materials

Danger of fire or explosion

→ Avoid contact with hot parts or sources of ignition.

→ Use suction to remove ignitable vapors.

→ Attach warning sign in a clearly visible position.

# Information

A battery charger is required.   
Read operating instructions for the charger.   
The battery must have a minimum temperature of 0 °C.   
If possible, do not rapid-charge batteries as this can damage them.   
If exhaustively discharged batteries are charged quickly, they wil not take up a charge current or they will be identified too early as full due to the so-called "surface charge".

NOTE: A battery charger for providing an external power supply or for jump-lead starting is connected directly to the batery in the vehicle.

Risk of damage to the battery sensor.   
Battery sensor sends incorrect battery values to the vehicle electrical system.

→ Always connect a battery charger for providing an external power supply or for jump-lead starting to the defined connections in the engine compartment. → 2XOOIN BATTERY TRICKLE CHARGING

1. Switch off the battery charger.   
2. Switch off ignition and remove ignition key.   
3. Connect cables from the charger to the external power supply points.   
4. Set the charge current on the battery charger according to the battery capacity.   
Switch on the battery charger.

# Procedure for charging exhaustively discharged batteries:

Batteries that have not been used for a long time discharge automatically

A battery is exhaustively discharged if the open-circuit voltage has dropped below 11.6 V, see OPEN-CIRCUIT VOLTAGE MEASUREMENT

In exhaustively discharged batteries, the battery acid (sulfuric acid and water mixture) consists of virtually only water, as the sulfuric acid proportion is considerably reduced.

Exhaustively discharged batteries sulphatise, i.e. the entire plate surfaces of the batteries harden.

If exhaustively discharged batteries are immediately recharged after an exhaustive discharge, the sulphatisation recedes again.

If these batteries are not recharged, the plates continue to harden and charge take-up ability is limited. This results in reduced battery performance.

Exhaustively discharged batteries must be charged using a low charge current as follows:

1. Set the charge current to maximum 10% of battery capacity, i.e. with a 95 AH battery, the charge current is max. 9.5 A.

Charge the battery.

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > BATTERY TRICKLE CHARGING

When working or carrying out tests on the vehicle or when the vehicle is in the workshop, a battery charger with a rated current of at least 40 A must be connected.

As soon as the vehicle is unlocked, e.g. the vehicle is in the workshop or salesroom, it must be trickle charged with a battery charging device.

1.Switch off the battery charger.   
2. Switch offignition and remove remote control (hand-held transmitter).   
3.Switch off all lectrical loads (e.g. lights).

4. Open protective cover on the positive terminal for jump-lead starting.

5. First, connect the positive cable to the positive terminal for jump-lead starting, then to the positive terminal of the donor battery.   
6. First, connect the negative cable to the negative terminal of the donor battery, then to the ground point for jump-lead starting.   
7. Set the charge current on the battery charger according to the battery capacity.   
. Switch on the battery charger.

# WM 2706IN GENERAL INFORMATION ON AGM VEHICLE BATTERY (ALL MODELS) > CONNECTING THE BATTERY FOR TRICKLE CHARGING

A charger with a current rating of at least 40 A must be connected to the external power supply points/jump-lead starting points.

Set the charger to maximum A (amps).

Switch off allunnecessary loads (e.g. lights).

When working on the vehicle for more than 15 minutes.

When running diagnostics using the Porsche System Tester.

When adjusting the headlights.

When working on or with the Infotainment system.

If the doors, bonnet and rear lid are open for a long period of time or if these components are actuated frequently.

# WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK > WHEN DOES DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR CONTROL UNIT NEED TO BE ADJUSTED?

The distance measuring sensor control unit must be re-adjusted in the following situations:

1. Suspension was aligned and adjusted.   
2. Distance measuring sensor control unit or distance measuring sensor control unit holder was loosened or removed and installed.   
3. Bumper was loosened or removed and installed.   
4. The front end is damaged.   
5. Fault memory entry: ACC sensor incorrectly adjusted (Do0004).   
1.5.1. The misalignment angle is outside of the range -1.5° to +1.5°.

# WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK > REQUIREMENTS FOR TESTING AND ADJUSTMENT

1. Tyre tread depth of the tires of one axle must not deviate by more than 2 mm.   
2. Tyre inflation pressure in accordance with regulations ("Comfort" or "Normal" tire pressure).   
3. As with complete suspension alignment, make sure that there is no sliding base or turnplate at the end stop during alignment.   
1. 3.1. Take the track width and wheel base into consideration.   
4. Check that vehicle weight corresponds to empty weight. Weight of the vehicle ready for driving (completely full fuel tank, reducing agent tank and water reservoir for the windscreen washer/headlight cleaning system, spare wheel, tool kit, jack) without driver.   
5. Spare wheel, tool kit and jack must be located at the positions specified by the vehicle manufacturer.   
6. Vehicle aligned correctly, having been bounced multiple times.   
7. Wheel suspension, steering and steering linkage show no signs of play or damage.   
1.7.1. Check for play and damage and carry out repairs if necessary.   
8. Set vehicles with air suspension to normal level.   
1. 8.1. Switch off ignition, close and lock all doors.   
2. 8.2. Wait 15 seconds until vehicle has settled in normal level.   
3.8.3. Open door and leave it open during the measurement, switch on ignition.

# WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK > SETTING UP THE MEASURING SYSTEM

Check that there is suficient floor space between the vehicle and the adjustment device - the gap between the adjustment device and vehicle must be approx. 120 cm.

The vehicle can be reversed onto the axle alignment platform if there is not enough floor space in front of the measuring platform.

The vehicle must be positioned so that the front and rear axles are centered on turnplates/sliding plates.

# Information

The procedure described here is for the wheel alignment system ML 5000 Porsche WE 1272 and the axle alignment system with DSP508XF sensors WE 1328.

Deviations can occur with other alignment systems.

1. Select the relevant vehicle in the wheel alignment computer.   
2. Select quick function Calibrate distance measuring sensor .   
3. Fit instrument holders onto the wheels on the rear axle.   
4. Fit the rear sensors onto the rear axle using the spoiler adapter (Beissbarth only, this sets the sensors to a lower position).   
5. Align the rear sensors on the rear axle using the spirit level and clamp the instrument holders using the wing screws.

# Information

Once the vehicle and adjustment tool are aligned, the vehicle and adjustment tool must no longer be moved.

1. The vehicle is standing on turnplates/sliding plates that are released on one side , allowing the vehicle to be moved slightly.   
2. If the vehicle is moved while taking measurements on the turnplates, the measurement process must be repeated.   
3. If the adjustment tool is moved following alignment, the measurement process must be repeated.

.Attach the front sensors to the measuring mirror, align using the spirit level and clamp.

1.6.1. Centre the adjustment tool.   
2.6.2. Set distance of adjustment tool and vehicle in accordance with the specifications provided by the measuring equipment manufacturer.   
3. 6.3. The distance between the left sensor and the vehicle -Bl- should be identical to the distance between the right sensor and the vehicle -Br- .

![](images/b983fae759f4f9dda6c0b8658de0f9457c5a3c5a3f077c6a0763fe56f2b74315.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Right Sensor Dimension   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Switch on (initialize) the sensors.

# WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK > PREPARATION FOR ADJUSTING DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR

1. Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least 40 A to the external power feed points.

2. Read out the fault memory using Piwis Tester Il 9818 , create a vehicle analysis log if necessary → OXO3IN CREATING VEHICLE ANALYSIS LOG (VAL) and correct any faults.

3. Remove trim cover -1- from the distance measuring sensor control unit.

1.3.1. Push trim cover up -a-.

2. 3.2. Pull trim cover forward and remove it -b- .

![](images/38f5b8076ee312cca0e42229ec858e4e86b47784d293381621f14d4bdab535cc.webp)  
Fig 1: Removing Trim Cover   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Clean distance measuring sensor control unit and trim cover using commercially available cleaning agent.   
5. Fit the front sensors onto the adjustment device, align using the spirit levels and clamp using the wing screws, and switch them on (initialize).   
6. Set the distance between the adjustment device with reflector VAS 6430/1 WE 1362 and the vehicle in accordance with the specifications provided by the measuring equipment manufacturer.   
1. 6.1. The distance between the left sensor and the vehicle -Bl- should be identical to the distance between the right spirit level and the vehicle -Br- .

![](images/0474b77f1ba52729b15c67f96e9269fb69fc293ca7ee7b34d7b2b26bac2d2f95.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Right Sensor Dimension   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. On the adjustment device, move the mirror into the position -2- in alignment with the marking (-A- the number 2 on the rotary knob must point towards the vehicle).

![](images/01318cf91e19b2090f902786b3b9c08bfc7055b887181bf8278dd2aa27a1506b.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Adjustment Device Position   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# Information

Once the vehicle and adjustment tool are aligned, the vehicle and adjustment tool must no longer be moved.

1. The vehicle is standing on turnplates/sliding plates that are released on one side, allowing the vehicle to be moved.

2. If the vehicle is moved while taking measurements on the turnplates, the measurement process must be repeated.

3. If the adjustment tool is moved following alignment, the measurement process must be repeated.

8. Release turnplates/sliding plates on one side of the vehicle .

9. Start the menu for adjusting the distance measuring sensor control unit, see operating instructions for measuring platform .

10. Before starting the adjustment process, use the laser beam at the mirror -3- on the adjustment device (for switching on the laser beam, see operating instructions for adjustment device) to check that the laser beam strikes the sensor lens. Info:

1. 10.1. The adjustment device is positioned correctly if the laser beam still strikes the sensor lens even after the identical individual toe values have been set.

2. 10.2. If the laser beam does not strike the sensor lens, the alignment of the adjustment device must be repeated.

![](images/1a272347aa93152642472052d5e0a3912331d6de8cd00f9fd867f8ce42667434.webp)  
Fig 4: Identifying Adjustment Device Position   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

11. Align adjustment device at the side:

1. 11.1. The laser beam of the adjustment device must strike the center of the sensor lens.

![](images/091f6acd7db0720df006abfdb61fb81ae52124caec8227425613f0f66448acb7.webp)  
Fig 5: Aligning Adjustment Device   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

12. Use the adjusting screws -1, 2, 3, 4, 5- on the adjustment device to level the mirror's spirit levels -A, B- horizontally.   
13. Use the crank -arrow- on the adjustment device to adjust the mirror so that the laser beam strikes the center of the sensor lens on the vertical line.

![](images/598ba4c67fe26b9f21702a7fd683005b4de12c32f65241092a66262defa1a662.webp)  
Fig 6: Aligning Mirror's Spirit Levels   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

14. Turn the adjustment bar on the adjustment device to the side using the adjustment screw -5- until the green indicator on the adjustment bar is displayed on the measuring platform screen.

![](images/f4c44ae2fce8730597ae6a9d394731970e52413fac035c1457995a5b1a40c320.webp)  
Fig 7: Example Of Adjustment Bar Display

![](images/a198ca16f94086a2775c44e30b7aa9b40aa2d8de89aa352b31d3e5293f5683e9.webp)

# WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR

1. Connect PiWis Tester Il 9818 to the vehicle and start it.

2. Switch on ignition.   
3. Select the required vehicle and the Adaptive cruise control control unit. Press [F12] to continue.   
4. Select the Maintenance/repairs sub-menu in the Adaptive cruise control menu. Press [F12] to continue.   
5. Follow the instructions on Piwis Tester Il 9818 and adjust the distance measuring sensor control unit -1- as required using adjustment tool T-socket wrench for ACC sensor VAS 6190/2 WE 1364 -2- by turning the relevant adjusting screw -3- according to specifications.

![](images/4908f3306ca8f692d9c24224c1afe82b2dc6be653a66a3472f75a71865407167.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Sensor Control Unit Adjusting Screws

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. Repeat the process until PIWIS Tester II 9818 displays the message Adjustment successful.

# WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Switch off ignition and pull remote control out of ignition lock.

2. PIWis Tester Il 9818 must now be disconnected from the vehicle.

3. Disconnect battery charger.

4. Remove sensors and instrument holders.

# Information

Before and after fitting the trim cover for the distance measuring sensor control unit, check the following points:

1. The holder for the distance measuring sensor control unit must not show any signs of deformation, which may have been caused, for example, by removing or installing the trim

cover for the distance measuring sensor control unit. If the holder for the distance measuring sensor control unit is deformed, carefully push it back into shape.

2. If the trim cover is damaged or cracked, replace the trim cover.

3. After fitting the trim cover, check that it is seated correctly and securely.

5. Installtrim cover -1- on the distance measuring sensor control unit.

1.5.1. Fit trim cover -a- .

2.5.2. Push trim cover down -b- until it engages securely.

Fig 1: Installing Trim Cover On Distance Measuring Sensor Control Unit

![](images/4b8a85572d565ef721be2d7d0af9cb09631eae546fcd918afc9903188112bee5.webp)  
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. Perform a test drive and check operation of distance measuring sensor control unit.

7. Read out the fault memory of the distance measuring sensor control unit.

# Information

Always comply with the regulations for handling ESD-sensitive components!

1. Assembly work may only be carried out if the mechanic is wearing the working clothes and shoes approved by Porsche. 2. The new part must only be removed from the ESD (electrostatic discharge) protective

packaging just before installation and at the position at which the part is to be installed.

3. Never touch the electric pins and plug contacts.

3. Release electric plug connection -1- (-2- ) and disconnect it from the distance measuring sensor control unit -3- .

4. Unclip bracket for electric line -4- at the holder for the distance measuring sensor control unit and set electric line aside.

# WM 278519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR

Information

3efore and after fitting the trim cover for the distance measuring sensor control unit, check the following ooints:

The holder for the distance measuring sensor control unit must not show any signs of deformation, which may have been caused, for example, by removing or installing the trim cover for the distance measuring sensor control unit. If the holder for the distance measuring sensor control unit is deformed, carefull push it back into shape.   
If the trim cover is damaged or cracked, replace the trim cover.   
After fitting the trim cover, check that it is seated correctly and securely. 1. Installation is performed in reverse order to removal. 2. Tighten fastening screw at the bottom of the holder for the distance measuring sensor control unit. Tightening torque 2.5 Nm (2 ftlb.) 3. Tighten fastening screw at the top of the holder for the distance measuring sensor control unit. Tightening torque 8 Nm (6 ftlb.)

Check the hallsender rotor before installing it.   
The hallsender rotor must not come into contact with a magnet.

# WM 284419 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HALL-SENDER ROTOR (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > INSTALLING HALL-SENDER ROTOR > INSTALLING ROTOR FOR HALL SENDER

Check the hallsender rotor before installing it.   
The hall-sender rotor must not come into contact with a magnet.

If the hall-sender rotor does come into proximity of a magnet, replace it without exception.

# Information

Sealing rings become damaged as a result of improper fitting. Do not oil sealing rings on the running surface and do not pull sealing rings off the plastic sleeve.

1. Fit hallsender rotor to crankshaft flange using the insertion tool 9837.

# WM 8209AN TEACHING REMOTE CONTROL FOR AUXILIARY HEATING (ALL MODELS)  TEACHING REMOTE CONTROL FOR AUXILIARY HEATING

The remote control for the auxiliary heater can only be taught using the Porsche System Tester.   
A maximum of three remote controls can be taught per vehicle.

![](images/d6eaeea20d6bad39e7c98dce9be63d7efcae32baa0371ea3472514ad905b565b.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Auxiliary Heating Remote Control

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

1. ON button

2. LED

3. OFF button

1. PlWis Tester Il9818 must be connected to the vehicle before starting the System Tester. Switch on ignition.

2. Select the vehicle type.

3. Select the Drive links/checks menu and press [F12] to continue.

4. Select the Teach remote control to receiver menu, press [F12] and follow the instructions on the System Tester.

5. Press [F8] to start the teaching process.

6. After the SEND message appears, press the [OFF] button -3- on the remote control within 5 seconds until the "saved" message appears. The remote control is now taught.

7. To teach other remote controls, repeat the process.

. Carry out a function test on the remote control and then read out the fault memory.

9. PIWis Tester Il 9818 must now be disconnected from the vehicle.

# WM 822019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COMPLETE HEATER (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEATER > REMOVING HEATER

NOTE: Danger of scalding

•Coolant can be very hot.   
•Coolant may be pressurized. → Only remove the heater when the cooling system has cooled down.   
→ By carefully opening the catch on the reservoir, make sure that the cooling system is depressurized.

NOTE: Danger of slipping due to emerging coolant

The emerging coolant will make the floor of the workshop slippery and may cause people to slip and fall over.

→ Collect emerging coolant in a suitable pan.

1. Remove coolant hoses.

1. 1.1. Clamp coolant hoses -1- using hose clamp 3094 -3- .

2. 1.2. Loosen spring band clamps -2- using assembly pliers Nr.72 Pos.1 and pull off coolant hoses -1- .

WARNING: Emerging fuel

1. Risk of fire

Fig 1: Identifying Coolant Hoses

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

→ Avoid contact with hot parts or sources of ignition.   
→ Collect emerging fuel, absorb it if necessary with a suitable binding material and dispose of properly.   
→ Use suction to remove ignitable vapors.   
— Attach warning sign to vehicle in a clearly visible position.

1. 2.1. Loosen spring band clamp -3- using assembly pliers Nr.72 Pos.1  and disconnect fuel line -2- .

# CALIFORNIA > LEGEND

ESC - Emission Standard Category

GVWR - Manufacture's Gross Vehicle Weight Rating

LVW - Loaded Vehicle Weight

PC - Passenger Car

LDT1 - Light-Duty Truck up through 3750 LVW and GVWR no greater than 6000 Ibs.

LDT2 - Light-Duty Truck greater than 3750 LVW and GVWR no greater than 6000 Ibs.

MDV - Medium-Duty Vehicle, GVWR from 6001 to 8500 Ibs.

HC - Hydrocarbon, ppm

CO - Carbon Monoxide, %

NO - Nitric Oxide, ppm

# CALIFORNIA > PASS/FAIL EMISSION STANDARDS = A+B / VTW

PASS/FAIL STANDARDS - Emission standards used to determine if a vehicle passes the emission inspection. A vehicle passes if the emission levels are equal to or less than the standards for HC, CO and NO for ASM 5015 and ASM 2525.

GROSS POLLUTER STANDARDS - Emission standards used to designate a vehicle as a gross polluter A vehicle is designated as a gross polluter if the emission levels at the time of the initial inspection, before repairs are greater than the gross poluter standards for HC, CO or NO for ASM 5015 or ASM 2525.

NOTE: If test data on emission pass/fail rates or gross polluter identification rates indicate adjustments are required, the emission standards may be increased or decreased by the bureau by 30% or by the following tolerances, or standards may be set for any specific vehicle and engine configuration which the bureau determines has excessive errors of commission of omission, whichever is necessary to comply with Section 44001.5 of the Health and Safety Code.

# U. S. EPA REVISED FINAL ASM EMISSION STANDARDS (ASM5015 & ASM2525)

NOTE: EPA has not published a revised final standards for High Altitude, Light Duty Trucks 2 (6000-8500 GVWR), or vehicles older than 1980 model year. EPA guidance as of February 2003 states that a program may choose to use combinations of the Original and the Revised Final Standards.

# U.S. EPA REVISED FINAL ASM EMISSION STANDARDS

![](images/5fbb93535d3c77f3cf7a46c24cd435100b043619d587c60f3314fcc51fc29b6e.webp)

![](images/4949e1a2affc04605d041d3ee0d63872352dd7e1afc6a337a667fd588cdac139.webp)

# U.S. EPA IM240 EMISSION STANDARDS > START-UP STANDARDS

Start-up standards should be used during the first 2 years of program operation. Tier 1 standards are recommended for all 1996 and newer vehicles and may be used for 1994 and newer vehicles certified to Tier 1 standards as well.

# Service Manual: 80 - HEATING - (95B) - MACAN WM 803019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEAT EXCHANGER SUPPLY HOSE (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Drain refrigerant —→ 870317 DRAINING AND FILLING REFRIGERANT .   
2. Remove cowI panel cover — 508719 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COWL PANEL COVER .

# WM 803019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEAT EXCHANGER SUPPLY HOSE(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEATEXCHANGER SUPPLY HOSE > REMOVING HEAT EXCHANGER SUPPLY HOSE

The procedure for removal and installation can be different for other vehicle types.

1. Loosen spring band clamp -1- (-arrow-) .   
2. Pull hose -2- off the heat exchanger connection piece.

![](images/cf57d39f6b8bc927aefe5db7bdad29a4fb59f5e57786bedeccfbdb54053de661.webp)  
Fig 1: Removing Heat Exchanger Hose Connection

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Loosen spring band clamp -1- (-arrow-.

![](images/4f57f68a5823aa416b3c4fbc3baceb7549278cb766f434eb09fa77ee70c42007.webp)  
Fig 2: Loosening Spring Band Clamp

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Pull hose through the grommet in the plenum panel wall and remove it.

# WM 803019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEAT EXCHANGER SUPPLY HOSE(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEATEXCHANGER SUPPLY HOSE > INSTALLING HEAT EXCHANGER SUPPLY HOSE

1. Installation is performed in reverse order.

# WM 803019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEAT EXCHANGER SUPPLY HOSE(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Install cowI panel cover → INSTALLING COWL PANEL COVER .   
2. Fil i refrigerant → DRAINING AND FILLING REFRIGERANT .

# WM 803219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEAT EXCHANGER RETURN HOSE(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Drain refrigerant → 870317 DRAINING AND FILLING REFRIGERANT .   
2. Remove cowI panel cover — 508719 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COWL PANEL COVER .

# WM 803219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEAT EXCHANGER RETURN HOSE(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEATEXCHANGER RETURN HOSE > REMOVING HEAT EXCHANGER RETURN HOSE

The procedure for removal and installation can be different for other vehicle types.

1. Loosen spring band clamps -1- (-arrows-) .

2. Pull hose -2- off the heat exchanger return connection piece and directional-control valve connection piece.

![](images/2ef25d15818a5b8e994847d9c5c7f36b08a99c7e6f07db7838ff8a8593416b4a.webp)  
Fig 1: Removing Heat Exchanger Return Hose

# WM 803219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEAT EXCHANGER RETURN HOSE(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEATEXCHANGER RETURN HOSE > REMOVING HEAT EXCHANGER RETURN HOSE(AUXILIARY HEATING)

1. Loosen spring band clamps -1- (-arrows-) .

2. Pull hose -2- off the heat exchanger return connection piece and directional-control valve connection piece.

![](images/e9aade415f3fe9bbaa96855ef4973ee2183aec8ceea18a455279df3193bd7e52.webp)  
Fig 1: Removing Heat Exchanger Return Hose

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# If auxiliary heating system is not installed:

3. Disconnect spring band clamp -1- on heat exchanger return connection piece -arrow- .

![](images/9c8db2ab175964a3bf816b8b13c7cb31bfa7584cb89acc7c48c33e6716575d35.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Loosen spring band clamp -1- on the auxiliary pump connection piece -arrow- .

![](images/dc74705a987ff1811a2c8314f146b36ec67449816d5081ba168a4dfd13c35f9a.webp)  
Fig 3: Loosening Spring Band Clamp On Auxiliary Pump Connection

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Pull heat exchanger return hose -2- through the grommet in the plenum panel wall and remove it.

# WM 803219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEAT EXCHANGER RETURN HOSE(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEATEXCHANGER RETURN HOSE > INSTALLING HEAT EXCHANGER RETURN HOSE

1. Installation is performed in reverse order.

# WM 803219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEAT EXCHANGER RETURN HOSE(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Install cowI panel cover → 508719 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COWL PANEL COVER .   
2. Fil in refrigerant → DRAINING AND FILLING REFRIGERANT .

# WM 805519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT FOOTWELL OUTLET VENTS(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Applies to left footwell outlet vent:

Remove trim panel under dashboard at the left → 70191901 REMOVING AND INSTALLING TRIM PANEL UNDER DASHBOARD AT THE LEFT .

# Applies to right footwell outlet vent:

Remove glove compartment → 681519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING GLOVE COMPARTMENT .

# WM 805519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT FOOTWELL OUTLET VENTS(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT LEFTFOOTWELL OUTLET VENTS > REMOVING FRONT LEFT FOOTWELL OUTLET VENT

1. Release and disconnect connector -1- for the temperature sensor.   
2. Unscrew fastening screw -2- .   
3. Guide footwell outlet vent out to the left -arrow- .

![](images/b6a8f936e87c43583bcba1421faaab3a7d094e330674625496f39329be921305.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Front Left Footwell Outlet Vent Temperature Sensor

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. If the footwell outlet vent will be replaced, the temperature sensor must be converted beforehand. → Temperature sensor

![](images/93bcb46a46a9e6114a73731927ebbeef194b6270e8e04d453903e591f08d1b91.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Temperature Sensor

# WM 805519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT FOOTWELL OUTLET VENTS(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT LEFTFOOTWELL OUTLET VENTS > INSTALLING FRONT LEFT FOOTWELL OUTLET VENT

1. Installation is performed in reverse order.

# WM 805519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT FOOTWELL OUTLET VENTS(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT RIGHTFOOTWELL OUTLET VENTS > REMOVING FOOTWELL OUTLET VENT AT THEFRONT RIGHT

1. Release and disconnect connector -1- for the temperature sensor.   
2. Unscrew fastening screw -2- .   
.Guide footweloutlet vent out to the right -arrow-.

![](images/602eacd5a3fd16b270a2720636e92e5208721669ba0957e8f3f2dd6a76c4d6b1.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Front Right Footwell Outlet Vent Temperature Sensor

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. If the footwell outlet vent will be replaced, the temperature sensor must be converted beforehand. → Temperature sensor

![](images/23da0f92c2417d1e0f71c4d60d80144fe1721c0c4d1c6eb56d2ad09540f7d775.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Temperature Sensor

# WM 805519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT FOOTWELL OUTLET VENTS(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT RIGHTFOOTWELL OUTLET VENTS > INSTALLING FOOTWELL OUTLET VENT AT THEFRONT RIGHT

1. Installtion is performed in reverse order. Observe specified tightening torques: Left footwell outlet vent to body: Right footwell outlet vent to air conditioner:

# WM 8209AN TEACHING REMOTE CONTROL FOR AUXILIARY HEATING (ALL MODELS)  TEACHING REMOTE CONTROL FOR AUXILIARY HEATING

The remote control for the auxiliary heater can only be taught using the Porsche System Tester.   
A maximum of three remote controls can be taught per vehicle.

![](images/d289167b37e00ef9a3ce079b3a7385c89d29d4748f1888061198cce89bf18ce8.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Auxiliary Heating Remote Control

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

1. ON button

2. LED

3. OFF button

1. PlWis Tester Il9818 must be connected to the vehicle before starting the System Tester. Switch on ignition.

2. Select the vehicle type.

3. Select the Drive links/checks menu and press [F12] to continue.

4. Select the Teach remote control to receiver menu, press [F12] and follow the instructions on the System Tester.

5. Press [F8] to start the teaching process.

6. After the SEND message appears, press the [OFF] button -3- on the remote control within 5 seconds until the "saved" message appears. The remote control is now taught.

7. To teach other remote controls, repeat the process.

. Carry out a function test on the remote control and then read out the fault memory.

9. PIWis Tester Il 9818 must now be disconnected from the vehicle.

# WM 822019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COMPLETE HEATER (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEATER > REMOVING HEATER

NOTE: Danger of scalding

•Coolant can be very hot.   
•Coolant may be pressurized. → Only remove the heater when the cooling system has cooled down.   
→ By carefully opening the catch on the reservoir, make sure that the cooling system is depressurized.

NOTE: Danger of slipping due to emerging coolant

The emerging coolant will make the floor of the workshop slippery and may cause people to slip and fall over.

→ Collect emerging coolant in a suitable pan.

1. Remove coolant hoses.

1. 1.1. Clamp coolant hoses -1- using hose clamp 3094 -3- .

2. 1.2. Loosen spring band clamps -2- using assembly pliers Nr.72 Pos.1 and pull off coolant hoses -1- .

WARNING: Emerging fuel

1. Risk of fire

Fig 1: Identifying Coolant Hoses

![](images/1a7df25032c468d52c91a33913ac635fb28c1b9c2f2d24233df7fd206c990720.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

→ Avoid contact with hot parts or sources of ignition.   
→ Collect emerging fuel, absorb it if necessary with a suitable binding material and dispose of properly.   
→ Use suction to remove ignitable vapors.   
→ Attach warning sign to vehicle in a clearly visible position.

2. Disconnect fuel line.

1. 2.1. Loosen spring band clamp -3- using assembly pliers Nr.72 Pos.1 and disconnect fuel line -2- .

# WM 824519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FUEL PUMP FOR AUXILIARY HEATING(ALL MODELS) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING FUEL PUMP FOR AUXILIARYHEATING > REMOVING FUEL PUMP FOR AUXILIARY HEATING

WARNING: Emerging fuel

Risk of fire → Disconnect the battery.

→ Avoid contact with hot parts or sources of ignition.

→ Allow engine to cool down.

→ Relieve the fuel pressure before opening the fuel lines.

→ Collect emerging fuel, absorb it if necessary with a suitable binding material and dispose of properly.

→ Use suction to remove ignitable vapors.

— Attach warning sign to vehicle in a clearly visible position.

1. Loosen fuel pump -1- from the holder -2- .   
2. Release and disconnect connector -5- .   
3. Disconnect line -3- for the auxiliary heating and pull it off the fuel pump.   
4. Disconnect fuel line -4- to the fuel tank.

5. Remove fuel pump -1- .

![](images/3fcc2d5a741239cdc9aca7bffc8cda7c3604c921d0f0e0897a06f1906f3d4810.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Auxiliary Heating Fuel Pump

# Information

There is no guarantee that re-used clamps will secure the component properly.   
Removed clamps must be replaced.

•Coolant can be very hot.   
Coolant may be pressurized.

→ Only remove the heater when the cooling system has cooled down.

1. Release electric plug connection -1- from the circulating pump -2- and disconnect it.

9. Disconnect heat exchanger return hose at the connection point for the passenger compartment → 803219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEAT EXCHANGER RETURN HOSE .

10. Remove front footwell outlet vent (at the left and right) → 805519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT FOOTWELL OUTLET VENT .

Before re-installing the component, check the O-rings of the refrigerant lines for damage and replace them if necessary.

Wet the O-rings of the refrigerant lines with refrigerant oil.

Close offallines and connections using suitable stoppers during removal.

Do not open the stoppers for the lines and connections until shortly before installation.

# WM 870101 CHECKING AIR-CONDITIONING SYSTEM (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > TROUBLESHOOTING THE AIR-CONDITIONING SYSTEM FOLLOWING COMPLAINTS ABOUT COOLING OUTPUT

The troubleshooting steps shown must be used if complaints are received about the cooling output of the air-conditioning system.

→ 8XOOIN INSTRUCTIONS FOR REPAIRING AIR-CONDITIONING SYSTEMS AND STORING SPARE PARTS .

# Information

If it is not possible to clearly detect a leak using a leak detector, then only the leak detector additive supplied by SPEKTRONICS may be used. Leak detector additive: Traserline TP 3860 in dissolved form.

This leak detector additive is available from service equipment providers (e.g. Waeco). → WE1281 Air conditioning service equipment RS 2

For filing this Traser additive, special adapter kits are required, which are also available from service equipment providers (e.g. Waeco).

Information on how to use the air-conditioning system and the procedure for filing it can be found in the operating instructions for the adapter kits.

# WM 870101 FUNCTION TEST ON AIR CONDITIONING (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > FUNCTION TEST ON AIR CONDITIONING > GENERAL INFORMATION

The air outlet temperatures at the center vent on the dashboard and the high pressure in the air-conditioning system must not be higher or lower than the specified tolerance ranges after a running time of 7 minutes (high-pressure measurement).

# WM 870101 FUNCTION TEST ON AIR CONDITIONING (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > FUNCTION TEST ON AIR CONDITIONING > PROCEDURE AND GENERAL REQUIREMENTS FOR TESTING

The safety regulations must be observed during all work on the refrigerant system! → 8X00IN SAFETY REGULATIONS FOR WORKING ON AIR-CONDITIONED VEHICLES AND DEALING WITH REFRIGERANT R134A , → 8XOOIN SAFETY REGULATIONS FOR EXTRACTION AND FILLING SYSTEMS .

# Information

If the specified nominal values are not reached, the air conditioning must be checked for leaks and repaired.

# Information

Check condensed water drain tubes: Must not be blocked by wax or underbody protection or otherwise dirty. Condensate must be able to drain away freely.   
Check fresh-air intake system: Water must not be allwed to run into the air conditioner. Must be completely dirt-free.   
Check that there is suficient ventilation in the outside-temperature sensor area.   
•Do not allow heat from the warm engine to build up near the outside-temperature sensor.

Check particle fiter: Must be dry and not excessively dirty.

Condenser must be dirt-free.

Make sure that all servo motors/flaps move to their end positions.

Switch on MONO mode or SYNC mode using the button on the front air conditioning control panel.

1. Connect air conditioning service unit. → 870317 DRAINING AND FILLING REFRIGERANT .

. Measure outside temperature using a thermometer.

3. Open allair outlet vents on the dashboard/center console (direct the blower towards the test person if necessary).

4. Insert sensor of the temperature measuring device approx. 4 cm into the middle of the left center vent.

5. Check stopwatch and keep an eye on the relevant temperature and high pressure on the air conditioning service unit.

6. Switch on ignition.

7. Open driver's and passenger's side windows and close sliding roof.

8. Press A/C Max button.

9. Start the engine and leave it running at idle speed (do not rev engine unnecessarily after starting!).

10. Operate air conditioning for 5 minutes at idle speed.

11. Increase engine speed depending on engine type and maintain a constant engine speed for 2 minutes. Start the time measurement immediately.

1. 11.1. Increase engine speed on V6 petrol vehicles to 2, 000 RPM.

2. 11.2. Increase engine speed on diesel vehicles to 1, 500 RPM.

12. Note center vent temperature and pressure values after 2 minutes.

13. Compare values (center vent temperature and pressure values) with the specified tolerances.
