# WM 870317 DRAINING AND FILLING REFRIGERANT (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > TECHNICAL VALUES

![](images/7472f76a796e1c996210e49bb2ed0d5e87746b5786344c3a7ecfab3f1a5345e2.webp)

# WM 870317 DRAINING AND FILLING REFRIGERANT (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > DRAINING AND FILLING REFRIGERANT > ASSEMBLY WORK INVOLVING THE REFRIGERANT SYSTEM

During all work on the air-conditioning system which necessitates opening the refrigerant system, the system contents must first be disposed of in accordance with regulations!

Dirt and moisture must be kept out of the air-conditioning system's pipe system!

Thorough cleanliness must be ensured during all work!

System components must never be cleaned on the inside with hot steam!

Use only nitrogen for cleaning purposes!

When replacing a component, all openings must be closed offusing suitable stoppers immediately after opening the system!

# WM 870317 DRAINING AND FILLING REFRIGERANT (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > DRAINING AND FILLING REFRIGERANT > GENERAL INSTALLATION SEQUENCE

The charging valves are located in the plenum panel at the rear left.

1. Screw off the protection caps on the charging valves. Be careful of the sealing rings when disconnecting or connecting the hose connections! Before connecting the high-pressure and low-pressure lines for the air conditioner to the vehicle, remove any refrigerant remaining in the lines by suction. 2. Connect the high-pressure and low-pressure lines on the air conditioner.

# Information

In the case of servicing equipment with a transparent oil separator, read and take note of the oil level before removing the refrigerant.

Do not carr out this step on empty air-conditioning systems (pressure gauge approx. 0 bar) because if you do, air will get into the refrigerant bottle.

If the vehicle is cold, it may be necessary to repeat the suction procedure until all refrigerant has been removed from the air-conditioning system. This step is carried out automatically with some units.

1.2.1. 2. 2.2. Leave the engine running for a short time with the air conditioning on, then connect the high-pressure and low-pressure lines of the air conditioner. 3.2.3. Open the valves of the high-pressure and low-pressure lines.

3. Remove refrigerant by suction.

1. 3.1. If the vehicle is cold, it may be necessary to repeat the suction procedure until all refrigerant has been removed from the air-conditioning system. This step is carried out automatically with some units.

2. 3.2. Wait for approx. 2 minutes after the servicing equipment has switched itself off. If the pressure gauge reading rises above 0 bar, repeat the suction process.

3.3.3. Drain the extracted refrigerant oil into a measuring cup on the servicing equipment and determine the volume.

# Information

The open air-conditioning system should not be left open unnecessarily, but must be closed off using suitable stoppers immediately after being opened.

4. Carry out repairs.

# The desiccator must be replaced in the following situations:

1. Refrigerant circuit is open for > 20 minutes.

Amount of refrigerant extracted is < 30% of the required quantity.

3. Refrigerant circuit has been open for an indefinite period of time (gradual leak, stone damage to condenser).

4. Air-conditioning compressor has become blocked.

5. Dryer cartridge is damaged.

6. After opening the packaging and line connections (on a new desiccator), the desiccator must be installed within 20 minutes at the latest and the refrigerant circuit must be closed, evacuated and filled.

# The desiccator must not be replaced in the following situations:

1. If the components are closed off using stoppers immediately after opening the refrigerant circuit and the refrigerant circuit is closed and evacuated within 20 minutes at the latest.

1.4.1. Before closing off the refrigerant circuit, check whether the desiccator needs to be replaced.

2.4.2. If necessary, reconnect high-pressure and low-pressure lines.

5. Evacuate the system and check for leaks.

1. 5.1. If the air-conditioning system has been opened, evacuation should last at least 20 minutes so that the moisture can evaporate and be removed by suction.

2. 5.2. If the air-conditioning system has been open for a long time, evacuation can be carried out for up to 120 minutes.

3. 5.3. Check the pressure gauge for approx. 2 minutes. If the pressure rises, air is entering the vehicle's air-conditioning system. The leak must be located and repaired.

If the pressure remains constant, add refrigerant oil.

# Information

Only ND8 refrigerant oil must be used.

6. Add refrigerant oil.

1.6.1. For units without an integrated oil filing system:

2. 6.2. Start the vacuum pump. At the start of this vacuum phase, add the measured quantity of refrigerant oil using an oil injector or a hose disconnected from the servicing equipment. Reconnect the hose to the servicing equipment immediately after adding the oil.

3.6.3. For units with an integrated oil filling system: Add the measured quantity of refrigerant oil and wait for it to be taken in.

4.6.4. Do not allow any air to be taken in, otherwise Step 5 must be repeated.

7. Evacuate the system.

1. 7.1. If the air-conditioning system has been opened, evacuation should last at least 20 minutes so that the moisture can evaporate and be removed by suction.

2. 7.2. If the air-conditioning system has been open for a long time, evacuation can be carried out for up to 120 minutes.

3.7.3. For equipment with an integrated oil fling system, add refrigerant oil now.

. Fill the air-conditioning system.

1.8.1. Using the servicing equipment, add the refrigerant quantity stated in the service information to the air-conditioning lines → 8XOOIN TECHNICAL DATA FOR AIR-CONDITIONING SYSTEM .

2. 8.2. As refrigerant usually flows instead of being pumped, it may not be possible - especially if the vehicle is warm and the servicing equipment is cold - to add the entire quantity. If this is the case, switch the engine and air conditioning on. Wait for the suction pressure to fall below 2 bar. Now open the low-pressure valve on the unit slowly and carefully until the remaining quantity has been added.

NOTE: Excessively high pressure in refrigerant circuit

1. Risk of damage to air-conditioning compressor → Do not allow the low-pressure gauge to exceed — Nominal value: 3 bar at any time.

# 3.8.3.

9. Add refrigerant from both connection hoses to the air-conditioning system in the vehicle.

1.9.1. The refrigerant in the high-pressure and low-pressure lines is part of the filing capacity of the refrigerant in the air-conditioning system in the vehicle.

2.9.2. Close the valve on the high-pressure line and disconnect it from the vehicle.

3.9.3. Start the engine and air-conditioning system. When the pressure on both pressure gauges falls below 2 bar, close the valve on the low-pressure line and disconnect it from the vehicle.

# Information

After filing the air-conditioning system, the valve on the high-pressure and low-pressure connection must be checked using a leak detector.

The protection caps must not be fitted.

Position the leak detector at a specified distance (see operating instructions for each leak detector) above the valves and check the valves for signs of any leaks.

10. If there are no leaks in the high-pressure and low-pressure connection valves, fit the caps.

WM 873419 REMOVING AND INSTALLING AIR-CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING AIR-CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR > REPLACING AIR-CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR

NOTE: Fill level too low

Risk of damage to components.

→ Do not start the engine.

→ Do not tow the vehicle.

NOTE: Too much or too litle refrigerant oil in air conditioning circuit •Reduced cooling output • Lack of lubrication and failure of the air conditioning compressor → If a new air conditioning compressor or a component in the circuit is replaced, the oil quantity must be checked and adjusted.

# Information

All connection points must be completely dirt-free.

The air-conditioning compressor must be dry (washing the vehicle) and the air-conditioning compressor and lines must be free of moisture.

The connection points must be closed after they have been opened. Use the original transport caps.

A clean measuring cylinder with a capacity of approx. 300 ml is required.

# Information

•If the air-conditioning compressor is blocked or seized up, then additional steps must be carried out to ensure that the air-conditioning system is working. See  WORK STEPS FOR BLOCKED OR SEIZED UP AIR-CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR

# Information

New air-conditioning compressors are pressurized and filled with the required amount of oil for the refrigerant circuit.   
The remaining oil quantity in the individual components must therefore be taken into account!   
Refrigerant oil from the compressor or refrigerant oil removed by suction from a previously run air-conditioning system may no longer be used (special-category waste)! 1. Carefully open the cap on the high-pressure side and relieve the pressure from the air-conditioning compressor -A- . .Open the oil fller screw -B- on the air-conditioning compressor.

![](images/adabf2841956de08241277ea16e67bdd461cdd15fe8be20a3e0f9fac606afc0d.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Cap And Oil Filler Screw (Shown Examples, Original May Differ)   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Empty approx. 40 cm3 of refrigerant oil out of the air-conditioning compressor and into a measuring glass. The remaining quantity of oil (approx. 60 cm3 ) remains in the air-conditioning compressor.

4. Always replace the sealing ring for the oil filler screw.

5. Use fastening screws from the new air-conditioning compressor. Replace O-rings and coat new O-rings with refrigerant oil.

# WM 873419 REMOVING AND INSTALLING AIR-CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING AIR-CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR > WORK STEPS FOR BLOCKED/SEIZED UP AIR-CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR

1. Remove desiccator from the condenser. → REMOVING AND INSTALLING DESICCATOR .   
2. Check the desiccator for wear/chips.

If there are signs of wear/chips:

3. Remove the refrigerant line between the compressor and condenser. → 874319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COMPRESSOR/CONDENSER LINE .

4. Replace the refrigerant line between the compressor and condenser.

5. Replace the condenser with desiccator. → 875019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CONDENSER .

6. Instal the new refrigerant line between the compressor and condenser. → INSTALLING COMPRESSOR/CONDENSER LINE .

7. Install air-conditioning compressor → 873419 REMOVING AND INSTALLING AIR-CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR .

# If there are no signs of wear/chips:

1. Replace the desiccator. → REMOVING AND INSTALLING DESICCATOR .

# WM 8XOOIN AIR CONDITIONING (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > DISTRIBUTIONOF OIL QUANTITY IN REFRIGERANT CIRCUIT

Oil removed by suction must be returned to the system!   
Refrigerant oil removed from a previously run air-conditioning system may no longer be used (special-category waste)!   
After the refrigerant has been removed by suction and a component has been replaced, the oil quantity must be determined and topped up by the quantity remaining in the removed component!

When individual components listed in the follwing table are replaced, the measured oil quantity removed by suction from the refrigerant circuit and the quantity in the component must be returned to the refrigerant circuit.

In order to use a new compressor in a refrigerant circuit that is already functional, the oil quantity of the new compressor must be reduced by max. 47 cm . The compressor oil quantity is 110 cm for a new compressor in as-delivered state. 3 3

# WM 8XOOIN INSTRUCTIONS FOR CARRYING OUT GENERAL REPAIRS ON VEHICLES WITH AUXILIARY HEATING (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > INSTRUCTIONS FOR CARRYING OUT GENERAL REPAIRS ON VEHICLES WITH AUXILIARY HEATING

Perform on-board diagnosis of the auxiliary heating system using the vehicle diagnostic tester. If parts of the fuel system were removed or replaced, make sure that allcomponents for extracting fuel for the auxiliary heating system are installed properly.

•To avoid confusing the coolant hoses, mark them before removal.

-ollowing repair work near the fuel line for the auxiliary heating system, check the following points:

Check that the fuel lines are routed flush with the underbody and are protected from mechanical damage.   
Check that the fuel line for the auxiliary heating system is protected against high temperatures that could cause malfunctions.   
Check that the fuel line is not touching any hot components.

# WM 8XOOIN INSTRUCTIONS FOR REPAIRING AIR-CONDITIONING SYSTEMS AND STORING SPARE PARTS (ALL MODELS) > INSTRUCTIONS FOR REPAIRING AIR-CONDITIONING SYSTEMS AND STORING SPARE PARTS

If you need to work on the refrigerant circuit, close off all openings immediately using commercially available rubber stoppers.

Store air-conditioning components in a dry and sealed-off area.

Blast air-conditioning components with nitrogen before refitting.

When fitting parts, do not remove stoppers until shortly before installtion. Likewise, do not remove the protective foil from the desiccator until just before installation. The desiccator absorbs moisture from the air and is then useless.

Do not carry out repairs in the open during damp weather.

The desiccator should be replaced as soon as one component of the air conditioning system has beer replaced or if the air conditioning system was open for > 20 minutes.

Moisture in the refrigerant circuit not only leads to poor cooling, but oversaturation can also cause the desiccator to disintegrate and contaminate the air-conditioning system from inside. This can result in expensive and complicated repairs.

Evacuate the refrigerant circuit according to instructions.

Use a pressure reducer when working with nitrogen.

# WM 8XOOIN NOMINAL VALUES FOR PRESSURES AND TEMPERATURES (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > GENERAL INFORMATION

The air outlet temperatures at the center vent on the dashboard and the high pressure in the air-conditioning system must not be higher or lower than the specified tolerance ranges after a

# WM 8XOOIN NOMINAL VALUES FOR PRESSURES AND TEMPERATURES (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > PROCEDURE AND GENERAL REQUIREMENTS FOR TESTING

The safety regulations must be observed during al work on the refrigerant system! → 8X00IN SAFETY REGULATIONS FOR WORKING ON AIR-CONDITIONED VEHICLES AND DEALING WITH REFRIGERANT R134A , → 8XOOIN SAFETY REGULATIONS FOR EXTRACTION AND FILLING SYSTEMS .

# Information

If the specified nominal values are not reached, the air conditioning must be checked for leaks and repaired.

# Information

Check condensed water drain tubes: Must not be blocked by wax or underbody protection or otherwise dirty. Condensate must be able to drain away freely.   
Check fresh-air intake system: Water must not be allowed to run into the air conditioner. Must be completely dirt-free.   
Check that there is sufficient ventilation in the outside-temperature sensor area.   
Do not allow heat from the warm engine to build up near the outside-temperature sensor.   
Check particle filter: Must be dry and not excessively dirty.   
Condenser must be dirt-free.   
Make sure that all servo motors/flaps move to their end positions.   
Switch on MONO mode or SYNC mode using the buton on the front air conditioning control panel. 1. Connect air conditioning service unit. → 870317 DRAINING AND FILLING REFRIGERANT . 2. Measure outside temperature using a thermometer. 3. Open al air outlet vents on the dashboard/center console (direct the blower towards the test person if necessary). 4. Insert sensor of the temperature measuring device approx. 4 cm into the middle of the left center vent. 5. Check stopwatch and keep an eye on the relevant temperature and high pressure on the air conditioning service unit. 6. Switch on ignition. 7. Open driver's and passenger's side windows and close sliding roof.

8. Press A/C Max button.

9. Start the engine and leave it running at idle speed (do not rev engine unnecessarily after starting!).

10. Operate air conditioning for 5 minutes at idle speed.

11. Increase engine speed depending on engine type and maintain a constant engine speed for 2 minutes. Start the time measurement immediately.

1. 11.1. Increase engine speed on V6 petrol vehicles to 2, 000 RPM.

2. 11.2. Increase engine speed on diesel vehicles to 1, 500 RPM.

12. Note center vent temperature and pressure values after 2 minutes.

13. Compare values (center vent temperature and pressure values) with the specified tolerances.

# WM 8XOOIN RULES RELATING TO CLEANLINESS FOR WORKING ON THE AUXILIARY HEATING SYSTEM AND FUEL SYSTEM (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > RULES RELATING TO CLEANLINESS FOR WORKING ON THE AUXILIARY HEATING SYSTEM AND FUEL SYSTEM

•Thoroughly clean connection points and adjacent areas before loosening them. Place removed parts on a clean surface (use film or paper, no fibre-shedding cloths) and cover

them.

If repair work will not be carried out immediately, the parts must be covered carefully or sealed.

•Only install clean parts.

Do not take spare parts out of the packaging until just before installation.

Do not use parts that have been left without packaging.

When the fuel system is open, do not:

• Use compressed air.   
Start the engine.   
Switch on auxiliary heating.

# WM 8XOOIN SAFETY MEASURES WHEN WORKING ON VEHICLES WITH AUXILIARY HEATING (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > SAFETY MEASURES WHEN WORKING ON VEHICLES WITH AUXILIARY HEATING

It is important to ensure that the auxiliary heating timer is deactivated during a workshop visit and while working on the vehicle in order to prevent the auxiliary heating system from coming on unintentionally.   
The preset timer must be activated again following repair work.   
The auxiliary heating system must not be on or switched on in areas in which there is a danger of fire and risk of explosion.   
The auxiliary heating system must not be on or switched on in enclosed spaces without an exhaust extraction system.   
Always comply with the applicable safety regulations when working on the fuel system.   
The engine must not be started if components of the fuel system (e.g. metering pump, fuel line, fuel supply indicator) are removed or open.   
Before starting repair work on the auxiliary heating system: Relieve overpressure in the cooling system by carefully opening the catch on the coolant reservoir.   
The function of the auxiliary heating system must be checked following repair work on the auxiliary heating system or fuel system.   
When repair work is complete, perform on-board diagnosis of the auxiliary heating system using the vehicle diagnostic tester.

# WM 8XOOIN SAFETY REGULATIONS FOR EXTRACTION AND FILLING SYSTEMS (ALL MODELS) > SAFETY REGULATIONS FOR EXTRACTION AND FILLING

WARNING: Improper handling of the filing system for the air conditioning.

•Unnecessary damage to the environment due to emerging refrigerant.

→ Before connecting the filing system to the air-conditioning, make sure that the manual shut-off valves are closed.

→ Before disconnecting the filing system from the air-conditioning, make sure that the process is complete so that no refrigerant can escape into the atmosphere.

→ After the purified refrigerant has been filled into an external compressed gas botle from the filing system, the manual shut-off valves on the bottle and on the filling system should be closed.

→ Do not expose the filling system to moisture or use in a damp environment.

— Shut off the power supply at the filling system before carrying out maintenance work.

→ An extension cable with cross-sectional area of at least 2.5 mm 2 should be used only when absolutely necessary.

→ In the case of fire, the external bottle should be removed.

→ Fil the oil extracted from the air-conditioning system into a suitable closable container (the refrigerant oil contains small quantities of refrigerant).

→ The filig system must be secured to prevent rolling.

# WM 8XOOIN SAFETY REGULATIONS FOR WORKING ON AIR-CONDITIONED VEHICLES AND HANDLING REFRIGERANT R134A (ALL MODELS) > GENERAL SAFETY REGULATIONS FOR REFRIGERANTS

CAUTION: Extreme heating of air-conditioning system e.g. from sunlight shining into the vehicle or as a result of welding and soldering work.

Danger of fire due to excessive heating of air conditioning.

Danger of environmental pollution due to emerging refrigerant.

→ When carrying out repairs on the air-conditioning system, the system must be emptied by suction and the refrigerant must be purified. Chlorine-free refrigerants must also not be allowed to escape into the atmosphere and must be disposed of correctly.

→ Due to their chemical composition, different refrigerants must not be mixed with each other! This also applies for smaller quantities.

→ No welding, soldering or hot-air heating may take place on parts of the filed air-conditioning system or

in its immediate vicinity.

→ While drying after painting work, the temperature burden on the vehicle must not exceed two hours at a maximum temperature of 80°C.

→ Whether or not the system is filled with refrigerant, the heating causes a very strong overpressure which can cause damage to the system or even lead to an explosion.

→ R 134a is completely non-toxic at normal temperatures, but it decomposes upon contact with a flame or at high temperatures.

→ Refrigerant bottles must not be thrown and must not be subjected to direct sunlight or other heat sources for an extended period when full.

→ The maximum permissible temperature of a filled refrigerant bottle must not exceed 45 °C.

→ Risk of injury! High temperatures from open flames or hot solids causes chemical breakdown of refrigerant gas. Inhalation of the resulting breakdown products leads to coughing and nausea.

WARNING: Caustic fluids

• Danger of chemical burns

→ Avoid contact with caustic fluid.

→ Wear personal protective gear.

→ Ensure that there is good ventilation.

→ If you do come into contact, wash off immediately with plenty of warm water and contact a doctor if necessary.

WARNING: Refrigerant

Danger of freezing

→ Avoid contact with refrigerant.

→ Wear personal protective gear.

→ Observe the safety regulations for working on air-conditioned vehicles and dealing with refrigerant.

→ Observe the safety regulations for extraction and filing systems.

→ Observe the instructions for repairing air conditioning systems and storing spare parts.

# Information

The following safety measures should be followed for refrigerant R134a (additional regulations may apply in certain countries).

If repair work necessitates opening the refrigerant circuit, the refrigerant circuit must first be emptied.

Avoid all contact with liquid or gaseous refrigerants. If refrigerant should escape despite all safety measures having been taken, do not inhale the resulting refrigerant/air mixture. Switch on extraction systems, protect hands with rubber gloves and protect eyes with protective goggles.

If refrigerant gets onto any other body parts despite all safety measures having been taken, these should also be rinsed immediately and thoroughly with water for at least 15 minutes.

Although refrigerant R134a is non-flammable, smoking, welding, soldering and hard-soldering is prohibited in a room containing refrigerant.

# WM 8XOOIN SAFETY REGULATIONS FOR WORKING ON AIR-CONDITIONED VEHICLES AND HANDLING REFRIGERANT R134A (ALL MODELS) > EMPTYING THE REFRIGERANT CIRCUIT

Refrigerant R134a contributes to the greenhouse effect as soon as it is released into the Earth's atmosphere.

Refrigerant should not be released into the environment but is to be extracted from the refrigerant circuit using an extraction or service station. The extracted refrigerant is then prepared again on-site or returned to the manufacturer for environmentally-friendly disposal (varying or additional regulations may apply in certain countries).

# WM 8XOOIN SAFETY REGULATIONS FOR WORKING ON AIR-CONDITIONED VEHICLES AND HANDLING REFRIGERANT R134A (ALL MODELS) > WORKING ON THE REFRIGERANT CIRCUIT

WARNING: Toxic substances

Danger of poisoning or suffocation •Danger of burns to the eyes and skin

→ Ventilate the work area well.   
→ Never ingest or inhale.   
→ Read specific information on the Hazard Sheet.   
→ Do not smoke, eat or drink in the work area.

# WM 8XOOIN SAFETY REGULATIONS FOR WORKING ON AIR-CONDITIONED VEHICLES AND HANDLING REFRIGERANT R134A (ALL MODELS) > PAINTING

WARNING: Painting work on vehicles with air-conditioning

Material damage due to the air-conditioning system bursting.

→ When carrying out repairs involving painting work, object temperatures in the drying oven or its preheating zone should not exceed 80 °C.

# WM 8XOOIN SAFETY REGULATIONS FOR WORKING ON AIR-CONDITIONED VEHICLES AND HANDLING REFRIGERANT R134A (ALL MODELS) > NOTES ON GENERAL REPAIRS

The refrigerant circuit of the air-conditioning system may only be emptied and opened if this is necessary in order to comply with safety measures or if components of the refrigerant circuit have to be replaced.

The air-conditioning refrigerant circuit also remains closed during all other standard vehicle repair work

# Contact corrosion!

For this reason, the manufacturer only fits connecting elements with a special surface coating.

Contact corrosion can occur if unsuitable connecting elements (screws, nuts, washers, rivets, plugs, adhesives, etc.) are used.

Only use original Porsche parts!

Risk of damage to control unit

Coding in the control unit is aborted   
• Malfunctions in control unit, even during programming

The PIWis Tester Il9818 is connected to the vehicle via a diagnostic socket. The diagnostic socket is located inside the vehicle close to the driver's A-pillar below the instrument panel.

The diagnostic application starts. 3. Select the DME menu and press [F12]. 4. Select the Actual values, input signals menu. 5. Select the Catalytic converter diesel particle filter menu and press [F12]. 6. Select K100 diesel particle filter, bank 1, soot mass (soot level) calculated and press [F12]. 7. The value is now displayed in grams.   
oIf the value is greater than 40 g , the message "Check DPF" appears in the instrument cluster. Release the diesel particle filter by performing a regeneration drive as described in the Driver's Manual. If the regeneration drive could not be completed successfully, cary out a service regeneration. — 033500 FAULT MEMORY FOR ON-BOARD DIAGNOSIS

# EMISSIONS MAINTENANCE REMINDER RESET INDEX

![](images/bb38412560612e37707f5d5b48d59a50e30892febd3af0017d8e1ac62e7c285e.webp)

# EMISSIONS MAINTENANCE REMINDER > EMISSIONS MAINTENANCE REMINDER RESET - PROCEDURE 1

Oxygen sensor (O2S) light wil come on at 30,000 mile intervals as a reminder to replace sensor. After replacing sensor, reset warning light as follows:

1. On 911 models, disconnect battery ground cable and remove speedometer. Counter will be visible through speedometer mounting hole. Using a thick piece of wire or a thin rod, press White reset button all the way in against stop. Ensure warning light is out.   
2. On 924 models, after replacing oxygen sensor and with vehicle stillraised, locate mileage counter on left engine mount. Using a thick wire or thin metal rod, push in reset button all the way to stop. Ensure warning light is out.   
3. On 928 and 928S with ClS system, counter is located to right of passenger seat floor (near door sill. Remove counter cover retaining screw and cover. Press reset button all the way in against stop. Ensure warning light is out.

# MAINTENANCE SERVICE REMINDER > MAINTENANCE SERVICE REMINDER RESET - PROCEDURE 2

If the engine oil is replaced during maintenance work, the service interval must be reset.

# Standard Service Interval Reset:

1. In the PST2 (Porsche System Tester 2), select Instrument cluster, then press >.

2. Select the Coding menu, then press >>.

3. Select Reset Service Interval Display menu, then press >.

NOTE: Depending on the country, additional items are checked in the case of the V6 model. These items must be selected on a country-specific basis.

4. Select Reset menu and confirm with F8.

5. Quit menu, shut down PST and disconnect from vehicle.

# Maintenance Calculator Reset:

NOTE: All Cayenne V6 engines are factory filled with an engine oil of VW specification "50300". New vehicles produced have their maintenance calculator set for an oil change service interval of 10,000 miles (15,000 km) or 1 year. The maintenance calculator in the Cayenne (V6) determines the time of the engine oil change depending on the vehicle load and driving style, and requests for "Service" via the multi-function display.

After changing the oil, the oil change service interval must be reset in the instrument cluster using the PST2 (Porsche System Tester 2). The country version for which the new vehicle was produced is stored in the control modules. The PST2 automatically detects this country version before resetting the maintenance calculator and depending on this, offers the following options for oil change service intervals:

1. The country version of the vehicle corresponds to one of the countries listed in Table 1. Depending on the engine oil used for the oil change, the following selection options for oil change service intervals are available in the selection menu of the PST2 for these vehicles, when resetting the maintenance calculator with the PST2:

1. 1.1 If an engine oil in accordance with the VW specification "50300" was used: The oil change service interval is set in the maintenance calculator for an oil change service interval of up 30,000 km or 2 years, after selecting and confirming this oil quality in the PST2 menu => "Engine oil according to WW spec. "50300".

2. 1.2 If an engine oil not in accordance with the WW specification "50300" was used: The oil change service interval is set in the maintenance calculator for a fixed oil change service interval of 10,000 miles (15,000 km) or 1 year, after selecting and confirming this oil quality in the PST2 menu => "Engine oil with general Porsche approval".

. The country version of the vehicle "does not" correspond to one of the countries listed in Table 1. For vehicles having these country versions, all engine oils approved by Porsche may be used which are listed in this bulletin below and Cayenne Technical Information Bulletin, GROUP 1, NO. 4/04 . Even when an engine oil meeting the WW specification "50300" is used, the oil change service interval of 10,000 miles (15,000 km) or 1 year is to be observed.

1.2.1 If an engine oil approved by Porsche was used: The oil change service interval is set for a fixed oil change service interval of 10,000 miles (15,000 km) or 1 year when resetting the maintenance calculator with the PST2.

For more information about the oil change interval for Cayenne V6 and how to reset the "Maintenance Calculator" in the instrument cluster, see CAYENNE (V6) - ENGINE OILS APPROVED BY PORSCHE - OIL CHANGE SERVICE INTERVAL technical service bulletin (GROUP 1, NO. 3/04).

# TIRE PRESSURE MONITOR SYSTEM REMINDER

4 NOTE: To determine the appropriate reset procedure, refer to TPMS REMINDER RESET INDEX . Only vehicles listed in this index have a TPMS reset.

CAUTION: 1st generation TPM wheel electronics are not compatible with 2nd generation TPM wheel electronics. 1st generation is up to 2008, and 2nd generation is 2009 and beyond.

If wheels with wheel electronics from the 1st TPM generation are mounted on a vehicle with a 2nd generation TPM system (or vice versa), the wheel electronics will not be recognized by the TPM system. The TPM system is not active and a corresponding warning is displayed in the multi-function display of the instrument cluster. The wheel electronics will also be stored as defective in the fault memory of the TPM control unit.

Wheel electronics unit (sensor) part numbers are: • 2005-07: 997.606.021.00 433MHz) • 2008: 997.606.021.01 (433 MHz) • 2009-: 997.606.021.20 (433 MHz)

# TPMS REMINDER RESET INDEX

![](images/2f84379ce4bc5f966651932d3ba58c2c7c29c5883e27e6f2e9d5e2ba51395324.webp)

# TIRE PRESSURE MONITOR SYSTEM REMINDER > TPMS REMINDER RESET - PROCEDURE 1

Tire Pressure Monitoring begins to "learn" the wheels after a wheel change, wheel transmiter replacement, a tire pressure adjustment (when a warning message has been displayed), once an update of the tire settings has been performed. During this process, Tire Pressure Monitoring recognizes the wheels and their locations. The message "No monitoring, system is learning" appears on the multipurpose display. The wheel learning process takes place exclusively when the vehicle is being driven above 16 mph (25 km/h). Tire Pressure Monitoring requires a certain amount of time to learn the wheels.

. NOTE: The tire type and size must be updated even if the settings for the new set of wheels are the same as for the old wheels. If the tire setings are not updated, the message "TIRE CHANGE? UPDATE SETTINGS!" is displayed on the multi-purpose display.

# Starting TPMS Learn:

1. Select menu "TIRE PRESSURE", then "ADJUST". Set tire type and tire size (both items must be set). See Operating Multi-Purpose Display .

2. The learning process is now started, and wil be completed when vehicle is driven. The message "NO MONITORING - SYSTEM LEARNING" is displayed. The current tire pressure will be displayed once the learning phase is complete.

# Operating Multi-Purpose Display:

With multi-function steering wheel:

•Selecting menu, function, setting option: Rotary knob (top right button).

Confirming selection: Press rotary knob.

Moving back one or several selection levels: Button below rotary knob (middle right button).

Vithout multi-function steering wheel: (Use the lower lever on the right of the steering column.)

•Selecting menu, function, setting option: Push the lever downwards or upwards.

Confirming selection: Push the lever forward.

Moving back one or several selection levels: Pul the lever back (toward rear of vehicle).

After repairing flat tire with tire sealant, select "SEALING SET". The display wil return to the basic screen after acknowledgement. A warning message will display if vehicle speed exceeds 50 mph (80 km/h).

NOTE: If tires have been rotated, or a tire pressure sensor or wheel has been replaced, e TPM system must be reset. See procedure below.

Tire Pressure Monitoring begins to "learn" new tire pressure sensors after a wheel change or sensor replacement after updating the tire specification settings. During the Learn process, the TPMS recognizes the wheels and their locations. A "No Monitoring" message appears on the multi-purpose display. The wheel learning process takes place exclusively when the vehicle is being driven above 16 mph (25 km/h). Tire Pressure Monitoring requires a certain amount of time to learn the wheels.

# Updating Tire Specification Settings:

![](images/1f059db9bfdd3ec798f72a977e4149d5bc79ed023a01aa6f531b281e41259c11.webp)

NOTE: The on-board computer is operated with the lower left lever on the steering lumn.

1. Push operating lever forward in order to switch on the selection field.

2. Select "TPC" with the operating lever.

3. Push operating lever forward. The display changes to the Tire pressure menu.

4. Select "Set" with the operating lever.

5. Push the operating lever forward. Select desired tire type: summer or winter.

6. Push operating lever forward. A display for confirming the selected type of tire appears.

7. Select "Continue" and push the operating lever forward.

8. Select the appropriate tire size (18 or 19 inch) and push operating lever forwards. A display for confirming the selected tire size appears.

9. If "Process complete" is displayed, learning mode will be initiated.

10. Drive vehicle above 16 mph (25 km/h) until correct tire pressures are displayed.

NOTE: The message "Process aborted" appears if the setting process is interrupted. All entries made up to this point are lost, and the original setings remain in effect. Only if the message "Process complete" appears after the setings have been made will the tire pressure monitoring re-learn the wheels.

# WM 691119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT THREE-POINT BELT (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING FRONT THREE-POINT BELT

WARNING: Incorrect handling of seat-belt pretensioner unit

Triggering of seat-belt pretensioner unit

→ Observe safety regulations for handling seat-belt pretensioner units.

→ Observe disposal regulations for seat-belt pretensioner units.

→ After disconnecting the battery, wait 1 minute before disconnecting the seat-belt pretensioner unit.

→ Remove ignition key and disconnect the battery. Route or insulate the ground strap so that all contact with a ground carrier is avoided. Read and follow work instructions after disconnecting the battery.

→ If removed for an extended period, the seat-belt pretensioner unit must be stored in a safe place.

→ Transport the seat-belt pretensioner unit in such a way that the seat belt can retract safely if it is actuated.

NOTE: Incorrect handling of spring plate on seat belt mount

The seat belt must be replaced.

→ Only bend the spring plate up as far as required to allow you to push the seat belt mount off the mounting pin.

→ The spring plate must be touching the mounting pin during installation with preload.

# WM 691119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT THREE-POINT BELT (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Install B-pillar trim panel. → INSTALLING LOWER PART OF B-PILLAR TRIM PANEL .

2. Connect the battery. → 2XOOIN GENERAL INFORMATION ON DISCONNECTING THE BATTERY

3. Perform a function test.

1. The belt strap must be fully rolled up when the function test is started.

2. Move the seat belt height adjustment to the highest position.

3. Pull out belt strap completely as far as it will go.

4. Roll up the belt strap again slowly. An audible clattering noise can be heard when you do this.

5. If the rolling-up process is interrupted, the belt strap cannot be pulled out again (permanent belt blockage). 6. The permanent belt blockage function must switch off at least 100 mm before the belt strap is rolled up fully, thereby ensuring that the belt strap can be pulled out again.

# WM 691301 CHECKING SEAT BELTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > GENERAL WARNING NOTES > WARNING NOTE FOR SEAT BELTS

WARNING: Road tests on public roads

• Danger to other people on the roads

—→ Perform drive tests on a stretch of road with no traffic.

# Information

After any accident, the seat belt system must be checked systematically for signs of damage. If damage

is found, the entire seat belt system must be replaced.

# WM 691301 CHECKING SEAT BELTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CHECKING SEAT BELTS > PROCEDURE FOR CHECKING SEAT BELTS

After any accident, the seat belt system must be checked systematicall for proper function and damage.   
If damage is found according to the test points, the entire seat belt system must be replaced.

# Information

In the case of damage which does not occur as the result of an accident, e.g. wear, only the damaged part needs to be replaced.

# Information

The following requirements must be met when fitting the seat belt.

If one of the requirements listed below is not met, the seat belt or seat-belt buckle must be replaced.

# WM 691301 CHECKING SEAT BELTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CHECKING SEAT BELTS > CHECKING BELT STRAP

oPull the belt strap on the automatic belt device out fully.   
Check the belt strap for soiling. Clean it, if necessary, using mild soap suds. Avoid direct sunshine when drying.

# 1. Damage type 1

1. 1.1. If one of the damage types shown below -Damage type 1, 2- is found on an vehicle involved in an accident, the seat belt and seat-belt buckle must be replaced.

![](images/35eb9f88e206ed9883c102e3f764d4a137067c080184c28f51a3956a6fe5f313.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Seat-Belt Damage Area (Type 1)   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# 2. Damage type 2

1.2.1. If damage such as damage type -Damage type 1, 2, 3- is found on a vehicle not involved in an accident, it is sufficient to replace the damaged seat belt.

![](images/d7a36ce3d880536558fc89d91ef12effc3b4e93fc89d2c70f4053d1b8e4f730a.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Seat-Belt Damage Area (Type 2)   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# 3. Damage type 3

1.3.1. Burn hole from cigarettes, for example.

![](images/39a01e3b37fca2dc3a4aa999d01eea09feb285bad8b231795a941042f51efe1c.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Seat-Belt Burn Hole Area (Type 3)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# 4. Damage type 4

1. 4.1. The seat-belt pretensioner must always be replaced if it has been triggered. The seat belt is damaged by the deflector -Damage type 4- .

![](images/7347b8ab86d2005678f6a4db1be9297d933d1f85d5d415460b8ea39ba3aeb8a0.webp)  
Fig 4: Identifying Seat-Belt Damage Area (Type 4)

# WM 691301 CHECKING SEAT BELTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CHECKING SEAT BELTS > CHECKING AUTOMATIC BELT DEVICE (LOCKING EFFECT)

The first locking function is triggered by pulling the seat belt out quickly (belt extension acceleration).

# WM 691301 CHECKING SEAT BELTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CHECKING SEAT BELTS > CHECKING AUTOMATIC BELT DEVICE (LOCKING EFFECT) > CHECK

oPull the belt strap out of the automatic belt device with a strong pull.

If no locking effect occurs, the entire seat belt and seat-belt buckle must be replaced.

In the case of faults in the extension or retraction of the seat belt, check whether the locking tab of the automatic belt device is engaged correctly in the sheetmetal bracket on the body.

The second locking function is triggered by a change in the sequence of vehicle movement (vehicle-dependent locking function).

WARNING: Road tests on public roads

Danger to other people on the roads

→ Perform drive tests on a stretch of road with no traffic.

Fasten the seat belt.

WARNING: Road tests on public roads

•Danger to other people on the roads

→ Perform drive tests on a stretch of road with no traffic.

oAccelerate the vehicle to 20 km/h (12 mph) and then perform an emergency stop by pressing the footbrake.

If the belt is not locked by the blocking mechanism during the braking phase, the entire seat belt and seat-belt buckle must be replaced.

# WM 691301 CHECKING SEAT BELTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) >CHECKING SEAT BELTS > CHECKING LOOK AND OPERATION OF SEAT-BELTBUCKLE

Inspect the seat-belt buckle for crack formation and flaking.

In the case of damage, the entire seat belt and seat-belt buckle must be replaced.

# WM 691301 CHECKING SEAT BELTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) >CHECKING SEAT BELTS > CHECKING LOOK AND OPERATION OF SEAT-BELTBUCKLE > CHECK SEAT-BELT BUCKLE

oPush the belt latch into the seat-belt buckle untilit engages with an audible click. Check whether the lock mechanism has engaged by puling strongly on the belt strap.

If the belt latch fails to lock in the seat-belt buckle even just once in at least 5 test procedures, the entire seat belt and seat-belt buckle must be replaced.

WM 691301 CHECKING SEAT BELTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) >

# CHECKING SEAT BELTS > CHECKING LOOK AND OPERATION OF SEAT-BELTBUCKLE > CHECK SEAT-BELT BUCKLE RELEASE

oRelease the seat belt by pressing your finger on the button on the seat-belt buckle.

Carry out the test procedure at least 5 times. If the belt latch fails to jump out even just once, the entire seat belt and seat-belt buckle must be replaced.

# Information

Lubricants must never be used to eliminate noises or stiffness of the buttons on the seat-belt buckles.

# WM 691301 CHECKING SEAT BELTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CHECKING SEAT BELTS > CHECKING SASH GUIDE COVERS

Plastic-coated covers show fine, paralle scores after the belt system has been subjected to stress (seat belt buckled during accident). On the other hand, wear caused by frequent use is indicated by a stripe-free, smooth surface.

oCheck the sash guide covers for distortion, flaking and crack formation. In the event of scoring and/or damage, the entire seat belt and seat-belt buckle must be replaced.

# WM 691301 CHECKING SEAT BELTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CHECKING SEAT BELTS > CHECKING MOUNTING PARTS AND FASTENING POINTS

Check the belt buckle strap for distortion.   
Check the function of the height adjuster.   
Check fastening points (seat, B-pilar, C-pillar, vehicle floor) for distortion or thread damage.

If the parts are damaged, the entire seat belt and seat-belt buckle must be replaced.

Replace damaged or distorted fastening points.

# WM 695119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING AIRBAG SENSOR (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AIRBAG SENSOR > REMOVING FRONT AIRBAG SENSOR

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag units

Triggering of airbag unit.   
System faults can occur.

→ Switch off ignition and remove ignition key or remote control (hand-held transmitter).

→ A power supply (e.g. battery charger) must not be connected to the external power supply/jump-lead starting terminals.

→ Disconnect the battery and insulate the ground strap so that al contact with a ground carrier is avoided.

→ Wait 1 minute after disconnecting the battery.

→ Only pull off connector on the triggering unit after the waiting time has elapsed.

→ Make sure that no foreign objects are located in front of the airbag unit during installation.

→ Replace damaged parts during removal.

→ Always position airbag units so that the blow-out opening is facing upwards, e.g. crest on driver's airbag.

→ Do not position anything on the airbag units.

→ If removed for an extended period, the airbag units must be stored in a safe place.

→ Airbag units must not come into contact with grease, oil, detergents, liquids, or similar substances.

→ Do not expose airbag units to temperatures above 90°.

→ Do not remove the short-circuit spring on the plug-in contacts.

→ Ignition and preparations may only be carried out by skilled staff, supervised by a second responsible person.

→ Before disposal, the airbag unit must be rendered harmless by electrical ignition performed in accordance with all precautionary measures, thereby preventing it from being used incorrectly.

NOTE: Voltage peaks

•Risk of damage to electrical load or to the control unit

# Information

Some of the repair illstrations show only one side of the vehicle.

Naturally, some steps also have to be performed on the opposite side of the vehicle as well.

1. Unscrew fastening screw -1- and remove sensor -B- .

2. Guide airbag sensor out of the lock carrier.

3. Release electric plug connection -a- and disconnect it -A- .

Fig 1: Removing Airbag Sensor

# WM 695355 REPLACING TRIGGERING UNIT FOR AIRBAG (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REPLACING TRIGGERING UNIT FOR AIRBAG

NOTE: Voltage drop

•Risk of irreparable damage to control unit   
Risk of damage to control unit   
Fault entries in the control unit   
•Coding in the control unit is aborted   
•Malfunctions in control unit, even during programming

→ Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch offignition and remove ignition key.

→ Ensure that the power supply is not interrupted during programming.

→ Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least — Nominal value: 40 A to the vehicle battery.

# Information

The PIWis Tester Il9818 instructions take precedence since the description may be different with later Tester releases.

The procedure described here has been structured in general terms. Different text or additional information may appear in PiWis Tester Il 9818 .

1. Connect the PIWis Tester to the vehicle and start the diagnostic application. Switch on   
ignition.   
2. Select vehicle type.   
3. When the overview is displayed, start the control unit search by pressing [F12].   
4. Once the control unit search is complete, press [F7].   
5. Select Maintenance of vehicle data and press [F12].   
6. Compare the displayed data with the vehicle equipment and write it down if necessary.

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag units

1. Triggering of airbag unit.

2. System faults can occur.

→ Switch of ignition and remove ignition key or remote control (hand-held transmitter).

→ A power supply (e.g. battery charger) must not be connected to the external power supply/jump-lead starting terminals.

→ Disconnect the battery and insulate the ground strap so that all contact with a ground carrier is avoided.

→ Wait 1 minute after disconnecting the battery.   
→ Only pulloff connector on the triggering unit after the waiting time has elapsed.   
→ Make sure that no foreign objects are located in front of the airbag unit during installtion.   
→ Replace damaged parts during removal.   
→ Always position airbag units so that the blow-out opening is facing upwards, e.g. crest on driver's airbag.   
→ Do not position anything on the airbag units.   
→ If removed for an extended period, the airbag units must be stored in a safe place.   
→ Airbag units must not come into contact with grease, oil, detergents, liquids, or similar substances.   
→ Do not expose airbag units to temperatures above 90°.   
→ Do not remove the short-circuit spring on the plug-in contacts.

→ Ignition and preparations may only be carried out by skilled staff, supervised by a second responsible person.

→ Before disposal, the airbag unit must be rendered harmless by electrical ignition performed in accordance with al precautionary measures, thereby preventing it from being used incorrectly.

7. Switch off ignition and disconnect the charger from the power connection and the ground strap from the battery.

8. The airbag control unit can be replaced after a wait time of at least 1 minute. → 695319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING TRIGGERING UNIT FOR AIRBAG

9.Connect the ground strap for the battery and switch the charger on again.

10. Switch on ignition.

11. When the overview is displayed, start the control unit search by pressing [F12].

12. Once the control unit search is complete, press [F7].

13. Select Maintenance of vehicle data and press [F12].

14. Compare the vehicle data with the vehicle equipment and the data you read out earlier. Change the data if necessary.

15. Select the Airbag control unit in the overview and press [F12].

16. Select Maintenance/repairs and Lock and press [F12].

17. Read the warnings displayed on the Tester and proceed according to the instructions on the Tester.

18. Once you have locked the airbag control unit, the occupant detection control unit must be calibrated on vehicles with the country variant C02 (USA, Canada, Mexico).

1. 18.1. Select the Maintenance/repairs menu. Then select Calibrate occupant detection and complete the calibration process according to the instructions on the Tester.

19. Switch off ignition and remove the remote control (hand-held transmitter) from the ignition lock.

20. Insert the remote control back into the ignition lock and switch on ignition.

21. Read out the fault memory and erase it if necessary.

22. Perform function test: Switch the ignition off and then on again. The airbag warning light in the instrument cluster comes on and must go off again after a few seconds.

# WM 695355 REPLACING TRIGGERING UNIT FOR AIRBAG (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REPLACING TRIGGERING UNIT FOR AIRBAG

NOTE: Voltage drop

•Risk of irreparable damage to control unit   
Risk of damage to control unit   
Fault entries in the control unit   
•Coding in the control unit is aborted   
•Malfunctions in control unit, even during programming

→ Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch offignition and remove ignition key.

→ Ensure that the power supply is not interrupted during programming.

→ Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least — Nominal value: 40 A to the vehicle battery.

# Information

The PIWis Tester Il9818 instructions take precedence since the description may be different with later Tester releases.

The procedure described here has been structured in general terms. Different text or additional information may appear in PIWis Tester Il 9818 .

1.Connect the PIWiS Tester to the vehicle and start the Tester. Switch on ignition.

2. Select the vehicle type and start the diagnostic application.

3. When the overview is displayed, start the control unit search by pressing [F12].

4. Once the control unit search is complete, press [F7].

5. Select Maintenance of vehicle data and press [F12].

6. Compare the displayed values with the vehicle values and press [F4] to save. Then press [F11] to go back.

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag units

1. Triggering of airbag unit.

2. System faults can occur.

→ Switch offignition and remove ignition key or remote control (hand-held transmitter).

→ A power supply (e.g. battery charger) must not be connected to the external power supply/jump-lead starting terminals.

→ Disconnect the battery and insulate the ground strap so that all contact with a ground carrier is avoided.

→ Wait 1 minute after disconnecting the battery.

→ Only pull of connector on the triggering unit after the waiting time has elapsed.

→ Make sure that no foreign objects are located in front of the airbag unit during installation.

→ Replace damaged parts during removal.

→ Always position airbag units so that the blow-out opening is facing upwards, e.g. crest on driver's airbag.

→ Do not position anything on the airbag units.

→ If removed for an extended period, the airbag units must be stored in a safe place.

→ Airbag units must not come into contact with grease, oil, detergents, liquids, or similar substances.

→ Do not expose airbag units to temperatures above 90°.

→ Do not remove the short-circuit spring on the plug-in contacts.

→ Ignition and preparations may only be carried out by skilled staff, supervised by a second responsible person.

→ Before disposal, the airbag unit must be rendered harmless by electrical ignition performed in accordance with all precautionary measures, thereby preventing it from being used

incorrectiy.   
7. Switch off ignition, remove the battery charger from the power supply and disconnect the battery.   
8. The airbag control unit can be replaced after a wait time of at least 1 minute. → 695319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING TRIGGERING UNIT FOR AIRBAG   
9. Select the Airbag control unit in the overview and press [F12].   
10. Select Maintenance/repairs  and Lock and press [F12].   
11. Read the warnings on the Tester.   
12. Press [F8] to start programming and follow the instructions on the Tester.   
13. Read out the fault memory and erase i if necessary.   
14. Switch the ignition off and then on again. The airbag warning light in the instrument cluster comes on and must go off again after a few seconds.

# WM 696619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEAD AIRBAG UNIT (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING HEAD AIRBAG UNIT

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag units

Triggering of airbag unit.

•System faults can occur.

→ Switch of ignition and remove ignition key or remote control (hand-held transmiter).

→ A power supply (e.g. battery charger) must not be connected to the external power supply/jump-lead starting terminals.

→ Disconnect the battery and insulate the ground strap so that all contact with a ground carrier is avoided.

→ Wait 1 minute after disconnecting the battery.

→ Only pull off connector on the triggering unit after the waiting time has elapsed.

→ Make sure that no foreign objects are located in front of the airbag unit during instalation.

→ Replace damaged parts during removal.

→ Always position airbag units so that the blow-out opening is facing upwards, e.g. crest on driver's airbag.

→ Do not position anything on the airbag units.   
→ If removed for an extended period, the airbag units must be stored in a safe place.   
→ Airbag units must not come into contact with grease, oil, detergents, liquids, or similar substances.   
→ Do not expose airbag units to temperatures above 90°.   
→ Do not remove the short-circuit spring on the plug-in contacts.

→ Ignition and preparations may only be carried out by skilled staff, supervised by a second responsible person.

→ Before disposal, the airbag unit must be rendered harmless by electrical ignition performed in accordance with all precautionary measures, thereby preventing it from being used incorrectly.

Naturally some steps also have to be performed on the opposite side of the vehicle as well .

If occupant detection components (installed for country equipment USA/Canada/Mexico) must be

replaced, the repair kit comprising padding, occupant detection control unit and pressure sensor mat must always be replaced as a complete unit .

The spare parts are grouped in a repair kit (comprising padding -1-, occupant detection control unit -2- and pressure sensor mat -3-), which must always be replaced as a complete unit.

1. Padding   
2. Occupant detection control unit   
3. Pressure sensor mat

![](images/e54876c037c57325c4724f82fc5846f8656063f681092eb212d4bf10c62087ea.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

A mixed installation, e.g. "old" pressure sensor mat and "new" control unit, is not permitted .

The padding, pressure sensor mat and occupant detection control unit are calibrated together by the manufacturer and must therefore only be replaced as a complete unit.

The occupant detection control unit does not have to be coded.

# Information

The connector of the occupant detection control unit must be inserted straight as otherwise the seal will be damaged. The seating of the seal must then be checked.

NOTE: Voltage drop

• Risk of irreparable damage to control unit   
Risk of damage to control unit   
• Fault entries in the control unit   
• Coding in the control unit is aborted   
• Malfunctions in control unit, even during programming

→ Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch offignition and remove ignition key.

→ Ensure that the power supply is not interrupted during programming.

→ Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least — Nominal value: 40 A to the vehicle battery.

# Information

If occupant detection components (installed for country equipment USA/Canada/Mexico) must be replaced, the repair kit comprising padding, occupant detection control unit and pressure sensor mat must always be replaced as a complete unit .

The spare parts are grouped in a repair kit (comprising padding -1-, occupant detection control unit -2- and pressure sensor mat -3-), which must always be replaced as a complete unit.

1. Padding   
2. Occupant detection control unit   
3. Pressure sensor mat

![](images/210a58ccbf93a114ef8a6ced645cfcba8d1bf46f342c2521d0b53bfea49c164b.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Occupant Detection Repair Kit Contents   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

A mixed installation,e.g. "old" pressure sensor mat and "new" control unit, is not permitted.

The padding, pressure sensor mat and occupant detection control unit are calibrated together by the manufacturer and must therefore only be replaced as a complete unit.

The occupant detection control unit does not have to be coded.

# Information

The PIwis Tester Il9818 instructions take precedence since the description may be different with later Tester releases.

The procedure described here has been structured in general terms. Different text or additional information may appear in PIWis Tester Il 9818 .

1. Switch off ignition and replace control unit → 696819 REMOVING AND INSTALLING   
OCCUPANT DETECTION CONTROL UNIT   
2. Connect the PlWiS Tester to the vehicle and start the Tester. Switch on ignition.   
3. Select the vehicle type under Diagnostics.   
4. Select Airbag control unit in the overview .   
5. Maintenance and repairs must now be selected.   
6. Select Calibrate occupant detection and press [F12] to continue.   
7. Follow the instructions on the Tester and press [F12] to continue.   
8. Start the function by pressing [F8]   
9. The message "Function has been executed" appears. Press [F11] to go back.   
10. Read out the fault memory and erase it if necessary.   
11. Perform function test: Switch the ignition off and then on again. The airbag warning light in the   
instrument cluster comes on and must go off again after a few seconds.

# (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > SUBSEQUENT WORK > SUBSEQUENT WORK FOR KNEE AIRBAG ON DRIVER'S SIDE

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag units

• → Observe specified tightening torques.   
• → Carry out a visual inspection of all re-used parts.

→ Switch off ignition and remove ignition key or remote control (hand-held transmitter).

→ A power supply (e.g. battery charger) must not be connected to the external power supply/jump-lead starting terminals.

→ Disconnect the battery and insulate the ground strap so that all contact with a ground carrier is avoided.

→ Wait 1 minute after disconnecting the battery.

→ Only pull off connector on the triggering unit after the waiting time has elapsed.

→ Make sure that no foreign objects are located in front of the airbag unit during installation.

→ Replace damaged parts during removal.

→ Always position airbag units so that the blow-out opening is facing upwards, e.g. crest on driver's airbag.

→ Do not position anything on the airbag units.

→ If removed for an extended period, the airbag units must be stored in a safe place.

→ Airbag units must not come into contact with grease, oil, detergents, liquids, or similar substances.

→ Do not expose airbag units to temperatures above 90°.

→ Do not remove the short-circuit spring on the plug-in contacts.

→ Ignition and preparations may only be carried out by skilled staff, supervised by a second responsible person.

→ Before disposal, the airbag unit must be rendered harmless by electrical ignition performed in accordance with all precautionary measures, thereby preventing it from being used incorrectly.

# Information

After replacing airbag components, proof of replacement must be documented in the Warranty and Maintenance booklet.

1. Install trim panel under dashboard → INSTALLING TRIM PANEL UNDER DASHBOARD AT THE RIGHT .

NOTE: Voltage drop

•Risk of irreparable damage to control unit   
Risk of damage to control unit   
•Fault entries in the control unit   
•Coding in the control unit is aborted   
•Malfunctions in control unit, even during programming

→ Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch offignition and remove ignition key.

→ Ensure that the power supply is not interrupted during programming.

→ Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least — Nominal value: 40 A to the vehicle battery.

# Information

The PlWis Tester Il9818 instructions take precedence since the description may be different with later Tester releases.

The procedure described here has been structured in general terms; different text or additions may appear in PIWis Tester II 9818 .

# Information

All remote controls (keys) are required for teaching a DME, front-end electronics (front BCM), rear-end electronics (rear BCM), electronic steering lock (ELV) control unit or remote controls (keys) for example.

Remote controls (keys) that are not taught during this teaching procedure wil no longer be recognized by he vehicle.

1. PIWis Tester Il9818 must be connected to the vehicle before starting the Tester. Switch on ignition using original remote control.

2. Select the menu Diagnostics -> Online teaching function -> Engine immobilizer on the Start page.

3. Vehicle  must now be selected. Then press [F12] to continue. Vehicle data will be read out.

4. Follow the instructions on the Tester.

5. The vehicle identification number (VIN) is displayed. Change the vehicle identification number if necessary.

6. Enter the repair order number and press [F12] to continue.

7. Enter the PPN user name and password and press [F12] to continue.

8. Login is performed.

9. The Tester displays the message Login successful . Press [F12] to continue.

10. Follow the instructions on the Tester to select the required menu.

11. Once the teaching process is completed successfull, the Tester shows the following status, for example:

2 keys taught

Front BCM: taught

ELV: taught

Rear BCM: taught

DME: taught Overall vehicle status: taught. Continue with [F12]

12. Press [ESC] to exit the Online teaching function and select the vehicle type on the Start page.

13. Read out the fault memory and delete faults if necessary.

14. Lock, open and start the vehicle using al remote controls (hand-held transmitters).

15. Read out the fault memory again.

# WM 4815IN ASSESSMENT OF STEERING COLUMN AFTER ACCIDENT DAMAGE (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > INFORMATION > FUNDAMENTALS

Various kinds of damage can be caused to steering columns in the event of accidents or driving conditions similar to accidents. In cases where the steering column shows no external damage it can be difficult to detect damage. This damage represents an unacceptable risk for the vehicle, since it could lead to failure of the steering system.

To decide whether the steering column of a vehicle involved in an accident must be replaced or may continue to be used, the following guidelines are helpful.

# WM 4815IN ASSESSMENT OF STEERING COLUMN AFTER ACCIDENT DAMAGE (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > INFORMATION > ASSESSMENT OF THE STEERING COLUMN OF A VEHICLE INVOLVED IN AN ACCIDENT

The steering column may remain in the vehicle if allthe following conditions are met:

No visible damage (breakage, cracks, deformation) to such front-axle parts as steering arms, steering gear, steering column mountings, steering wheel and airbag unit, wheel rims, wheel bearing housing (wheel carriers), tie rods, steering shaft or to the points on the body where wheel suspension parts are bolted on.

No unacceptable rise in torque and no jamming or catching when the steering gear is turned from stop to stop. The front wheels must be free (front axle raised) when turning and the ignition must be switched off (no power assistance).

The steering column does not catch/jam when turned separately without steering gear.

No axial play in the steering column.

The steering column must be replaced by a new or replacement unit if one of the follwing points applies:

Impact is felt by occupants.

Airbag has been triggered.

Visible or perceptible damage to the steering column.

Play in steering shaft line.

Fire damage.

In addition, for vehicles with electrically adjustable steering columns, if the adjustment does not function perfectly (the axial and/or vertical adjustment time from stop to stop is too long, unusual noises are heard in this area).

The steering intermediate shaft and/or a universal joint is touching another component or has clearance of less than 5 mm.

The steering wheel is more than 10° out of line when the marking for steering center position overlaps → 449503 SUSPENSION ALIGNMENT, COMPLETE refer to "Adjusting toe".

If permanent deformation, breakage, cracks or play have been detected in:

steering gear,   
steering column mountings,   
tie rods,   
steering arms,   
spring struts,   
wheel carriers,   
control arms,   
front-axle carrier (chassis subframe)

then the steering column must be checked according to the criteria listed above.

NOTE: Voltage drop

•Risk of irreparable damage to control unit   
Risk of damage to control unit   
Fault entries in the control unit   
•Coding in the control unit is aborted   
•Malfunctions in control unit, even during programming

→ Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch offignition and remove ignition key.

→ Ensure that the power supply is not interrupted during programming.

→ Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least — Nominal value: 40 A to the vehicle battery.

# Information

The PIWis Tester Il9818 instructions take precedence since the description may be different with later Tester releases.

The procedure described here has been structured in general terms. Different text or additional information may appear in PIWis Tester Il 9818 .

1. Connect the PIWis Tester to the vehicle and start the Tester. Switch on ignition.   
2. Select the vehicle type and start the diagnostic application.   
3. Extended identifications must now be selected.   
4. Enter the vehicle identification number and press[Enter] to confirm your entry.   
5. Select the Front-end electronics control unit in the overview .   
6. Maintenance/repairs must then be selected.   
7. Select Steering column adjustment normalizing run and press [F12] to continue.   
8. Follow the instructions on the Tester.   
9. Start the Steering column adjustment normalizing run by pressing [F8].   
10. The normalizing run ends once all end stops have been set.   
11. Once the procedure has been completed successfully , press [F12] to continue.   
12. Read out the fault memory and erase it if necessary.   
13. Carry out a function test.

# WM 487919 REMOVING AND INSTALLING TIE ROD (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > PRELIMINARY WORK

Information

Before removing the tie rod, always check the tie rod joints on both sides. If a joint does not meet the test conditions, it must be replaced.

Only if there is no play in the steering can it be set correctly and the operating reliability of the vehicle can thus be guaranteed.

1. Check tie rod joint.

Test conditions: The vehicle must be standing on its wheels in order to check the tie rod joints; vehicles with air suspension must be adjusted to maximum ground clearance.

![](images/daa66741406b419f70caa1c3345c3ea353e0db6fbd39e9d9003ba7cea607aa21.webp)  
Fig 1: Checking Tie Rod Joint

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

1. 1.1. Check that the dust boots, bellows and joints are working perfectly and have no leaks.

2.1.2. Check the left tie rod joint.

Turn the wheels to the right and take hold of the tie-rod ball -1- . Get a second mechanic to turn the steering by moving the steering wheel back and forth slightly.

There must be no play on the joint.

If you detect a certain amount of play that is not caused by the tie rod joint, the axial joint between the steering gear and tie rod is worn.

3.1.3. Check the right tie rod joint.

Turn the wheels to the left and take hold of the tie-rod ball -1- . Get a second mechanic to turn the steering by moving the steering wheel back and forth slightly.

There must be no play on the joint.

If you detect a certain amount of play that is not caused by the tie rod joint, the axial joint between the steering gear and tie rod is worn.

2. Remove tie-rod ball → REMOVING AND INSTALLING TIE-ROD BALL .

3. Remove front underbody panelling → 519219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COVER FOR FRONT UNDERBODY .

# WM 487919 REMOVING AND INSTALLING TIE ROD (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING TIE ROD > REMOVING TIE ROD

Mark the position of the tie-rod ball on the thread before unscrewing it from the tie rod.

Count the number of turns when unscrewing it (turns of tie-rod ball).

This avoids the need to perform an approximate adjustment of the steering trapeze when reassembling.

This is not a substitute for the suspension alignment.

# Information

After removing the tie rod, the steering track must be adjusted.

5. Remove tie rod. If the tie rod is replaced, the marking for the old tie rod on the wheel side must be copied to the new tie rod.

# WM 488119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING TIE-ROD BALL (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING TIE-ROD BALL > REMOVING TIE-ROD BALL

![](images/56f5f580bcfc175572f79eddb97734e0f307944e051ff417c7f6edc4d3cf99ed.webp)  
Fig 1: Locating Tie-Rod Ball Position

1. To make it easier to remove the tie-rod ball, swivel the relevant wheel bearing housing so that the tie rod is fully extended.

# Information

Mark the position of the tie-rod ball on the thread before unscrewing it from the tie rod.

Count the number of turns when unscrewing it (turns of tie-rod ball).

This avoids the need to perform an approximate adjustment of the steering trapeze when reassembling.

This is not a substitute for the suspension alignment.

2. Detach tie-rod ball -1- from tie rod.

1.2.1. Counter the tie-rod ball -1- at the flattened areas -arrows- using a suitable open-ended wrench.

2. 2.2. Loosen lock nut -2- .

![](images/cd279e1fa1b5d2a6859a7e06b39f2a82788860e7afb237ba53c5ac1063c26aeb.webp)  
Fig 2: Detaching Tie-Rod Ball   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Unscrew fastening nut -1- on the joint pin for the tie-rod ball-2- until it is flush with the thread of the joint pin.

![](images/476e3e5d0031e8300326d443b00421d09c7d45d86d7a9238cd42074f7846d4cd.webp)  
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Loosen tie-rod bal from the wheel bearing housing. When doing so, make sure not to damage the speed sensor.

1.4.1. Position ball joint puller T40010 over the joint pin and fit it on the fastening nut.

2.4.2. Press tie-rod balloff the tapered end of the wheel carrier using ball joint puller T40010.

Screw in hexagon on the ball joint puller T40010 until the tie-rod ball becomes detached from the tapered end of the wheel carrier.

Make sure that the lever arms of the ball joint puller are parallel to each other when the greatest amount of force is applied. Readjust if necessary. → Pressing off tie-rod ball

![](images/2ec28376f06f6466084ab770664960965f3eece701bdc258f169630ac78755ae.webp)  
Fig 4: Pressing Off Tie-Rod Ball   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Loosen fastening nut -1- from the joint pin on the tie-rod ball -2- .

![](images/c03ab22c3aa4f66248d1538b1f5b3093e83264341866f509ed94024c6c8d15f4.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. Unscrew tie-rod ball -3- from tie rod -1- and remove it.

![](images/2402ca7aadb814600fdc1058a32bfbb3f02e87ce565374aeff8492548c349a2c.webp)  
Fig 6: Identifying Tie-Rod Ball

# WM 488119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING TIE-ROD BALL (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING TIE-ROD BALL > INSTALLING TIE-ROD BALL

Clean the thread of the tie-rod ball before screwing the tie-rod ball onto the tie rod.

To prevent any damage when screwing the tie-rod ball onto the tie rod, make sure in particular that the thread engages uniformly.

Screw on the tie-rod ball by the number of turns you wrote down during removal. Then turn it as far as the marking.

This is not a substitute for a later suspension alignment, but merely avoids the need for an approximate adjustment of the steering trapeze.

1. Instaltion is performed in reverse order to removal. Pay particular attention to the following:

Fastening nut -1- securing tie-rod ball to tapered end of wheel carrier: Tightening torque 100

# Nm (74 ftlb.)

Always use a new nut following removal.

Fig 1: Identifying Tie-Rod Ball On Wheel Bearing Housing

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

Lock nut -2- securing tie-rod ball to tie rod: Tightening torque 90 Nm (67 ftlb.)

![](images/97515dbcf665fc111fadc1b7b3dee0dc1723b6a50c0f57696a8ae05b7d3f6b16.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Tie-Rod Ball

WM 489025 POWER-STEERING GEAR: TEACHING STEERING LOCK SETTINGS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > TOOLS   
![](images/c05d4c47cca0fae3791e5d15639c767aecfb81f33603d54fd9077d9d2e316321.webp)

# (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > POWER-STEERING GEAR: TEACHING STEERING LOCK SETTINGS

If the steering gear is replaced, the steering lock settings must be taught.

The steering lock settings are cleared after calibrating the steering-angle sensor and must be re-taught.

1. Calibrate the steering-angle sensor. (This wil clear the limit stops.) → 456005 INITIALIZING AND CALIBRATING STEERING-ANGLE SENSOR

2. Teach steering lock settings.

To do this, select >>Power steering<< in the control unit overview on Plwis Tester Il9818 , then select >>Calibrate<< in the >>Maintenance/repairs<< menu and press [F12] to start.

# WM 489055 REPLACING POWER-STEERING GEAR (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > INFORMATION

The power-steering gear is purely electrically-assisted. There is no hydraulic assistance.

# WM 489055 REPLACING POWER-STEERING GEAR (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Raise the vehicle → 4XOOIN LIFTING THE VEHICLE .

2. Remove front wheels — 440519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WHEEL .

3. Remove front underbody panelling → 519219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COVER FOR FRONT UNDERBODY .

# WM 4890IN ASSESSMENT OF STEERING GEAR AFTER ACCIDENT DAMAGE (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > INFORMATION > FUNDAMENTALS

Various kinds of damage can occur to the steering gear in the event of accidents or driving conditions similar to accidents. In cases where the steering gear shows no external damage it can sometimes be difficult and costly to detect damage. Nevertheless, this damage represents an unacceptable risk for the vehicle, since it could lead to failure of the steering system.

A comprehensive check on al individual parts of the steering gear is not usuall feasible due to the relatively high cost and is not possible using ordinary workshop resources. Instead, consideration must be given to the condition of other components that are easier to check.

To decide whether the steering gear of a vehicle involved in an accident must be replaced or may continue to be used, the following guidelines are helpful.

# WM 489OIN ASSESSMENT OF STEERING GEAR AFTER ACCIDENT DAMAGE (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > INFORMATION > ASSESSMENT OF THE STEERING OF A VEHICLE INVOLVED IN AN ACCIDENT

The steering gear may remain in the vehicle if al the following conditions are met:

No visible damage to such front-axle parts as wheel rims, spring struts, wheel carriers, control arms, steering arms, tie rods, chassis subframe, the steering shaft or to the points on the body where wheel suspension parts are bolted on.

No impermissible rise in torque and no jamming or catching when the steering gear is turned from stop to stop. The front wheels must be free (front axle raised when turning and the ignition must be switched off (no power assistance).

The permissible tolerances for wheel alignment must not be exceeded.

The steering gear must be replaced by a new or exchange unit if one of the following points applies:

Visible or perceptible damage to the steering gear.

Fire damage (e.g. steering bellows burnt).

Permanent deformation or breakage of:

Steering-gear mountings

Tie-rod ball

Tie rods

Control dimension for tie-rod ball: If a control dimension is < 188 mm, the complete steering gear with tie rod and tie-rod ball must be replaced.

![](images/b1badd14c8a77a9f646a6903694d4cda95ed80ce794addd5f927c4ffb5a5df7c.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Tie-Rod Ball Control Dimension

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

Steering arms

Spring struts

Wheel carriers

Control arms

Chassis subframe

If the listed criteria are insuficient for a decision, we recommend that the steering gear be replaced with a new or exchange unit.

# WM 489OIN ASSESSMENT OF STEERING GEAR AFTER ACCIDENT DAMAGE (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > INFORMATION > EXCEPTIONAL REGULATION/ORDER HANDLING

If a workshop's intended exchange of steering gear is refused by a customer or insurer for reasons of costs, an expert or - if this is impossible abroad, the importer - should be called in at the cost of the

refusing party. If the decision contradicts the guideline, we recommend that a memorandum be drawn up on the point and that it be countersigned by the expert.
