# WM 440593 BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS (ALL MODELS) > TOOLS

![](images/3566292c53cf6e606f17769486f0bf4a8492087eeee3e9576d3d53e15553c2b3.webp)

![](images/93da32e85c905014fe8396bca6f9706d06a125355e01f75adc5b7d16120a1014.webp)

# WM 440593 BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS (ALL MODELS) > BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS > GENERAL INFORMATION ON BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS

Excessive rough running of the wheels, caused by wheel imbalance, flat spots and securing the wheel on the vehicle, causes vibrations and shaking in the steering wheel. This in turn leads to increased wear on various parts of the chassis.

Even if wheels are correctly balanced, roling and steering imbalance can still occur. E.g.:

oexcessive geometric errors (radial and lateral runout), oradial force variations (softer and more rigid areas in the tire).

# Information

Achieving a good result requires utmost care, observance of the instructions and procedure, and attempting to eliminate even the very last gram of imbalance.

Recommendations/prerequisites:

Wheel suspension elements must be in good working order.

The wheels must be clean with no foreign objects in the tire.

Use a tire measuring gauge, e.g. measuring gauge Nr.136 to check radial and lateral runout values on wheels without flat spots. Values of less than 1 mm are desirable - around 0.5 mm would be better.

To limit the number of radial runout errors and to optimize rolling smoothness, it is a good idea - and even necessary in some cases - to match the tire (i.e. to fi it at a favorable position with respect to the rim). Follow tips and fitting instructions as well as information on tire mounting paste for tires.

If the disc wheels (wheels without tires) are perfect but the complete wheels have large radial and lateral runout values (due to ply breakage or other damage), it may be necessary to replace the tire.

Balance used wheels only after they have been warmed up by driving, otherwise flat spots wil simulate imbalance. Never perform matching on wheels with flat spots. In the event of flat spots, wheels must be warmed up by driving 25 - 30 km (16 - 20 miles) on a motorway. Lift up the vehicle immediately on return. This prevents new flat spots from forming.

Correct tire pressure is an important prerequisite.   
Place the balancing weights at the prescribed position.

# WM 440593 BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS (ALL MODELS) > BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS > EXPLANATION OF TERMS > GEOMETRIC ERROR (RADIAL AND LATERAL RUNOUT)

Radial and lateral runout of the rim and/or rim/tire assembly.

# WM 440593 BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS (ALL MODELS) > BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS > EXPLANATION OF TERMS > FLAT SPOTS

Flat spots can occur on the tires if the vehicle is idle for extended periods.

WM 440593 BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS (ALL MODELS) > BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS > EXPLANATION OF TERMS > RADIAL FORCE VARIATIONS

![](images/d554d2598899f479fa78ed3f08a585b2523613a9abd5ab56602d64fbcfbb8127.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Rim/Tire Assembly Radial And Lateral Runout

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

The radial force is a force that compresses a tire. Based on its size, a tire has softer (-item A- ) and more rigid zones (-item B- ) due to constructive and production-related factors. Given this, the tire compresses to various extents at a constant wheel load (-arrow 1- ) and a constant tire pressure (-arrows 2- ). This varying spring action (-X- ) in the tire can cause vibrations in the chassis on even road surfaces and the driver may notice this as shaking in the steering wheel, for example. Measuring the radial force variation involves running the tire on a wheel balancer that measures radial force variation while applying a constant load to the tire. This simulates the rolling of the tire on a driving surface. Variations in radial force occur independently of the direction of rotation of the tire and are measured as the difference between the maximum and minimum radial force ("peak-to-peak" value).

# WM 440593 BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS (ALL MODELS) > BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS > EXPLANATION OF TERMS > 1. HARMONIC

The changes in radial force variation can be broken down mathematicall into individual variations. Porsche uses the value of the 1st Harmonic Variation (basic variation) to assess the tire from the point of view of rigidity. The 1st Harmonic Variation relates to the changes in radial force that cause the strongest vibrations. Changes in radial force can also result in further harmonic variations (2nd-4th Harmonic). These relate to the changes in radial force that cause weaker vibrations.

# WM 440593 BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS (ALL MODELS) > BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS > EXPLANATION OF TERMS > UNCONTROLLED MATCHING

Turn the tire on the wheel by 90° or 180° if necessary in order to achieve an acceptable value with regard to rolling smoothness (true running, imbalance and distribution of balance weights).

# WM 440593 BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS (ALL MODELS) > BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS > EXPLANATION OF TERMS > CONTROLLED MATCHING

With a balancing machine with matching program. In most cases, this produces an even beter result with regard to the rolling smoothness (true running, imbalance and distribution of the balance weights) than can be achieved with uncontrolled matching.

# WM 440593 BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS (ALL MODELS) > BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS > EXPLANATION OF TERMS > TIRE SEATING PRESSURE

This is the filing pressure after the tire has been fitted on the rim at which the tire bead, coming out of the deep bed, must pop over the hump of the rim bead. This seating pressure must not exceed 4 bar.

# WM 440593 BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS (ALL MODELS) > BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS > BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS

In certain cases, it may be necessary to measure radial force variations. This should be done before normal balancing is performed.

The entire process is subdivided into several operations:

1. Fitting the tire on the rim.

2.2.

A. Measuring radial force variations and optimizing the wheels if necessary. Then balancing the wheels.   
B. As an alternative to item 2 A, if there is no device available to measure radial force variations: Stationary balancing of the wheel (eliminating static and dynamic imbalance) with optimization of rolling smoothness.

3. Fitting the wheel on the vehicle.

# BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS > FURTHER TO 1: FITTING THE TIRE ON THE RIM

oRemove rubber residues and dried-on tire paste from the rim, especially from the rim bead and the hump.   
Check rim for damage; remove old balancing weights.   
o Use the specified tire mounting pastes Remaxx Sport mounting paste (from Rema Tip Top/Item No. 593 0577) or Bead Lubricant (from Rema Tip Top/Item No. 514 4985) or Gleitmittel VA sliding compound (from Azett/Item No. 5000-021-220) so that the tire does not turn on the rim - undoing all your careful work - the first time you drive the vehicle. If the tire turns by as litle as 20 mm with respect to the rim, this can worsen an optimum balancing result.   
o Fit tire on the rim. When doing so, it is a good idea - and even necessary in some cases - to fit the tire at a favorable position with respect to the rim (matching). Compare Controlled and Uncontrolled matching below.

# WARNING: High tire seating pressure

Risk of squashing or bruising → Use a tire filling cage.

![](images/8fadc82b9cebcf128dcdae18ba36e6dac3298e100cb5b9a76743dffaaec8fdfd.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Tire Filing Cage   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

oFill the tire to a maximum pressure of 4.0 bar. By the time the pressure reaches 4.0 bar, at the latest, the tire beads must pop out of the deep bed and over the hump of the rim bead in order to avoid fractures of the bead core. If necessary, interrupt the process and generously coat all necessary surfaces with sliding compound (tire mounting paste). Then repeat the process.   
oUncontrolled matching: Turn the tire on the wheel by 90° or 180° if necessary in order to achieve an acceptable value with regard to rolling smoothness (true running, imbalance and distribution of balance weights).   
oControlled matching: With a balancing machine with matching program. In most cases, this produces an even better result with regard to the rolling smoothness (true running, imbalance and distribution of the balance weights) than can be achieved with uncontrolled matching.   
Check the fit of the tire on the rim using the bead centering line.   
Set the prescribed tire pressure.

# BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS > FURTHER TO 2A: MEASURING RADIAL FORCE VARIATIONS

oTension wheel on balancing machine with radial force variation measurement (vibration monitoring system).   
oObserve the operating instructions of the balancing machine (adjust the machine from time to time).   
oThe contact surface of the wheel on the balancing flange (flat surface) and the centering surface must be clean.   
oThe display disabling function must be switched off.   
oAdjust tire pressure to 2.7 bar (best test pressure) when balancing and measuring radial force variations.   
oParticular attention must be paid to the wheel mounting when measuring radial force variations and when balancing. Using the special pressure pieces provided by the manufacturer of the balancing machine wil ensure that wheels are balanced accurately and there is the highest possible repeat accuracy. Read the operating instructions.

Maximum deviations permitted in radial force variation results:

![](images/ff4cf9afe99be6578e980dfa33cb086910ec9e231967437c8bf3b6ed5649b8cd.webp)

If these values are exceeded, the tire must be matched on the rim.

If these values are not reached, the wheel must be balanced.

# Information

A new tire must be fitted if the radial force variation cannot be reduced to the values listed in the table.

# WM 440593 BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS (ALL MODELS) > BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS > FURTHER TO 2B: STATIONARY BALANCING WITH OPTIMIZATION OF ROLLING SMOOTHNESS

Clamp wheel on stationary balancing machine.   
oRead the operating instructions for the balancing machine; adjust the machine from time to time, if necessary.   
The contact surface of the wheel on the balancing flange (flat surface) and the centering surface must be clean.   
Centre (clamp) the wheel from the inside using centering clamping device . This centering clamping device fits all wheel-balancing machines approved by Porsche.   
Set required tire pressure (tire-pressure plate).

Centre (clamp) the wheel from the inside using centering clamping device . This centering clamping device fits all wheel-balancing machines approved by Porsche.

Check radial and lateral runout during the first measuring run. Values of less than 1.0 mm are desirable - around 0.5 mm would be better.

Consider the size of the measured balancing weights and their distribution on the inner and outer planes (inner and outer rim flanges) critically.

A uniform distribution with low values (e.g. 35g/40g) means that the tire was fitted correctly and the quality of the tire and rim is good.

A value of 70g/90g (70g/90g with tire Pressure Monitoring) should not be exceeded with interior balancing behind the wheel center. A considerably different distribution, e.g. 40g/90g is not good; this usually indicates incorrect fitting. Problem wheels of this kind often have pronounced radial and lateral runout values.

This can be remedied by matching (use correct mounting paste). This can be improved with uncontrolled matching (manual); significant improvement is possible in almost all cases using the rolling smoothness optimization program (controlled matching).

tire pressure during balancing at required pressure.

Permissible residual imbalance of max. 8g on the rim flange. Panamera: Permissible residual imbalance of less than 3g, or max. 3g per plane

# WM 440593 BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS (ALL MODELS) > BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS > FURTHER TO 3: FITTING THE WHEEL ON THE VEHICLE

Never use an impact bolter.   
Observe the description on wheel removal and installation (fiting wheel on vehicle) → 440519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WHEEL .   
Fit the wheels with the lowest residual imbalance values on the front axle. Observe the rolling direction of the wheels.   
Fit wheel using a suitable commercially available tool.   
oScrew in wheel bolts by hand and then tighten evenly. Start at the top when tightening. Always observe the specified tightening torque of 160 Nm (118 flb.)   
Set required tire pressure (tire-pressure plate).

# WM 440593 BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS (ALL MODELS) > BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS > BALANCING WEIGHTS

Balancing weights: For balance stick-on weights .

Attach both weights to the inner side.

# WM 440593 BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS (ALL MODELS) > BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS > ATTACHING BALANCE STICK-ON WEIGHTS

Remove the protective film just before sticking on the weight, as prolonged exposure to the air will reduce the bonding strength.

Pay attention to cleanliness.

o Determine exact position of the balancing weights (if necessary, temporarily stick on the balancing weights with a strip of adhesive tape until the correct position is determined).

Prepare bonding surface on the rim. The bonding surface must be perfectly clean and free of grease.   
oRemove protective paper from the bonding surface of the weight and press the weight firmly into place.   
oThe balance stick-on weight must be in uniform contact over the entire surface.   
oCheck that the balancing weight is seated securely. A freshly affixed weight must not become detached from the rim when a shear load is applied at right angles to its longitudinal axis.

# WM 4405IN WHEELS AND TIRES (ALL MODELS) > CHECKING > CHECKING CONDITION

Tires are a safety element that meet the demands placed on them only if they have the correct air pressure and sufficient tread depth.

# Information

The > Tire pressure < display is for information purposes only.

tire pressure settings can only be entered according to the values in > Filing information<<. 1. Check condition and tire pressures. Valve caps protect the valve from dust and dirt and therefore from damage. 2. Always screw on valve caps tightly and replace missing valve caps.

For vehicles with Tire Pressure Monitoring (TPM), which can be identified by aluminum valves, the tire pressure must be adjusted according to the > Filing information << on the multi-function display. To do this, select > Main menu >> TPM > Filling information <<. Adjust the deviation values so that they range from 0.0 bar to +0.1 bar. Fill the tires according to the display using the tire-inflating device. Example: If the tire pressure display > Filling information << shows - 0.2 bar, 0.2 bar pressure must be added.

# Information

The > tire pressure << display is for information purposes only.

tire pressure settings can only be entered according to the values in >> Filing information <<.

Due to the pressure and temperature relationship (approx. 0.1 bar/10° C), the actual pressure values displayed under > tire pressure << on the multi-function display, or on the pressure gauge of the tire-inflating device, can deviate from the required pressure specified at 20° C on the tire pressure plate if the air temperature in the tire is significantly above (higher values) or significantly below 20° C (lower values). Changes in tire pressure are displayed after max. 1 minute under > Filing information << after switching on the ignition. A series of dashes (.-) wil appear instead of the tire pressure during this time.

For vehicles with tire Pressure Monitoring (TPM), always use plastic valve caps. Plastic valve caps protect against dust, dirt and humidity, and therefore against damage (corrosion).

Tires are a safety element that meet the demands placed on them only if they have the correct air pressure and sufficient tread depth.

X WARNiNG: Risk of accidents if the air pressure in the tires falls below the minimum pressure, if the tread depth is insufficient or if there are foreign bodies, pricks, cracks and bulges in the sidewall (ply breakage).

Modified handling behavior can cause accidents and significant material damage.

→ The tire pressure must never fall below the values specified (these are minimum pressures).

→ The tread depth must never fall below the minimum value.

→ A visual inspection of the tires (for cracks, pricks, bulges in the sidewall and/or foreign bodies) must

be carried out.

# WM 442655 REPLACING TIRE SEALING COMPOUND (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION ON TIRE SEALING COMPOUND

The intended position for the tire sealing compound should be taken from the Driver's Manual (index: tire sealing compound/sealant set for defective tires).

The use-by date of the tire sealing compound must be checked every 2 years.

If the tire sealing compound is out of date (or will be out of date by the next maintenance event), the tire sealing compound must be replaced.

The expiry date can be found on the packaging of the tire sealing compound/sealant set.

The Driver's Manual for the vehicle describes its use in detail (sealing of tire in the event of minor slashing damage). The tire sealing compound/sealant set is also supplied with instructions.

The tire sealing compound is extremely flammable and hazardous to health. Warnings to this effect are printed on the bottle and given in the Driver's Manual.

# WM 443219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WHEEL ELECTRONICS (ALL MODELS) > TECHNICAL VALUES

![](images/5872f52a70414081cacab192383035d1154e0bd7703fcb2ae75ea70fe60487ea.webp)

# WM 443219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WHEEL ELECTRONICS (ALL MODELS) > GENERAL INFORMATION ON WHEEL ELECTRONICS

The tire Pressure Monitoring (TPM) system is designed to constantly monitor the tire pressure when the vehicle is moving. One set of wheel electronics -8- per wheel is mounted in the rim well base. These measure tire pressure and temperature at regular intervals and transfer the values to a central control unit via a high-frequency route. The control unit evaluates the information and transfers the data to the instrument cluster if required. In this way, the driver is warned and informed if the tire pressure needs to be adjusted.

There are different types of wheel electronics -8- . Wheel electronics units with amplified transmitting power are used on the Macan. These transmit in the high-frequency range of:

• 433 MHz or 315 MHz.

The following points can be used as distinguishing features:

The labelling - 433 MHz or 315 MHz.   
The color (dark grey - 433 MHz; light grey - 315 MHz).   
The part number.   
No stars on the left and right of the slot.

# Valve must be replaced complete with screw -1, 3, 4- if:

The wheel electronics unit is removed   
The selflocking fastening screw -1- is loose The valve body -5- is bent   
The union nut -7- is loose.

# The wheel electronics unit -2- must be replaced if:

The housing is visibly deformed   
The filter surface (round, porous section on back of wheel electronics) is so badly soiled that it can no longer be cleaned by wiping   
tire sealing compound (tire sealing liquid) has been used   
The service life of the battery is exceeded   
There is a fault inside the wheel electronics unit.

# Information

The PIWis Tester Il9818 instructions take precedence since the description may be different with later Tester releases.

The procedure described here has been structured in general terms. Different text or additional information may appear in PIWis Tester Il 9818 .

1. Connect the PIWis Tester to the vehicle and start the Tester. Switch on ignition.   
2. Select the vehicle type and start the diagnostic application.   
3. Select the required control unit, e.g. tire Pressure Monitoring system in the overview.   
4. Extended identifications must now be selected.   
5. Enter the vehicle identification number and press [Enter] to confirm your entry.   
6. Maintenance/repairs must then be selected.   
7. Control unit replacement must now be selected. Then press[F12] to continue.   
8. Follow the instructions on the Tester.   
9. The Tester displays the message Coding has been completed successfull. Press [F12] to   
continue.   
10. Teach wheel IDs must now be selected. Then press [F12] to continue.   
11. Select the desired teaching process, then press [F12].   
12. Follow the instructions on the Tester and press [F12] to continue.   
13. Read out the fault memory and erase it if necessary.   
14. Check the TPM function during the test drive.

tire temperature during removal/mounting must be approx. 20 °C (at least 15 °C). Alow enough time to heat the vehicle/tires in a suitable environment if necessary (at room temperature of more than 15 °C). Example: If the room temperature of the workshop is approx. 20 C and the tire temperature is approx. - 15 °C, approx. 3 hours are required to heat the tires to the required temperature.

Before removal/mounting, it is important to establish whether a tire Pressure Monitoring system (TPM) is fitted! The tire valve serves as the distinguishing feature. Without TPM: rubber valve. With TPM: aluminum valve. If a TPM system is fitted, read the special information on the tire Pressure Monitoring system .

Vehicles with TPM: Before changing a tire, read out the remaining life span of the wheel electronics unit (battery capacity) using the PIWis Tester. The value you read out gives an indication as to whether or not it needs to be replaced (not a 100% value). If the values are considerably lower than expected for the next tire change, talk to the customer and determine whether he/she is happy to have the wheel electronics unit(s) replaced at this time.

• Use only TIP TOP Universal, Order No. 593 0601 (3.5 kg bucket) or Contifix as the removal/mounting paste (sliding compound). Use sufficient sliding compound.

No large point load for wheel (rim) and tire during removal/mounting. If this is not observed, damage will occur that will render a tire unusable (ready for disposal) and/or require a new rim.

•Before removal/mounting, check the mounting head (of the mounting machine) for damage (scoring, soiling). Clean or replace the mounting head if necessary to prevent paint damage and pressure marks on the rim flange.

Al parts that touch the disc wheel and tire are made of plastic to prevent damage to paintwork during removal/mounting. Protect the rim flange with adhesive tape if necessary. The mounting lever can also be covered with adhesive tape in order to avoid damaging the area around the spokes (during removal).

If you do not have a mounting lever with plastic protection, use a rim flange protector (assembly aid) and avoid letting it slip on to the rim flange.

Check the disc wheel for damage (sealing face between tire/rim, true running, superficial damage and deformation).

If you intend to continue using the tire, check it for damage (sealing face between tire/rim, ply damage, tire beads, sidewalls and tread depth).

The rubber valve must generally be replaced when a tire change is necessary. In vehicles with TPM (aluminum valve), the valve only needs to be replaced in exceptional cases. This is elaborated further in: "Special information on TPM" (module in this service information).

When mounting tires, pay particular attention to the direction of rotation and the inside/outside.

When replacing only one tire on an axle, make sure that the tread depth of the new tire does not differ from that of the other tire by more than 30%!

# WM 44019 MOUNTING TIRES (REMOVING AND INSTALLING TIRES) (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING/MOUNTING TIRES (REMOVING AND INSTALLING TIRES) > REMOVING TIRES

-or correct tire removal/mounting, follow the instructions provided for the tire removal/mounting machine.

See REQUIREMENTS/INFORMATION ON REMOVING/MOUNTING TIRES !

1. Fit and clamp a clean disc wheel on the tire removal/mounting machine. Check that the tire is seated securely and without damage (as described in the instructions provided for the tire removal/mounting machine).   
2. Unscrew the valve insert and release the air so that the tire is depressurized.   
3. Set the tire bead press-off tool (in accordance with the tire size).

![](images/8fbcf4e10384695cd27238feff3c52a627f7117fb63995eb2cd8d2bdef28b7ef.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Tire Press-Off Tool

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

1.3.1. Set the tire bead press-off tool to the inch graduation (rough setting in accordance with the tire size).

2.3.2. Then adjust the setting precisely (the press-off roller must not touch the rim when positioned on the tire). If this is not the case, the rim flange may be damaged by the press-off rollers.

4. Loosen the lower and upper tire bead (press the tire off the rim).

1. 4.1. The wheel must be turned anti-clockwise (anti-clockwise rotation of the mounting table) when pressing the tire off the rim (loosening the tire bead). Otherwise, excessive forces occur on the fastening bolts of the machine which can break the bolts.

First press off the lower tire bead and then the upper tire bead (to ensure that the wheel remains seated securely on the machine).

Coat the tire beads with mounting paste even at this stage of the procedure to make it easier to press the tire bead off.

2. 4.2. Loosen the two bead press-of tools again (by moving them back to their original position).

5. Before removing the tire, coat the tire beads with mounting paste again if necessary to facilitate removal.

# Information

1. Always use a bead holding-down device for removing the upper tire bead (second tire bead).   
2. Use the Wulstboy bead holding-down device (type 2 in section 6.2) for tire/wheel combinations that are difficult to remove.

# 1.6.1. Removing upper tire bead - type 1

Valve/wheel electronics unit at 12 o'clock position.

Fit the mounting head on the rim flange.

The mounting lever (with plastic protection) is pushed into the deep bed underneath the upper tire bead, and then guided over the mounting shoe and pushed down.

Lift the tire bead out of the rim bed by turning the wheel clockwise. Check the following while doing this:

1. Check that the bead lip is facing outwards and is full visible. Otherwise, the tire bead can become jammed and be damaged irreparably.   
2. The mounting lever must be the same distance from the inside of the tire and the valve during the entire removal procedure.   
3. Constantly check that the plastic protection (on the mounting lever) is positioned correctly in order to protect the rim.   
4. The lower (second) tire bead must be in the deep bed during removal.   
5. The tire bead must not be pressing against the wheel electronics unit.

# 2. 6.2. Removing upper tire bead using bead holding-down device type 2 = Wulstboy

Valve/wheel electronics unit at approx. 12 o'clock position.

Use the upper plastic press-off roller on the mounting machine to press the upper tire bead approx. 4 to 5 cm below the rim flange (max. 5 cm/the belt edge of the tire must not be deformed by the plastic press-off roller). This makes space for the bead holding-down device blocks.

Fit the bead holding-down device (Wulstboy) into the middle of the "wheel/rotary plate". Move the arm of the bead holding-down device to the 1 o'clock position.

Turn the wheel slowly in a clockwise direction (clockwise rotation) and insert the blocks of the bead holding-down device.

Remove the upper press-off roller on the mounting machine from the tire and fit the mounting head on the rim flange. Insert the mounting lever (with plastic protection) -1-and lever the upper tire bead over the mounting head.

Continue turning the disc wheel slowly (clockwise rotation) until the bead holding-down device (Wulstboy) is just in front of the mounting head. Remove the Wulstboy using holding-down device 9539. Continue turning the disc wheel slowly (clockwise rotation) until the upper bead is completely removed.

![](images/3164795470c62127fd470d671145c5c3648893a4eab9d1a7fe54a2ff8e295ae8.webp)  
Fig 2: Removing tire Using Wulstboy   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# 7. Removing lower tire bead:

Valve/wheel electronics unit at 12 o'clock position.

Pul he tire upwards and push it into the rim bed underneath the second tire bead using the mounting lever (plastic protection). Make sure that the valve/wheel electronics unit is not damaged.

Check the position of the mounting lever. The mounting lever must be the same distance from the inside of the tire and the valve during the entire removal procedure. Constantly check that the plastic protection (on the mounting lever) is positioned correctly in order to protect the rim.

Turn the wheel slowly clockwise until the tire is removed.

![](images/f7fb35b78c811b7db7d8c3fe89b28e072af2c5a7b734720ce8dba189da18a490.webp)  
Fig 3: Removing tire

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

8. Set the mounting lever and tire aside (in a safe/clean place).

Detach the disc wheel from the machine, remove it and lay it carefully aside (store in a safe place).

# WM 44019 MOUNTING TIRES (REMOVING AND INSTALLING TIRES) (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING/MOUNTING TIRES (REMOVING AND INSTALLING TIRES) > MOUNTING TIRES

NOTE: Wheel electronics

Wheel electronics unit and valve may have been fited incorrectly.

•Wheel electronics units may not have been assigned correctly.

→ Read and follow the installation instructions for the wheel electronics units. → 443219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WHEEL ELECTRONICS

→ Check that the wheel electronics units are assigned correctly.

# Information

For correct tire mounting, follow the instructions provided for the tire removal/mounting machine.   
Always use approved tires and tire sizes (specification code/speed index/load capacity). This data can be found in the applicable/current Technical Information.   
tire temperature during removal/mounting must be approx. 20 °C (at least 15 °C). Alw enough time to heat the vehicle/tires in a suitable environment if necessary (at room temperature of more than 15 °C). Example: If the room temperature of the workshop is approx. 20 °C and the tire temperature is approx. - 15 °C, approx. 3 hours are required to heat the tires to the required temperature.   
The wheel electronics must not be treated with compressed air, tire mounting paste, cleaning agents or any other solvents.   
Disc wheels with wheel electronics must not be cleaned with a high-pressure power cleaner before tires have been fitted.   
Do not expose filter surface of wheel electronics. Remove soiling with a lint-free cloth. Do not apply tire mounting paste to the wheel electronics unit. Alltraces of tire mounting paste must be removed from the wheel electronics unit.   
During fiting, ensure that the tire bead is not pressed against the wheel electronics unit.   
•Huge tension can be transferred to the tire bead when the mounting paste dries quickly. It is therefore absolutely essential to mount the upper and lower tire bead quickly and without delay.

# 1. Complete preparatory steps for mounting tires:

1. Remove abraded rubber particles from the disc wheel and check for damage. → 441202 CHECKING DISC WHEELS .   
2. Fit and clamp the clean wheel as described in the instructions provided for the tire removal/mounting machine.   
3. On vehicles with TPM, check the valve and wheel electronics unit for damage. Replace these components if they are damaged or if they do not comply with specifications (special information on TPM).   
4. Always replace the rubber valve (on vehicles without TPM). Use a commercially available insertion tool and tire mounting paste.   
5. If you intend to continue using the tire, check it for damage (sealing face between tire/rim, ply damage, tre beads, sidewalls and tread depth).   
6. As a general rule, check the bead area (mounting and sealing face) for damage before mounting tires (even new tires). Ensure that this area is perfectly clean to prevent any

slow air leaks (loss of tire pressure) in this area (after mounting the tire). A loss of tire pressure often goes unnoticed on vehicles without TPM. Serious consequence: Reduced driving dynamics and the tire can be damaged irreparably as a result of increased kneading action (overheating).

2. Coat the rim and tire (both bead areas) with a sufficient amount of tire mounting paste TIP TOP Universal, Order No. 593 0601 or Contifix. Absolute cleanliness is essential (clean brush/clean tire mounting paste). Make sure that there are no traces of tire mounting paste on the wheel electronics unit.

# 3. Fitting lower tire bead (first tire bead).

Place the tire at the correct position on the disc wheel (check direction of rotation and inside/outside position).

Push in mounting arm and position on top of the rim flange. The mounting head must be offset by 180° with respect to the valve.

![](images/382846aaf11208201ff2f6956b31297e25e0f259fcab533f07009ddb0a52a165.webp)  
Fig 1: Installing tire

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

Push the lower tire bead (first tire bead) partly over the rim flange and guide it through the mounting head → Mounting tire, lower tire bead, Figure 2Fig 2. Turn the disc wheel slowly in a clockwise direction (clockwise rotation of mounting table) until the lower tire bead is completely fitted.

![](images/74d4ad902a7bca8a8d1d0d1c7f8f77653d677291e5928ae337ace65ef97fe4c9.webp)  
Fig 2: Installing tire

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Fitting upper tire bead (second tire bead) using bead holding-down device. This presses the tire bead into the deep bed.

# Information

1. Always use a bead holding-down device for mounting the upper tire bead (second tire bead).   
2. There are two types of bead holding-down devices. These are described in sections 4.1 and 4.2 below.   
3. Use the Wulstboy bead holding-down device (type 2 in section 4.2) for tire/wheel combinations that are difficult to mount.

# 1. 4.1. Fitting upper tire bead (second tire bead) using bead holding-down device type 1 = special tool 9539

Position the mounting head -1- approx. 15 cm to the right of the valve -2- .

Hold the upper tire bead (second tire bead) in the deep bed using the bead holding-down device 9539 and turn the disc wheel slowly at the same time (clockwise rotation of mounting table) until the upper tire bead is completely fitted.

![](images/3c377892e1b5909227396669846481e17996dfbc91b30efac5fd514366a7629c.webp)  
Fig 3: Installing tire Using Holding-Down Device 9539   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# 2. 4.2. Fitting upper tire bead (second tire bead) using bead holding-down device type 2 = Wulstboy

Position the mounting head approx. 15 cm to the right of the valve.

Use the upper plastic press-off roller (on the mounting machine) to press the upper tire bead approx. 4 to 5 cm below the rim flange (max. 5 cm/the belt edge of the tire must not be deformed by the plastic press-off roller). This makes space for the bead holding-down device blocks.

Fit the bead holding-down device (Wulstboy) into the middle of the "wheel/rotary plate" -1- . Move the arm -2- of the bead holding-down device to the 1 o'clock position.

Turn the wheel slowly in a clockwise direction (clockwise rotation) and insert the blocks -3- of the bead holding-down device.

Continue turning the disc wheel slowly (clockwise rotation) until the upper bead is completely fitted.

After fitting the upper tire bead, loosen the bead holding-down device by turning the disc wheel anti-clockwise (anti-clockwise rotation) and remove the blocks using the upper press-off roller.

![](images/410daf3e0b346d6d1497f1f6b23ae9bd167da4dc91b30098727db7efac1d9f41.webp)  
Fig 4: Identifying Wulstboy Blocks

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# 5. Filling/setting tires.

1.5.1. Remove entire wheel from tire fitting unit.

WARNING: High tire seating pressure

1. Risk of squashing or bruising → Use a tire filling cage.

2.5.2. Fil the tire (without the valve insert) with air immediately in the tire filling cage (while the tire mounting paste is still fully effective). Continue filing the tire until the tire beads slide/jump over the humps (max. 3.3 bar/48 psi).

If the tire is not seated correctly when the maximum permitted tire seating pressure (max. 3.3 bar/48 psi) is applied, coat the wheel and tire again with tire mounting paste TIP TOP Universal or Contifix and repeat the procedure.

![](images/5c6ac69c59e358c866f33b745def66634012d913186830417f670812e62a1f44.webp)  
Fig 5: Identifying tire Filing Cage

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. 5.3. Screw in new valve insert. Counter at the valve body when tightening. Required tightening torque is 0.2 Nm/0.1 ftlb to 0.35 Nm/0.2 ftlb. (20 to 35 Ncm/1.6 to 3 inlb.). A safety valve screw-on tool with tightening control (e.g. from Butler) is ideal for this.

Fill tire to the setting pressure of 4.0 bar (58 psi). Check that the tire bead is seated correctly. The tire must be lying evenly against the rim all the way around.

Set the prescribed tire pressure. → 4405IN WHEELS AND TIRES/tire PRESSURE .   
Screw on valve cap.

6. Balance the wheel → 440593 BALANCING/OPTIMIZING WHEELS

7. Perform a test drive. Avoid extreme driving maneuvers (acceleration, braking) during the test drive to prevent the tire from turning on the rim.

This can happen if the tire mounting paste is not completely dry. Optimum balancing will be impaired as a result.

Observe the following criteria during the test drive:

1.7.1. TPM function (tire Pressure Monitoring system).

Before starting the test drive (with "ignition on'"), select the mounted set of wheels under Main menu > tire pressure > Settings in the instrument cluster. The control unit then learns the wheel positions again while the vehicle is driving.

The system starts learning as soon as you accelerate above 25 km/h (16 mph). The learning time is normally about 30 seconds, but can take several minutes when the vehicle is driven in a metallic environment (e.g. multi-storey car park, bridge and other concrete, highly metallic surfaces).

2. 7.2. Rough running performance and vibrations

3.7.3. Vehicle handling.

# WM 4440IN INFORMATION ON TIRES/MOUNTING TIRES (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > TIRES > TIRE DAMAGE - CAUSED WHILE DRIVING

If a tire is damaged and it cannot be determined with absolute certainty that there is no ply damage - with all of its consequences - or if the tire was thermally or mechanically overloaded due to a loss of pressure or other prior damage, we recommend replacement of the tire in question for safety reasons.

# WM 4440IN INFORMATION ON TIRES/MOUNTING TIRES (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > TIRES > TIRE DAMAGE - CAUSED WHILE REMOVING/MOUNTING TIRES

When mounting tubeless tires, check the sealing face of the tire and the disc wheel for cleanliness and any signs of damage. Bear in mind here that the bead base performs the sealing function on tubeless tires. When mounting the tire beads, use only the specified tire mounting pastes. The follwing can occur if an unsuitable mounting paste is used:

Twisting of the tire on the rim.   
Fracture of the bead bundle during mounting and if the seating pressure is too high.   
Damage to the tire bead.   
Damage to the rim surface by aggressive substances.

# WM 4440IN INFORMATION ON TIRES/MOUNTING TIRES (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > TIRES > REPLACING TIRES

Tires should not be more than 6 years old!

Repairs to the tires are not permitted nor is the use of inner tubes in tubeless tires.

When replacing a tire on an axle, make sure that the tread depth of the new tire does not differ from that of the other tire by more than 30%.

If new tires are mounted or the tires of one axle are replaced, tres of the same make and with the same specification code must always be used on each of the two axles.

If tires are replaced on one axle only, the diferent tread depth in relation to the other axle can cause a noticeable change in the handling the driver has become accustomed to. This is especially true if new tires are mounted on the rear axle. This effect decreases with increasing tire mileage.

The overview of summer and winter tires is included in Technical Information (Tl), Group 4. When replacing summer tires, pay close attention to the tire specification number for the same make of tire. The specification code (for example NO) distinguishes the summer tires specially authorized by Porsche from other models of the same tire type and size.

Customers should be informed that the ful performance of new or newly mounted tires is achieved only after driving the vehicle for a distance of 100 to 200 km (60 to 120 miles). Extreme driving maneuvers (acceleration, braking) should be avoided.

# WM 440IN INFORMATION ON TIRES/MOUNTING TIRES (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > TIRES > TIRE STORAGE

Tires must be stored in a cool, dry and dark room with adequate ventilation. They must never come into contact with fuel, oil, grease or chemicals. Complete wheels can be stacked for storage. It is advisable to increase the tire pressure by 0.4 bar (6 psi).

If the tires are not mounted on wheels, store them in the vertical position. Tires stored in vertical position should be turned every two weeks in order to prevent excessive flat spots. If the tires are stacked in horizontal position, they will become severely deformed and cannot be seated in the rim flange easily when mounted.

Tires age due to physical and chemical processes, which can impair their function. If they are stored for an extended period, they wil harden and become brittle faster than tires that are in continual use. Hairline ageing cracks can occur on older tires. If tires are in use, the kneading action activates the plasticizer in the rubber and thereby prevents hardening and cracking.

# WM 40IN INFORMATION ON TIRES/MOUNTING TIRES (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > TIRES > TIRE IDENTIFICATION (SPEED CLASSES/TIRE AGE)

Tires should not be more than 6 years old!

The age of the tire can be determined from the manufacturer's code, which is shown behind the DOT code on the tire sidewall The date of manufacture (the last four digits) is shown at the end of the code!

# WM 4440IN TIRES (ALL MODELS) > GENERAL MOUNTING INSTRUCTIONS > GENERAL

Always use new rubber valves when changing tires.

The metal valve only needs to be replaced in certain cases. → 443219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WHEEL ELECTRONICS   
When fitting tires, the direction of rotation and the inner and outer sides should be noted.   
Only use TIP TOP Universal or Contifix tire fitting paste.

Before mounting the tires on the wheels, check for damage (cracks, dents, etc.) as well as radial and lateral runout. Maximum permissible radial runout and lateral runout of alloy wheels = 0.7 mm. Maximum permissible radial runout and lateral runout of the wheel with tire = 1.25 mm. Try to keep the values at less than 1.0 mm - around 0.5 mm is better.

When mounting tubeless tires, check the sealing face of the tire and the disc wheel for cleanliness and any signs of damage. Bear in mind here that the bead base performs the sealing function on tubeless tires. When mounting the tire beads, use only the specified tire mounting pastes. The following can occur if an unsuitable mounting paste is used:

Twisting of the tire on the rim   
Fracture of the bead core during mounting if the seating pressure is too high Damage to the tire bead   
Damage to the rim surface by aggressive substances.

If Contifix is used, apply sparingly to the tire beads (due to risk of the tire turning on the rim). If possible, the vehicle should not be driven for 24 hours after tire mounting or matching.

# Information

Customers should be informed that the full performance of new or newly mounted tires is achieved only after a distance of 100 to 200 km (60 to 120 miles) has been driven. Extreme driving maneuvers (acceleration, braking) should be avoided.   
The absolute limit on how far the tire can turn on the wheel must be regarded as 20 mm. Furthermore, this will worsen the result of optimum balancing.   
Mark the relative positions of the tire and wheel for reference.

In order to optimize roling smoothness, it is important - and necessary in some cases - to mount the tir at a good position with respect to the rim (matching).

# WM 4440IN TIRES (ALL MODELS) > GENERAL MOUNTING INSTRUCTIONS > UNCONTROLLED MATCHING

Turn the tire on the wheel by 90° or 180° if necessary in order to achieve an acceptable value with regard to rolling smoothness (true running, imbalance and distribution of balance weights).

# WM 4440IN TIRES (ALL MODELS) > GENERAL MOUNTING INSTRUCTIONS > CONTROLLED MATCHING

With a balancing machine with matching program. In most cases, this produces an even better result

with regard to the roling smoothness (true running, imbalance and distribution of the balance weights) than can be achieved with uncontrolled matching.

# WM 4440IN TIRES (ALL MODELS) > GENERAL MOUNTING INSTRUCTIONS > MOUNTING TIRES

WARNING: High tire seating pressure

Risk of squashing or bruising → Use a tire filling cage.

![](images/c131961b2ce67e5bf12e03703586213a4d89907e121c977219e46197e338958f.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Tire Filing Cage

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

oAfter mounting the tubeless tires, inflate them without valve insert to max. 4.0 bar (58 psi) gauge pressure to ensure they are seated properly on the rim. By the time the pressure reaches 4.0 bar (58 psi), at the latest, the tire beads must pop out of the deep bed and over the hump of the rim bead in order to avoid fractures of the bead core. Interrupt the process if necessary and generously coat all necessary surfaces with sliding compound (tire mounting paste) again. Then repeat the process. Screw in the valve insert and set the specified tire pressure.

If new tires are to be mounted or the tires of one axle are to be replaced, tires of the same make and with the same specification code must always be used on each of the two axles. If tires are replaced on one axle only, the different tread depth in relation to the other axle can cause a noticeable change in the handling the driver has become accustomed to. This is especially true if new tires are mounted on the rear axle. This effect decreases with increasing tire mileage.

# Information

If a tire is damaged and it cannot be determined with absolute certainty that there is no ply damag - with all of its consequences - or if the tire was thermally or mechanically overloaded due to a los: of pressure or other prior damage, we recommend replacement of the tire in question for safety reasons.   
When replacing a tire on an axle, make sure that the tread depth of the new tire does not differ from that of the other tire by more than 30 %.   
Repairs to the tires are not permitted nor is the use of inner tubes in tubeless tires.   
When replacing summer tires, pay close attention to the tire specification number.

The overview of summer and winter tires is included in Technical Information (Tl), Group 4. When replacing summer tires, pay close attention to the tire specification number for the same make of tire. The specification characters (for example NO) distinguish the summer tires specially authorized by Porsche from other models of the same tire type and size.

# WM 449503 SUSPENSION ALIGNMENT, COMPLETE (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > GENERAL PROCEDURE FOR SUSPENSION ALIGNMENT

Perform suspension alignment using an electronic wheel-alignment analyzer. Measurement procedures are described in the operating instructions for the wheel-alignment analyzer used.

For nominal value for front and rear axles, refer to the Technical data. → 4495TW ADJUSTMENT VALUES FOR SUSPENSION ALIGNMENT .

In order to exclude erroneous measurements, the following preconditions must be met before alignment and the following points should be given special attention:

Empty weight of vehicle according to DIN 70020, i.e. vehicle in ready-to-drive condition with full tank and including tools but without driver or additional weights.

Joint and wheel-bearing play OK (wheel-bearing play cannot be adjusted).

tire pressure in accordance with regulations, fairly uniform tire tread.

Use puller hook 9229/1to pulloff the hub caps (in order to fit the quick-clamping holders).

Quick-clamping holder with adapter (for the measured-value pickups/measuring reflectors) correctly secured to the wheels.

Use quick-clamping unit WE 1621 → Self-centering quick-clamping holder (example) to secure the measured-value pickups/measuring reflectors to the wheels.

The self-centering quick-clamping holders are positioned centrall (with the claws first) in the center of the rim and are tautened in the rim by turning the straining ring (clockwise).

![](images/cc579088c9ab396fea245ba345a1cd852c5cc21805c931ec074eabebea99f97e.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Self-Centering Quick-Clamping Holder   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

Receiving surfaces for the quick-clamping holders on the wheels and the adapter surfaces must be clean and flat. Always check the levelling surface on the wheels precisely in particular before fitting the quickclamping holders.

Strictly comply with maintenance intervals for measuring equipment and measuring platform. If the levelling of the measuring platform or measuring station is done in-house, leveling equipment is required. A spirit level is not adequate.

Skilled handling of measuring equipment and measuring platform.

Sliding plates with transverse motion (rotary motion) at the rear axle are advisable.

Refer to the Technical Literature provided the manufacturer of the measuring equipment and the manufacturer of the measuring platform.

Do not treat measured values as a whole, but very critically with regard to driving dynamics, high-speed strength of the tires, tire wear and cost/benefit effects (time required for correction of insubstantial deviations). The toe values are of decisive significance for driving dynamics and tire wear.

Perform suspension alignment only in the sequence specified in the service information. The camber

values at the front axle are valid if the wheels are in the straight-ahead position. Steering wheel and steering gear in center position when toe is being adjusted.

Before wheel alignment values are adjusted at front and rear axles, it is recommended that the vehicle height be checked at the DIN empty weight. Conclusions can then be drawn about wheel alignment values in the event of any suspension alignment that becomes necessary later.

# WM 449503 SUSPENSION ALIGNMENT, COMPLETE (ALL MODELS) > HEIGHT CHECK > SPECIAL NOTES FOR VEHICLES WITH AIR SUSPENSION

On vehicles with air suspension, the vehicle must be set to normal level. The vehicle may be aligned and adjusted in this position only.

If the control unit or one of the level sensors was replaced, calibration must be carried out using the Porsche System Tester. → 430115 CALIBRATING THE LEVELLING SYSTEM

Adjust vehicle to normal level:

1. Drive vehicle onto the wheel-alignment platform, switch off engine and move selector lever to position P.

2. PIWis Tester Il 9818 must now be connected.

Do not get into or out of the vehicle while adjusting the vehicle to normal level and after adjusting it to normal level for suspension alignment. This can give false alignment results.

3. Select >>Levelling system/PASM<< >>Drive links/checks<<>>Adjust vehicle level<< in the control unit overview.

4. Select the value Low level 1 and press [F8] to start. The vehicle adjusts to Low Level.

5. Once Low Level has been reached, select Normal Level and press [F8] to start. The vehicle now adjusts to Normal Level.

# WM 449503 SUSPENSION ALIGNMENT, COMPLETE (ALL MODELS) > HEIGHT CHECK > CHECKING VEHICLE HEIGHT

1. To check the height, position ready-to-drive vehicle (fully tanked with tire repair kit or spare wheel and tools) on a flat surface or on the measuring station. The normal vehicle level must be set for vehicles with air suspension. Please read the section: Special notes for vehicles with air suspension

2. On vehicles with air suspension/levelling system, switch off the levelling system (and switch it back on again when work is complete).

1.2.1. Use PIWis Tester Il 9818 to select >>Levelling system/PASM<< >>Drive links/checks<< >>Activate/deactivate vehicle<< in the control unit overview.

2. 2.2. Select the value Deactivate levelling system (permanently) and press [F8] to start. The levelling system is now switched off.

3. Compress vehicle at front and rear axles by approximately 25 mm 2-3 times and allow it to spring back freely.

4. Open the bonnet.

5. Measure the vehicle height -dimension 1- at all four wheels on the vehicle.

Fig 1: Identifying Wheel To Wing Lower Edge Dimension (Rear Axle)

# WM 449503 SUSPENSION ALIGNMENT, COMPLETE (ALL MODELS) > REAR-AXLE AND FRONT-AXLE WHEEL ALIGNMENT > CHECKING/ADJUSTING WHEEL ALIGNMENT

Toe difference angle and caster cannot be adjusted.   
Camber at the front axle cannot be adjusted. But camber can be centered evenly within the tolerance range by moving the front-axle carrier. 1. Prepare vehicle for checking and/or adjusting wheel alignment values. Place front wheels on

turntable and rear wheels on rotary/sliding plates.

2. Compress vehicle as far as possible (by a few mm) at front and rear axles twice or three times and allow it to spring back freely.

# WM 449503 SUSPENSION ALIGNMENT, COMPLETE (ALL MODELS) > REAR-AXLE AND FRONT-AXLE WHEEL ALIGNMENT > CENTERING CAMBER ON THE FRONT AXLE

Camber at the front axle cannot be adjusted. But camber can be centered evenly within the tolerance range by moving the front-axle carrier.

All axle adjustment values must be checked whenever the camber is adjusted!

1. Remove front underbody panelling → 519219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COVER FOR FRONT UNDERBODY .

2. Unscrew fastening screws -1 and 2- and remove heat shields at the left and right.

![](images/82b0e94ce4c65269a6c4e5e9548a61772c9715da3a016f9b23ade49ff796e491.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Front-Axle Carrier Heat Shield

3. Loosen fastening screws -1 and 3- on the transmission support -2- . This ensures that the transmission mount is not strained.

![](images/17a729cc85ba2bd1eb38f7b9730f45ab668b98c5cfbe5fadbfd88d9df361ad16.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Transmission Support Screws

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Loosen fastening screws -1 to 8- on the front-axle carrier.

![](images/f37b47279ee1059f0e0164e78fbed9dcbba1ec8d25bbff63f0922fe4b1dca20e.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Front-Axle Carrer Mounting   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Raise the front of the vehicle at the lifting platform jacking points using an axle lift.

6. Move the front-axle carier with engine mount and anti-roll bar to the required position using a plastic-coated tire iron — Moving front-axle carrier . Before checking the camber values, compress the vehicle at the front axle several times.

![](images/825c14481cdb42daaac98002835b2c98d739e012cfce00bfe7a0dd447e542b62.webp)  
Fig 4: Moving Front-Axle Carrier

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Screw in and tighten new fastening screws -1 and 4- one after the other. Step 1: Initial tightening 115 Nm (85 ftlb.) Step 2: Final tightening +90°   
8. Screw in and tighten new fastening screws -2 and 3- one after the other. Step 1: Initial tightening 115 Nm (85 ftlb.) Step 2: Final tightening +90°   
9. Screw in and tighten new fastening screws -5 and 8- one after the other. Step 1: Initial tightening 115 Nm (85 ftb.) Step 2: Final tightening +90°   
10. Screw in and tighten new fastening screws -6 and 7- one after the other. Step 1: Initia tightening 115 Nm (85 fb.) Step 2: Final tightening +90°

![](images/2a067390461ad5c6315b39995d6d24f013f8734b768bdf9bd5e16005a3b54693.webp)  
Fig 5: Identifying Front-Axle Carrer Mounting   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

11. Tighten fastening screws -1 and 3- on the transmission support -2- . Tightening torque 70 Nm (52 ftlb.)

![](images/36c35a30034c098c8f800ee14bbf4f39aa09302a57540d3395b9d07208f81e78.webp)  
Fig 6: Identifying Transmission Support Screws   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

12. Check the camber value again.

13. Install heat shields at the left and right and tighten fastening screws -1 and 2- . Fastening screws -1- : Tightening torque 9 Nm (6.5 ftlb.) Fastening screw -2- : Tightening torque 20 Nm (15 ftlb.)

![](images/ca7d81f32a5b89da432cda9a29ebc089fd92cd6e22f51706a88e77ef4b870a30.webp)  
Fig 7: Identifying Front-Axle Carrier Heat Shield

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

14. Install front underbody panelling → 519219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COVER FOR FRONT UNDERBODY .

# WM 449503 SUSPENSION ALIGNMENT, COMPLETE (ALL MODELS) > REAR-AXLE AND FRONT-AXLE WHEEL ALIGNMENT > ADJUSTING REAR-AXLE CAMBER

# WM 449503 SUSPENSION ALIGNMENT, COMPLETE (ALL MODELS) > REAR-AXLE AND FRONT-AXLE WHEEL ALIGNMENT > ADJUSTING FRONT-AXLE TOE

1. Clamp steering wheel in center position using steering-wheel holder -A- . Use only steering-wheel holders that do not project into the area of the airbag unit -B- . If necessary, shorten the guide rod on the steering-wheel holder at the top -arrow- .

![](images/6088cf1c77844225b1825fe33abd089cd8504ed3e28f5e8a0aebf0cbc11d11bd.webp)  
Fig 1: Locating Steering-Wheel Holder

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

For fast and reliable steering wheel alignment in center position, use a steering wheel alignment gauge WE 1343 (with integrated angle measurement box).

![](images/03246248a5216cf94f527bca453b4d564ad1d24550cd5a836ae0cde6a60abc75.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Steering Wheel Alignment Gauge

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Measure dimension -a- between the tie-rod ball -1- and tie rod -2- at the left and right and take note of the value. Dimension -a- should be the same before and after alignment at the left and right (maximum difference between left and right < 2.5 mm).

![](images/bc37302bd646598a7569f288b1f1b6b1b03eb0b2ad0959a2fddb0429f196b6be.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Tie Rod Dimension

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Loosen lock nut -B- . Counter at the tie-rod ball-c- while doing this.

# Information

Make sure that the bellows are not twisted after turning the tie rods!

4.Adjust the toe at the left and right wheel using hexagon -A- .

![](images/f8985db907e03c89de8f2d30886d15921bcf1f0dadfc41b6cf47a5464e5dd10f.webp)  
Fig 4: Identifying Front-Axle Toe Lock Nut And Tie Rod Ball

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5.Tighten lock nut -B- and check the toe value again. Tightening torque 90 Nm (67 ftlb.)

# WM 449503 SUSPENSION ALIGNMENT, COMPLETE (ALL MODELS) > REAR-AXLE AND FRONT-AXLE WHEEL ALIGNMENT > SUBSEQUENT WORK

WARNiNG: Steering-angle sensor not calibrated or calibrated incorrectly •Unexpected vehicle handling •Steering-angle sensor does not function Malfunction in steering-angle sensor

→ After working on wheel suspension parts, when replacing the steering-angle sensor and after changing the wheel alignment values, calibrate the steering-angle sensor using PIWis Tester II 9818 → Keep the front wheels in straight-ahead position on the measuring platform during calibration.

→ On vehicles with electromechanical steering, also re-teach the electric steering lock settings.

1.The steering-angle sensor must be calibrated if the previous wheel alignment values (on rear and/or front axle) have been changed. → 456005 INITIALIZING AND CALIBRATING STEERING-ANGLE SENSOR . In addition, calibrate the distance measuring sensor (ACC sensor) control unit and front camera (if fitted). → 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR → 9638K2 CALIBRATING FRONT CAMERA .

2. Once you have calibrated the steering-angle sensor, re-teach the electric steering lock settings with the engine running.

In each phase, turn the steering wheel fully to the right and then to the left and hold it at full lock for a short time (follow instructions on the Tester).

# WM 4495TW ADJUSTMENT VALUES FOR SUSPENSION ALIGNMENT (ALL MODELS)

Information

# Adjusting the front axle

The front axle of the Macan can be adjusted as follows:

Toe : Adjustment using the tie rod   
Camber : Adjustment by moving the front-axle carrier (necessary if max. difference from left to right is exceeded)   
Caster: Cannot be adjusted!

For a detailed description, see — 449503 SUSPENSION ALIGNMENT, COMPLETE .

→ On vehicles with electromechanical steering, also re-teach the electric steering lock settings.

# WM 4495TW CONVERSION TABLE FOR WHEEL ALIGNMENT VALUES (ALL MODELS) > MINUTES TO DECIMAL DEGREES

Information

The wheel alignment values are specified in degrees and minutes in the Technical Manual (division in 60 units).   
In countries in which the decimal degree is widely used, the electronic wheel alignment testers can be converted from degrees/minutes (division in 60 units) to decimal degrees (division in 100 units) by pressing a key (special function). This function is standard for the electronic wheel alignment testers approved by Porsche.   
Minutes (') can be converted into decimal degrees and decimal degrees into minutes (') using the conversion table. To do this, read out the required values from the table using the co-ordinates.

![](images/1f6d03f54ef98d272e5ef4904126f1afe2cb6fa55476ccbcacca8e07ee064d5f.webp)

# WM 4495TW CONVERSION TABLE FOR WHEEL ALIGNMENT VALUES (ALL MODELS) > MINUTES TO DECIMAL DEGREES > CONVERSION FROM MINUTES TO DECIMAL DEGREES (EXAMPLES)

Example 1: toe 17 min (17') = 0.283 decimal degrees according to table. Procedure for this: The imaginary line starting at the top of the 7-min column moving downwards and the line starting on the left in the 10-min row moving right meet at point/column 0.283.

Example 2: camber 1° 25' (1 degree and 25 min) = 1.417 decimal degrees. This is the result from the table (1 degree or 60 min) = 1.000 + 0.417 (25 min).

# WM 4495TW CONVERSION TABLE FOR WHEEL ALIGNMENT VALUES (ALL MODELS) > MINUTES TO DECIMAL DEGREES > CONVERSION FROM DECIMAL DEGREES TO MINUTES (EXAMPLES)

Example 1: toe 0.350 decimal degree = 21 min (21'). A search is performed for the decimal value (0.350) in the table. The co-ordinates are then formed from this point/value. Line to the left = 20' and line upwards = 1' (which equals 20' + 1').

Example 2: camber 1.683 decimal degrees = 1° 41' (1 degree and 41 min). This result is obtained as follows: Split the value into 1.000 = 1 degree (1°) and search for the remainder 0.683 in the table. Then form the co-ordinates again. Line to the left = 40' and line upwards = 1' (which equals

40' + 1').

# WM 370235 CHECKING AND TOPPING UP ATF (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > TEST CONDITIONS

Always pay particular attention to the following before raising the vehicle:

Deactivate the leveling system before raising the vehicle (press and hold the levelling system button for at least 10 seconds).   
If a transmission range is engaged while the vehicle is raised, the levelling system must first be deactivated using PIWIS Tester Il 9818 . To do this, select >>Levelling system/PASM<< >>Drive links/checks<< >>Activate/deactivate vehicle<< in the control unit overview. Select the value "Deactivate levelling system (permanently)" and press "Start" [F8] to execute the function. Re-activate the levelling system when the work is complete. To do this, select the value "Activate levelling system" in the same menu item and press "Start" [F8] to execute the function.   
Transmission must not be in limp-home mode.   
•Warm up transmission in lower load range. Switch al transmission ranges several times while doing so.   
Read out the ATF temperature using PIWis Tester Il 9818.   
ATF temperature: 30 - 50 °C. •Selector lever is in position P.   
Parking brake actuated.   
Test and filing process at idle speed.   
Air conditioning and heating switched off.   
The ATF temperature must not be higher than 30 C at the beginning of the test.   
If the ATF temperature is higher than 30 C, let the transmission cool down.

# WM 370235 CHECKING AND TOPPING UP ATF (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK

To ensure that the transmission is filled correctly, the vehicle must be horizontal on the lifting platform.

1. Remove cover for front underbody. → Removing cover for front underbody   
2. Place oil collection pan under the transmission.

# WM 370235 CHECKING AND TOPPING UP ATF (ALL MODELS) > CHECKING AND TOPPING UP ATF

WARNING: Hot fluid

•Danger of scalding

→ Let the fluid cool down.   
→ Wear personal protective gear.

NOTE: Dirt and contamination

Risk of damage to units or components

→ Protect components from dirt and contamination.   
→ Clean or replace dirty components.

NOTE: Fill level too low

Risk of damage to components.

→ Do not start the engine.   
→ Do not tow the vehicle.

# Information

Only use oil approved by Porsche in the Porsche Doppelkupplung (PDK) .

# Information

Read out the ATF temperature using PIWIS Tester II 9818.   
The ATF temperature must not be higher than 30 C at the beginning of the ATF test.   
The ATF level changes as the ATF temperature changes.   
Perform ATF test when the engine running and selector lever in position P.   
An ATF test performed when the ATF temperature is too low willresult in overfilling.   
An ATF test performed when the temperature is too high will result in insufficient filling.   
An ATF level that is too high or too low wil impair the function of the transmission.

# Information

The ATF level is checked at the ATF inspection plug.   
The ATF level is correct if a small amount of fluid still emerges at the ATF inspection plug at an ATF temperature of between 30° and 50 °C.

# Information

Always pay particular attention to the following before raising the vehicle:

Deactivate the levelling system before raising the vehicle (press and hold the levelling system button for at least 10 seconds). If a transmission range is engaged while the vehicle is raised, the levelling system must first be deactivated using PIWIS Tester Il 9818. To do this, select >>Levelling system/PASM<< >>Drive links/checks<< >>Activate/deactivate vehicle<< in the control unit overview. Select the value "Deactivate leveling system (permanently)" and press "Start" [F8] to execute the function. Re-activate the levelling system when the work is complete. To do this, select the value "Activate levelling system'" in the same menu item and press "Start" [F8] to execute the function.

.Read off the ATF temperature on PIWis Tester ll 9818 while the engine is running.

2. Leave engine running at idle speed.

3. Place oil collection pan underneath.

4. Fill manual metering pump Manual metering pumps HDP 500 Porsche WE 1372 with ATF for the Porsche Doppelkupplung (PDK).

5.Check and top up ATF.

1.5.1. When an ATF temperature of 30 C is reached, unscrew the ATF inspection plug -arrow- .   
2.5.2. If ATF emerges from the ATF control opening before the ATF temperature has reached 40 °C, the ATF level is OK.   
3.5.3. If no ATF emerges at a temperature of up to 40 C, add ATF using manual metering pump HDP 500 Porsche WE 1372 until ATF emerges.

Fig 1: Locating ATF Inspection Plug

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# Information

1. The ATF inspection plug must be closed again at 50 °C at the latest. . Switch off the engine if necessary, let the transmission cool down and repeat the test.

6. Screw in and tighten new ATF inspection plug with a new sealing ring. Tightening torque 45 Nm (33 ftlb.)

# WORK

1. Install cover for front underbody. → Installing cover for front underbody   
2. Move oil collection pan away.   
3. Perform a test drive.

# WM 3704K2 CALIBRATING SELECTOR KNOB (ALL MODELS) > CALIBRATING SELECTOR KNOB

Do not operate the brakes during the entire procedure.

1. Switch off ignition.   
2. Move selector knob to position P .   
3. Open the driver's door.   
4. Switch ignition on and then off again.   
5. The four position displays (P; R; N; D) must flash in the instrument cluster.   
6. Plug in selector lever connector.   
1.6.1. Position display in the instrument cluster changes to P .   
7. Wait 2 seconds.   
8. Press the emergency release button -arrow- five times within 3 seconds.   
1.8.1. The four position displays (P; R; N; D) must now flash again in the instrument cluster.   
2.8.2. If this does not happen, repeat the procedure starting from Step 4.

![](images/760c2fc20493d5665830d770cfb41b688bcec737ac2dbb1faacb7b813ebaf65a.webp)  
Fig 1: Locating Emergency Release Button

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

9. Press the emergency release button once (i.e. 6 times in total),I shift from P to D and wait 1 second .

1.9.1. The emergency release button must be released again immediately after shifting Out of P .

10. Move selector knob to position M .

1. 10.1. Do not shif into position M+ or M- while doing this.

11. Leave the selector knob in position Muntil the position displays stop flashing in the instrument cluster and position D is indicated.

1. 11.1. This can take up to 7 seconds.

12. The calibration process is now complete. If the flashing display stopped even before this, calibration must be repeated.

13. Checking calibration.

1.13.1. Start the engine.

2. 13.2. Shift through all positions using the selector knob - all positions must now be displayed correctly in the position display in the instrument cluster.

3. 13.3. If this is not the case, calibration must be repeated.

14. Delete the fault memory in the transmission and instrument cluster control unit using the PIWIS Tester.

# WM 371315 ADJUSTING LOCKING CABLE (ALL MODELS) > FUNCTION TEST

1. Move selector lever from position "P" to "D" and from position "D" to "M" and back again several times.

.Check that the parking lock is disengaged.

1.2.1. Insert ignition key into the ignition lock.

2. 2.2. Move selector lever to position "P". "P" appears in the instrument cluster.

3.2.3. Actuate the service brake.

4.2.4. Start the engine.

5. 2.5. Move selector lever to position "D". "D" appears in the instrument cluster.

6.2.6. Release the service brake. If the vehicle moves forward, the test is complete. Otherwise, all connecting pieces must be checked again.

3. Check that the parking lock is engaged (engine running).

1.3.1. Insert ignition key into the ignition lock.

2. 3.2. Move selector lever to position "P". "P" appears in the instrument cluster.

3.3.3. Actuate the service brake.

4.3.4. Start the engine.

5. 3.5. Release the service brake. The vehicle must not move. Otherwise, the entire system must be checked.

6.3.6. Switch off engine.

4.Check that the parking lock is engaged (blocking effect).

1.4.1. Insert ignition key into the ignition lock.

2. 4.2. Move selector lever to position "P". "P" appears in the instrument cluster.

3. 4.3. Move selector lever to position "N". "N" appears in the instrument cluster.

4. 4.4. Get another person to help you to push the vehicle for a distance of at least one metre. It must be possible to move the vehicle. Otherwise, the entire system must be checked.

5.4.5. Actuate the service brake.

6. 4.6. Move selector lever to position "P". "P" appears in the instrument cluster.

7. 4.7. Get another person to help you to push the vehicle. The vehicle must not move (a max. movement of 150 mm is acceptable). Otherwise, the entire system must be checked.

# WM 371319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING LOCKING CABLE (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK > FUNCTION TEST

1. Move selector lever from position "P" to "D" and from position "D" to "M" and back again several times.

.Check that the parking lock is disengaged.

1.2.1. Insert ignition key into the ignition lock.

2. 2.2. Move selector lever to position "P". "P" appears in the instrument cluster.

3.2.3. Actuate the operating brake.

4.2.4. Start the engine.

5. 2.5. Move selector lever to position "D". "D" appears in the instrument cluster.

6. 2.6. Release the operating brake. If the vehicle moves forward, the test is complete. Otherwise, all connecting pieces must be checked again.

3. Check that the parking lock is engaged (engine running).

1. 3.1. Insert ignition key into the ignition lock.

2. 3.2. Move selector lever to position "P". "P" appears in the instrument cluster.

3.3.3. Actuate the operating brake.

4.3.4. Start the engine.

5.3.5. Release the operating brake. The vehicle must not move. Otherwise, the entire system must be checked.

6.3.6. Switch off engine.

4. Check that the parking lock is engaged (blocking effect).

1.4.1. Insert ignition key into the ignition lock.

2. 4.2. Move selector lever to position "P". "P" appears in the instrument cluster.

3. 4.3. Move selector lever to position "N". "N" appears in the instrument cluster.

4. 4.4. Get another person to help you to push the vehicle for a distance of at least one metre. It must be possible to move the vehicle. Otherwise, the entire system must be checked.

5.4.5. Actuate the operating brake.

6. 4.6. Move selector lever to position "P". "P" appears in the instrument cluster.

7. 4.7. Get another person to help you to push the vehicle. The vehicle must not move (a max. movement of 150 mm is acceptable). Otherwise, the entire system must be checked.

WM 375519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING ATF PAN (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY

# WORK

1. Move selector lever to position "P" .   
2. Remove cover for center underbody. —Removing cover for center underbody

# WM 375519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING ATF PAN (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING ATF PAN

WARNING: ATF!

Possible danger of injury or damage (swollen hoses, skin irritation, danger of slipping, etc.)

→ Before lines are opened, place a cloth underneath them!   
→ Components that come into contact with ATF must be cleaned IMMEDIATELY with water! → Take appropriate protective measures (e.g. use gloves, safety goggles, oil binding material) → Collect emerging ATF!

WARNING: Danger of objects or loads falling down

Risk of squashing or crushing → Secure components to prevent them from falling down.

WARNING: Hot fluid

Danger of scalding

→ Let the fluid cool down.   
→ Wear personal protective gear.

NOTE: Dirt and contamination

Risk of damage to units or components

→ Protect components from dirt and contamination.   
→ Clean or replace dirty components.

# Information

The engine must not be started if there is no ATF in the transmission.

Risk of damage to the transmission.

1. Remove cross-strut for front-axle carrier.

1.1.1. Unscrew fastening screws -arrows - .

2.1.2. When removing the cross-strut, unclip line -1- .

Fig 1: Locating Cross-Strut Screws

![](images/fb36135a63da2cd37e0a239b951e05e79a5c5d9bdac4ea3bcb9878621e9d23ca.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Place a drip pan underneath.

3. Unscrew ATF oil drain plug -arrow- on the ATF oil pan and drain ATF.

![](images/5a6ae6b3af13dd9ebba18cc45f41bf371d7960168dc30cbbe82428d8b4a2ce53.webp)  
Fig 2: Locating ATF Drain Plug Screw

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Unscrew fastening screws -1.. 15- in diagonally opposite sequence and remove ATF pan.

![](images/489c3b2396da65bb7e12788c3f557de7803de6d7429f44d7731872ef7d96aa66.webp)  
Fig 3: ATF Oil Pan Screws Loosening Sequence

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Remove old seal on the ATF pan.

6. Place ATF pan on a clean surface.

# WM 375519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING ATF PAN (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING ATF PAN

NOTE: Dirt and contamination

Risk of damage to units or components

— Protect components from dirt and contamination.

→ Clean or replace dirty components.

# Information

•The engine must not be started if there is no ATF in the transmission.

Risk of damage to the transmission.

# 1. Fit a new seal.

1.1.1. Clean sealing face on the ATF pan.

2.1.2. Insert nubs -arrow- of the new seal -2- into the ATF pan -1- .

![](images/69f75a24523dc4345d309afa828287ee40647f2cd1672648ba72cc661fba5dfa.webp)  
Fig 1: Locating ATF Pan Seal   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Clean the magnetic strips -arrows- and check that they are fitted over the entire surface in the ATF pan.

![](images/8edf94614f76c4e204037cf4ce2d1a7b330d25220fecd1ac106dfce0785d1e0e.webp)  
Fig 2: Locating ATF Oil Pan Magnetic Strips   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

# 3. Install ATF pan.

1.3.1. Position ATF pan.

2.3.2. Fit fastening screws -1… 15- by hand and screw in as far as they will go.

3. 3.3. Tighten fastening screws. Tightening torque 10 Nm (7.5 ftlb.)

![](images/4898a0b5b59e64a1622ea662baac55607790ba5cadbecba678183621671eb5eb.webp)  
Fig 3: ATF Oil Pan Screws Tightening Sequence

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Fit and tighten ATF drain plug. Tightening torque 45 Nm (33 ftlb.)

![](images/80c324510d1b890f67fc10ed575690ebf9ff93e130d9c68da4188366d0493b69.webp)  
Fig 4: Locating ATF Drain Plug

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Install cross-strut for front-axle carrier.

1.5.1. Clip in line -1- .

2.5.2. Fit new fastening screws -2- and -3- and screw in as far as they will go.

3.5.3. Tighten new fastening screws -2- . Step 1 Initial tightening 90 Nm (67 ftlb.) Step 2 Final tightening +135°

4.5.4. Tighten new fastening screws -3- . Step 1 Initial tightening 90 Nm (67 ftlb.) Step 2 Final tightening +90°

![](images/7046aa6223375bbe6f71befd1c37353380abc78d9dae1b82417bcccaabda65a9.webp)  
Fig 5: Identifying Cross-Strut Screws

# WM 375519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING ATF PAN (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Top up ATF. → 370235 CHECKING AND TOPPING UP ATF   
2. Install cover for center underbody. → Installing cover for center underbody

Risk of burns

→ Wear personal protective gear.

# WM 387719 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CONTROL MECHANISM FOR TRANSMISSION (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING CONTROL MECHANISM FOR TRANSMISSION

WARNING: Hot fluid

•Danger of scalding

→ Let the fluid cool down.   
→ Wear personal protective gear.

CAUTION: Pointed or sharp objects

Risk of cracks, pricks or cuts

→ Wear personal protective gear.

NOTE: Voltage peaks

Risk of damage to loads or to the control unit

→ Disconnect the battery before removing the component or control unit.

# Information

Discharge the transmission electrostatically before removing control mechanism for transmission.   
The sealing face of the control mechanism for transmission must not be damaged.   
•Only loosen the fastening screws with brightly colored screw heads, otherwise damage can occur.   
Control mechanism for transmission is partly secured in the transmission.   
If the control mechanism for transmission has to be pried off get another mechanic to secure the control mechanism for transmission to prevent it from falling out.   
To pry off the control mechanism, two fastening screws can be screwed in slightly to prevent the control unit from falling down.   
Only set the control mechanism for transmission down with the screw head side facing downwards.

# Information

• Do not touch plug contacts in the connector for the transmission with your hands.   
When prying out the tappets, do not use the sensors for support. 1. Carefully pull ATF suction filter to the rear in -direction of arrow- and remove it from the control mechanism for transmission.
