# WM 387719 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CONTROL MECHANISM FOR TRANSMISSION (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING CONTROL MECHANISM FOR TRANSMISSION > ADJUSTING SHIFT FORKS AND GEAR ACTUATORS

Before installing the control mechanism for transmission, move shif forks and gear actuators into center position.

# Information

Do not touch plug contacts in the connector for the transmission with your hands.   
When prying out the tappets, do not use the sensors for support.

# Adjusting shift forks:

Every shift fork has 3 positions:

Gear engaged -G  
Idle speed -N- (center position)   
Gear engaged -G

# Information

Before installing the control mechanism for transmission, move shift forks and gear actuators into center position.

1. Adjust shift forks.

1.1.1. Check shift positions of shift forks -1… 4- manually.

2. 1.2. Shift each of the four shift forks to each position once one after the other. -arrows-.

3. 1.3. Move all shift forks back to center position.

![](images/d86217ae879ecd16cd1f2c3bfac6b5c4d9c3b110716737507c6b862eb0104da9.webp)  
Fig 1: Checking Shift Forks

# Adjusting gear actuators:

1. Dimension -a- = 33.5 mm

# Information

1. Before installing the control mechanism for transmission, move shift forks and gear actuators into center position.

2. Adjust gear actuators.

1. 2.1. Adjust the four gear actuators on the back of the control mechanism for transmission to center position with the dimension -a- .

![](images/34b2ed163740d45d83b1e2279ead30b098ca265b970baa4a28fbf6d337866793.webp)

# WM 387719 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CONTROL MECHANISM FOR TRANSMISSION (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK > REPLACING CONTROL MECHANISM FOR TRANSMISSION

After replacing control mechanism for transmission:

1. Program control mechanism for transmission. Automatic programming.

1. 1.1. Use PIWis Tester Il 9818 to program control mechanism for transmission automatically

2.1.2. Overview - PDK -> Programming - Automatic programming -> [F12].

3.1.3. Perform automatic programming

2. Teach engine immobilizer.

1. 2.1. Overview -> Diagnostics - Online teaching functions > Engine immobilizer -> [F12]

# 3. Calibrate control mechanism for transmission.

Calibrate control mechanism for transmission using PiWis Tester II 9818 .

1. 3.1. Overview -> PDK -> Maintenance/repairs -> Calibration after replacing mechatronics -> [F12]

2.3.2. Follow the instructions on PlWis Tester Il 9818 and press [F12]

3.3.3. Start the calibration process by pressing [F8].

4.3.4. Erase the fault memory.

4. Code control mechanism for transmission. Code control mechanism for transmission using Piwis Tester Il 9818 .

1. 4.1. Overview -> PDK -> Coding/adaptations -> Automatic coding - [F12]

2.4.2. Perform automatic coding.

### WM OXO1IN ALARM SYSTEM: CHECKING OPERATION OF MONITORING DEVICES(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > ALARM SYSTEM: CHECKING OPERATIONOF MONITORING DEVICES

1. Read out the fault memory and activate systems on the unlocked vehicle (see previous point in sales check).

2. Lock the vehicle using the remote control (key fob). A warning tone must not be emitted by the alarm system horn shortly after locking the vehicle (not relevant for USA).

3. If a warning tone is emitted, open and close all doors and outer lids one after the other (not relevant for USA).

4. As soon as the vehicle is locked, the LED in the driver's door panel must flash quickly for 2 seconds and then start to flash slowly.


### Fault indicator:

5. LED flashes quickly for 2 seconds, lights up for 28 seconds and then flashes slowly: Connect the System Tester and read out the fault memory.


### WM OXO1IN CHECKING EXTERIOR EQUIPMENT AND PAINTWORK (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CHECKING EXTERIOR EQUIPMENT AND PAINTWORK > CHECKING EXTERIOR EQUIPMENT

1. Check vehicle for secure fit of accessories such as trim strips, doors mirrors, front and rear spoilers.

2. Check underbody for noticeable areas where undersealing material is missing (e.g. scrapes).

3. Check side member of body flange for deformation of jacking points.

4. Check outer shell of vehicle for noticeable soiling with cavity sealing wax.


### WM OXO1IN CHECKING EXTERIOR EQUIPMENT AND PAINTWORK (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CHECKING EXTERIOR EQUIPMENT AND PAINTWORK > CHECKING PAINTWORK

1. Check outer shellof vehicle for noticeable sheetmetal damage such as dents and bulges. 2. Check painted surfaces of vehicle for noticeable defects such as scores, scratches, notches, scrapes, pores, bubbles or signs that the bodywork is coming through the paint.


### WM OXO1IN CHECKING LIDS AND DOORS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) >CHECKING LIDS AND DOORS > CHECKING LID LOCK AT FRONT AND REAR

Check that the lid locks engage when the lids (front and rear) are closed by engaging the upper parts of the lock and that they disengage again when the lid releases are activated.


### WM OXO1IN CHECKING LIDS AND DOORS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) >CHECKING LIDS AND DOORS > CHECKING SAFETY HOOK ON FRONT LID

Check that the front lid is held down by the safety hook (locking hook) after the lid lock is opened. Check that the return spring on the upper part of the lock pulls the safety hook back as far as the stop.


### WM OXO1IN CHECKING LIDS AND DOORS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) >CHECKING LIDS AND DOORS > FUNCTION TEST ON DOOR LOCKS

oCheck that the door locks engage in two stages when the doors are closed and that they disengage again when the door openers are actuated (inside and outside).


### WM OXO1IN CHECKING LIDS AND DOORS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CHECKING LIDS AND DOORS > FUNCTION TEST ON FUEL TANK CAP LOCK

oLock the vehicle.   
oCheck that the fuel tank cap is locked by the fuel tank cap lock in the closed position.


### WM OXO1IN CHECKING OPERATION OF ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT AS WELL ASWARNING AND INDICATOR LIGHTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) >CHECKING OPERATION OF ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT AS WELL AS WARNING ANDINDICATOR LIGHTS

oTurn ignition key and check function of warning and indicator lights (visual inspection).   
oActuate power windows and check that they are working correctly. Check that rear window heating is working.   
oAdjust heater blower and fans to high and low and check the air vents for air throughput.   
oFront seats and back seats: check function.   
Check audio function.   
oCheck function of exterior mirrors, check adjustment options.   
Check function of orientation lights.   
Check function of luggage compartment lamps.   
Check function of interior lights.   
oActuate central locking and check function.   
Operate cigarette lighter and check that it is working.

### 1.1.1. Switch on ignition.

2. Select the required vehicle.

3. When the overview of control units is displayed, press [F7] to continue.

4. Select Vehicle handover log menu and press [F12].

5. When Remove transport protection is displayed, press [F12] to continue.

6. The control units are activated and the status is displayed. Compare the chassis number displayed on the Tester with the chassis number of the vehicle. Press [F12] to continue.

7. If the vehicle is a new vehicle , press [F8] (Yes) to continue.

8. Select the relevant country and press [F12] to continue.

9. The Tester displays the message Write service interval . Press [F8] to confirm.

10. Service intervals will be written. Press [F12] to continue.

11. Chassis number is correct? . Press [F12] to confirm and then press [F11] to return to the data entry screen.

12. Archive the vehicle handover log file. Press [F12] to continue.

13. Carry out a test drive and read out the fault memory.

1. 13.1. Check faults following diagnosis if necessary and erase the fault memory before delivering the vehicle.


### SOILING (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CHECKING SEAT BELTS > FUNCTION TEST

The following requirements must be met when fitting the seat belt.   
If one of the requirements listed below is not met, the seat belt or seat-belt buckle must be replaced.

It must be possible to unrol he belt strap smoothly from the belt retractor via the deflector fiting by pulling evenly.

The tongue of the seat belt must engage audibly in the buckle.

An abrupt pull on the belt strap must lock the belt retractor.


### WM OXO1IN INTERIOR EQUIPMENT: VISUAL INSPECTION FOR DAMAGE AND SOILING (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CHECKING SEAT BELTS > CONDITION INSPECTION

Visuall inspect the belt strap for damage by unrolling it completely.

If there are signs of damage on the belt strap in the form of cuts, fraying, seam tears, etc., the seat beli must be replaced.


### WM OXO1IN MOBILE ROOFS: CHECKING FUNCTION (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) >CHECKING SLIDING ROOF AND PANORAMA ROOF SYSTEM

1. By operating the control switch, return to original tilting, opening and closing positions. During operation, check for malfunctions and noises.

2. Completely open and close trim panel/sun blinds for roof systems. During operation, check for noise and stiffness.

For vehicles with Tyre Pressure Monitoring (TPM), which can be identified by aluminium valves, the tire pressure must be adjusted according to the > Filing information << on the multi-function display. To do this, select >> Main menu > Tyre pressure > Filing information <<. Adjust the deviation values so thai they range from 0.0 bar to +0.1 bar. Fil the tires according to the display using the tire-inflating device. Example: If the tire pressure display >> Filing information < shows - 0.2 bar, 0.2 bar pressure must be added.

### WM GXOOIN DISPOSAL OF AIRBAG AND SEAT-BELT PRETENSIONER UNITS (ALL MODELS) > DISPOSAL OF AIRBAG AND SEAT-BELT PRETENSIONER UNITS

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag units

Triggering of airbag unit.   
System faults can occur.

→ Switch off ignition and remove ignition key or remote control (hand-held transmitter).

→ A power supply (e.g. battery charger) must not be connected to the external power supply/jump-lead starting terminals.

→ Disconnect the battery and insulate the ground strap so that all contact with a ground carrier is avoided.

→ Wait 1 minute after disconnecting the battery.

→ Only pull off connector on the triggering unit after the waiting time has elapsed.

— Make sure that no foreign objects are located in front of the airbag unit during installation.

→ Replace damaged parts during removal.

→ Always position airbag units so that the blow-out opening is facing upwards, e.g. crest on driver's airbag.

→ Do not position anything on the airbag units.   
→ If removed for an extended period, the airbag units must be stored in a safe place.   
→ Airbag units must not come into contact with grease, oil, detergents, liquids, or similar substances.   
→ Do not expose airbag units to temperatures above 90°.   
→ Do not remove the short-circuit spring on the plug-in contacts.

→ Ignition and preparations may only be carried out by skilled staff, supervised by a second responsible person.

→ Before disposal, the airbag unit must be rendered harmless by electrical ignition performed in accordance with all precautionary measures, thereby preventing it from being used incorrectly.

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag units

Triggering of airbag unit.   
System faults can occur.

→ Switch offignition and remove ignition key or remote control (hand-held transmitter).

→ A power supply (e.g. battery charger) must not be connected to the external power supply/jump-lead starting terminals.

→ Disconnect the battery and insulate the ground strap so that all contact with a ground carrier is avoided.

→ Wait 1 minute after disconnecting the battery.   
→ Only pull off connector on the triggering unit after the waiting time has elapsed.   
→ Make sure that no foreign objects are located in front of the airbag unit during installation.   
→ Replace damaged parts during removal.   
→ Always position airbag units so that the blow-out opening is facing upwards, e.g. crest on driver's airbag.   
→ Do not position anything on the airbag units.   
→ If removed for an extended period, the airbag units must be stored in a safe place.   
→ Airbag units must not come into contact with grease, oil, detergents, liquids, or similar substances. → Do not expose airbag units to temperatures above 90°.   
→ Do not remove the short-circuit spring on the plug-in contacts.   
→ Ignition and preparations may only be carried out by skilled staff, supervised by a second responsible person.   
→ Before disposal, the airbag unit must be rendered harmless by electrical ignition performed in accordance with all precautionary measures, thereby preventing it from being used incorrectly. Information

Only ignite airbag units that are securely installed and in original condition in the vehicle. Alow airbag units to cool down under observation following ignition.

Use only the ignition tool intended for this purpose. First remove all loose objects from the expansion area of the airbag.   
Every ignition circuit for all airbag units and seat-belt pretensioners must be ignited individually.   
Persons who may be affected must be informed of the resulting noise beforehand.   
• Wear ear protectors.   
Keep a safe distance by utilizing the entire cable length of the ignition tool. Do not connect the voltage source until all other preparations are complete.   
If ignition fails, wait for approx. 3 minutes before approaching the vehicle.   
Carry out ignition only in suitable, open areas.   
Do not allow ignited airbag units to come into contact with the skin.

### WM GXOOIN HANDLING AND REPLACING AIRBAG AND SEAT-BELT PRETENSIONER UNITS (ALL MODELS) > TOOLS

### WM GXOOIN HANDLING AND REPLACING AIRBAG AND SEAT-BELT PRETENSIONER UNITS (ALL MODELS) > GENERAL WARNING NOTES > GENERAL WARNINGS FOR HANDLING AIRBAG AND SEAT-BELT PRETENSIONER UNITS

CAUTION: Danger of injury and material damage if the airbag unit is not handled correctly!

Triggering of the airbag unit!

→ The airbag units are pyrotechnical items in hazard class T 1!

→ Handling, transport and storage of these units must conform to hazardous goods regulation and explosives legislation!

→ The listed statutory requirements . The relevant valid regulations must be observed in allother countries. Consult the importer for the country concerned!

→ The commencement of work with pyrotechnical items must be reported to the Trade Supervisory Office (responsible authority) 14 days in advance!

→ The airbag units may only be shipped in transport packaging officially approved for this purpose!

→ Internal and otherwise, they must always be transported in the luggage compartment or loadspace of a vehicle using the above-mentioned transport packaging!

→ They must never be transported in the passenger compartment!

→ Airbag units must be stored in accordance with the explosives legislation SprengLR 240 - Storage of airbag and seat-belt pretensioner units!

→ This ordinance stipulates that small quantities of materials and items may be stored at certain locations without special storage approval!

→ The airbag units must be kept in a locked place!

→ When storing airbag units, ensure that the blow-out opening is facing upwards (risk of injury as a result of inflation of the airbag units in the event of accidental ignition)!

→ The airbag units must be stored in a dry place and must not be stored together with other hazardous goods (lacquers, etc.)!

→ Loose airbag units or airbag units in a removed steering wheel must never become the actual (physical) property of the customer!

→ The possession of loose airbag units not installed in the vehicle is not permitted in the private sector! → Airbag units may become the property of the customer only when installed in the vehicle!


### WM GXOOIN HANDLING AND REPLACING AIRBAG AND SEAT-BELT PRETENSIONER UNITS (ALL MODELS) > GENERAL WARNING NOTES > WARNINGS ABOUT ASSEMBLY AND STRAIGHTENING WORK

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag triggering unit

• Malfunction in airbag system

→ Never drive with an untaught or unlocked airbag triggering unit.

→ Teach and lock the airbag triggering unit using the 2nd generation Plwis Tester 9818 . The warning light willflash continuously until such a time as you teach and lock the airbag triggering unit.

→ Inspection and assembly work may only be carried out by specialist staff.


### Airbag unit on driver's side:

1. Contact unit.   
2. Airbag unit on driver's side.   
3. Triggering unit after the system is triggered for the third time.   
4.Airbag sensors: see below → 1. → 14.


### Airbag unit on passenger's side:

1. Airbag unit on passenger's side.   
2. Triggering unit after the system is triggered for the third time.   
3. Dashboard.   
4. Check dashboard bracket for deformation and replace it if necessary.   
5. Airbag sensors: see below → 1. → 14.


### Side airbag unit, seat:

1. Side airbag unit, seat.   
2. Seat covering, deformed seat components.   
3. Triggering unit after the system is triggered for the third time.   
4. Airbag sensors: see below → 1. → 14.


### Head airbag unit:

1. Replace roof lining.

2. Airbag sensors: see below → 1. → 14.

3. Triggering unit after the system is triggered for the third time.


### Airbag sensor:

1. All irbag sensors in damaged/deformed areas of the vehicle must always be replaced.

2. Otherwise (i.e. even if the vehicle was not crashed), the airbag sensors must be replaced if they show signs of mechanical damage and/or if the airbag control unit detects that the airbag sensor is defective (use PiWis Tester Il 9818 to read out the fault memory).

3. Triggering unit after the system is triggered for the third time.


### Seat-belt pretensioner:

1. All seat-belt pretensioner units.   
2Triggering unit after the system is triggered for the third time.

Because it is difficult to visually determine if one or more seat-belt pretensioners has been


### triggered, check the following points:

Use PIwiS Tester Il 9818 to read out the fault memory.   
Check plug connection on the seat-belt pretensioner for damage.   
Pull out the belt strap as far as possible and check for wear.   
Perform a function test on the automatic belt device.

### WM 926619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING SPRAY NOZZLE FOR WINDSCREEN WASHER SYSTEM (ALL MODELS) > CHECKING AND ADJUSTING SPRAY NOZZLE FOR WINDSCREEN WASHER SYSTEM > CHECKING AND ADJUSTING SPRAY NOZZLES FOR WINDSCREEN WASHER SYSTEM

Information

Only use windscreen cleaning agents and antifreeze approved by Porsche.

Observe the required mixture ratio in accordance with manufacturer's specifications and season.

1. Fil the windscreen-washer reservoir with a mixture of water and window cleaner or antifreeze, depending on the season.

2. Mark the points at which you want the jet sprays to hit the windscreen.

1. 2.1. For the inner spray nozzles: Mark off dimensions -a- Length 200 mm and dimensions -b- Length 535 mm and mark the intersection point on the windscreen using commercially available adhesive tape.

2. 2.2. For the center spray nozzles: Mark off dimensions -c- Length 325 mm and dimensions -d- Length 335 mm and mark the intersection point on the windscreen using commercially available adhesive tape.

3. 2.3. For the outer spray nozzles: Mark off dimensions -e- Length 480 mm and dimensions -f- Length 165 mm and mark the intersection point on the windscreen using commercially available adhesive tape.

Fig 1: Setting Spray Nozzles

![](images/8a2ccd09f07b95f5079613ede52aa5cb849a2a2d7209d45bf8933e019160d45b.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Actuate the windscreen washer system and align the spray nozzles for the windscreen washer system to the marked spray points as required using adjusting tool T40187

4. Remove adhesive tape and any adhesive residues from the windscreen.

### WM 941415 ADJUSTING HEADLIGHT MOUNTING (ALL MODELS) > ADJUSTINGHEADLIGHT MOUNTING > CHECKING ADJUSTING ELEMENTS

Information

To restore the original installation position, thereby minimizing the amount of adjustment work required, the following steps must be carried out prior to removal:

Mark the position of the headlight mounting with respect to fastening screws.

Measure and take note of the height of the headlight mounting with respect to the body.

1. Check adjusting elements.

1. 1.1. Check adjusting elements -1- for damage and make sure they are seated securely. If an adjusting element -1- is damaged, it must be replaced. Check that the adjusting elements -1- are fitted correctly in the body.

2. 1.2. Measure the height -A- of the adjusting elements -1- using a calliper gauge and write it down so that you can set the original adjustment height again after the next test step.

3.1.3. Check that the adjusting rings -2-  are not stiff. Important: Left thread! It must be possible to turn adjusting ring -2- without resistance over the entire thread length, otherwise replace adjusting element -1- .

4.1.4. Set original height -A- of the adjusting elements -1- again.

![](images/9aa82f8ef2bff59a36166c181322534b142191ac404fe7a857105a550633a272.webp)  
Fig 1: Checking Adjusting Elements


### Left headlight mounting:

1. Clip antenna line holder -1- into the headlight mounting -2- .

2. Clip holders for electric plug connections -3- and headlight cleaning system hose -4- into the headlight mounting -2- .


### Headlight mounting at the left and right:

3. Position headlight mounting -2- on the adjusting elements.

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Fit fastening screws -1-

1.4.1. Press fastening screw -1- into adjusting element.   
2.4.2. Press headlight mounting -2- in the adjusting element area down -arrow F- and screw fastening screw -1- into adjusting element.   
3. 4.3. Align markings on the headlight mounting -2- - if markings were made - with the washers, press headlight mounting -2- down in the adjusting element area -arrow Fand tighten fastening screws -1- .

![](images/ed4e608d152c0064711422bd404987423450d3322ec0da811042672073f902b5.webp)  
Fig 2: Screwing Fastening Screws


### Procedure for lowering the headlight:

4. Loosen fastening screws -1- .

1.4.1. Press headlight mounting -2- in the adjusting element area down -arrow F- to ensure that the position of the adjusting element cannot be changed.

![](images/49dd27f97e306b2a1652c8b1b14a9e7af52bbc9e66a603cd92f6d310d6a04de4.webp)  
Fig 2: Loosening Fastening Screws   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Screw in the adjusting ring -3- on the adjusting element to lower the headlight mounting -2- .

1.5.1. Screw fastening screw -1- anti-clockwise.

2.5.2. Do not exert pressure on the headlight mounting -2- during the adjustment process.

![](images/ce4ffa8795b772ed936ca2e924ba30535d62df3e880bdebd559edcb850e5a322.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Lower Headlight Mounting

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.


### Once the required adjustment height is reached:

. Tighten fastening screws.

1.6.1. Press headlight mounting in the adjusting element area down to ensure that the position of the adjusting element cannot be changed.


### Procedure for raising the headlight:

7. Loosen fastening screws -1- .

1.7.1. Press headlight mounting -2- in the adjusting element area down to ensure that the position of the adjusting element cannot be changed.

8.Screw out the adjusting ring -3- on the adjusting element to raise the headlight mounting -2-

1.8.1. Screw fastening screw -1- clockwise.

### WM 944955 REPLACING CONTROL UNIT FOR FRONT-END ELECTRONICS (ALL MODELS) > REPLACING CONTROL UNIT FOR FRONT-END ELECTRONICS

Information

All remote controls (keys) are required for teaching a DME, front-end electronics (front BCM), rear-end electronics (rear BCM), electronic steering lock (ELV) control unit or remote controls (keys) for example.

Remote controls (keys) that are not taught during this teaching procedure wil no longer be recognized by the vehicle.

NOTE: Voltage drop

Risk of irreparable damage to control unit   
Risk of damage to control unit   
Fault entries in the control unit   
•Coding in the control unit is aborted   
•Malfunctions in control unit, even during programming

→ Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch offignition and remove ignition key.

→ Ensure that the power supply is not interrupted during programming.

→ Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least — Nominal value: 40 A to the vehicle battery.

Always comply with the regulations for handling ESD-sensitive components!

Assembly work may only be carried out if the mechanic is wearing the working clothes and shoes approved by Porsche. The new part must only be removed from the ESD (electrostatic discharge) protective packaging just before installation and at the position at which the part is to be installed.

•Never touch the electric pins and plug contacts.

### WM 945955 REPLACING GAS-DISCHARGE HEADLIGHT (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING GAS-DISCHARGE HEADLIGHT

NOTE: Incorrect handling of bulbs

Risk of damage to bulbs and the bulb housing

→ Switch off ignition and remove ignition key.   
→ Switch offthe relevant loads when changing bulbs.   
→ Only use bulbs listed in the bulb table.   
→ Only installclean bulbs that are free of grease.   
→ Always use a cloth or soft paper when working with bulbs.   
→ Observe the safety instructions when changing a bulb in a Bi-Xenon headlight.   
→ In certain states, it is compulsory to carry spare light bulbs.

1. Switch off position lights.   
2. Switch off ignition and pull remote control out of ignition lock.   
3. Release hose connection for the breather hose -1- (-a- ) and pull it off the headlight.   
4. Turn the rear cover -2- in direction of arrow and remove it.

![](images/50c15915fc127d33e8340e3c548f7edbfba1f26b804a994d79a4a5d7d277e60a.webp)  
Fig 1: Removing Rear Cover

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Turn gas-discharge headlight -1- in direction of arrow and carefully remove it from the headlight. 6. Disconnect electric plug connection -2- from the gas-discharge headlight.

![](images/91222ce05b5db0047c7cdfd1f3e7fd59711aaa9283bab0ffd4b5565b1fcb4855.webp)  
Fig 2: Removing Gas-Discharge Headlight


### WM 945955 REPLACING GAS-DISCHARGE HEADLIGHT (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING GAS-DISCHARGE HEADLIGHT

NOTE: Incorrect handling of bulbs

•Risk of damage to bulbs and the bulb housing

—→ Switch offignition and remove ignition key.

→ Switch offthe relevant loads when changing bulbs.

→ Only use bulbs listed in the bulb table.

→ Only install clean bulbs that are free of grease.

→ Always use a cloth or soft paper when working with bulbs.

→ Observe the safety instructions when changing a bulb in a Bi-Xenon headlight.

— In certain states, it is compulsory to carry spare light bulbs.

1.Connect electric plug connection -1- on the gas-discharge headlight -2- until it engages securely.

2. Position gas-discharge headlight in the headlight and lock it by turning it in direction of arrow.

![](images/09074751a622945bc8f4167130cacf4ee03376761a63d74153a1ee0e002dab78.webp)  
Fig 1: Installing Gas-Discharge Headlight

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Check condition of the seal -1- and check that it is fitted correctly on the rear cover -2- .

4. Position rear cover on the headlight and lock it by turning it in direction of arrow.

5 Check condition of O-ring -3- and check that it is seated correctly.

6.Connect hose connection -4- for the breather hose at the headlight until it engages securely.

![](images/4b2f0c0e1e930b86e943b0d176571dcff5443c0ec41f7d08f82a528924fa750d.webp)  
Fig 2: Installing Rear Cover

### Toolbox: Glass Repair System D Pro WE 1354

1. Clean the damaged area.

1. 1.1. Use a dry cloth (without any window cleaner) to clean the windscreen around the area of damage, but do not wipe across the area of impact itself.

2. 1.2. Remove loose splinters of glass from the chipped area using the hard metal stylus, but do not enlarge the impact crater unnecessarily. → Exposing stone chip i IMPORTANT: The more glass missing from the chipped surface, the more obvious the blemish following repairs.

![](images/abbbb2f950f90f3b8d44c7e3febd2048f107c9a89ce717f9dc756c0530a7c633.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Stone Chip   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Secure the mirror.

Apply gel to the suction areas of the inspection mirror and attach the mirror to the inside of the windscreen so that the procedure can be monitored from outside. → Securing mirror

![](images/f770f294015d23fb135d8dda19096559ab854dcb34080da4c224a8f7eff29577.webp)  
Fig 2: Securing Mirror

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Drill out

If necessary, use a drillto mill glass splinters and dirt out of the impact hole to a depth of approx. 1 mm.

0 IMPORTANT: Always hold the dril firmly with both hands! This is the only way to ensure that the drill is positioned securely.

![](images/35d03649509366fe23a6e59a1beea7d61dd2874a2772a0e7e4c09fe4ff289d05.webp)  
Fig 3: Drilling Stone Chip   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Secure the bridge.

1.4.1. Rub gel into the suction area on the bridge. This allows the tool to be repositioned after it has been secured in place.   
2.4.2. Press the bridge -1- firmly onto the windscreen so that the threaded hole is directly above the point of impact.   
3.4.3. Stick the bridge firmly onto windscreen by operating the vacuum pump until the red marking -2- is no longer visible.

i IMPORTANT: The bridge must remain firmly seated on the windscreen for the duration of the repair work. Operate the pump again if the red mark becomes visible.

4.4.4. Align the bridge directly over the point of impact with respect to the windscreen and secure it in place using the central screw -3- .

5.4.5. Adjust the bridge so that it is parallel to the windscreen using the screws at the rear -4-.

![](images/2861f6f87a07d297a7bc15ca0b47cb3e7914fa20b53eaeec8c2262f3240e03ef.webp)  
Fig 4: Securing Bridge


### WM 0720IN GLASS REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > REPAIR PROCEDURE

1. Fit the bridge.

1.1.1. Screw injector with seal -5- into the bridge until the seal is touching the glass. Then press the injector against the window by completing one more turn.

![](images/3faead4463d1eee4417bdb13c0438b12d3578c8312110a7ce230ebd917e22839.webp)  
Fig 1: Turning Injector Seal   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2.1.2. Attach needle to the syringe and fil with approx. 0.15 ml of resin. → Filling syringe

![](images/11b44d6004cb767502774ea46dfc47780344293e1ecbb04433dc78ab531ad736.webp)  
Fig 2: Filling Syringe   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3.1.3. Inject resin into the injector. → Filing injector

![](images/9ffb0dbcc03017fb94981b622d3a5e7edeac41ab259df4368af26f6e0e050115.webp)  
Fig 3: Filling Injector

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.


### 2. Pressurizing phase

1.2.1. Slowly screw the plunger -6- into the injector -5- until resistance is felt and the shape of the seal changes → Seal under pressure . Keep a firm hold on the injector barrel while doing this.   
2. 2.2. Leave the plunger pressed down at this position for around 5 min., in which time the plunger will automatically build up pressure.

![](images/d942f10a449e3056b45fa1ed7d6e36e2bd52edf4411561c34fc45297ab0cf7ec.webp)  
Fig 4: Installing Plunger Into Injector

![](images/2dc0f394a94035a955e67d710115901d8576f8cff3518eaec29c2c55f8454f15.webp)  
Fig 5: Identifying Pressure Seal   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.


### 3. Vacuum phase

1. 3.1. Pull up the plunger -6- with one hand -A- and secure it in position by turning it 90° clockwise -B- . This allows any air to escape out of the damaged area.

2.3.2. Release the plunger so that pressure can build up again.

3. 3.3. Repeat steps → 3.1. and → 3.2. about 5-10 times until there is no more air in the damaged area.

![](images/f2df52ea8f3a169e173b28e78418928eb124b31223a1d238964515bfa5900712.webp)  
Fig 6: Pulling Plunger

![](images/b119080b45bbddf3165b20907f42b1de6472e459ec47f01db22ccc0c27dd8988.webp)  
Fig 7: Identifying Vacuum Seal   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Heating

If the damage is more severe, the removal of trapped air can be speeded up by heating the area gently. To do this, use a lighter to heat the area of damage from the inside for 3-5 seconds.

0 IMPORTANT: Heat during the vacuum phase only, otherwise the expanding air would cause excessive pressure in the damaged area.

5. Remove the bridge.

1.5.1. Release the plunger a litte (do not create a vacuum) and unscrew the injector.

2. 5.2. Remove the bridge from the windscreen. 6. Apply finishing resin.

1.6.1. Add a drop of finishing resin directly onto the impact point.

2.6.2. Slide film across the windscreen.

![](images/ca7f241fd3298fc6de8af69c55d48b1a465bbe4b69e64fa9035bbee092a90971.webp)  
Fig 8: Applying Resin   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Curing under a UV lamp

1.7.1. Place a UV lamp over the damaged area from the outside and switch it on. → Curing under a UV lamp

2.7.2. Curing takes around 10 minutes, depending on the size of the stone chip.

![](images/5194570b075d5f379a2d319b72809a2e0c4d56df2b08a995aa38bcee29852781.webp)  
Fig 9: Identifying UV Lamp

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

Scrape off repair resin.

1.8.1. Remove film and scrape of excess resin using a razor blade held at a 90 degree angle to the windscreen. → Scraping off resin

0 IMPORTANT: Risk of damage to the windscreen. Use only blades that are in perfect condition, otherwise they could damage the windscreen.

2.8.2. If there is an indentation at the point of repair, steps → 6. → 7. and → 8.1. will need to be repeated to obtain a perfect finish.

![](images/5021e5899cae4ce30f7429aba7778f0472251e35486ce6338c93b0638473a6b7.webp)  
Fig 10: Removing Resin

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.


### . Polishing

Polish the repair area with polish and a soft cloth.

i IMPORTANT: Do not polish for too long as this can wear down the repair resin and the surface will no longer be flat.

![](images/57897ab8747fd267f68d4b05c352ec74a79498638cfa7a950d35a19870e5f2cb.webp)  
Fig 11: Applying Polish On Glass   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.


### 10. Cleaning tools

After completing repairs, clean the tools using a dry, lint-free cloth. Otherwise, the resin will damage the seals.


### WM 0730IN DENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > TOOLS

![](images/2861cd46e23becff5c6825eb219c183831f51568472e4d893d50194857245aa4.webp)

![](images/ddaba6df95342d3cc4c77302a8a8f130a50f94950a25dd35f84b64920c912224.webp)


### NM 0730IN DENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > DENT REPAIRS > PREREQUISITES

The dent must not have any cracks in the paintwork. Examine the damaged area using an illuminated magnifier or reflected-light microscope.   
Measure thickness of paint layer around the damaged area. Paint layers up to approx. 450 μm thick are straightforward. With thicker layers of paint there is a danger that the paint will crack.   
High level of workmanship and skill   
Intensive training   
Continuous practice   
Use of recommended tools


### WM 0730IN DENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > DENT REPAIRS > SUCCESS FACTORS

The factors below affect the outcome of the repair work considerably:

The location of the damage   
The extent of the damage   
The shape of the damage   
The condition of the paintwork   
Skills and experience of the technician   
Color (dark colors are trickier than light colors)   
With silver colors, sharp-edged and pointed dents may cause slight changes to the color pigments (dark sports).   
Condition of tools


### WM 0730IN DENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > DENT REPAIRS > TECHNICAL RESTRICTIONS FOR CARRYING OUT REPAIRS

No/poor accessibility (for safety reasons, holes must never be drilled in order to make an area more accessible.)   
Workmanship skills, lack of practice.   
• Dents with paint defects/cracks cannot be repaired.   
Damage to folded edges or reinforcements usually cannot be repaired.   
Dents with crumpled edges usually cannot be corrected.   
It may not be possible to correct creased or pointed dents. With the bonding technique it is usually only possible to repair flat or minor dents.   
The maximum size of the dent should not exceed a diameter of 50 mm.


### WM 0730IN DENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > PROCEDURE > GENERAL PROCEDURE

1. Clean the surface to be treated to obtain good light reflection.

2. Mark the dent using the wax chalk.

3. Assess accessibility of the dent.

4. Try to find the best access, even if this is difficult for some areas.

5. Remove body parts in accordance with the Service information. When doing so, always be careful with safety-critical components, such as airbags, seat-belt pretensioners, electronic components, cables, etc.

6. Locate the dent using a locating lamp and find the tool tip on the metal panel.

7. Work according to the clock method described below.

8. Work calmly and patiently.

9. When working on bumps or bulges, it is much better to tap the metal gently and repeatedly rather than using one heavy strike.

10. Be very careful when using knife tools and cutter tools as these tools can easily cause the panel to buckle.

11. Sand down rough areas and high points with a sanding block (P2000 - 4000) and then polish them.

12. After removing the dent, seal the repair area with wax or cavity protection.


### NM 0730IN DENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > PROCEDURE > CLOCK METHOD

With the clock method, the lines of force running through the center of the dent are removed, with the result that the material stress is reduced and the panel is flat again.

The dent should be envisaged as a dial with "12" being the furthest away. In other words, the person performing the work is standing at 6 o'clock.

Start at the edge of the dent -A- at 9 o'clock and work clockwise through 12 o'clock to 3 o'clock. When doing this, always remember to press the panel at as many points as possible and as close together as possible. From 3 o'clock, move further inwards and carry on through 12 o'clock to 9 o'clock. Carry out the remaining steps in this same way.

![](images/d5c109cf319af5fc9807ff03340d09291f80b0721dec906535b7478e9f836377.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Dent Repair Clock Method   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

With a dent of approx. 2 cm in diameter, it will be necessary to press the panel at around 100 - 150 points. Any point that is pressed too hard must be pushed back again before continuing. Strain can be created in the panel as a result of too many high points, with the result that the metal sheet can no longer spread out evenly.


### WM 0730IN DENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > PROCEDURE > DENT MASSAGE (FOR LARGER DENTS)

With this method, the lines of force are removed not by pressing at numerous points but instead by short movements.

For this process, first draw a boundary circle -B- at the center of the dent using wax chalk. This circle is to prevent the tool from being pulled too far into the center. This could cause the dent to break up into numerous tiny dents and make any further work more difficult.

Use the large ball tool with the large round plastic attachment. Place the tool at the edge of the dent -Afirst at 12 o'clock and using gentle pressure approach the boundary circle with gradually increasing

pressure. Continue working from 11 o'clock to 1 o'clock, from 10 o'clock to 2 o'clock, etc. from the outer edge of the dent right up to the boundary circle. The pressure must not be too great as this could cause ridges. Once the dent has been shrunk back to the boundary circle, continue using the point-by-point clock method -c- .

![](images/ed25b89d3457fb4beee9f03c10a0e1521f4a5ef1d9dfb0df9ae9cc5c45493a94.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Dent Massage Method For Larger Dents   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

The various dent repair methods can only be learned through intensive training and continuous practice.

### WM 0740IN INTERIOR COSMETIC REPAIRS (EXCEPT MACAN) > PAINTING AND DYEING

WARNING: Toxic substances Danger of poisoning or suffocation • Danger of burns to the eyes and skin

→ Ventilate the work area well.   
→ Never ingest or inhale.   
→ Read specific information on the Hazard Sheet.   
→ Do not smoke, eat or drink in the work area.   
1. From the color samples choose the color that most closely matches the original.   
. Shake paint container thoroughly before mixing.   
3. Mix paint on the paint scales interior repair scales, small(0.01g scale) WE 1357 in accordance with the formulary.   
4. Mix paints thoroughly and compare the color obtained with the original. To do this, dab or spray some of the paint onto the original part. Critically examine the color match of the paint when dry. It is often necessary to adapt the color mixture and sometimes this may take several attempts.   
5. If necessary, match the sheen and color intensity using the additive "Opacante A". The amount of this additive that can be added to the paint must not exceed 25%.   
6.Check adhesion of paint by gently scratching the dry paint.   
7. If the color is correct, apply paint to the damaged area using paint-spraying gun - Sata-Minijet WE 1146 or an airbrush gun.

For small areas of damage, the paint can also be applied using a clean, lint-free cloth. In this case, apply the paint in several layers using a circular motion.

![](images/4c81ab7a87481d697d951402f9485d698838fbcf2e8b3c240101e5f18b4f3827.webp)  
Fig 1: Applying Paint In Repaired Area

8. Leave paint to dry at a temperature of no less than 16 C for approx. 90 min. It may take less time to dry at warmer temperatures.

The drying time should be increased if the paint was applied in several layers.

. Match the lustre, if necessary:

1. "Matt fix scan" provides a matt finish.

2. "Gloss fix scan" provides a gloss finish.

3. A satin finish is achieved by mixing the two gloss regulators.

1.9.1. Shake gloss regulators thoroughly and filter through a paper filter.

2. 9.2. Mix "Mat fix scan" and "Gloss fix scan" thoroughly in the desired ratio.

3. 9.3. Test gloss regulator in a concealed area.

4.9.4. Check the lustre when dry and adapt if necessary.

5.9.5. Apply the gloss regulator using paint-spraying gun - Sata-Minijet WE 1146 or an airbrush gun.

For small areas of damage, the gloss regulator can also be applied using a clean, lint-free cloth. Apply it using a circular motion.

10. Leave the paint to dry overnight before applying any load.

Observe the information and instructions provided by the tool manufacturer as well.

### Areas of application:

•Paint repairs are possible on plastic and sheet metal.

Single-layer, double-layer and metallic paint finishes can be painted in this way.

This painting method can be used to its full extent in areas with low light reflection (e.g. bumpers, door sills, edges of parts). -green area

Paint repairs to components with larger surfaces are only possible to a limited extent -yellow area- . In these areas, only small areas of damage with a diameter of up to 35 mm or a length of up to 100 mm should be repaired.

•Damage to large surface areas cannot be corrected using paint repair methods. -red area

### RESTRICTIONS AND CONDITIONS

NOTE: Thermal stripping of alloy wheels

•Reduced rigidity of aluminum alloy Risk of breaks and irreparable damage to the rim

→ Do not use thermal stripping procedures or heat treatment on alloy wheels

NOTE: Incorrect repair of alloy wheels

Reduced endurance strength • Alloy wheel breaks

→ Only repairs to the surface paint finish on alloy wheel are permitted

The alloy wheel is a highly stressed vehicle component which may be subjected to extreme loads during operation. The repair restrictions must be strictly observed in order to ensure safe operation and prevent any potential hazards.


### WM 0760IN ALLOY WHEEL RECONDITIONING (ALL MODELS) > REPAIR RESTRICTIONS AND CONDITIONS > REPAIR RESTRICTIONS

The base material of the alloy wheel must not be damaged. For example: → NON-permissible damage , → NON-permissible damage

Repairs that affect the base material of the wheel (deposit-welding, filing and metal-cutting machining) → Prohibited machining operations are not permitted.

There must be no signs of corrosion on the alloy wheel.

• It is imperative to avoid sanding down areas through to the base material.

### WM 503955 REPLACING SPRING STRUT MOUNT (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK > PRELIMINARY WORK FOR BODY REPAIRS (WITH STRAIGHTENING SYSTEM)

1. Remove accessories in the repair area.

1. 1.1. Remove accessories in the repair area according to the extent of damage on the vehicle.

2. Set up straightening bench with straightening system.

3. Set vehicle on straightening bench.

4. Cover accessories adjacent to the repair area on the vehicle.

1. 4.1. Cover all accessories remaining on the vehicle and adjacent areas with fire-proof protective covers.

5. Expose joint areas.

1.6.1. Remove underbody protection, paint, etc. from the joint areas of the body using a hot-air gun or rotary brush.


### WM 503955 REPLACING SPRING STRUT MOUNT (ALL MODELS) > PREPARING SPRING STRUT MOUNT FOR INSTALLATION

1. Align the sealing surface and connections of the body.

2. De-bur connection points and prepare them for welding.


### WM 503955 REPLACING SPRING STRUT MOUNT (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK > SUBSEQUENT WORK FOR BODY REPAIRS

1. Release and remove vehicle from the straightening system.

2. Clean joint areas and sheetmetal flanges with a wire brush.

3. Prime joint areas and sheetmetal flanges with 2K primer.

4. Restore standard seal with body sealant → 5X00IN42 SEAM SEALING .

Also seal the repair area carefully.

5. Paint repair area and adjacent surfaces, if necessary.   
6. Restore standard underbody protection with underbody sealant → 5X00IN43 UNDERBODY PROTECTION .   
7. Apply standard cavity preservation → 5X00IN44 CAVITY PRESERVATION . Also carefully apply cavity preservation to the repair area.   
8. Install removed accessories in the repair area.

### WM 505519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WING (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Remove front wheel housing liner. → 505619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT WHEEL HOUSING LINER   
2. Remove windscreen-washer reservoir on the left wing. → 926019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WINDSCREEN-WASHER RESERVOIR   
3. Partly remove heater on the right wing. → 822019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COMPLETE HEATER


### WM 505519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WING (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING WING

1. Installation is performed in reverse order to removal.   
. Tighten fastening screws on outer wing to the specified tightening torque Tightening torque 10 Nm (7.5 ftlb.) until secure.   
3. Tighten fastening screws on inner wing to the specified tightening torque Tightening torque 10 Nm (7.5 ftlb.)  until secure.


### WM 505519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WING (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Install heater on right wing → INSTALLING HEATER .   
2. Install windscreen-washer reservoir on the left wing → INSTALLING WINDSCREEN-WASHER

RESERVOIR .

3. Install front wheel housing liner → INSTALLING FRONT WHEEL HOUSING LINER .

### WM 505619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT WHEEL HOUSING LINER (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING FRONT WHEEL HOUSING LINER

Installation is performed in reverse order. Pay particular attention to the following:

1. Screw in and tighten fastening screws to Tightening torque 2 Nm (1.5 ftlb.) .   
. Tighten fastening nuts to Tightening torque 2.5 Nm (2 ftlb.)until secure.


### WM 505619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT WHEEL HOUSING LINER (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Lower the vehicle. → 4XOOIN LIFTING THE VEHICLE

### The help of another person is required for steps 15 to 18.

15. Press air conditioner -1- in direction of arrow -arrow- using a suitable tool and guide retaining lug -2- out of the bracket -3- .

16. Carefully pull support -4- forward until the support -4- is removed fully at the studs -5- .

17. Pad the strut -6- with foam to prevent damage to the windscreen.

18. Carefully lift up the support -4- and remove it.

CAUTION: Incorrect handling of gas-filled shock absorbers

Gas-filled shock absorbers can burst   
Risk of eye injuries   
Risk of bruising

→ Gas-filled shock absorbers must be in idle state before removal.

→ Open the lid.

→ Secure the lid to prevent it from closing accidentally following removal of the gas-filled shock absorbers.

→ Do not use force to open the gas-filled shock absorbers because of their high internal pressure.

### WM 559015 ADJUSTING REAR LID (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CHECKING REAR LID LOCK > FUNCTION TEST ON REAR LID LOCK

1. Check the function of the rear lid lock.

1. 1.1. Lock the lid lock using a screwdriver and then unlock it again using the lid release. The lock must swivel out freely.

2.1.2. Check that the rear lid stays open automatically in the upper positions.

3. 1.3. From the middle position, the rear lid must fall nto the lock automatically and lock fully. (with gas-filled shock absorbers)

4.1.4. Perform a visual inspection to check that the lock releases again correctly.

2. Check electric operation of rear lid lock.

1. 2.1. Open the lock using the electric release or remote control.

3. Check electric tailgate drive mechanism.

1. 3.1. Check opening and closing function using the outer handle on the rear lid, the remote control and the switch in the driver's door.

2. 3.2. It must be possible to stop rear lid operation at any time using all actuators.

3. 3.3. Check the obstacle detection function.

Simulate an obstacle while opening and closing by holding the rear lid firmly.

### WM 559019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR LID (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING REAR LID

CAUTION: Incorrect handling of gas-filled shock absorbers

Gas-filled shock absorbers can burst   
Risk of eye injuries   
Risk of bruising

→ Gas-filled shock absorbers must be in idle state before removal.

→ Open the lid.

→ Secure the lid to prevent it from closing accidentally following removal of the gas-filled shock absorbers.

→ Do not use force to open the gas-filled shock absorbers because of their high internal pressure.

### WM 575115 ADJUSTING FRONT DOOR (ALL MODELS) > ADJUSTING FRONT DOOR

WARNING: Incorrect handling of safety bolts

Danger of injury

Loss of torque

### WM 575115 ADJUSTING FRONT DOOR (ALL MODELS) > CHECKING FRONT DOOR LOCK

1. Check the function of the front door lock.

2. Check closing and opening forces and compare with the other doors. If these forces differ, re-adjust the door.

### WM 575119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT DOOR (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING FRONT DOOR

1. Slide the locking mechanism -1- up using a suitable tool and disconnect plug connection -2- .

![](images/caeec5f2df5ffff2fd663c3c2c9ae3e09f7655fcadf7004227838178ad1dad5c.webp)  
Fig 1: Disconnecting Electric Plug Connection

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Unscrew and remove fastening screw on the door arrester -4- at the vehicle door.

![](images/e60e42b5bd52387307323fc9f25d1ffeb7cf82d4c0d60daa2d06d06030e2ef20.webp)  
Fig 2: Removing Screw On Door Arrester

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Pull plastic caps -3- off the hinge screws at the top and bottom hinge joints -6- .

![](images/04143088161693a52dc5aeff2b4577e3e98c566fab3ce67c9edaf4b99ce8d4e4.webp)  
Fig 3: Pulling Off Caps On Hinge Screws

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Loosen fastening screws -5- on the top and bottom hinge joint -6- .

![](images/c3315453abfa80f039d4e0a19569d6a04ccf569ffa9d84d96aad1249ff5ef458.webp)  
Fig 4: Loosening Hinge Joint

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Get another person to hold the vehicle door.

6. Lift the vehicle door up slightly until the hinge bolts come out of the hinge halves on the door side.

![](images/ef541d428e9291179724871b262ea1a8f15b505096106813dfcc9e2127ce6b3d.webp)  
Fig 5: Lifting Vehicle Door   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Remove vehicle door.


### WM 575119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT DOOR (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING FRONT DOOR

1. Installation is performed in reverse order to removal.   
2. Tighten fastening screw on door hinge to Tightening torque 27 Nm (20 ftlb.) +/-3.5 Nm (+/-2.5 ftib.) .   
3. Tighten fastening screw for door arrester to Tightening torque 33 Nm (24 ftlb.) .

### Service Manual: 5X - BODY - GENERAL - (95B) - MACAN WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS) > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR RAISING VEHICLES > DANGER OF INJURY WHEN RAISING VEHICLES

WARNING: Vehicle can fall down

Risk of squashing or crushing Risk of damage to the vehicle

→ Do not place any solid objects under the raised vehicle.   
→ Ensure that the lifting platform is prevented from lowering.   
→ Remove solid objects before lowering the vehicle.   
→ Raise the vehicle only at the jacking points provided.   
→ The outer jacking points should be used primarily.


### WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS) > GENERAL WARNING NOTES > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR GRINDING WORK

WARNiNG: Excessively high dust concentration during grinding work

Risk of explosion

→ Remove any grinding dust using the relevant vacuum cleaner approved for use on the material.

→ Remove dust in the work area regularly.

→ Do not use compressed air to blow away dust deposits.

→ Always separate the dust from different materials (separate aluminum, steel and carbon fibrereinforced plastic).

→ Clean the extraction system at regular intervals.   
→ Never weld and grind in the same room at the same time.   
→ Only use pneumatic grinders if possible.


### WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS)  GENERAL WARNING NOTES > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR FUEL TANK

WARNING: Grinding and welding work

Danger of fire or explosion

→ Avoid working in an area with highly inflammable or explosive materials.

→ Cover highly inflammable or explosive areas.

→ Remove highly inflammable or explosive parts.


### WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS) > GENERAL WARNING NOTES > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR AIR CONDITIONING

CAUTION: Danger of injury! Bursting of the filled air-conditioning system during welding and brazing work!

Danger of injury due to the filled air-conditioning system bursting during welding and brazing work.

→ No welding, brazing or hot-air heating may be performed on parts of the filled air-conditioning system!

→ While drying after painting work, the temperature burden on the vehicle must not exceed two hours at a maximum temperature of 80 °C!

→ Make sure that parts of the air-conditioning system do not heat up during welding or brazing work on the vehicle!

→ In the case of extreme heating of filled air-conditioning systems, a very strong overpressure may be caused in the system which may lead to an explosion.


### WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS) > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR ADHESIVE BONDING > DANGER OF POISONING AND INJURY WHEN USING ADHESIVE

• Danger of poisoning or suffocation Danger of burns to the eyes and skin

→ Ventilate the work area well.

→ Never ingest or inhale.

### WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS) > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR ADHESIVE BONDING > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR TEROMIX-6700 TWO-COMPONENT ADHESIVE

Risk of damage to side panel

### WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS) > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR INSTALLATION WORK > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR AIRBAG SYSTEM

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag units

Triggering of airbag unit.   
System faults can occur.

→ Switch off ignition and remove ignition key or remote control (hand-held transmitter).

→ A power supply (e.g. battery charger) must not be connected to the external power supply/jump-lead starting terminals.

→ Disconnect the battery and insulate the ground strap so that all contact with a ground carrier is avoided.

→ Wait 1 minute after disconnecting the battery.

→ Only pull off connector on the triggering unit after the waiting time has elapsed.

→ Make sure that no foreign objects are located in front of the airbag unit during installation.

→ Replace damaged parts during removal.

→ Always position airbag units so that the blow-out opening is facing upwards, e.g. crest on driver's airbag.

→ Do not position anything on the airbag units.

→ If removed for an extended period, the airbag units must be stored in a safe place.

— Airbag units must not come into contact with grease, oil, detergents, liquids, or similar substances.

→ Do not expose airbag units to temperatures above 90°.

→ Do not remove the short-circuit spring on the plug-in contacts.

→ Ignition and preparations may only be carried out by skilled staff, supervised by a second responsible person.

→ Before disposal, the airbag unit must be rendered harmless by electrical ignition performed in accordance with all precautionary measures, thereby preventing it from being used incorrectly.

WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS) > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR CORROSION PROTECTION > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR STOPPER LOCATION PLAN (BODY)

NOTE: Removing stoppers

Risk of corrosion •Uncontrolled water leakage

→ Body apertures that are sealed with stoppers at the factory must be re-sealed with the stoppers


### WM 5XOOIN SAFETY NOTES (ALL MODELS) > SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR CORROSION PROTECTION SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS FOR WATER DRAINS (BODY)

NOTE: Water drain hoses not cleaned correctly

Water drain hoses are pushed out or pressed into the body.

→ When cleaning water drain hoses, only blow the hoses out with light compressed-air pressure.   
→ The water hoses should only be blown out when the slide/tit roof is closed.


### Porsche long-life guarantee conditions

All body repairs must be carried out correctly and according to the specific Porsche instructions for sheetmetal, paint and corrosion protection/preservation work.   
To avoid jeopardising the long-life guarantee, a paint condition report wil be drawn up two years after delivery of the vehicle. This condition report must be drafted annually by every Official Porsche Centre.

### WM 5XOOIN WORKING WITH BODY STRUCTURAL FOAM (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH BODY STRUCTURAL FOAM > PRODUCT DESCRIPTION

Processing time is approx. 60 - 90 minutes. The structural foam is hardened after 8 - 24 hours. The

hardening time depends on temperature, area of application, amount of foam used and exposed surface.   
The hardening process can be speeded up by heating the components to up to 50 °C.


### WM 5XOOIN WORKING WITH BODY STRUCTURAL FOAM (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH BODY STRUCTURAL FOAM > APPLICATIONS

The body structural foam is ideal for increasing the rigidity, strength and fatigue endurance limit of cavities, plates and structural parts , e.g. pillars, door sills and frame sections.

### CONSTRUCTION > SEPARATING BODY COMPONENTS

In the case of 3-layer spot-welded panel joints with a hardened bonded layer in which only the outer panel needs to be replaced, drill the outer panel in the area of the spotwelds sufficiently without damaging the spotweld and bonded joint in the second component layer.

![](images/4269789c334f574a0eed0e8a7ec8c95bc903084e03bb6acd6ada50b6cdd2cbab.webp)  
Fig 1: Separating Body Components

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

In the case of 3-layer spot-welded panel joints with a hardened bonded layer on the outer panel, drilthe outer panel in the area of the spotwelds suficiently without damaging the spotweld in the second component layer.

![](images/c7ff82a0fab8833530bd314186e8cbafebceb9f30014bd5f31a39810eeebacf0.webp)  
Fig 2: Separating Bonded Body Components

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

After removing the loosened body part, old adhesive must be removed and any uneven spots must be sanded down.

The flange area must then be pre-treated for bonding.


### WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > PREPARING BONDING SURFACES > CLEAN

Sticky, solid layers such as dirt, rust, layers of paint (cathodic-dip layers), etc. must be removed using 100 to 150 grain sandpaper in order to improve the strength of a bonding area.


### WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > PREPARING BONDING SURFACES > DEGREASE

To prevent possible grease residue from spreading onto the surface when grinding down the surface unti bare at a later stage, the bonding surfaces must be cleaned using a lint-free cloth soaked in acetone.

H 7


### WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > PREPARING BONDING SURFACES > SAND/GRIND UNTIL BARE

To improve adhesion, it is important to sand the bonding surfaces until bare using 150 to 180 grain sandpaper. The sanding effect can be improved by cross-sanding.

Only use abrasive products based on pure silicon carbide (SIC) for sanding/grinding down the bonding surface until bare.

![](images/468c1c2b9b5289fd7a3d96f592194d8c45e6559e4f6522c5cee4c87551399953.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Sanding Bonding Surfaces


### WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > PREPARING BONDING SURFACES > DEGREASE

The bare bonding flange areas must then be cleaned using a lint-free cloth soaked in acetone.   
Leave cleaned surfaces to dry ofor approx. 5 - 10 minutes; bonding surfaces must be completely dry.

п . .

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.


### WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > PREPARING BONDING SURFACES > PRIME

Apply primer to the cleaned surfaces.


### WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > PROCESSING CONDITIONS

During processing, the ambient and material temperature must be at least — Minimum temperature: 15°C and must not exceed → Maximum temperature: 35°C.

The optimal processing temperature is → Minimum temperature: 18°C to → Maximum temperature: 23°C.

Higher processing temperatures reduce processing time.

→ Processing time at 15 °C: 75 min → Processing time at 18 °C: 70 min → Processing time at 20 °C: 65 min → Processing time at 23 °C: 60 min → Processing time at 25 °C: 55 min → Processing time at 30 °C: 45 min → Processing time at 35 °C: 35 min


### WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > JOINING PROCESS

1. Check to see how much adhesive oozes out.

1.1.1. Make sure that the two-component adhesive is mixed evenly in the mixing tube.

2. 1.2. Before applying adhesive to the joints, apply a bead of adhesive with a length of → Length: 10 cm to a paper towel or similar object and dispose of it later. The hardening process can also be checked using this bead.

2. Apply adhesive.

1.2.1. Apply adhesive to the flanges of the joints.

![](images/302faded72e8b0853495dbc60e30957103f4f86d819721fa28d5c2074633eea3.webp)  
Fig 2: Applying Adhesive

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2.2.2. Spread the adhesive out over the flanges of the joint. → Application depth: 0.5 mm

![](images/1c9969fcecae0b418729ad75e53921d522e73ceafeab2961cdb980ba094d2a8c.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Spread Adhesive

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. 2.3. Areas not covered by cathodic immersion paint and exposed body panels in cavities must be brushed or filled with structural adhesive.

3. Apply adhesive to the edges.

![](images/979ecba800461b353ea338344e812ecfb16dc3b25a7e166870bad3d8d4b3e812.webp)  
Fig 4: Identifying Bead Of Adhesive At Edges   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

1. 3.1. Apply additional beads of adhesive at the edges and center of the joint. → Application depth: 3 mm


### WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > HARDENING

The body structural adhesives used harden at temperatures of between → Minimum temperature: 18°C and — Maximum temperature: 80°C.


### WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > CORROSION PROTECTION

After adhesive has hardened, carefully prime accessible bonding areas and seal with body sealant.

Protect bonding areas in cavities against corrosion using cavity preservation.

WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) >


### WORKING WITH ADHESIVES > DISPOSAL

Small amounts remaining after mixing and complete hardening may be disposed of as industrial waste.

Dispose of used acetone-soaked cleaning cloths as special-category waste.


### WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > HANDLING PRIMER > GENERAL

Primers improve the long-term durability of the bonded area

Primers reveal the actual condition of the surface to be bonded.

Primers protect the bonding surface from environmental influences, thereby increasing corrosion protection.

To achieve a better effect, apply primer only very lightly.

Primer prevents oxidation of the surface. This is particularly important when bonding aluminum.


### WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > HANDLING PRIMER > 2-COMPONENT SIP

Information

Use the primer within 8 hours. Apply a thin, even coat to the bonded flanges and remove excess primer. Protect surfaces you have already primed from dirt and soiling. Otherwise, the bonded joint may be defective.


### WM 5XOOIN PROCESSING STRUCTURAL BODY ADHESIVE (ALL MODELS) > HANDLING PROCESSING DEVICES > APPLICATOR GUN

1. Open holder.

1.1.1. Release holder -arrow- and fold up.

![](images/2665050c7e5eb6c7ce2c6d4d7911b4bfb8b606120b421209a21c807a071ce754.webp)  
Fig 1: Releasing Holder   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.


### 2. Press sliding lock upwards

1.2.1. Press sliding lock upwards in direction of arrow -arrow- .

![](images/c18ec0c42b6e45f2ce9dbefff8978a1cec7d6f2c7c6b5a68362bb18f3b98cf27.webp)  
Fig 2: Pressing Sliding Lock   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Insert piston rod.

1.3.1. Hold sliding lock pressed and insert piston rod -B1- completely into the gun grip -B1- .

![](images/6989f8f9e39958458764533c0b22cbc54b2f68f340db44aec2937127646baf4d.webp)  
Fig 3: Inserting Piston Rod   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Insert mixing cartridge.

1.4.1. Insert double cartridge -c1- into the gun -B- from above. Insert the cartridge until the muzzle of the gun engages in the groove of the cartridge.

![](images/2be535e44d481e033df54fd8c5b18056edba12cd01d1e859eb3860066c025a06.webp)  
Fig 4: Inserting Cartridge   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.


### 5. Engage holder.

1.5.1. Swivel holder downward and engage on handle of gun.

![](images/914c8659b3c34655b2c51b926d21699d50b2290ab236bb4b3a01f7d479331500.webp)  
Fig 5: Engaging Holder

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.


### 6. Open cartridge.

1.6.1. Turn screw cap 90 ° counter-clockwise and remove.

![](images/3c87609237110465caf5cac0fe06040ff986124fe165e72b8c357ce9b5edefd2.webp)  
Fig 6: Opening Cartridge   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Squeeze adhesive to the front.

1. 7.1. Press the gun grip to allow the piston rod to move out slowly until an equal amount of both components emerges.

2.7.2. Wipe off any adhesive that emerges.

8. Fit processing nozzle.

1. 8.1. Before fitting the processing nozzle, make sure that the muzzle -A- and the mixing ducts are aligned; turn the bayonet locking mechanism on the processing nozzle by 90° if necessary.

2. 8.2. Position processing nozzle -C2- and turn clockwise 90°.

![](images/fd284ba86c78fee9edbfcb8334f8df97f6771417d2a99046a793ef7ead66a7e7.webp)  
Fig 7: Fitting Nozzle   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

9. Mix adhesive components.

1.9.1. Press the gun grip to allow the piston rod to move out slowly until the adhesive is visible in the processing pipe.

10. Bond the body part within the specified processing time.

![](images/87d4f9a32770972154ad7a97798c18b5884dc1c23f258df5bbbd7e4082f1f4f0.webp)  
Fig 8: Identifying Working Time Of Structural Adhesive


### WM 5XOOIN WORKING WITH BODY FOAM FILLER (ALL MODELS) > PRODUCT DESCRIPTION

The processing time is approx. 15-18 minutes. Processing can be interrupted briefly for up to approx. 5 minutes. The chemical reaction is essentially complete after approx. 30 minutes. The hardened foam does not swell or shrink.


### WM 5XOOIN WORKING WITH BODY FOAM FILLER (ALL MODELS) > APPLICATIONS

The foam filler is ideal for filling, insulating and sealing cavities, e.g. on pillars, door sils and frame sections.

WM 5XOOIN WORKING WITH BODY FOAM FILLER (ALL MODELS) > PROCESSING Information

Always observe the relevant work safety regulations when working with the foam filler.

WARNING: Toxic substances

Danger of poisoning or suffocation • Danger of burns to the eyes and skin

→ Ventilate the work area well   
→ Never ingest or inhale.   
→ Read specific information on the Hazard Sheet. → Do not smoke, eat or drink in the work area.


### Observe temperature limits:

Can and ambient temperature: 10-35°C •Optimal temperature: 18-23°C


### Activation process:

1. Break open the seal on the activation lid.   
2.Use a piece of wire to pull the activation lid out as far as it will go (approx. 11 cm up to the notch).   
. Break off the wire at the required rupture point (notch) over the valve.   
0 4. Screw plastic adapter into the valve.   
05. Shake can vigorously up and down (approx. 20 times).   
06. Release foam downwards out of the can with the valve.


### Subsequent work:

The hardened foam filler can be processed further by sanding, cutting or sawing. It can be painted

or varnished.


### WM 5XOOIN SETTING SELF-TAPPING SCREWS (ALL MODELS) > TOOLS

![](images/d5d7ff2f6ad55e92c56ae51a5595d2a4f812d3c2280ee2bf9501b089218f8f97.webp)


### WM 5XOOIN SETTING SELF-TAPPING SCREWS (ALL MODELS) > SETTING SELF-TAPPING SCREWS

1. Align and secure body parts.   
. Drill body parts using a small drill it (-X- mm).   
3. Remove body parts.   
4. Drill holes in the outer component (-Y- mm).

![](images/fa8d5a35920e01134547e02543c3d03a4f37919fe7d1e23fcdb4fa1d0a222288.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Hole Geometry

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. De-burr all bore holes.

6. Prepare bonding surfaces and bond body parts. → 5X00IN21 WORKING WITH BODY STRUCTURAL ADHESIVE

7. Align and secure body parts.

8. Screw on body parts using a special screw.

1.8.1. Fit screw.

![](images/d20313943143417f5d396792e4231c148f66f805f7a962e2f47c3a61284d1fa9.webp)  
Fig 2: Fitting Screw

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2.8.2. Shape the cylindrical extrusion by screwing in at high speed (> 1, 000 RPM). Cordless drill CXS 10 Li 1.3 set WE 1448

![](images/fedf38f78b49b4bf10cae7fda9d3153f998cba1754fe761a10e11f2592933ca5.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Shape Cylindrical Extrusion   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. 8.3. Groove the metric thread without tension.

![](images/98ca76e313ccfe8a2b45b29ab767d1cb2f11f3e73fe4c0ea0479e03bec69dea0.webp)  
Fig 4: Identifying Groove Thread

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4.8.4. Continue to screw in at low speed (< 100 RPM).

![](images/d0cdfde3b29e8a13cc8cd2f808f534be74e5bf47e8efd7963eeba0e084a414e8.webp)  
Fig 5: Identifying Screw   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.


### WM 5XOOIN REPLACING THREADED BOLTS (ALL MODELS) > TOOLS

![](images/23321f1a93c6f11e9cfdcf0e0bef26b09e2fa5697869c39a563abe935b9d1bcd.webp)

WM 5XOOIN REPLACING THREADED BOLTS (ALL MODELS) > TECHNICAL VALUES   
![](images/c09fd0e6a6125deffd76f7b0217be14c1780b904205de0d9f9a873b6ff8d4e91.webp)


### WM 5XOOIN REPLACING THREADED BOLTS (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Remove add-on parts in the repair area.


### WM 5XOOIN REPLACING THREADED BOLTS (ALL MODELS) > REPLACING THREADED BOLTS

Fig 1: Identifying Threaded Bolts Installation Position

![](images/467f5f8a91ae3624445ef522b934a05d3d3d1969aeaf0ad39aff25a7d32cd5c8.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.


### 2.3.2. Drill out the hole.

For M6 threaded bolts → Diameter: 9.0 mm

![](images/525dd27ff22726a7a52ee71366a98760e44911b9d38da4af36256a33a14f09b7.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Threaded Bolts Hole   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Prime rivet area.

5. Prepare threaded bolt for installation.

1. 5.1. On the back of the bolt -1- , apply sealing compound → SEALING MATERIAL 000.043.204.38 as a continuous bead of sealant -2- .

![](images/fcc44b3d908e64737cee27fd80b91a3c1964861d38c36710ba8d141af2e0a393.webp)  
Fig 4: Applying Sealing Compound   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. Rivet in threaded bolt.

1.6.1. Insert threaded bolt into the bore.   
2.6.2. Rivet in threaded bolt using the riveting tool pop rivet nut pliers WE 1476.

![](images/dd58ebf39c59a413565a3c445606a15b70fb110f3d8267e82a1865f2ab325f18.webp)  
Fig 5: Identifying Riveted Threaded Bolt   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Remove any sealing compound that has oozed out.

WM 5XOOIN REPLACING THREADED BOLTS (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Apply primer to the repair area.   
2. Seal the joint for the threaded bolt.   
3. Install add-on parts in the repair area.   
4. Apply cavity protection to the repair area. → 5X00IN44 CAVITY PRESERVATION

### WM 5XOOIN WORK SEQUENCE FOR ACCIDENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > WORK SEQUENCE FOR ACCIDENT REPAIRS > PROCEDURE FOR ACCIDENT REPAIRS

1.Determine scope of damage

2. Expose the area to be repaired

3. Make an economic or technical decision: Should parts be repaired or replaced?

4. Determine the scope of replacement parts and order the parts

See "REPAIRS " below. See "REPLACEMENT " below. 5. If necessary, prime and seal the seam areas 6. If necessary, renew the stone impact protection 7. Paint the repaired area If necessary, touch up the undersealing 9. Seal cavities 10. Fit accessories


### WM 5XOOIN WORK SEQUENCE FOR ACCIDENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > WORK SEQUENCE FOR ACCIDENT REPAIRS > REPAIR

1. Cover undamaged areas of the vehicle . Reshape damaged areas 3. Fill or apply body solder to reshaped areas 4. Apply fine filler on repair areas


### WM 5XOOIN WORK SEQUENCE FOR ACCIDENT REPAIRS (ALL MODELS) > WORK SEQUENCE FOR ACCIDENT REPAIRS > REPLACEMENT

1. Cover undamaged areas of the vehicle so that they are protected against fire   
2. Disconnect battery   
3. Pre-paint new parts from the inside   
4. Roughly cut out damaged areas   
5. Cut out remaining pieces   
6. Fit new parts in, then check the gap dimensions with the accessories fitted   
7. Protect panel flanges against corrosion   
8. Weld in new parts   
9.Grind visible weld seams flat; if necessary apply body solder or filler

![](images/4dc6852047bc86fa9bedd4b13608c153e811da30fe079a7d835ea5cc78ed3edf.webp)


### WM 5XOOIN PROCEDURE FOR DAMAGE DIAGNOSIS (ALL MODELS) > PROCEDURE FOR DAMAGE DIAGNOSIS

1. Identify impact points on the exterior panelling or wheels.

. Remove accessories that restrict the view of the impact area.

3. Check unit mounts, chassis parts and steering parts for deformation and cracks.

Determine the scope of damage to the body. See: IDENTIFIABLE DEFORMATIONS ON THE BODY STRUCTURE

5. Repair vehicle, if necessary.

### WM 631519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT APRON (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING FRONT APRON

Installation is performed in reverse order. Pay particular attention to the following:

1. Tighten fastening screws securing front apron to inner lock carrier to the specified tightening torque. Tightening torque: 8 Nm (6 ftlb.)   
.Tighten fastening screws securing front apron to retaining strip to the specified tightening torque. Tightening torque: 2 Nm (1.5 ftlb.)   
3. Tighten fastening screws securing front apron to outer lock carrier to the specified tightening torque. Tightening torque: 8 Nm (6 ftlb.)   
4.Tighten fastening screws securing front apron to lock carrier at the bottom to the specified tightening torque. Tightening torque: 2 Nm (1.5 ftlb.)   
5. Tighten fastening screws securing front apron to lock carrier at the sides to the specified tightening torque. Tightening torque: 2 Nm (1.5 ftlb.)   
6. Tighten fastening screws securing wheel housing liner to lock carrier to the specified tightening torque. Tightening torque: 2 Nm (1.5 ftlb.)

NOTE: Smears

•Impaired vision and dazzling

→ A coating may only be applied to the side windows.   
— Never apply a coating on the windscreen in particular.


### WM 642949 REWORKING (COATING) FRONT CORNER WINDOW PANE (ALL MODELS) > CHECKING WINDOW GLASS > CLEANING WINDOW SURFACES

Information

The window must be coated immediately after being polished.

1. Clean the window using commercially available glass cleaner.   
2. Shake the polish well before use.   
3. Dampen polishing cloths with water, apply polish and buff for several minutes.   
4.Allow the film of polish to dry and then wipe it off completely.

1. Install front door panel. → Removing front door panel

2. Teach end positions of front power window motor.

1.2.1. Pul rocker switch and close window fully.

2.2.2. Pull rocker switch again. (The upper end position is stored).

3.2.3. Press rocker switch and open window fully.

4.2.4. Press rocker switch again. (The lower end position is stored).

### WM 645419 REMOVING AND INSTALLING POWER WINDOW MOTOR (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING POWER WINDOW MOTOR

WARNING: Electrically moved components • Danger of limbs being trapped or severed → Switch off electric power to drive motor.

→ Make sure it does not switch on again.

→ Check that there is no electric charge.

1. Switch off ignition and pull remote control out of ignition lock.   
2. Pull out locking mechanism -a- , press release button -b- and pull off electric plug connection -1- .   
3. Unscrew fastening screws -2- and remove front power window motor -3- .

![](images/e00628c908cbf28705359bf07d059bace82de4c923f63664dad0f33eb3b42a57.webp)  
Fig 1: Removing Front Power Window Motor


### WM 645419 REMOVING AND INSTALLING POWER WINDOW MOTOR (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING POWER WINDOW MOTOR

1. Installation is performed in reverse order to removal.

2. Tighten fastening screws used to secure front power window motor to front door. Tightening torque 3.3 Nm (2 ftlb.)


### WM 645419 REMOVING AND INSTALLING POWER WINDOW MOTOR (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Install front door panel. → Installing front door panel

2. Teach end positions of front power window motor.

1.2.1. Pul rocker switch and close window fully.

2.2.2. Pull rocker switch again. (The upper end position is stored).

3.2.3. Press rocker switch and open window fully.

4.2.4. Press rocker switch again. (The lower end position is stored).

### WM 647119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR POWER WINDOWS (ALL MODELS) > TECHNICAL VALUES
