### WM 647119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR POWER WINDOWS (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING REAR POWER WINDOWS

Fig 1: Identifying Power Windows Mechanism Position

![](images/1d68730ebf5d7fc9106489c6a7b39f7de8d982a74968129d8c427f0f0d960872.webp)  
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

1. Unclip cover on door inner panel, guide out door release cable at the cover and remove cover.

2. Disconnect electric plug connection for power window motor.

1. 2.1. Press release button -b- and disconnect electric plug connection -1- .

3. Unscrew fastening screws -2- and remove power window motor -3- .

![](images/2ace83f2450331df305ccd5717f838bf9bf04f9ddeb78b9805380606951d5c50.webp)  
Fig 2: Removing Rear Power Window Motor   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Loosen door window glass at the power windows mechanism.

1.4.1. Actuate locking mechanism -2- and remove limit stop -3- on the power windows mechanism. Move door window glass -1- down until the locking mechanism -5- is accessible. Actuate locking mechanism -5- using a suitable tool -arrow A- and carefully raise

the door window glass -1- (-arrow B- .

2.4.2. Pull door window glass -1- fully up -arrow B- out of the mounting points -4- . Fig 3: Releasing Door Window Mounting (Shown On Front Door)

![](images/0d605dd87fe76618860b3fd54de82f2cf4d3bbcb987a2e50421f38fd4e607b1d.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Slide door window glass up full and secure it to prevent it from falling down.

6.Remove stopper at the top of the bodyshel of the door.

1.6.1. Loosen fastening nut at the top and unscrew and remove fastening nuts at the bottom.

![](images/bd97420702623aaf728adf02728b2755ca0bf923a55ba67a17094963c6e9a317.webp)  
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Press mounting clip for power window motor together using a suitable tool and unclip it from the bodyshell of the door.   
8. Guide out power windows mechanism at the top and remove through the opening in the bodyshell of the door.

### WM 648619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR WINDOW (ALL MODELS) > PREPARING WINDOW APERTURE FOR INSTALLATION

1. Remove adhesive on the body.

Information

1. The surface coating of adhesive residue helps new adhesive to stick. Keep cut surfaces clean and free of grease and do not clean with cleaning solution.

1. 1.1. When removing adhesive residue from the body using a cutter and flashing knife, ensure that a surface coating of adhesive remains.

![](images/fe5e2b933bd7a6287e69b5d5bb9bb70eed146659f1eb3cba51a1074e411abfde.webp)  
Fig 1: Removing Adhesive Residue From Rear Lid   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Clean new paint areas or damaged paint surfaces in the non-visible area of the window aperture in the body with cleaning solution -H1- and coat with primer -H2- .


### WM 648619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR WINDOW (ALL MODELS) > PREPARING REAR WINDOW FOR INSTALLATION > PREPARING REAR WINDOW FOR INSTALLATION (NEW REAR WINDOW)

1. Clean and prime the glass.

1. 1.1. Clean the window glass with cleaning solution -H1- .   
2.1.2. Apply primer -H2- to the glass flange close to the marking.

![](images/31115b21853f33f1a4af8aec62f66620d4229ff3418e2fa26cdb3aba88880667.webp)  
Fig 1: Cleaning Glass

### WM 648619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR WINDOW (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING REAR WINDOW

A CAUTION: Danger of material damage if specified curing time of adhesive is not observed! In order to ensure that the bonded joint is sufficiently strong, the following conditions must be adhered to:

The vehicle must not be used until the curing time has elapsed. •Curing time: 2 hours   
Temperature: at least 10 C   
Fixing time: approx. 1 hour

### WM 701819 REMOVING AND INSTALLING DASHBOARD (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Remove glove compartment. → Removing Glove Compartment

2. Remove trim panel under dashboard at the left. → Removing Trim Panel Under Dashboard At The Left   
3. Remove PCM display and operator control unit. → Removing PCM display and operator control unit   
4. Remove cover for dashboard (defroster trim). → Removing Cover For Dashboard (Defroster Trim)   
5. Remove cover for left loudspeaker. → Removing Cover For Left Loudspeaker   
6. Remove cover for right loudspeaker. → Removing Cover For Right Loudspeaker   
7. Remove steering wheel. → Removing And Installing Steering Wheel   
8. Remove instrument cluster. → Removing Instrument Cluster


### WM 701819 REMOVING AND INSTALLING DASHBOARD (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING DASHBOARD

Installation is performed in reverse order. Pay particular attention to the following:

1. Engage tabs -1- for the dashboard -2- in brackets -3- on the body.

2. Check that the dashboard is fitted correctly at the contact surfaces.

3. The electric lines must be routed correctly and must not be kinked or trapped.

Fig 1: Removing Dashboard Holder

![](images/3fa874f60edb9e74e4ee3f058dbb077d5f8ecb6b7b44fc40408ffa85289668ee.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Tighten top fastening screws securing the dashboard to the bracket to the specified torque. Tightening torque 3 Nm (2 ftlb.)

5. Tighten bottom fastening screws securing the dashboard to the bracket to the specified torque. Tightening torque 3 Nm (2 ftlb.)

6. Tighten fastening screw securing airbag bracket to dashboard bracket to the specified torque. Tightening torque 4.5 Nm (3 ftib.)

7. Tighten fastening screws securing passenger's airbag to dashboard to the specified torque. Tightening torque 9 Nm (6.5 ftlb.)

8 Tighten fastening screws securing lower air guide to bracket to the specified torque. Tightening torque 1.5 Nm (1 ftlb.)

9Tighten fastening screws securing upper air guide to bracket to the specified torque. Tightening torque 3 Nm (2 ftlb.)

### WM 720119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT SEAT (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING FRONT SEAT

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag units

Triggering of airbag unit.   
•System faults can occur.

→ Switch off ignition and remove ignition key or remote control (hand-held transmitter).

→ A power supply (e.g. battery charger) must not be connected to the external power supply/jump-lead starting terminals.

→ Disconnect the battery and insulate the ground strap so that all contact with a ground carrier is avoided.

→ Wait 1 minute after disconnecting the battery.   
→ Only pull off connector on the triggering unit after the waiting time has elapsed.   
→ Make sure that no foreign objects are located in front of the airbag unit during installation.   
→ Replace damaged parts during removal.

→ Always position airbag units so that the blow-out opening is facing upwards, e.g. crest on driver's airbag.

→ Do not position anything on the airbag units.

→ If removed for an extended period, the airbag units must be stored in a safe place.

— Airbag units must not come into contact with grease, oil, detergents, liquids, or similar substances.

→ Do not expose airbag units to temperatures above 90°.

→ Do not remove the short-circuit spring on the plug-in contacts.

→ Ignition and preparations may only be carried out by skilled staff, supervised by a second responsible person.

→ Before disposal, the airbag unit must be rendered harmless by electrical ignition performed in accordance with all precautionary measures, thereby preventing it from being used incorrectly.

### WM 7XOOIN INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE CARE OF SOFT-TOUCH PAINT SURFACES (ALL MODELS)

A CAUTION: Risk of damage to the soft-look paint coat if the cleaning agents or solvents available as accessories for cleaning the vehicle interior are used. This also applies to the use of plastic polish from the Tequipment care set. The contents of these agents etch the paint coat (paint swells, rubber-like texture).

•Consequently, the paint coat can separate from the substrate when a mechanical load is applied. Furthermore, the surface may shine brightly after using the cleaning agents.

→ The following procedure is recommended for the care or cleaning of soft-look paint surfaces.


### WM 7XOOIN INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE CARE OF SOFT-TOUCH PAINT SURFACES (ALL MODELS) > LIGHT SOILING (E.G. DUST)

It is possible to clean light soiling by selecting an option from the following cleaning tools and cleaning fluids:

![](images/e6f47b4c5225ef8ee265366db8639652efbdf69169b188fe7745dfd04c512e67.webp)


### WM 7XOOIN INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE CARE OF SOFT-TOUCH PAINT SURFACES (ALL MODELS) > HEAVY SOILING

### WM 453019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HYDRAULIC UNIT (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING HYDRAULIC UNIT > REMOVING HYDRAULIC UNIT

NOTE: Replacing the hydraulic unit/control unit

•The hydraulic unit forms a single unit with the control unit.   
The hydraulic unit and control unit are always replaced together.   
When replacing the hydraulic unit/control unit, the new assembly must be to hand before the old one is removed.   
•The data as well as the coding of the old control unit must be transferred to the new unit before the old one is removed.

→ When replacing, note the following: —→ 453055 REPLACING HYDRAULIC UNIT/CONTROL UNIT .


### WM 453019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HYDRAULIC UNIT (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING HYDRAULIC UNIT > INSTALLING HYDRAULIC UNIT

1. Installation is performed in reverse order.

Observe specified tightening torques:

Only for left-hand drive (LHD) vehicles:

Brake lines to hydraulic unit: Tightening torque 14 Nm (10.5 ftlb.)

Only for right-hand drive (RHD) vehicles:

Brake lines (from brake caliper) to hydraulic unit: Tightening torque 14 Nm (10.5 ftlb.) Brake lines (from brake master cylinder) to hydraulic unit: Tightening torque 18 Nm (13 ftlb.)


### WM 453019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HYDRAULIC UNIT (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Bleed the brake system

. Install ront left trim panel → Installing front trim panel .

3. Bleed the brake lines again (following conventional bleeding using PlWis Tester Il 9818 (secondary brake circuit bleeding). To do this, select:

> Control unit overview > PSM > Maintenance/repairs > Bleed brakes

To finish, follow the menu guidance in PIwis Tester Il 9818.

4. If the hydraulic unit was replaced, code the control unit for the hydraulic unit → 453055 REPLACING HYDRAULIC UNIT .

5. Carry out a swap test using Piwis Tester Il 9818. To do this, select:

> Control unit overview > PSM > Maintenance/repairs > Hydraulic swap test

To finish, follow the menu guidance in PIwis Tester Il 9818.

6. Perform a function test.

1.6.1. During the test drive, perform at least one ABS control operation, taking the road conditions into consideration.   
2. 6.2. On vehicles with PDK transmission, test the HOLD function if possible. If the combination sensor has been taught incorrectly, the Hold function will not be active for inclines of more than 5%!   
3.6.3. Read out the fault memory. There must not be any stored faults.

### WM 456005 INITIALIZING AND CALIBRATING STEERING-ANGLE SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > CHECKING STEERING-ANGLE SENSOR > INITIALIZING STEERING-ANGLE SENSOR

WARNiNG: Steering-angle sensor not calibrated or calibrated incorrectly

Unexpected vehicle handling •Steering-angle sensor does not function Malfunction in steering-angle sensor

→ After working on wheel suspension parts, when replacing the steering-angle sensor and after changing the wheel alignment values, calibrate the steering-angle sensor using PIWis Tester Il 9818.

→ Keep the front wheels in straight-ahead position on the measuring platform during calibration.

→ On vehicles with electromechanical steering, also re-teach the electric steering lock settings.

NOTE: Voltage drop

•Fault entries in the control unit Coding in the control unit is aborted

→ Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch off the ignition and remove the ignition key.

→ Ensure that the power supply is not interrupted during programming.

→ Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least → Nominal value: 40 A to the vehicle battery.

### WM 460555 REPLACING BRAKE PEDAL (ALL MODELS) > REPLACING BRAKE PEDAL

1. Separate brake pedal from brake booster.

1. 1.1. Press brake pedal towards the brake booster.

2.1.2. Release tool T40136 must be fitted on the balljoint on the push rod.

3. 1.3. To press the retaining lugs on the mounting off the ball joint on the push rod, pull release tool T40136 towards the driver's seat and counter at the brake pedal at the same time (the brake pedal must not move towards the driver's seat).

4. 1.4. Release tool T40136 and brake pedal must both be pulled towards the driver's seat.

Risk of damage to (ceramic) brake discs

→ Use two assembly pins when removing and fitting the wheel.

→ Carefully guide the wheel towards the wheel hub, thereby preventing any heavy impact on the (ceramic) brake disc.

Screw the two assembly aids (assembly pins) -1- , instead of two wheel bolts, into the wheel hub before removing/fiting the wheel. During removal, first remove the three remaining wheel bolts and remove the wheel carefully without touching the brake discs.

Remove wheel. Use assembly aids (assembly pins) -1- .

→ Replace the brake discs on each axle upon reaching the wear limits.

### WM 463656 REPLACING FRONT DISC BRAKE PADS (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT DISC BRAKE PADS > REMOVING FRONT DISC BRAKE PADS

NOTE: Removing/fiting wheels

Risk of damage to (ceramic) brake discs

→ Carefully guide the wheel towards the wheel hub, thereby preventing any heavy impact on the (ceramic) brake disc.

Information

To gain better access for assembly work, it is a good idea to turn the wheels fully either to the right or lef!

NOTE: Removal of brake calliper

•Paint defects on brake calliper

—→ Proceed with care when setting back the brake pads.

→ Protect brake calliper from paint defects using a suitable cloth.

1. Carefully set the disc brake pads back slightly and evenly using water pump pliers.

2. Loosen warning contact from the brake calliper.

3. Fit brake piston on the brake calliper between the disc brake pads using piston reset tool (replaces P83) Nr.144 . Then press the brake pads evenly → Pressing back brake pads .

![](images/aa38ea6473716e7a17760fdbad9afdc01665773ad395973fc607dfc26ae2d96f.webp)  
Fig 1: Pressing Brake Pads

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.


### WM 463656 REPLACING FRONT DISC BRAKE PADS (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT DISC BRAKE PADS > INSTALLING FRONT DISC BRAKE PADS

WARNING: Old mounting parts fitted on the brake calliper

Reduced braking effect

Risk of damage to the brake calliper

→ Fit new pad retaining springs

→ Fit new fastening screws

WARNING: Instalation of brake pads with the wrong brake pad quality

Longer braking distance

More wear on brake pads

→ Only use the type-specific brake pads.

→ Replace the brake pads when the brake pad wear indicator light comes on, but no later than when there is a residual pad thickness of 2 mm on each axle.

→ Replace the brake discs on each axle as soon as the brake pad wear limit is reached.


### Applies only to 17" brakes (brake calliper color: Black):

Brake pads are bonded to the brake piston. Before installation, pull off the protective film on the new brake pads and remove adhesive residue on the brake piston.

Check running direction of brake pads (marked on brake pad by an arrow)!


### Applies to all brakes:

The back of the pad backing plates must not be greased.

Check the brake discs for wear. For wear limits, see → 465002 CHECKING FRONT BRAKE DISCS (WEAR ASSESSMENT) → 465102 CHECKING FRONT PCCB BRAKE DISCS (WEAR ASSESSMENT) .

Brake discs must be clean and free of grease.

The core of the warning contact wire must not be left exposed! Worn insulation is not important.

If necessary, remove a little brake fluid from the reservoir by suction in order to prevent an overflow when the disc brake pads are pushed back.

Use a new repair kit.

1. Fit new pad retaining springs.   
2. Place disc brake pad onto the sealing surfaces of the pad retaining springs -arrows- .

![](images/15c015f7f30dfb5ce7d9c5d16ebefe97ead0a9294b58b9e75982930d936aa5d3.webp)  
Fig 1: Installing Brake Pad   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Press brake pad into the brake calliper with slight pressure and slide it onto the pad retaining pins -arrows-.

![](images/7c519243fb9a540ad48e867bb2efc4fc6c2fe81229351cc06407ee8d12890c1f.webp)  
Fig 2: Positioning Brake Pad   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Fit disc brake pad -arrow- .

Fig 3: Installing Brake Pad   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

•Reduced braking effect Risk of damage to the brake calliper

→ Fit new pad retaining springs


### When replacing the brake pads, always pay attention to the following:

The back of the pad backing plates must not be greased.   
Check brake discs for wear. For details of wear limits, see → 465302 CHECKING REAR BRAKI DISCS (WEAR ASSESSMENT) .

The core of the warning contact wire must not be left exposed! Worn insulation is not important.

### WM 465002 CHECKING FRONT BRAKE DISCS (WEAR ASSESSMENT) (ALL MODELS) > CHECKING > CHECKING FRONT BRAKE DISCS - EVALUATING CRACKS

Different vehicle types have different brake disc sizes. This results in differences in terms of maximum crack length limits.

The maximum crack length limit is calculated as follows:

0.5 x a (-a- = width of friction surface in mm).

### WM 465002 CHECKING FRONT BRAKE DISCS (WEAR ASSESSMENT) (ALL MODELS) > CHECKING > CHECKING FRONT BRAKE DISCS - MINIMUM THICKNESS

Information

Normally, brake discs are used until the maximum wear dimension is reached. → WM 4650TW TECHNICAL DATA/BRAKE WEAR LIMIT . Only in a few exceptional cases is it advisable to skim the brake discs (if there is deep scoring or corrosion of the friction surface). In this case only the disc brake dressing machines approved by Porsche AG are to be used .

•Only as new brake discs may be reworked! Only rework the brake discs symmetrically, evenly from both sides!

As the pressure force of a brake piston on the brake pad varies in magnitude, different areas of wear arise on the friction surface. The brake disc can basically be divided into two areas of wear:

-A- Outer and inner wear area.   
-B- Central wear area.

Fig 1: Identifying Brake Disc Wear Areas

![](images/75e79599092923148a3637304f3d57bbf0816932c3751203b7fdbfd658e40d6d.webp)  
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

The central wear area -B- is the area with the highest degree of wear.

![](images/715f18cd4e16a7f6f410614e898e6c81386472fd8c0b26dd6619c0f3f17053c0.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Brake Disc Central Wear Area   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

oMeasure the brake discs using a suitable micrometer at a minimum of three different places (-A, B, C- ), off set by 120°.

![](images/05aae2139ca7f482eabb75d3e24f87e480df89ca0709c7a8aa08f0cda4416026.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Brake Disc Thickness Measurement Points

### Checking involves the following tasks:

1. Determining current actual values (wear condition) using tester VAS 6813 (at the three measurement markings).

Aligning/positioning tester VAS 6813 -1- using a laser beam -2- at the measurement marking.

Observe the required conditions! See: → 465102 CHECKING FRONT PCCB BRAKE DISCS (WEAR ASSESSMENT USING TEST EQUIPMENT VAS 6813)

![](images/3cc34673c27f10417a911ebbb6d5ef72085cccf61edc99a0f812f6bbf4f43dee.webp)  
Fig 1: Positioning Tester On PCCB Brake Disc


### 2. Visual inspection of the brake disc friction surfaces for surface changes.

Flaking/fractures as a result of unusual usage conditions (e.g. stone chip damage).

Max. 1.0 cm2 permitted!

Surface roughness.

Surface roughness (Rk), max. 80 um permitted since this affects braking comfort (noises), braking behavior/pedal pressure and brake pad service life.


### WM 465102 CHECKING FRONT PCCB BRAKE DISCS (WEAR ASSESSMENT USING TEST EQUIPMENT VAS 6813) (ALL MODELS) > CHECKING PCCB BRAKE DISCS (WEAR ASSESSMENT) > CHECKING BRAKE DISCS FOR MINIMUM WEAR VALUE

Information

The pictures shown in this document may differ from the original.


### 3. Exact measurement: Wheel and brake caliper removed.

Turn the measurement marking and brake disc so that the tester can be placed at the position at which the brake calliper was removed.

The removed brake calliper must not be placed closer than 50 mm to the back of the brake disc when taking measurements.

Always follow the operating instructions for the tester to make sure you are using it correctly.

1. 3.1. Measuring procedure: Align laser beam -2- onto the measurement marking on the brake disc hub.

1. Test equipment VAS 6813   
2. Laser beam for positioning   
3. Measured value display

![](images/67b7d5c33f73fcb4359eeaec5f3e1d212acca19907738d821133d6de551d50e6.webp)  
Fig 6: Positioning Tester On Brake Disc

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

When taking measurements, the tester must be positioned over the entire surface of the brake disc with the roller stops and the underside of the device.

Fig 7: Locating Tester On Brake Disc   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2.3.2. Compare the values you read off with the wear value -3- (lower value).

If the wear value (lower value) is reached or if the measured value is less than the wear value at a measuring point, replace the brake discs on both sides of the axle.

Applies to exact measurement (not quick measurement).

NOTE: Removal of brake calliper

1. Paint defects on brake calliper

— Proceed with care when setting back the brake pads.   
— Protect brake calliper from paint defects using a suitable cloth.

2. Set the disc brake pads back slightly and uniformly using water pump pliers.

3. Disconnect the brake line -arrow- at the brake caliper and collect brake fluid in a suitable container.

4.Close off brake line using a suitable stopper.

Information Never use an impact bolter to loosen and tighten the brake calliper on the wheel carrier.

5. Loosen fastening screws -arrows- and remove brake calliper from the wheel carrier.

![](images/a5f80071a1ad765389eda18588aeb402527a214c9fd71f589b96738a2a80baae.webp)

### WM 477019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING BRAKE BOOSTER (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Actuate the brake pedal as often as required until there is no more brake force boosting (brake booster is "empty", brake pedal becomes hard).

2. Remove brake light switch → 943619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING BRAKE LIGHT SWITCH

3. Remove cowI panel cover — 508719 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COWL PANEL COVER .

4. Remove croSs panel → 508119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CROSS PANEL (DISASSEMBLING PLENUM PANEL) .


### WM 477019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING BRAKE BOOSTER (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING BRAKE BOOSTER > REMOVING BRAKE BOOSTER

1. Separate brake pedal from brake booster.

1. Brake pedal   
2. Push rod   
3. Retaining lugs

![](images/05f5558aeb6a760e496c4d641ce50d8144495cbb7f788900c7d6cd9b90031550.webp)  
Fig 1: Separating Brake Pedal From Booster

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

1. 1.1. Press the brake pedal -1- towards the brake booster

2. 1.2. Release tool T40136 must be fitted on the ball joint on the push rod -2- .

3. 1.3. To press the retaining lugs -3- on the mounting off the ball joint on the push rod -2-, pull release tool T40136 towards the driver's seat and counter at the brake pedal -1-at the same time (the brake pedal must not move towards the driver's

seat).

4. 1.4. Release tool T40136 and brake pedal must both be pulled towards the driver's seat.

2. Pull vacuum line -2- out of the brake booster.

3. Unscrew fastening screws -1- for the mounting saddle.


### Damage when installing a new brake booster:

If the brake booster was replaced, the stopper at the vacuum line connection must be removed before connecting the brake pedal to the brake booster.

If this is not done, there is a risk of damage to the brake booster.

3. Connect brake pedal to the brake booster.

![](images/9e63de123fd39c1a5ec707238a91ddb676bd6c774dc80fcd78bceb8a89a69f8e.webp)  
Fig 3: Positioning Brake Pedal On Push Rod   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

1. 3.1. Position brake pedal on the push rod for the brake booster.

2.3.2. Press the brake pedal fully until the push rod -2- engages with an audible click in the holder -1- on the brake pedal.

3. 3.3. Check that the push rod -2- is full engaged in the holder -1- .


### WM 477019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING BRAKE BOOSTER (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Install brake master cylinder → Installing Brake Master Cylinder .

2. Install cross panel —→ Installing Cross Panel .

3. Install cowl panel cover → 508719 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COWL PANEL COVER .

4. Install brake light switch → 943619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING BRAKE LIGHT SWITCH .

5. If the brake booster was replaced: Check the brake booster in accordance with the instructions below.


### WM 477019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING BRAKE BOOSTER (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK > CHECKING BRAKE BOOSTER

1. Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least 40 A to the jump-start terminals in the engine compartment.

2. Switch on ignition.

3. PlWis Tester Il 9818 with the current software version installed must be connected to the vehicle communication module (VCl) via the USB cable . Then, connect the communication module to the vehicle and switch on the PIWis Tester.

4. On the PIWis Tester start screen, call up the ==> 'Diagnostics' menu and select the vehicle type ==> 'Macan' . The diagnostic application is then started and the control unit selection screen is populated.

1. Select the control unit ==> 'PsM in the control unit selection screen (==> 'Overview menu) and press [>>] to confirm your selection → see Fig 1.

![](images/4595005d5c5827805c6f50d62bb638e3db924aede19a77afb49465fe1e43d58e.webp)  
Fig 1: Display - Control Unit Selection Screen

2. Press [F11] to skip the question as to whether you want to create a vehicle analysis log (VAL).

3. Press [>] to acknowledge the message that may appear informing you that campaigns for the vehicle are stored in the PIWIS information system.

4. Once the PSM control unit has been found and is displayed in the overview, select the ==> 'Actual values/input signals' menu → see Fig 2.

Selecting Actual values/input signals

5. In the 'Actual values/input signals' menu, highlight the sensors to be checked ==> 'Brake pressure (hydraulic unit sensor)' and ==> 'Brake booster vacuum (vacuum sensor)' and press [F12] to confirm.

6. Start the engine in selector-lever position "P" and leave it running for approx. 30 seconds at idle speed until the 'Vacuum' is no longer increasing and remains constant.

### WM 392519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HALFSHAFT FLANGE (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > TECHNICAL VALUES > PORSCHE DOPPELKUPPLUNG (PDK) MECHANISM

Housing to intermediate housing on cover. → Initial tightening: 8 Nm (6 ftlb.) → Final tightening: +120°

Cover to intermediate housing. → Initial tightening: 15 Nm (11 ftlb.) → Final tightening: +90°

Differential flange to transmission housing. → Initial tightening: 20 Nm (15 ftlb.) — Final tightening: +90°

Oil pan to transmission housing. → Tightening torque: 10 Nm (7.5 ftlb.)

Clutch cover to transmission housing. → Tightening torque: 10 Nm (7.5 ftlb.)

Speed module to bearing bracket. → Tightening torque: 10 Nm (7.5 ftlb.)

Pump to housing. → Tightening torque: 25 Nm (19 ftlb.)

Hydraulic system to transmission housing. → Initial tightening: 8 Nm (6 ftlb.) → Final tightening: +120°

Bearing bracket to intermediate housing. → Initial tightening: 8 Nm (6 ftlb.) → Final tightening: +120°   
Idler gear support to bearing bracket. → Tightening torque: 25 Nm (19 ftlb.)   
Sucking jet pump to pump module. → Tightening torque: 4.5 Nm (3 ftlb.)   
Pressure filter to transmission housing. → Tightening torque: 10 Nm (7.5 ftlb.)   
Screw on drive shaft. → Initial tightening: 100 Nm (74 ftlb.) → Final tightening: +120°+30°   
Screw on intermediate shaft. → Tightening torque: 205 Nm (151.5 ftlb.)   
Screw on inner intermediate shaft. → Tightening torque: 205 Nm (151.5 ftb.)


### Left fanged shaft. → Initial tightening: 15 Nm (11 ftlb.) → Final tightening: 45°

Drain plug on intermediate shaft housing/oil inspection plug on transmission housing. → Tightening torque: 45 Nm (33 ftlb.)

Drain plug on oil pan. → Tightening torque: 45 Nm (33 ftlb.)

Cable guide to transmission housing. → Tightening torque: 8 Nm (6 ftlb.)

Sealing sleeve to transmission housing. → Tightening torque: 10 Nm (7.5 ftlb.)

Oil inspection plug on intermediate housing. → Tightening torque: 45 Nm (33 ftlb.)

Bending vibration balancer to cover. → Initial tightening: 20 Nm (15 ftlb.) → Final tightening: +90°+/-20°

### WM 4XOOIN LIFTING THE VEHICLE (ALL MODELS) > LIFTING THE VEHICLE > LIFTING THE VEHICLE

1. Drive vehicle onto the lifting platform. Pay particular attention to the following:

1. When driving onto a lifting platform, ensure that there is sufficient distance between the lifting platform and the vehicle.   
. If work has to be done in the front footwell, the vehicle should be positioned in such a way that the doors can be opened far enough.

2. On vehicles with air suspension/levelling system: Switch off the levelling system.

1.2.1. Switch on ignition.

2. 2.2. Press and hold the levelling system button until the message >>Levelling system switched off<< appears on the instrument cluster.

![](images/dee0e7802d39849e9b054be2464733a4dca659a81bf6e7de3e9cf64d1400cd7f.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Levelling System Button

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

WARNING: Vehicle can fall down

1. Risk of squashing or crushing

2. Risk of damage to the vehicle

→ Do not place any solid objects under the raised vehicle.   
→ Ensure that the lifting platform is prevented from lowering.   
→ Remove solid objects before lowering the vehicle.   
→ Raise the vehicle only at the take-up points provided.

3. Raise the vehicle at the four jacking points -1- .

![](images/36897f11343af1ff19fe1c14f9cf8131727cd059b1c125d44609cd1de99d26fd.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Vehicle Jacking Points


### WM 4XOOIN LIFTING THE VEHICLE (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK > SWITCHING ON THE LEVELLING SYSTEM

1. Lower the vehicle.

2. Switch on ignition.

3. Press and hold the levelling system button until the message >>Levelling system switched on<< appears on the instrument cluster.

Alternatively, the levelling system wil switch on automatically while driving (→ Speed greater than: +7 km/h (4 mph)) .

WM 2706IN EXTERNAL POWER CONNECTION, JUMP-LEAD STARTING (ALL MODELS) > INFORMATION > EXTERNAL POWER CONNECTION, JUMP-LEAD STARTING

WARNING: Live jump leads

Risk of electric shock Risk of short circuit

→ Route the jump leads so that they do not become entangled in moving parts in the engine compartment.

→ There must be no contact between the vehicles.

NOTE: Using charging cables/jump leads directly on the vehicle battery.

Risk of damage to battery sensors.

→ Always connect charging cables/jump leads to the external power supply for jump-lead starting.


### This test can be used to determine:

Whether the battery housing is damaged. Leak-free operation and function of the battery cannot be guaranteed if the housing is damaged.   
Whether the battery terminals (battery line connections) are damaged. The line connections might not make contact if the battery terminals are damaged. This can cause the lines to catch fire and can result in malfunctions in the electrical system.


### Procedure for charging exhaustively discharged batteries:

Batteries that have not been used for a long time discharge automatically.

A battery is exhaustively discharged if the open-circuit voltage has dropped below 11.6 V, see OPEN-CIRCUIT VOLTAGE MEASUREMENT

In exhaustively discharged batteries, the battery acid (sulfuric acid and water mixture) consists of virtually only water, as the sulfuric acid proportion is considerably reduced.

Exhaustively discharged batteries sulphatise, i.e. the entire plate surfaces of the batteries harden.

If exhaustively discharged batteries are immediately recharged after an exhaustive discharge, the sulphatisation recedes again.

If these batteries are not recharged, the plates continue to harden and charge take-up ability is limited. This results in reduced battery performance.

Exhaustively discharged batteries must be charged using a low charge current as follows:

1. Set the charge current to maximum 10% of battery capacity, i.e. with a 95 AH battery, the charge current is max. 9.5 A.

Charge the battery.

### WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > TOOLS

![](images/44aff77720a992fd0d97cae1dd5e1dfb2d7ff68fa393492145e7879e2c534657.webp)

![](images/89733ee29ee3718d67da3c300a81f81363566574b667d2ee0281f43e56985fd9.webp)


### WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK > WHEN DOES DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR CONTROL UNIT NEED TO BE ADJUSTED?

The distance measuring sensor control unit must be re-adjusted in the following situations:

1. Suspension was aligned and adjusted.   
2. Distance measuring sensor control unit or distance measuring sensor control unit holder was loosened or removed and installed.   
3. Bumper was loosened or removed and installed.   
4. The front end is damaged.   
5. Fault memory entry: ACC sensor incorrectly adjusted (Do0004).   
1.5.1. The misalignment angle is outside of the range -1.5° to +1.5°.


### WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK > REQUIREMENTS FOR TESTING AND ADJUSTMENT

1. Tyre tread depth of the tires of one axle must not deviate by more than 2 mm.   
2. Tyre inflation pressure in accordance with regulations ("Comfort" or "Normal" tire pressure).   
3. As with complete suspension alignment, make sure that there is no sliding base or turnplate at the end stop during alignment.   
1. 3.1. Take the track width and wheel base into consideration.   
4. Check that vehicle weight corresponds to empty weight. Weight of the vehicle ready for driving (completely full fuel tank, reducing agent tank and water reservoir for the windscreen washer/headlight cleaning system, spare wheel, tool kit, jack) without driver.   
5. Spare wheel, tool kit and jack must be located at the positions specified by the vehicle manufacturer.   
6. Vehicle aligned correctly, having been bounced multiple times.   
7. Wheel suspension, steering and steering linkage show no signs of play or damage.   
1.7.1. Check for play and damage and carry out repairs if necessary.   
8. Set vehicles with air suspension to normal level.   
1. 8.1. Switch off ignition, close and lock all doors.   
2. 8.2. Wait 15 seconds until vehicle has settled in normal level.   
3.8.3. Open door and leave it open during the measurement, switch on ignition.


### WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK > PREPARATION FOR ADJUSTING DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR

1. Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least 40 A to the external power feed points.

2. Read out the fault memory using Piwis Tester Il 9818 , create a vehicle analysis log if necessary → OXO3IN CREATING VEHICLE ANALYSIS LOG (VAL) and correct any faults.

3. Remove trim cover -1- from the distance measuring sensor control unit.

1.3.1. Push trim cover up -a-.

2. 3.2. Pull trim cover forward and remove it -b- .

![](images/121411af757b32f8de093806cdbd3d5ef3c3f965202ad8046d93a6c9c599e477.webp)  
Fig 1: Removing Trim Cover   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Clean distance measuring sensor control unit and trim cover using commercially available cleaning agent.   
5. Fit the front sensors onto the adjustment device, align using the spirit levels and clamp using the wing screws, and switch them on (initialize).   
6. Set the distance between the adjustment device with reflector VAS 6430/1 WE 1362 and the vehicle in accordance with the specifications provided by the measuring equipment manufacturer.   
1. 6.1. The distance between the left sensor and the vehicle -Bl- should be identical to the distance between the right spirit level and the vehicle -Br- .

### WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR

1. Connect PiWis Tester Il 9818 to the vehicle and start it.

2. Switch on ignition.   
3. Select the required vehicle and the Adaptive cruise control control unit. Press [F12] to continue.   
4. Select the Maintenance/repairs sub-menu in the Adaptive cruise control menu. Press [F12] to continue.   
5. Follow the instructions on Piwis Tester Il 9818 and adjust the distance measuring sensor control unit -1- as required using adjustment tool T-socket wrench for ACC sensor VAS 6190/2 WE 1364 -2- by turning the relevant adjusting screw -3- according to specifications.

![](images/a6ca1494fe1e8ac7e5b121373394baf99ac6a256a1d3e3315f3f981964750e91.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Sensor Control Unit Adjusting Screws

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. Repeat the process until PIWIS Tester II 9818 displays the message Adjustment successful.

3. Disconnect battery charger.

4. Remove sensors and instrument holders.

### WM 2XOOIN BATTERY TRICKLE CHARGING (ALL MODELS) > BATTERY TRICKLE CHARGING > CONNECTING THE BATTERY FOR TRICKLE CHARGING

A suitable battery charger must be connected to the vehicle electrical system when performing the following tasks. All unnecessary electrical loads must be switched off.

When working on the vehicle for more than 15 minutes.

When running diagnostics using the Porsche System Tester.

When adjusting the headlights.

When working on or with the Infotainment system.

If the doors, bonnet and rear lid are open for a long period of time or if these components are actuated frequently.

### 7. Risk of short circuit! Disconnect the ground line at the battery!

1.7.1. Open cover -1- on the negative terminal.

2. 7.2. Loosen terminal clamp -2- for the ground line from the negative terminal.

3.7.3. Insulate terminal clamp or route ground line to prevent any contact with the negative terminal!

![](images/6f173cb2a79b81e3ed99871634cd9a4df8d76549d0fe55fa17a2c4d881548a73.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Battery Terminal Clamp And Cover


### Control unit memories

Values and faults stored in the control units can be deleted if the batery is disconnected or completely discharged.

If possible, al fault memories should be checked and, if necessary, printed out before the battery is disconnected.


### Supply voltage fault entry

The entry "supply voltage" may be stored in various control units if the battery has been completely discharged.

Delete the "supply voltage" entry from the control units in question.


### Ready status

In some countries (presently the U.S.A. and Canada), after disconnecting the battery, it is necessary to reach the Ready status by a test drive and/or by using the Porsche System Tester DME control module menu). If in doubt about this, contact the relevant importer.


### 2470 DME control module

With all DME systems, the engine must run for several minutes before the engine control module can relearn the idle speed and mixture adaptation values!

After disconnection of the power supply, the idle speed might change or fluctuate briefly until the throttle valve adjusting unit has been readapted.

The mixture adaptation is also lost.


### After the battery is connected:

With the DME, it is necessary to carry out a learning and adaptation routine as described below:

Switch ignition on for 30 seconds without starting the engine.

• Do not actuate accelerator pedal.

This completes the adaptation of the throttle valve adjusting unit.


### Tyre pressure monitoring system

When the battery is disconnected and connected, the tire pressure is first displayed as "- - - ".

Once the battery has been disconnected and work is complete, the vehicle must be driven for a short distance.

The actual pressures will then be displayed again.


### 4560 Steering angle sensor

The steering angle sensor must be re-initialized when the battery is disconnected and connected.

Turn wheels to straight-ahead position.   
Switch ignition off and then on again twice.   
Start engine.   
From the straight-ahead position, turn steering wheel approx. 20° to the right, past the straight-ahead position.   
Drive the vehicle straight ahead for at least one second at a speed above 4 km/h (2.5 mp

The steering angle sensor segment is recognized again in this process.

Once the sensor has been successfull initialized, the fault code that is stored in the fault memory is documented using the fault deletion counter.

The fault memory erases itself automatically.

The PSM indicator light in the instrument cluster goes out.


### 6014 Motor for sunroof

The limit positions of the sunroof are deleted from the control unit when the battery is disconnected and connected.

Switch on ignition.   
Press the sunroof button for several seconds in direction of travel.   
After approx. 10 seconds, the sunroof performs an automatic standardization process anId resets all positions.   
Keep the button pressed during the standardization process.

Afterwards, the sunroof is standardized correctly.


### 6452 Power windows

The limit positions of the power windows are deleted from the control unit when the battery is disconnected and connected.

Perform the following procedure for all power windows:

Pull rocker switch and fully close window once.   
Pull rocker switch once more.

The upper end position of the window is stored.

Press rocker switch and fully open window once.   
Press rocker switch once more.

The lower end position of the window is stored.


### 4815 Electrical steering column adjustment (ELVS)

The electrical steering column adjustment end positions (ELVS) are deleted when the battery is disconnected and connected.

The following buttons must be pressed in sequence in order to re-initialize electrical steering column adjustment.

Press the extend button three times (extend towards the driver).   
Press the retract button once.   
Press the extend button once (towards the driver).   
Press the up button once.   
Press the down button once.

Once the buttons have been pressed correctly, the steering column automatically moves all axles and stops at the center position (only works when the vehicle is stationary).

1. Erase error messages from the control units.   
2. Perform the required initialization steps, depending on vehicle equipment.

NOTE: Incorrect handling of wire harness

Risk of damage to lines

→ The wire harness contains allairbag lines, antenna lines and optical waveguides.

→ The wire harness must not be separated and is always replaced as a complete wire harness when carrying out extensive repairs.

→ If individual lines are damaged, shut off these lines and install new lines. Route the new lines along the wire harness and secure them to the wire harness.

NOTE: Incorrect handling of optical waveguides

Risk of damage to optical waveguide

→ Observe the requirements for working with and installing optical waveguides.

### COMPARTMENT AT THE RIGHT (ALL MODELS) > SECURING MAIN WIRE HARNESS IN PASSENGER COMPARTMENT AT THE RIGHT

NOTE: Incorrect handling of main wire harness

Risk of damage to lines

→ The main wire harness contains all airbag lines, antenna lines and optical waveguides.

→ The main wire harness must not be separated and is always replaced as a complete wire harness when carrying out extensive repairs.

→ If individual lines are damaged, shut off these lines and install new lines. Lay the new lines along the main wire harness and secure them to the main wire harness.

NOTE: Incorrect handling of optical waveguides

Risk of damage to optical waveguide

→ Observe the requirements for working with and installing optical waveguides.

1. The main wire harness is secured in reverse order to the steps required for loosening it.

1.1.1. Make sure that the individual sub-parts of the wire harness in the passenger compartment at the right are not twisted or entangled.

3.1.3. Clip all electric lines for the main wire harness in the passenger compartment at the right in securely at the designated positions.   
4.1.4. Connect all electric plug connections until they engage securely.   
5.1.5. Lock allelectric plug connections by hand using the manual slide lock.

2. Tighten fastening nuts securing ground lines to the body. Tightening torque 9 Nm (6.5 ftlb.)

### WM 974619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CUTOFF RELAY (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING CUTOFF RELAY

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag units

Triggering of airbag unit.   
System faults can occur.

→ Switch off ignition and remove ignition key or remote control (hand-held transmitter).

→ A power supply (e.g. battery charger) must not be connected to the external power supply/jump-lead starting terminals.

→ Disconnect the battery and insulate the ground strap so that all contact with a ground carrier is avoided.

→ Wait 1 minute after disconnecting the battery.

→ Only pullof connector on the triggering unit after the waiting time has elapsed.

→ Make sure that no foreign objects are located in front of the airbag unit during installation.

→ Replace damaged parts during removal.

→ Always position airbag units so that the blow-out opening is facing upwards, e.g. crest on driver's airbag.

→ Do not position anything on the airbag units.

— If removed for an extended period, the airbag units must be stored in a safe place.

— Airbag units must not come into contact with grease, oil, detergents, liquids, or similar substances.

→ Do not expose airbag units to temperatures above 90°.

→ Do not remove the short-circuit spring on the plug-in contacts.

→ Ignition and preparations may only be carried out by skilled staff, supervised by a second responsible person.

→ Before disposal, the airbag unit must be rendered harmless by electrical ignition performed in accordance with all precautionary measures, thereby preventing it from being used incorrectly.

1. Screw off fastening nuts -1- .   
2. Removing cutoff relay -2- from the power distributor.

![](images/5ca7894695031083fa23368516ba26ca1ae3bc9f15e18588e95533bd6f68bd2e.webp)  
Fig 1: Removing Cutoff Relay

### WM 975219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WIRE HARNESS FOR ENGINE (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > INSTALLING WIRE HARNESS FOR ENGINE

1. Installation is performed in reverse order to removal.

1.1.1. Make sure that the individual sub-parts of the engine wire harness are not twisted or entangled.   
2.1.2. Check that the wire harness is routed correctly and without tension so that no chafing occurs.   
3.1.3. Connect allelectric plug connections until they engage securely.   
4. 1.4. Lock all electric plug connections by hand using the manual slide lock.   
5.1.5. Clip in all sections of the engine wire harness securely at the relevant positions.

2. Tighten fastening screws for the wiring ducts at the left and right on the cylinder head.

3. Tighten fastening screws for the wiring ducts at the left and right on the valve cover.

4. Tighten fastening screws for the wiring ducts on the thermostat housing.

5. Tighten fastening screws for the wiring ducts on the crankcase.

6. Tighten fastening screw for the vent line on the cylinder head. Tightening torque 10 Nm (7.5 ftib.)   
7. Tighten fastening screw securing holder to left cylinder head.   
8. Tighten fastening nut used to secure the electric B+ line to the starter. Tightening torque 18 Nm (13 ftlb.)   
9. Tighten fastening nut used to secure the electric line for terminal 50 to the starter. Tightening torque 10 Nm (7.5 ftlb.)   
10. Tighten fastening screw securing wiring duct to the timing chain housing cover.   
11. Tighten fastening screws securing coolant line to the timing chain housing cover.


### WM 975219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WIRE HARNESS FOR ENGINE (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Install vacuum reservoir with secondary-air pump → INSTALLING VACUUM RESERVOIR .   
2. Connect oxygen sensors downstream of the catalytic converter at the left and right and clip in all holders for the lines → INSTALLING OXYGEN SENSOR DOWNSTREAM OF CATALYTIC CONVERTER .   
3. Connect oxygen sensors upstream of the catalytic converter at the left and right and clip in all holders for the lines → INSTALLING OXYGEN SENSOR UPSTREAM OF CATALYTIC CONVERTER .   
4. Install the generator → INSTALLING GENERATOR .   
5. Install engine → INSTALLING ENGINE .

### WM 978919 REMOVING AND INSTALLING POWER DISTRIBUTOR (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING POWER DISTRIBUTOR

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag units

Triggering of airbag unit.   
System faults can occur.

→ Switch off ignition and remove ignition key or remote control (hand-held transmitter).

→ A power supply (e.g. battery charger) must not be connected to the external power supply/jump-lead starting terminals.

→ Disconnect the battery and insulate the ground strap so that all contact with a ground carrier is avoided.

→ Wait 1 minute after disconnecting the battery.

→ Only pull off connector on the triggering unit after the waiting time has elapsed.

→ Make sure that no foreign objects are located in front of the airbag unit during installation.

→ Replace damaged parts during removal.

→ Always position airbag units so that the blow-out opening is facing upwards, e.g. crest on driver's airbag.

→ Do not position anything on the airbag units.

→ If removed for an extended period, the airbag units must be stored in a safe place.

→ Airbag units must not come into contact with grease, oil, detergents, liquids, or similar substances.

→ Do not expose airbag units to temperatures above 90°.

→ Do not remove the short-circuit spring on the plug-in contacts.

→ Ignition and preparations may only be carried out by skilled staff, supervised by a second responsible person.

→ Before disposal, the airbag unit must be rendered harmless by electrical ignition performed in accordance with all precautionary measures, thereby preventing it from being used incorrectly.

1. Open cover -1- on the positive terminal.

2. Loosen terminal clamp -2- for the power distributor from the battery terminal.

Fig 1: Loosening Terminal Clamp On Positive Terminal

![](images/1590531526474ec7984aebc08a2da9790872a8a840e2bd9ea226e7dcee98846d.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Release cover -1- (-a- ) and fold it up towards the rear.

![](images/88ae72484f78ca72fe3bd49d33dfeb39d76c480183c81523c6f4dada7ae2d8c2.webp)  
Fig 2: Opening Cover

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Unscrew fastening screw -1- and remove electric line.

5. Unscrew fastening nuts -2- and remove ground lines.

![](images/656200d0b1ebd7c56feeae7fee8d087ae10fbea7f8034fbdab374cf7f623cb77.webp)  
Fig 3: Disconnecting Electric Lines

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. Lift the power distributor and release and disconnect electric plug connection -1- on the cutoff relay -2- (-a- ).

![](images/a0c9f99962433150feb39e57ad0a3a6cf7125f1fb41057f9d3ecbcd30d301ca0.webp)  
Fig 4: Disconnecting Electric Plug Connection On Cutoff Relay


### WM 978919 REMOVING AND INSTALLING POWER DISTRIBUTOR (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING POWER DISTRIBUTOR

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag units

Triggering of airbag unit.   
System faults can occur.

→ Switch off ignition and remove ignition key or remote control (hand-held transmitter).

→ A power supply (e.g. battery charger) must not be connected to the external power supply/jump-lead starting terminals.

→ Disconnect the battery and insulate the ground strap so that al contact with a ground carrier is avoided.

→ Wait 1 minute after disconnecting the battery.

→ Only pull off connector on the triggering unit after the waiting time has elapsed.

→ Make sure that no foreign objects are located in front of the airbag unit during installation.

→ Replace damaged parts during removal.

→ Always position airbag units so that the blow-out opening is facing upwards, e.g. crest on driver's airbag.

→ Do not position anything on the airbag units.

→ If removed for an extended period, the airbag units must be stored in a safe place.

→ Airbag units must not come into contact with grease, oil, detergents, liquids, or similar substances.

→ Do not expose airbag units to temperatures above 90°.

→ Do not remove the short-circuit spring on the plug-in contacts.

→ Ignition and preparations may only be carried out by skilled staff, supervised by a second responsible person.

→ Before disposal, the airbag unit must be rendered harmless by electrical ignition performed in accordance with all precautionary measures, thereby preventing it from being used incorrectly.

1. Installation is performed in reverse order to removal.   
2. Tighten M6 fastening nuts used to secure electric lines to the power distributor. Tightening torque 7.5 Nm (5.5 ftlb.)   
3. Tighten M8 fastening nut used to secure electric line to the power distributor. Tightening torque 16 Nm (12 ftlb.)   
4. Tighten fastening screw used to secure electric line to the power distributor. Tightening torque 7.5 Nm (5.5 ftlb.)

### WM 9XOOIN BASIC INSTRUCTIONS AND PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE PIWIS TESTER (ALL MODELS) > TOOLS

![](images/acce784ffeb3bc0a61f7398ba4c35dbea315cfe4dc799c91cccc56979bc6646d.webp)


### or

•Using the "Campaign" function in the Additional menu on the PIWis Tester by entering a specific programming code.

The type of control unit programming to be used is described in the relevant Service Information or in the relevant Technical Information.


### WM 9XOOIN BASIC INSTRUCTIONS AND PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE PIWIS TESTER (ALL MODELS) > GENERAL PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least 40 A (e.g. battery charger HFL 65 WE 1353) to the jump-start terminals in the engine compartment and switch it on.

.Switch on the ignition using the original driver's key.

On vehicles with "Porsche Entry & Drive", do this by replacing the control panel in the ignition lock with the original driver's key if necessary.

3. PIWis Tester Il 9818 must be connected to the vehicle communication module (VCl) via the USB cable. Then, connect the communication module to the vehicle and switch on the PIWIS Tester.


### or

Using the "Campaign" function in the Additional menu on the PIWis Tester by entering a specific programming code → Control unit programming using the "Campaign" function in the Additional menu on the PIWIS Tester.

The type of control unit programming to be used is described in the relevant Service Information or in the elevant Technical Information.


### WM 9XOOIN BASIC INSTRUCTIONS AND PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE PIWIS TESTER (ALL MODELS) > BASIC PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE PIWIS TESTER > CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE "PROGRAMMING" MENU

1. On the PIWiS Tester start screen, call up the ==> 'Diagnostics' menu and select the relevant vehicle type.

The diagnostic application is then started and the control unit selection screen is populated.

2. Select the control unit to be programmed in the control unit selection screen (==> "Overview" menu) and press [>] to confirm your selection → see Fig 1.

![](images/02d4a562fab1e55f9cea3a6d47f94aa487adb017d25a302b5508b3556ec924d3.webp)  
Fig 1: Screen Display - Control Unit Selection

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. When the question "Create Vehicle Analysis Log (VAL)?" appears, either press [F12] to create a VAL or press [F11] if you do not want to create a VAL.

4. Press [>] to acknowledge the message that may appear informing you that campaigns for the vehicle are stored in the PIWIS information system.

5. Once the control unit to be programmed has been found, select the ==> 'Programming' menu

6. Select the ==> 'Automatic programming'function and press [>>] to confirm your selection and start the guided programming sequence → see Fig 2.

![](images/3f42c2ead07221d67bcc57b8bdfc2cfdb78ff12229050f84e820444bb45e4b5d.webp)  
Fig 2: Screen Display - Automatic Programming

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Read and follow the information and instructions on the Plwis Tester during the guided programming sequence. Then press [>>] to continue.

During the programming sequence, the control unit is re-programmed and then re-coded automatically if necessary.


### Do not interrupt programming and coding.

Once control unit programming - and coding if necessary - is complete, you will be prompted to switch the ignition off and then back on again after a specified waiting time.


### WM 9XOOIN BASIC INSTRUCTIONS AND PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE PIWIS TESTER (ALL MODELS) > BASIC PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE PIWIS TESTER > CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE "CAMPAIGN" FUNCTION IN THE ADDITIONAL MENU ON THE PIWIS TESTER

1. On the PlWis Tester start screen, call up the ==> 'Diagnostics' menu and select the relevant vehicle type.

The diagnostic application is then started and the control unit selection screen is populated.

2. In the control unit selection screen ("Overview" menu), press [F7] to callup the ==> 'Additional menu' (→ see Fig 1).

![](images/3226223f8a6cd70ffdcb7bf187c4a0c07433deaa8946eb5e7c022ad50da3e216.webp)  
Fig 1: Screen Display - Control Unit Selection

3. When the question "Create Vehicle Analysis Log (VAL)?" appears, either press [>] to create a

VAL or press [F11] if you do not want to create a VAL.

4. Press [>] to acknowledge the message that may appear informing you that campaigns for the vehicle are stored in the PIWiS information system.

5. Select the ==> 'Campaign' function and press [>>] to confirm your selection → see Fig 2. You are then prompted to enter a programming code.

![](images/6bd7eaa160e5df81b0f25f4c592d0b929400d4c10ca3bbc699b918927c71e4d6.webp)  
Fig 2: Screen Display - Additional Menu - Campaign

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. To enter the programming code, click in the relevant text box so that the cursor starts to flash → see Fig 3.

![](images/27d559ff2b518efc479bf6b41e1aef87c96a29fd9cfcc629c513c4ad69bb033d.webp)  
Fig 3: Screen Display - Programming Code Input Field

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Enter the programming code specified in the relevant description (Technical Information, Service Information) and press Enter to confirm your entry.

The text box turns blue.

8. Press [>>] to start the guided programming sequence.

Read and follow the information and instructions on the Piwis Tester during the guided programming sequence. Then press [>>] to continue.

During the programming sequence, the control unit is re-programmed and then re-coded automatically if necessary.


### WM 9XOOIN BASIC INSTRUCTIONS AND PROCEDURE FOR CONTROL UNIT PROGRAMMING USING THE PIWIS TESTER (ALL MODELS) > GENERAL SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Read out and erase allfault memories.

1.1.1. In the control unit selection screen (==> 'Overview menu), press [F7] to callup the ==> 'Additional menu' (→ see Fig 1).

![](images/472e0b9866a6d7f75c581318cfe6d2958ea167e13f4f8b40a2f9761291bcfcf6.webp)  
Fig 1: Screen Display - Control Unit Selection

2. 1.2. Select the function ==> 'Read all fault memories and erase if required' and

press [>>] to confirm → see Fig 2.

The fault memories of the control units are read out.

![](images/42430194f4c2058497a14cbd4c240fcdb77a5294de04a47ccffeb76a0c687a63.webp)  
Fig 2: Screen Display - Erasing Fault Memories

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3.1.3. Once you have read out the fault memories, delete the fault memory entries by pressing [F8].

4. 1.4. Press [>>] ("Yes") in response to the question as to whether you really want to delete all fault memory entries.

The faults stored in the fault memories of the various control units are deleted.

### VM 100119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING ENGINE (MACAN) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Remove ignition key.   
2. Disconnect the battery. → 270619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING BATTERY   
3. Remove engine cover.   
4. LooSen drive belt. → 137819 REMOVING AND INSTALLING DRIVE BELT   
5. Remove cowI panel cover. → 508719 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COWL PANEL COVER   
6. Remove fillr neck from windscreen-washer reservoir. → 926019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WINDSCREEN-WASHER RESERVOIR   
7. RemOve front strut. → 408619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT STRUT   
8. Remove front wheels. — 440519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WHEEL   
9. Remove front wheel housing liner. → 505619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT WHEEL HOUSING LINER   
10. Remove cover for front underbody. → 519219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COVER FOR FRONT UNDERBODY   
11. Drain Coolant. → 193817 DRAINING AND FILLING COOLANT   
12. Remove croSs panel. → 508 119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CROSS PANEL (DISASSEMBLING PLENUM PANEL)   
13. Remove catalytic converter. → 267319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CATALYTIC CONVERTER

Risk of burns

### WM 101802 PRESSURE LOSS TEST (MACAN) > TEST EVALUATION

тhe toot docs nor onow any тeanmgraгтeoun on a now сhgmo (r.o. оne hat пasm рoonтan n).

A difference in pressure loss between the individual cylinders of approx. 5% is not significant.   
If the test shows an excessive loss of pressure (> 30%), a few drops of oil can be sprayed into the combustion chamber. Repeat the test. If the loss in pressure is now significantly less, the seal between the piston and cylinder is damaged.   
The air that is escaping causes hissing noises, which provide information about the component that is causing the damage.


### If the limit values are exceeded, the engine must be started and the test repeated.

![](images/3ed103ffb239e2f415593be3dd2b6b161b033235e340989b3ace2b91f5a117fc.webp)

4. Insert bearing shels into the connecting rod and connecting-rod bearing cap. Do not mix up worn bearing shells. Dimension -a- must be the same at the left and right.

NOTE: Drive belt breaks and becomes jammed

Risk of damage to components (trim panels, electric cables, etc.) •Sealing ring on crankshaft vibration balancer can start to leak •Vibration balancer can overheat and lose its strength

→ Following belt breakage, check adjacent components and the interior of the engine compartment for damage, and repair or replace damaged parts if necessary.

→ Find out why the belt broke. Check deflection rollers or crankshaft vibration balancer for prior damage.   
→ If the drive belt is jammed, replace vibration balancer.

WARNING: Rotating components

•Danger of limbs being trapped or severed

→ Disconnect power supply to the drive motor of components or to the battery.

### WM 150516 SETTING TIMING FOR CAMSHAFTS (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > SETTING TIMING FOR CAMSHAFTS

NOTE: Incorrect handling of crankshafts

Risk of damage to the timing system

→ Never turn the crankshaft against the rolling direction or when the chain tensioner is removed.

— Proceed carefully with your work.

→ Only turn the engine at the crankshaft.

— After working on the camshaft, re-set the valve timing.

→ Observe general warning notes and working regulations.

NOTE: Timing not set correctly

Risk of engine damage • Rough running engine Loss of engine power

→ Do not use force when fitting the staking tool.   
→ Make sure that the gap is equal on both sides.   
→ When inserting the staking tools, do not use force to turn the camshafts against any resistance. → The engine must be exactly at top dead center.   
→ The opposite cylinder must be at ignition TDC.


### 8. If you accidentally turn the vibration balancer too far, do not try to turn it back again!

1. 8.1. The staking tools must be removed and the camshafts must be turned in such a way that there is only the slightest pressure on the valve springs.

2.8.2. Turn the crankshaft once and start the setting procedure again.

9. Camshafts and crankshaft are fixed correctly.

1. 9.1. Screwed-in assembly chain tensioner with approx. 5.0 to 5.5 bar pressure.

2.9.2. Two fixed staking tools on the camshafts.

3.9.3. Staking pin secures crankshaft in TDC of cylinder 1.

10. Tighten central screws on the four camshafts as instructed. To do this, counter at the hexagon on the camshaft controllers and observe the specified sequence!

1.10.1. Tightening torque: Initial tightening 30 Nm (22 ftlb.) Final tightening +40°

2. 10.2. Tightening sequence:

![](images/39ea4d8ec58fa5c10c9de1666be28c9ddb6ac852a8c3fb4fde902ad48359fe94.webp)

![](images/7ab93eae3e14da2e38253942f807180738d2bb019693a9645a535d2cd0324461.webp)

11. Remove tools.

12. Install chain tensioner.

13. Check by turning the engine twice.

### WM 157019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CYLINDER HEAD (MACAN) > INSTALLING CYLINDER HEAD

NOTE: Risk of damage if components are not cleaned and handled correctly when ng the cylinder head.

Risk of damage to sealing faces.   
Risk of damage to the crankcase.   
Risk of leaks at the cylinder-head gasket.   
Risk of damage to open valves.   
Risk of damage to valves and piston crowns after working on the valve drive.

→ Carefully remove any residual sealant from the cylinder head and crankcase. Make sure there are no long scores or scratches.

→ Carefully remove lubricating gel and sanding residues.

→ There must be no oil or coolant in the blind holes for the cylinder-head fastening screws in the crankcase.

To prevent damage to the silicone layer and seam area of the cylinder-head gasket, do not remove the new cylinder head-gasket from its packaging until just before installation and handle with extreme care.

→ If you are using a replacement head, do not remove the plastic socket used to protect the open valves until just before you install the cylinder head.

→ To prevent valve problems when starting the engine, careful turn the engine with your hand for at least two turns.

### WM 170301 CHECKING OIL PRESSURE (ENGINE OIL) (MACAN) > CHECKING > CHECKING OIL PRESSURE

Test prerequisites:

Park the vehicle on a level surface   
Oil level OK.   
• Oil temperature 80 °C (radiator fan must have come on once) 1. Disconnect plug connection -3- on oil pressure switch for reduced oil pressure.

WARNING: Hot fluid

1. Danger of scalding

→ Let the fluid cool down.   
→ Wear personal protective gear.

2. Unscrew and remove oil pressure switch for reduced oil pressure -4- .

![](images/30430348960daab56f19337c77c80232a0befe9e394be7202244a5d6b8991018.webp)  
Fig 1: Locating Oil Pressure Switch

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Screw in oil pressure tester oil pressure tester WE 1068 instead of the oil pressure switch -4-.

1.3.1. Screw oil pressure switch for reduced oil pressure into the oil pressure tester.   
2. 3.2. Connect plug connection for oil pressure switch again.

4. Start the engine and read of the oil pressure.

1. Oil pressure at idle speed: 1.2 to 2.1 bar   
2. Oil pressure at 2, 000 RPM: 1.6 to 2.1 bar (3.0 to 4.0 bar possible during the intake phase).   
3. Oil pressure at 3, 700 RPM: 3.0 to 4.0 bar

2. Install il pressure switch for reduced oil pressure.

### WM 170301 CHECKING OIL PRESSURE (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CHECKING OIL PRESSURE

WARNING: Toxic substances

• Danger of poisoning or suffocation

Danger of burns to the eyes and skin

→ Ventilate the work area well

→ Never ingest or inhale.

→ Read specific information on the Hazard Sheet.

→ Do not smoke, eat or drink in the work area.

• Danger of scalding

→ Let the fluid cool down.   
→ Wear personal protective gear.

WARNING: Highly inflammable or explosive materials

Danger of fire or explosion

→ Avoid contact with hot parts or sources of ignition.   
→ Use suction to remove ignitable vapors.   
→ Attach warning sign in a clearly visible position.


### The oil pressure may be too low for a number of reasons:

Oil is diluted (e.g. fuel gets into the oil due to too many cold starts without warming up the engine afterwards).   
Oil pump is faulty.   
•Too much bearing clearance (e.g. crankshaft bearing).   
• Oil level is too low.   
Oil pressure regulating valve is faulty.   
Oil pressure sensor is faulty.   
Incorrect oil has been used. Use only oil that has been approved by Porsche for the measurement.


### The oil pressure may be too high for a number of reasons:

•Oil has thickened or is very cold after a cold start and high engine speeds.   
Oil pump is faulty.   
Mechanical oil pump pressure relief valve is faulty (oil pump needs to be replaced).   
• Oil pressure regulating valve is faulty.   
Cable plug of oil pressure regulating valve has fallen off or open circuit between it and the control unit (oil pressure may be up to 11 bar, engine loses approximately 10 kW of engine power) • Oil pressure sensor is faulty.   
Incorrect oil has been used. Use only oil that has been approved by Porsche for the

1. Unscrew screw plug at the measuring point -5- . When doing so, make sure that the sealing ring -6- does not fall off.

1. 1.1. Soak up emerging engine oil with a cloth.

Fig 1: Identifying Oil Pressure Sensor And Oil Pressure Measuring Point

![](images/f718955f3db703b18b2bff8401f402ac8d4c5853cb23c9b3e6c1a92812f7016b.webp)  
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Screw adapter for oil-pressure gauge -1- with sealing ring -2- into the measuring point. Carefully tighten to max. 10 Nm (7.5 ftlb.).

![](images/6faa9c2c181a6b4607db7f4b825003d03d91601c628c20fe1fded5b77cbf9257.webp)  
Fig 2: Placing Adapter In Measuring Point

![](images/33f28848ff9476630b3aa78aeed10bff68719019f43da1cddc6cc701a320ad8f.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Adapter Setup

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Screw oil-pressure gauge -3- onto the adapter -2- . Counter screw torque using an open-ended wrench -1- .

![](images/4ad2a7802aae500adafd3b9550205947540176a8790fc1285c0c6a40771506ce.webp)  
Fig 4: Installing Oil-Pressure Gauge On Adapter

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Secure oil-pressure gauge.

1.4.1. Secure oil-pressure gauge to the oil filter or coolant line using tie-wraps/wire.

2.4.2. Make sure that the oil-pressure gauge and hose are not touching any rotating components.

5. Complete the engine for taking measurements.

6. Check that there are no rotating components touching the measuring hose and that the pressure gauge is easy to read when positioned.

7. Connect the PIWIS Tester and battery charger.

1. Use the PIWiS Tester to display the actual values for oil pressure, engine temperature and engine speed in DME. The oil pressure displayed in the PIWIS Tester is always higher than that on the pressure gauge by the value of the ambient pressure (depending on the altitude, e.g. 1, 000 hPa).

2. The pressure display on the oil-pressure gauge must be the same as the value on the PIWIS Tester once adjusted by the ambient pressure value.

3. The pressure display on the oil-pressure gauge is much slower than that on the PIWIS Tester. The measured value on the PIWis Tester fluctuates rapidly. The trend between

the two measuring instruments is significant.

4. The measured oil pressure remains virtually constant over different rev ranges. The measurement using the oil-pressure gauge merely confirms that the oil pressure sensor's display is correct. 5. The pressure readings can be shown graphically in the data logger.

8Start the engine and leave it running until t reaches the measurement temperature. → Engine temperature: 90°C

Measured values (examples)

1. For a cold start (e.g. 24 °C), pressure immediately jumps to 8 bar briefly (oil-pressure gauge).   
2. Following a cold start, oil pressure drops briefly to 3 bar (oil-pressure gauge) - 4, 000 hPa (PIWIS Tester).   
3. During warm-up phase at idle speed, pressure drops from 3 bar to 1.8 bar (oil-pressure gauge) - 4, 000 hPa drops to 2, 800 hPa (PIWiS Tester).   
4. At engine temperature of 90 C at idle speed, pressure is 1.5 to 1.6 bar (oil-pressure gauge) - 2, 600 hPa (PIWIS Tester).   
5. At engine temperature of 90 °C at 1, 000 RPM, pressure is 2.8 bar (oil-pressure gauge) - 3, 800 hPa (PIWIS Tester).   
6. At engine temperature of 90 °C at between 2, 000 RPM and 4, 000 RPM, the oil pressure is almost constant at 3.0 bar (oil-pressure gauge) - 4, 000 hPa (PIWIS Tester). The value can fluctuate by 0.1 bar (100 hPa).

### WM 190101 CHECKING THE COOLING SYSTEM (MACAN) > CHECKING ENGINE COOLANT LEVEL

Engine cold.

•Vehicle horizontal.

1. Check coolant level at the reservoir.

1. 1.1. The ideal level must be between the -MAX- marking -1- and -MIN- marking -2- .

2. 1.2. If the level is under -MIN-, the level must be corrected.

3. 1.3. If the level is above -MAX-, some coolant must be extracted.

![](images/0260230e948d54a1521afcfbf8518fa011aaaf3c1b758da0dff9e795884ca279.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Coolant Reservoir


### WM 190101 CHECKING THE COOLING SYSTEM (MACAN) > CHECKING ENGINE COOLANT LEVEL > CHECKING ANTIFREEZE IN COOLANT

1. Check antifreeze content.

1. 1.1. Check antifreeze content using antifreeze tester -1- .

2.1.2. If it is below -35 °C, correct the antifreeze content by increasing the proportion

of pure coolant accordingly.

![](images/fb77036a5acf4db422a96f7bc6ba078acd1fdf0368196f6f28fe040ce2cc5659.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Antifreeze Tester

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Close the maintenance flap.

![](images/7907aae3ac64988d4c8a8adad78455868ca78f3d886ba80fbbc625e25907186f.webp)


### WM 190101 CHECKING THE COOLING SYSTEM (MACAN) > CHECKING ENGINE COOLANT LEVEL > CHECKING THE COOLING SYSTEM FOR LEAKS

1. Check the engine coolant level. Top up to the maximum fill level if necessary. → CHECKING ENGINE COOLANT LEVEL .

2. Screw adapter K65 onto the coolant expansion tank. Then apply a test pressure of approx. 1.5 bar using the cooling system test device and check the hose connections, connection pieces, cooling system components for leaks. The pressure must not drop. There must be no drops of coolant.


### WM 190101 CHECKING THE COOLING SYSTEM (MACAN) > CHECKING ENGINE COOLANT LEVEL > CHECKING COOLING SYSTEM FOR DIRT

1. Check radiator for external dirt. The radiators should not be excessively dirty. They can be cleaned using a vacuum cleaner with a brush attachment if necessary.

2. Check charge air coolers for external dirt. The charge air coolers should not be excessively dirty. They can be cleaned using a vacuum cleaner with a brush attachment if necessary.

3. Check air guides to the radiators for external dirt and collected leaves. They can be cleaned using a vacuum cleaner with a brush attachment if necessary.

WARNING: Hot fluid

Danger of scalding → Avoid contact with hot fluid.

→ Wear personal protective gear.

NOTE: Cooling circuit not filled correctly

Risk of damage to vehicle components — Do not start the engine after relieving the system pressure.

→ Fill he cooling system correctly and bleed it before starting the engine.


### V1 and V2 are at a 90° angle to the flow direction

5.2.5. Connect the Venturi nozle to the vacuum gauge.

7. 2.7. Route the return line -1- from the Venturi nozzle to a second container -2- .

8.2.8. Connect the compressed air supply -4- to the filler hose -3- .

9. 2.9. Build up overpressure of 6 to 10 bar.

![](images/c7879613c06345dbdd874e8a154deba63064e5322f2f16eeb1fbb23468a82b98.webp)  
Fig 4: Locating Shut-Off Valve On Filler Hose

Then remove the complete filing tool (including the adapter K65).

Fig 10: Locating Front Bleeder Screw

21

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

15. For vehicles with an auxiliary heater, switch this on and allow it to run for approx. 30 seconds.

Fig 13: Locating Heater Control In Passenger Compartment

19. Press the "Sport button". Leave "Sport" mode activated during the bleeding process.

20. Check the following while the vehicle is warming up.

1. 20.1. Coolant temperature -2- and engine oil temperature -1- in the instrument cluster. Figure shows normal, acceptable values.

21. The cooling system has been filled and bled correctly if:

1. All coolant hoses are uniformly warm.   
2. The temperature display in the instrument cluster is in the normal range.

3. The passenger compartment heater is warm.

4. The electric fan for engine cooling comes on.

22. Correct level:

1. When the engine is cold, the coolant level must be up to the -MAX- marking.

2. When the engine is at operating temperature, the engine coolant level may be above the -MAX- marking.

WARNING: ATF!

Possible danger of injury or damage (swollen hoses, skin irritation, danger of slipping, etc.)

→ Before lines are opened, place a cloth underneath them!   
→ Components that come into contact with ATF must be cleaned IMMEDIATELY with water! → Take appropriate protective measures (e.g. use gloves, safety goggles, oil binding material) → Collect emerging ATF!

CAUTION: Hot components

Risk of burns

→ Let hot components cool down.

→ Wear personal protective gear.

1.Release ATF lines -1 and 2- at the top of the engine compartment -arrows- and disconnect them.

1. 1.1. Soak up emerging ATF with a cloth.

### 1. Step 2: Check the fuel system for leaks =>

1. 1.1 Read out the fuel high pressure actual value in the DME control unit using the PIWIS Tester.

1. Nominal pressure is approx. 5000 to 5500.0 hPa. Monitor the fuel pressure for about 5 to 10 minutes.

2. The pressure is not maintained. In other words: the fuel high-pressure actual value has dropped considerably. There is an internal or external leak in the fuel system.

3. The pressure is maintained. In other words: the fuel high-pressure

actual value has only dropped slightly.
