WARNING: Toxic substances

Danger of poisoning or suffocation   
•Danger of burns to the eyes and skin   
oVentilate the work area well.   
Never ingest or inhale.   
oRead specific information on the Hazard Sheet. oDo not smoke, eat or drink in the work area.


### WARNING: Highly inflammable or explosive materials

Danger of fire or explosion oAvoid contact with hot parts or sources of ignition. Use suction to remove ignitable vapours. Attach warning sign in a clearly visible position.

1. Remove engine compartment trim panel at the front right. → REMOVING FRONT TRIM PANEL .Disconnect fuel low-pressure line -2- at the front left of the wheel housing.

1.2.1 Loosen clamp -1- and pull off line -2- .

2.2.2 Collect escaping fuel.

![](images/f5eb1891600f8bba3c448a9819ed7257a5d344ba4cc2e544f2475e9a4c301dba.webp)  
Fig 1: Fuel Supply Line

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.


### 3. Check fuel supply pressure (low-pressure) =>

1. 3.1 Connect test equipment and secure connections with a clamp -1- or screw-type clamp -2- .

2. 3.2 The tool setup must be fitted with sealing rings (copper, aluminium, or plastic, etc.) between the individual components. The setup must be full sealed.

3. 3.3. Start the engine and leave it running at idle speed. Read off the fuel pressure on the pressure gauge. The pressure gauge pointer can oscillate slightly at idle speed. With increased idle speed (accelerator pressed slightly), the pointer deflection calms down. The fuel low-pressure system operates at a fuel pressure of 5.5 to 5.8 bar . The pointer oscillates at around this value. Measurements under load can even generate values of below 5 bar (4.5 bar) briefly. This is not a sign of a defect.

![](images/f54690c6390dfa55d35b1839dff835c39b94e2f4fc3c23cfeddf023c82009052.webp)  
Fig 2: Connection For Measuring Pressure On The Vehicle

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.


### 4. Check fuel retaining pressure (low-pressure) =>

1. Engine cold

2. Workshop air-conditioned to normal temperature

3. Fluctuations may occur if the engine is warm or if the outside temperature is high

4. Fully sealed measuring tool setup

1. 6.1 Same tool setup and connection as for measuring the fuel delivery pressure (see above).

2.6.2. Allow engine to run for a few minutes. Switch off engine. Check the pressure drop. Drop in fuel pressure after "ignition is switched of" must not exceed 1 bar after 1 hour . Make sure that the tool setup itself does not have any leaks (even the slightest leak). The fuel retaining pressure will decrease extremely rapidly and falsify the measured result with even the tiniest leak.

### WM 2015K2 CALIBRATING FUEL LEVEL SENDER (ALL MODELS) > CALIBRATING FUEL LEVEL SENDER > CALIBRATING FUEL LEVEL SENDER

1. Empty the fuel tank. → Emptying The Fuel Tank

2. Wait for a short time (approx. 1 minute) to allow the fuel-level sensor to settle at the current level.   
3. Connect the Porsche System Tester to the vehicle and start the System Tester. Switch on ignition. [>>] to continue.   
4. Select the vehicle type.   
5. Select Instrument cluster control unit, then press [>].   
6. Select the Maintenance/repairs menu and press [>>].   
7. Select Fuel tank calibration menu and press [F8] to start the calibration process.   
8. The message Fuel tank calibration completed successfully appears on the Tester screen.   
9. Press [F12] to exit.   
10. Fil the vehicle with fuel and check the fuel gauge in the instrument cluster. Wait a few minutes. Fuel gauge shows full.   
11. Change terminals.

1.11.1. Switch off ignition.   
2. 11.2. Wait approx. 30 seconds.   
3.11.3. Switch on ignition.

12. Check the fuel gauge in the instrument cluster again. Fuel gauge shows full.

### Procedure for charging exhaustively discharged batteries:

Batteries that have not been used for a long time discharge automatically

A battery is exhaustively discharged if the open-circuit voltage has dropped below 11.6 V, see OPEN-CIRCUIT VOLTAGE MEASUREMENT

In exhaustively discharged batteries, the battery acid (sulfuric acid and water mixture) consists of virtually only water, as the sulfuric acid proportion is considerably reduced.

Exhaustively discharged batteries sulphatise, i.e. the entire plate surfaces of the batteries harden.

If exhaustively discharged batteries are immediately recharged after an exhaustive discharge, the sulphatisation recedes again.

If these batteries are not recharged, the plates continue to harden and charge take-up ability is limited. This results in reduced battery performance.

Exhaustively discharged batteries must be charged using a low charge current as follows:

1. Set the charge current to maximum 10% of battery capacity, i.e. with a 95 AH battery, the charge current is max. 9.5 A.

Charge the battery.

![](images/84deb0cfbdb39245349d1898ca41b3d66892f29c2e728d57461667d50d7dfa49.webp)


### WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK > PREPARATION FOR ADJUSTING DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR

1. Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least 40 A to the external power feed points.

2. Read out the fault memory using Piwis Tester Il 9818 , create a vehicle analysis log if necessary → OXO3IN CREATING VEHICLE ANALYSIS LOG (VAL) and correct any faults.

3. Remove trim cover -1- from the distance measuring sensor control unit.

1.3.1. Push trim cover up -a-.

2. 3.2. Pull trim cover forward and remove it -b- .

![](images/38f5b8076ee312cca0e42229ec858e4e86b47784d293381621f14d4bdab535cc.webp)  
Fig 1: Removing Trim Cover   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Clean distance measuring sensor control unit and trim cover using commercially available cleaning agent.   
5. Fit the front sensors onto the adjustment device, align using the spirit levels and clamp using the wing screws, and switch them on (initialize).   
6. Set the distance between the adjustment device with reflector VAS 6430/1 WE 1362 and the vehicle in accordance with the specifications provided by the measuring equipment manufacturer.   
1. 6.1. The distance between the left sensor and the vehicle -Bl- should be identical to the distance between the right spirit level and the vehicle -Br- .

![](images/0474b77f1ba52729b15c67f96e9269fb69fc293ca7ee7b34d7b2b26bac2d2f95.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Right Sensor Dimension   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. On the adjustment device, move the mirror into the position -2- in alignment with the marking (-A- the number 2 on the rotary knob must point towards the vehicle).

![](images/01318cf91e19b2090f902786b3b9c08bfc7055b887181bf8278dd2aa27a1506b.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Adjustment Device Position   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.


### WM 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR

1. Connect PiWis Tester Il 9818 to the vehicle and start it.

2. Switch on ignition.   
3. Select the required vehicle and the Adaptive cruise control control unit. Press [F12] to continue.   
4. Select the Maintenance/repairs sub-menu in the Adaptive cruise control menu. Press [F12] to continue.   
5. Follow the instructions on Piwis Tester Il 9818 and adjust the distance measuring sensor control unit -1- as required using adjustment tool T-socket wrench for ACC sensor VAS 6190/2 WE 1364 -2- by turning the relevant adjusting screw -3- according to specifications.

![](images/4908f3306ca8f692d9c24224c1afe82b2dc6be653a66a3472f75a71865407167.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Sensor Control Unit Adjusting Screws

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

6. Repeat the process until PIWIS Tester II 9818 displays the message Adjustment successful.


### WM 278519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > TECHNICAL VALUES

![](images/d06c4e7f273502621e9b969472e0ebb97cc70bc2e5531d279331f576704708a1.webp)


### WM 278519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Remove front apron. → Removing Front Apron

WM 278519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR

NOTE: Voltage peaks

Risk of damage to load or to the control unit

→ Remove the ignition key and switch off load before disconnecting or removing load.

1. Switch off ignition and pull remote control out of the ignition lock.   
2. Disengage trim cover -1- at the left and right of the holder -2- for the distance measuring sensor control unit -3- and remove it.

![](images/b32e4823aac78be72831b14d81f9dddc0fd6d3320588c7fa02683857fe8f8c0c.webp)  
Fig 1: Removing Distance Measuring Sensor Control Unit Cover

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.


### WM 278519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > INSTALLING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR

Information

3efore and after fitting the trim cover for the distance measuring sensor control unit, check the following ooints:

The holder for the distance measuring sensor control unit must not show any signs of deformation, which may have been caused, for example, by removing or installing the trim cover for the distance measuring sensor control unit. If the holder for the distance measuring sensor control unit is deformed, carefull push it back into shape.   
If the trim cover is damaged or cracked, replace the trim cover.   
After fitting the trim cover, check that it is seated correctly and securely. 1. Installation is performed in reverse order to removal. 2. Tighten fastening screw at the bottom of the holder for the distance measuring sensor control unit. Tightening torque 2.5 Nm (2 ftlb.) 3. Tighten fastening screw at the top of the holder for the distance measuring sensor control unit. Tightening torque 8 Nm (6 ftlb.)


### WM 278519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. The distance measuring sensor control unit must be adjusted whenever it is removed and installed. → 278515 ADJUSTING CONTROL UNIT FOR DISTANCE MEASURING SENSOR

### WM 282020 REMOVING AND INSTALLING IGNITION COILS (MACAN) > REMOVING IGNITION COILS

1.1.1. Tightening torque for ignition coil,


### Tightening torque: 10 Nm (7.5 ftlb.)

2.1.2. Tightening torque for nut securing ground cable, Tightening torque: 10 Nm (7.5 ftlb.) Replace nut.

### WM 822019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COMPLETE HEATER (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEATER > REMOVING HEATER

NOTE: Danger of scalding

•Coolant can be very hot.   
•Coolant may be pressurized. → Only remove the heater when the cooling system has cooled down.   
→ By carefully opening the catch on the reservoir, make sure that the cooling system is depressurized.

NOTE: Danger of slipping due to emerging coolant

The emerging coolant will make the floor of the workshop slippery and may cause people to slip and fall over.

→ Collect emerging coolant in a suitable pan.

1. Remove coolant hoses.

1. 1.1. Clamp coolant hoses -1- using hose clamp 3094 -3- .

2. 1.2. Loosen spring band clamps -2- using assembly pliers Nr.72 Pos.1 and pull off coolant hoses -1- .

WARNING: Emerging fuel

1. Risk of fire

Fig 1: Identifying Coolant Hoses

![](images/0f2cb8ed4ca26ca2112d7c230afbe99e369e5e12b4cbc35b01bfb6806e10fc3b.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

→ Avoid contact with hot parts or sources of ignition.   
→ Collect emerging fuel, absorb it if necessary with a suitable binding material and dispose of properly.   
→ Use suction to remove ignitable vapors.   
— Attach warning sign to vehicle in a clearly visible position.

2. Disconnect fuel line.

1. 2.1. Loosen spring band clamp -3- using assembly pliers Nr.72 Pos.1  and disconnect fuel line -2- .

Fig 2: Locating Fuel Line In Wheel Housing

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Disconnect exhaust pipe from silencer.

1.3.1. Loosen screw-type clamp -1- .

2.3.2. Pull flexi-pipe -2- off the silencer pipe -3- .

![](images/c730297294ecddfbed393ba944d8180b052810f142f105fd10a2101cdd2f2699.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Exhaust Pipe On Silencer

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

NOTE: Danger of scalding

•Coolant can be very hot.   
Coolant may be pressurized.

→ Only remove the heater when the cooling system has cooled down.

→ By carefully opening the catch on the reservoir, make sure that the cooling system is depressurized.

1. Release electric plug connection -1- from the circulating pump -2- and disconnect it.

2 1 л

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Clamp both coolant hoses -2- and -4- using hose clamp 3094. → Mounting for coolant hoses on circulating pump

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

NOTE: Danger of slipping due to emerging coolant

1. The emerging coolant will make the floor of the workshop slippery and may cause people to slip and fall over.

— Collect emerging coolant in a suitable pan.

3. Loosen spring band clamps -1- and -3- using assembly pliers Nr.72 Pos.1 and pull off coolant hoses -2- and -4- .

4. Unscrew fastening screws -1- and remove circulating pump -2- .

![](images/42e5fdce98a3ec33e83085ba6791051b97d42f396774c274e5a6c47429870f92.webp)

2. Secure coolant hoses.

1.2.1. Push coolant hoses -2- and -4- as far as they will go over the adapters. Tighten spring band clamps -1- and -3- using assembly pliers Nr.72 Pos.1.

![](images/ba145383dd0b6e64465f057acd8961e604c00f48215261a71fa70ddec815149e.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Coolant Hoses On Circulating Pump

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. 2.2. Hose clamp 3094 must then be removed from the coolant hoses -2- and -4- .

3. Connect electric plug connection -1- to the circulating pump -2- until it engages securely.

### CALIFORNIA > LEGEND

ESC - Emission Standard Category

GVWR - Manufacture's Gross Vehicle Weight Rating

LVW - Loaded Vehicle Weight

PC - Passenger Car

LDT1 - Light-Duty Truck up through 3750 LVW and GVWR no greater than 6000 Ibs.

LDT2 - Light-Duty Truck greater than 3750 LVW and GVWR no greater than 6000 Ibs.

MDV - Medium-Duty Vehicle, GVWR from 6001 to 8500 Ibs.

HC - Hydrocarbon, ppm

CO - Carbon Monoxide, %

NO - Nitric Oxide, ppm


### CALIFORNIA > PASS/FAIL EMISSION STANDARDS = A+B / VTW

PASS/FAIL STANDARDS - Emission standards used to determine if a vehicle passes the emission inspection. A vehicle passes if the emission levels are equal to or less than the standards for HC, CO and NO for ASM 5015 and ASM 2525.

GROSS POLLUTER STANDARDS - Emission standards used to designate a vehicle as a gross polluter A vehicle is designated as a gross polluter if the emission levels at the time of the initial inspection, before repairs are greater than the gross poluter standards for HC, CO or NO for ASM 5015 or ASM 2525.

NOTE: If test data on emission pass/fail rates or gross polluter identification rates indicate adjustments are required, the emission standards may be increased or decreased by the bureau by 30% or by the following tolerances, or standards may be set for any specific vehicle and engine configuration which the bureau determines has excessive errors of commission of omission, whichever is necessary to comply with Section 44001.5 of the Health and Safety Code.

### U. S. EPA REVISED FINAL ASM EMISSION STANDARDS (ASM5015 & ASM2525)

NOTE: EPA has not published a revised final standards for High Altitude, Light Duty Trucks 2 (6000-8500 GVWR), or vehicles older than 1980 model year. EPA guidance as of February 2003 states that a program may choose to use combinations of the Original and the Revised Final Standards.


### U.S. EPA REVISED FINAL ASM EMISSION STANDARDS

![](images/4949e1a2affc04605d041d3ee0d63872352dd7e1afc6a337a667fd588cdac139.webp)


### U.S. EPA IM240 EMISSION STANDARDS > START-UP STANDARDS

Start-up standards should be used during the first 2 years of program operation. Tier 1 standards are recommended for all 1996 and newer vehicles and may be used for 1994 and newer vehicles certified to Tier 1 standards as well.

### Service Manual: 80 - HEATING - (95B) - MACAN WM 803019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEAT EXCHANGER SUPPLY HOSE (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Drain refrigerant —→ 870317 DRAINING AND FILLING REFRIGERANT .   
2. Remove cowI panel cover — 508719 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COWL PANEL COVER .


### WM 803019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEAT EXCHANGER SUPPLY HOSE(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Install cowI panel cover → INSTALLING COWL PANEL COVER .   
2. Fil i refrigerant → DRAINING AND FILLING REFRIGERANT .


### WM 803219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEAT EXCHANGER RETURN HOSE(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Drain refrigerant → 870317 DRAINING AND FILLING REFRIGERANT .   
2. Remove cowI panel cover — 508719 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COWL PANEL COVER .


### If auxiliary heating system is installed:

1. Loosen spring band clamps -1- (-arrows-) .

2. Pull hose -2- off the heat exchanger return connection piece and directional-control valve connection piece.

![](images/e9aade415f3fe9bbaa96855ef4973ee2183aec8ceea18a455279df3193bd7e52.webp)  
Fig 1: Removing Heat Exchanger Return Hose

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.


### If auxiliary heating system is not installed:

3. Disconnect spring band clamp -1- on heat exchanger return connection piece -arrow- .

![](images/9c8db2ab175964a3bf816b8b13c7cb31bfa7584cb89acc7c48c33e6716575d35.webp)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. Loosen spring band clamp -1- on the auxiliary pump connection piece -arrow- .

![](images/dc74705a987ff1811a2c8314f146b36ec67449816d5081ba168a4dfd13c35f9a.webp)  
Fig 3: Loosening Spring Band Clamp On Auxiliary Pump Connection

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Pull heat exchanger return hose -2- through the grommet in the plenum panel wall and remove it.


### WM 803219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING HEAT EXCHANGER RETURN HOSE(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Install cowI panel cover → 508719 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COWL PANEL COVER .   
2. Fil in refrigerant → DRAINING AND FILLING REFRIGERANT .


### WM 805519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT FOOTWELL OUTLET VENTS(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Applies to left footwell outlet vent:

Remove trim panel under dashboard at the left → 70191901 REMOVING AND INSTALLING TRIM PANEL UNDER DASHBOARD AT THE LEFT .


### Applies to right footwell outlet vent:

Remove glove compartment → 681519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING GLOVE COMPARTMENT .


### WM 805519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT FOOTWELL OUTLET VENTS(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT LEFTFOOTWELL OUTLET VENTS > REMOVING FRONT LEFT FOOTWELL OUTLET VENT

1. Release and disconnect connector -1- for the temperature sensor.   
2. Unscrew fastening screw -2- .   
3. Guide footwell outlet vent out to the left -arrow- .

![](images/b6a8f936e87c43583bcba1421faaab3a7d094e330674625496f39329be921305.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Front Left Footwell Outlet Vent Temperature Sensor

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. If the footwell outlet vent will be replaced, the temperature sensor must be converted beforehand. → Temperature sensor

![](images/93bcb46a46a9e6114a73731927ebbeef194b6270e8e04d453903e591f08d1b91.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Temperature Sensor


### WM 805519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT FOOTWELL OUTLET VENTS(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT RIGHTFOOTWELL OUTLET VENTS > REMOVING FOOTWELL OUTLET VENT AT THEFRONT RIGHT

1. Release and disconnect connector -1- for the temperature sensor.   
2. Unscrew fastening screw -2- .   
.Guide footweloutlet vent out to the right -arrow-.

![](images/602eacd5a3fd16b270a2720636e92e5208721669ba0957e8f3f2dd6a76c4d6b1.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Front Right Footwell Outlet Vent Temperature Sensor

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

4. If the footwell outlet vent will be replaced, the temperature sensor must be converted beforehand. → Temperature sensor

![](images/23da0f92c2417d1e0f71c4d60d80144fe1721c0c4d1c6eb56d2ad09540f7d775.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Temperature Sensor


### WM 805519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT FOOTWELL OUTLET VENTS(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT RIGHTFOOTWELL OUTLET VENTS > INSTALLING FOOTWELL OUTLET VENT AT THEFRONT RIGHT

1. Installtion is performed in reverse order. Observe specified tightening torques: Left footwell outlet vent to body: Right footwell outlet vent to air conditioner:

WM 805519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT FOOTWELL OUTLET VENTS(MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > SUBSEQUENT WORK


### 1. Applies to left footwell outlet vent:

Install rim panel under dashboard at the left → INSTALLING TRIM PANEL UNDER DASHBOARD AT THE LEFT .


### Applies to right footwell outlet vent:

Install glove compartment → INSTALLING GLOVE COMPARTMENT .

### WM 8209AN TEACHING REMOTE CONTROL FOR AUXILIARY HEATING (ALL MODELS) > SWITCHING AUXILIARY HEATING ON AND OFF WITH REMOTE CONTROL > SWITCHING ON AUXILIARY HEATING WITH REMOTE CONTROL

1. [ON] button -1- must be pressed for approx. 2 seconds. The LED -2- flashes green and goes out once the auxiliary heater is started completely.

1. ON button

### MODELS) > SWITCHING AUXILIARY HEATING ON AND OFF WITH REMOTE CONTROL > SWITCHING OFF AUXILIARY HEATING WITH REMOTE CONTROL

1. [OFF] button -3- must be pressed for approx. 2 seconds. The LED -2- flashes red and goes out once the auxiliary heater is shut down completely.

NOTE: Danger of scalding

•Coolant can be very hot.   
•Coolant may be pressurized. → Only remove the heater when the cooling system has cooled down.   
→ By carefully opening the catch on the reservoir, make sure that the cooling system is depressurized.

NOTE: Danger of slipping due to emerging coolant

The emerging coolant will make the floor of the workshop slippery and may cause people to slip and fall over.

→ Collect emerging coolant in a suitable pan.

→ Collect emerging fuel, absorb it if necessary with a suitable binding material and dispose of properly.

### WM 870317 DRAINING AND FILLING REFRIGERANT (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > DRAINING AND FILLING REFRIGERANT > GENERAL INSTALLATION SEQUENCE

The charging valves are located in the plenum panel at the rear left.

1. Screw off the protection caps on the charging valves. Be careful of the sealing rings when disconnecting or connecting the hose connections! Before connecting the high-pressure and low-pressure lines for the air conditioner to the vehicle, remove any refrigerant remaining in the lines by suction. 2. Connect the high-pressure and low-pressure lines on the air conditioner.


### The desiccator must be replaced in the following situations:

1. Refrigerant circuit is open for > 20 minutes.

Amount of refrigerant extracted is < 30% of the required quantity.

3. Refrigerant circuit has been open for an indefinite period of time (gradual leak, stone damage to condenser).

4. Air-conditioning compressor has become blocked.

5. Dryer cartridge is damaged.

6. After opening the packaging and line connections (on a new desiccator), the desiccator must be installed within 20 minutes at the latest and the refrigerant circuit must be closed, evacuated and filled.


### The desiccator must not be replaced in the following situations:

1. If the components are closed off using stoppers immediately after opening the refrigerant circuit and the refrigerant circuit is closed and evacuated within 20 minutes at the latest.

1.4.1. Before closing off the refrigerant circuit, check whether the desiccator needs to be replaced.

2.4.2. If necessary, reconnect high-pressure and low-pressure lines.

5. Evacuate the system and check for leaks.

1. 5.1. If the air-conditioning system has been opened, evacuation should last at least 20 minutes so that the moisture can evaporate and be removed by suction.

2. 5.2. If the air-conditioning system has been open for a long time, evacuation can be carried out for up to 120 minutes.

3. 5.3. Check the pressure gauge for approx. 2 minutes. If the pressure rises, air is entering the vehicle's air-conditioning system. The leak must be located and repaired.

If the pressure remains constant, add refrigerant oil.


### 3.8.3.

9. Add refrigerant from both connection hoses to the air-conditioning system in the vehicle.

1.9.1. The refrigerant in the high-pressure and low-pressure lines is part of the filing capacity of the refrigerant in the air-conditioning system in the vehicle.

2.9.2. Close the valve on the high-pressure line and disconnect it from the vehicle.

3.9.3. Start the engine and air-conditioning system. When the pressure on both pressure gauges falls below 2 bar, close the valve on the low-pressure line and disconnect it from the vehicle.

Risk of damage to components.

### WM 873419 REMOVING AND INSTALLING AIR-CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING AIR-CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR > WORK STEPS FOR BLOCKED/SEIZED UP AIR-CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR

1. Remove desiccator from the condenser. → REMOVING AND INSTALLING DESICCATOR .   
2. Check the desiccator for wear/chips.

If there are signs of wear/chips:

3. Remove the refrigerant line between the compressor and condenser. → 874319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COMPRESSOR/CONDENSER LINE .

4. Replace the refrigerant line between the compressor and condenser.

5. Replace the condenser with desiccator. → 875019 REMOVING AND INSTALLING CONDENSER .

6. Instal the new refrigerant line between the compressor and condenser. → INSTALLING COMPRESSOR/CONDENSER LINE .

7. Install air-conditioning compressor → 873419 REMOVING AND INSTALLING AIR-CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR .


### If there are no signs of wear/chips:

1. Replace the desiccator. → REMOVING AND INSTALLING DESICCATOR .

WM 873419 REMOVING AND INSTALLING AIR-CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING AIR-CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR > INSTALLING AIR-CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR

1. Installation is performed in reverse order.

Observe specified tightening torques:   
Air-conditioning compressor to engine: Tightening torque 25 Nm (19 ftlb.)   
Air-conditioning lines to air-conditioning compressor: Tightening torque 20 Nm (15 ftlb.)   
Air-conditioning line holder to engine: Tightening torque 9 Nm (6.5 ftlb.)   
Strut to lock carrier: Tightening torque 5 Nm (3.5 ftlb.)   
Strut to front-axle carrier: Tightening torque 23 Nm (17 ftb.)

### SYSTEMS

WARNING: Improper handling of the filing system for the air conditioning.

•Unnecessary damage to the environment due to emerging refrigerant.

→ Before connecting the filing system to the air-conditioning, make sure that the manual shut-off valves are closed.

→ Before disconnecting the filing system from the air-conditioning, make sure that the process is complete so that no refrigerant can escape into the atmosphere.

→ After the purified refrigerant has been filled into an external compressed gas botle from the filing system, the manual shut-off valves on the bottle and on the filling system should be closed.

→ Do not expose the filling system to moisture or use in a damp environment.

— Shut off the power supply at the filling system before carrying out maintenance work.

→ An extension cable with cross-sectional area of at least 2.5 mm 2 should be used only when absolutely necessary.

→ In the case of fire, the external bottle should be removed.

→ Fil the oil extracted from the air-conditioning system into a suitable closable container (the refrigerant oil contains small quantities of refrigerant).

→ The filig system must be secured to prevent rolling.


### WM 8XOOIN SAFETY REGULATIONS FOR WORKING ON AIR-CONDITIONED VEHICLES AND HANDLING REFRIGERANT R134A (ALL MODELS) > GENERAL SAFETY REGULATIONS FOR REFRIGERANTS

CAUTION: Extreme heating of air-conditioning system e.g. from sunlight shining into the vehicle or as a result of welding and soldering work.

Danger of fire due to excessive heating of air conditioning.

Danger of environmental pollution due to emerging refrigerant.

→ When carrying out repairs on the air-conditioning system, the system must be emptied by suction and the refrigerant must be purified. Chlorine-free refrigerants must also not be allowed to escape into the atmosphere and must be disposed of correctly.

→ Due to their chemical composition, different refrigerants must not be mixed with each other! This also applies for smaller quantities.

→ No welding, soldering or hot-air heating may take place on parts of the filed air-conditioning system or

in its immediate vicinity.

→ While drying after painting work, the temperature burden on the vehicle must not exceed two hours at a maximum temperature of 80°C.

→ Whether or not the system is filled with refrigerant, the heating causes a very strong overpressure which can cause damage to the system or even lead to an explosion.

→ R 134a is completely non-toxic at normal temperatures, but it decomposes upon contact with a flame or at high temperatures.

→ Refrigerant bottles must not be thrown and must not be subjected to direct sunlight or other heat sources for an extended period when full.

→ The maximum permissible temperature of a filled refrigerant bottle must not exceed 45 °C.

→ Risk of injury! High temperatures from open flames or hot solids causes chemical breakdown of refrigerant gas. Inhalation of the resulting breakdown products leads to coughing and nausea.

WARNING: Caustic fluids

• Danger of chemical burns

→ Avoid contact with caustic fluid.

→ Wear personal protective gear.

→ Ensure that there is good ventilation.

→ If you do come into contact, wash off immediately with plenty of warm water and contact a doctor if necessary.

WARNING: Refrigerant

Danger of freezing

→ Avoid contact with refrigerant.

→ Wear personal protective gear.

→ Observe the safety regulations for working on air-conditioned vehicles and dealing with refrigerant.

→ Observe the safety regulations for extraction and filing systems.

→ Observe the instructions for repairing air conditioning systems and storing spare parts.


### WM 8XOOIN SAFETY REGULATIONS FOR WORKING ON AIR-CONDITIONED VEHICLES AND HANDLING REFRIGERANT R134A (ALL MODELS) > WORKING ON THE REFRIGERANT CIRCUIT

WARNING: Toxic substances

Danger of poisoning or suffocation •Danger of burns to the eyes and skin

→ Ventilate the work area well.   
→ Never ingest or inhale.   
→ Read specific information on the Hazard Sheet.   
→ Do not smoke, eat or drink in the work area.


### WORK ON VEHICLES WITH AIR CONDITIONING

WARNING: Painting work on vehicles with air-conditioning

Material damage due to the air-conditioning system bursting.

→ When carrying out repairs involving painting work, object temperatures in the drying oven or its preheating zone should not exceed 80 °C.


### WM 8XOOIN SAFETY REGULATIONS FOR WORKING ON AIR-CONDITIONED VEHICLES AND HANDLING REFRIGERANT R134A (ALL MODELS) > NOTES ON GENERAL REPAIRS

The refrigerant circuit of the air-conditioning system may only be emptied and opened if this is necessary in order to comply with safety measures or if components of the refrigerant circuit have to be replaced.

The air-conditioning refrigerant circuit also remains closed during all other standard vehicle repair work


### Contact corrosion!

For this reason, the manufacturer only fits connecting elements with a special surface coating.

Contact corrosion can occur if unsuitable connecting elements (screws, nuts, washers, rivets, plugs, adhesives, etc.) are used.

Only use original Porsche parts!

### EMISSIONS MAINTENANCE REMINDER > EMISSIONS MAINTENANCE REMINDER RESET - PROCEDURE 1

Oxygen sensor (O2S) light wil come on at 30,000 mile intervals as a reminder to replace sensor. After replacing sensor, reset warning light as follows:

1. On 911 models, disconnect battery ground cable and remove speedometer. Counter will be visible through speedometer mounting hole. Using a thick piece of wire or a thin rod, press White reset button all the way in against stop. Ensure warning light is out.   
2. On 924 models, after replacing oxygen sensor and with vehicle stillraised, locate mileage counter on left engine mount. Using a thick wire or thin metal rod, push in reset button all the way to stop. Ensure warning light is out.   
3. On 928 and 928S with ClS system, counter is located to right of passenger seat floor (near door sill. Remove counter cover retaining screw and cover. Press reset button all the way in against stop. Ensure warning light is out.

### MAINTENANCE SERVICE REMINDER > MAINTENANCE SERVICE REMINDER RESET - PROCEDURE 2

If the engine oil is replaced during maintenance work, the service interval must be reset.


### Standard Service Interval Reset:

1. In the PST2 (Porsche System Tester 2), select Instrument cluster, then press >.

2. Select the Coding menu, then press >>.

3. Select Reset Service Interval Display menu, then press >.

NOTE: Depending on the country, additional items are checked in the case of the V6 model. These items must be selected on a country-specific basis.

4. Select Reset menu and confirm with F8.

5. Quit menu, shut down PST and disconnect from vehicle.


### Maintenance Calculator Reset:

NOTE: All Cayenne V6 engines are factory filled with an engine oil of VW specification "50300". New vehicles produced have their maintenance calculator set for an oil change service interval of 10,000 miles (15,000 km) or 1 year. The maintenance calculator in the Cayenne (V6) determines the time of the engine oil change depending on the vehicle load and driving style, and requests for "Service" via the multi-function display.

After changing the oil, the oil change service interval must be reset in the instrument cluster using the PST2 (Porsche System Tester 2). The country version for which the new vehicle was produced is stored in the control modules. The PST2 automatically detects this country version before resetting the maintenance calculator and depending on this, offers the following options for oil change service intervals:

1. The country version of the vehicle corresponds to one of the countries listed in Table 1. Depending on the engine oil used for the oil change, the following selection options for oil change service intervals are available in the selection menu of the PST2 for these vehicles, when resetting the maintenance calculator with the PST2:

1. 1.1 If an engine oil in accordance with the VW specification "50300" was used: The oil change service interval is set in the maintenance calculator for an oil change service interval of up 30,000 km or 2 years, after selecting and confirming this oil quality in the PST2 menu => "Engine oil according to WW spec. "50300".

2. 1.2 If an engine oil not in accordance with the WW specification "50300" was used: The oil change service interval is set in the maintenance calculator for a fixed oil change service interval of 10,000 miles (15,000 km) or 1 year, after selecting and confirming this oil quality in the PST2 menu => "Engine oil with general Porsche approval".

. The country version of the vehicle "does not" correspond to one of the countries listed in Table 1. For vehicles having these country versions, all engine oils approved by Porsche may be used which are listed in this bulletin below and Cayenne Technical Information Bulletin, GROUP 1, NO. 4/04 . Even when an engine oil meeting the WW specification "50300" is used, the oil change service interval of 10,000 miles (15,000 km) or 1 year is to be observed.

1.2.1 If an engine oil approved by Porsche was used: The oil change service interval is set for a fixed oil change service interval of 10,000 miles (15,000 km) or 1 year when resetting the maintenance calculator with the PST2.

For more information about the oil change interval for Cayenne V6 and how to reset the "Maintenance Calculator" in the instrument cluster, see CAYENNE (V6) - ENGINE OILS APPROVED BY PORSCHE - OIL CHANGE SERVICE INTERVAL technical service bulletin (GROUP 1, NO. 3/04).

### TIRE PRESSURE MONITOR SYSTEM REMINDER

4 NOTE: To determine the appropriate reset procedure, refer to TPMS REMINDER RESET INDEX . Only vehicles listed in this index have a TPMS reset.

CAUTION: 1st generation TPM wheel electronics are not compatible with 2nd generation TPM wheel electronics. 1st generation is up to 2008, and 2nd generation is 2009 and beyond.

If wheels with wheel electronics from the 1st TPM generation are mounted on a vehicle with a 2nd generation TPM system (or vice versa), the wheel electronics will not be recognized by the TPM system. The TPM system is not active and a corresponding warning is displayed in the multi-function display of the instrument cluster. The wheel electronics will also be stored as defective in the fault memory of the TPM control unit.

Wheel electronics unit (sensor) part numbers are: • 2005-07: 997.606.021.00 433MHz) • 2008: 997.606.021.01 (433 MHz) • 2009-: 997.606.021.20 (433 MHz)

### TIRE PRESSURE MONITOR SYSTEM REMINDER > TPMS REMINDER RESET - PROCEDURE 1

Tire Pressure Monitoring begins to "learn" the wheels after a wheel change, wheel transmiter replacement, a tire pressure adjustment (when a warning message has been displayed), once an update of the tire settings has been performed. During this process, Tire Pressure Monitoring recognizes the wheels and their locations. The message "No monitoring, system is learning" appears on the multipurpose display. The wheel learning process takes place exclusively when the vehicle is being driven above 16 mph (25 km/h). Tire Pressure Monitoring requires a certain amount of time to learn the wheels.

. NOTE: The tire type and size must be updated even if the settings for the new set of wheels are the same as for the old wheels. If the tire setings are not updated, the message "TIRE CHANGE? UPDATE SETTINGS!" is displayed on the multi-purpose display.


### Starting TPMS Learn:

1. Select menu "TIRE PRESSURE", then "ADJUST". Set tire type and tire size (both items must be set). See Operating Multi-Purpose Display .

2. The learning process is now started, and wil be completed when vehicle is driven. The message "NO MONITORING - SYSTEM LEARNING" is displayed. The current tire pressure will be displayed once the learning phase is complete.


### Operating Multi-Purpose Display:

With multi-function steering wheel:

•Selecting menu, function, setting option: Rotary knob (top right button).

Confirming selection: Press rotary knob.

Moving back one or several selection levels: Button below rotary knob (middle right button).

Vithout multi-function steering wheel: (Use the lower lever on the right of the steering column.)

•Selecting menu, function, setting option: Push the lever downwards or upwards.

Confirming selection: Push the lever forward.

Moving back one or several selection levels: Pul the lever back (toward rear of vehicle).

### TIRE PRESSURE MONITOR SYSTEM REMINDER > TPMS REMINDER RESET - PROCEDURE 2 > "SELECTION AFTER WARNING" RESET > WHEEL CHANGE

1. Select "WHEEL CHANGE" from "SELECTION AFTER WARNING" menu. The display will return to "SPARE WHEEL" menu after acknowledgement. Select spare wheel type.

2. If the tire type and size of the new tires have not been set , a "WHEEL CHANGE? CHECK SETTINGS" message will be displayed. When vehicle is stopped, display will return to "SELECTION AFTER WARNING" menu. Perform previous step.


### TIRE PRESSURE MONITOR SYSTEM REMINDER > TPMS REMINDER RESET - PROCEDURE 2 > "SELECTION AFTER WARNING" RESET > SEALING SET

After repairing flat tire with tire sealant, select "SEALING SET". The display wil return to the basic screen after acknowledgement. A warning message will display if vehicle speed exceeds 50 mph (80 km/h).


### TIRE PRESSURE MONITOR SYSTEM REMINDER > TPMS REMINDER RESET - PROCEDURE 3

NOTE: If tire pressures have been adjusted, no reset procedure is required.

o the

NOTE: If tires have been rotated, or a tire pressure sensor or wheel has been replaced, e TPM system must be reset. See procedure below.

Tire Pressure Monitoring begins to "learn" new tire pressure sensors after a wheel change or sensor replacement after updating the tire specification settings. During the Learn process, the TPMS recognizes the wheels and their locations. A "No Monitoring" message appears on the multi-purpose display. The wheel learning process takes place exclusively when the vehicle is being driven above 16 mph (25 km/h). Tire Pressure Monitoring requires a certain amount of time to learn the wheels.


### Updating Tire Specification Settings:

![](images/1f059db9bfdd3ec798f72a977e4149d5bc79ed023a01aa6f531b281e41259c11.webp)

NOTE: The on-board computer is operated with the lower left lever on the steering lumn.

1. Push operating lever forward in order to switch on the selection field.

2. Select "TPC" with the operating lever.

3. Push operating lever forward. The display changes to the Tire pressure menu.

4. Select "Set" with the operating lever.

5. Push the operating lever forward. Select desired tire type: summer or winter.

6. Push operating lever forward. A display for confirming the selected type of tire appears.

7. Select "Continue" and push the operating lever forward.

8. Select the appropriate tire size (18 or 19 inch) and push operating lever forwards. A display for confirming the selected tire size appears.

9. If "Process complete" is displayed, learning mode will be initiated.

10. Drive vehicle above 16 mph (25 km/h) until correct tire pressures are displayed.

NOTE: The message "Process aborted" appears if the setting process is interrupted. All entries made up to this point are lost, and the original setings remain in effect. Only if the message "Process complete" appears after the setings have been made will the tire pressure monitoring re-learn the wheels.

WARNING: Incorrect handling of seat-belt pretensioner unit

Triggering of seat-belt pretensioner unit

→ Observe safety regulations for handling seat-belt pretensioner units.

→ Observe disposal regulations for seat-belt pretensioner units.

→ After disconnecting the battery, wait 1 minute before disconnecting the seat-belt pretensioner unit.

→ Remove ignition key and disconnect the battery. Route or insulate the ground strap so that all contact with a ground carrier is avoided. Read and follow work instructions after disconnecting the battery.

→ If removed for an extended period, the seat-belt pretensioner unit must be stored in a safe place.

→ Transport the seat-belt pretensioner unit in such a way that the seat belt can retract safely if it is actuated.

NOTE: Incorrect handling of spring plate on seat belt mount

The seat belt must be replaced.

→ Only bend the spring plate up as far as required to allow you to push the seat belt mount off the mounting pin.

→ The spring plate must be touching the mounting pin during installation with preload.

### WM 691119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT THREE-POINT BELT (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Install B-pillar trim panel. → INSTALLING LOWER PART OF B-PILLAR TRIM PANEL .

2. Connect the battery. → 2XOOIN GENERAL INFORMATION ON DISCONNECTING THE BATTERY

3. Perform a function test.

1. The belt strap must be fully rolled up when the function test is started.

2. Move the seat belt height adjustment to the highest position.

3. Pull out belt strap completely as far as it will go.

4. Roll up the belt strap again slowly. An audible clattering noise can be heard when you do this.

5. If the rolling-up process is interrupted, the belt strap cannot be pulled out again (permanent belt blockage). 6. The permanent belt blockage function must switch off at least 100 mm before the belt strap is rolled up fully, thereby ensuring that the belt strap can be pulled out again.

### The automatic belt device has two locking functions

The first locking function is triggered by pulling the seat belt out quickly (belt extension acceleration).


### WM 691301 CHECKING SEAT BELTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CHECKING SEAT BELTS > CHECKING AUTOMATIC BELT DEVICE (LOCKING EFFECT) > CHECK

oPull the belt strap out of the automatic belt device with a strong pull.

If no locking effect occurs, the entire seat belt and seat-belt buckle must be replaced.

In the case of faults in the extension or retraction of the seat belt, check whether the locking tab of the automatic belt device is engaged correctly in the sheetmetal bracket on the body.

The second locking function is triggered by a change in the sequence of vehicle movement (vehicle-dependent locking function).

WARNING: Road tests on public roads

Danger to other people on the roads

→ Perform drive tests on a stretch of road with no traffic.

Fasten the seat belt.

WARNING: Road tests on public roads

•Danger to other people on the roads

→ Perform drive tests on a stretch of road with no traffic.

oAccelerate the vehicle to 20 km/h (12 mph) and then perform an emergency stop by pressing the footbrake.

If the belt is not locked by the blocking mechanism during the braking phase, the entire seat belt and seat-belt buckle must be replaced.


### WM 691301 CHECKING SEAT BELTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) >CHECKING SEAT BELTS > CHECKING LOOK AND OPERATION OF SEAT-BELTBUCKLE

Inspect the seat-belt buckle for crack formation and flaking.

In the case of damage, the entire seat belt and seat-belt buckle must be replaced.


### WM 691301 CHECKING SEAT BELTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) >CHECKING SEAT BELTS > CHECKING LOOK AND OPERATION OF SEAT-BELTBUCKLE > CHECK SEAT-BELT BUCKLE

oPush the belt latch into the seat-belt buckle untilit engages with an audible click. Check whether the lock mechanism has engaged by puling strongly on the belt strap.

If the belt latch fails to lock in the seat-belt buckle even just once in at least 5 test procedures, the entire seat belt and seat-belt buckle must be replaced.

WM 691301 CHECKING SEAT BELTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) >


### CHECKING SEAT BELTS > CHECKING LOOK AND OPERATION OF SEAT-BELTBUCKLE > CHECK SEAT-BELT BUCKLE RELEASE

oRelease the seat belt by pressing your finger on the button on the seat-belt buckle.

Carry out the test procedure at least 5 times. If the belt latch fails to jump out even just once, the entire seat belt and seat-belt buckle must be replaced.


### WM 691301 CHECKING SEAT BELTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CHECKING SEAT BELTS > CHECKING SASH GUIDE COVERS

Plastic-coated covers show fine, paralle scores after the belt system has been subjected to stress (seat belt buckled during accident). On the other hand, wear caused by frequent use is indicated by a stripe-free, smooth surface.

oCheck the sash guide covers for distortion, flaking and crack formation. In the event of scoring and/or damage, the entire seat belt and seat-belt buckle must be replaced.


### WM 691301 CHECKING SEAT BELTS (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CHECKING SEAT BELTS > CHECKING MOUNTING PARTS AND FASTENING POINTS

Check the belt buckle strap for distortion.   
Check the function of the height adjuster.   
Check fastening points (seat, B-pilar, C-pillar, vehicle floor) for distortion or thread damage.

If the parts are damaged, the entire seat belt and seat-belt buckle must be replaced.

Replace damaged or distorted fastening points.

### WM 695119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING AIRBAG SENSOR (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REMOVING AIRBAG SENSOR > REMOVING AIRBAG SENSOR IN REAR INNER WHEEL ARCH

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag units

Triggering of airbag unit.   
•System faults can occur.

→ Switch off ignition and remove ignition key or remote control (hand-held transmitter).

→ A power supply (e.g. battery charger) must not be connected to the external power supply/jump-leac starting terminals.

→ Disconnect the battery and insulate the ground strap so that all contact with a ground carrier is avoided.

→ Wait 1 minute after disconnecting the battery.

→ Only pull off connector on the triggering unit after the waiting time has elapsed.

→ Make sure that no foreign objects are located in front of the airbag unit during installation.

→ Replace damaged parts during removal.

→ Always position airbag units so that the blow-out opening is facing upwards, e.g. crest on driver's airbag.

→ Do not position anything on the airbag units.

→ If removed for an extended period, the airbag units must be stored in a safe place.

— Airbag units must not come into contact with grease, oil, detergents, liquids, or similar substances.

→ Do not expose airbag units to temperatures above 90°.

→ Do not remove the short-circuit spring on the plug-in contacts.

→ Ignition and preparations may only be carried out by skilled staff, supervised by a second responsible person.

→ Before disposal, the airbag unit must be rendered harmless by electrical ignition performed in accordance with all precautionary measures, thereby preventing it from being used incorrectly.

NOTE: Voltage peaks

• Risk of damage to electrical load or to the control unit

WARNING: Incorrect handling of airbag units

Triggering of airbag unit.   
•System faults can occur.

→ Switch offignition and remove ignition key or remote control (hand-held transmitter).

→ A power supply (e.g. battery charger) must not be connected to the external power supply/jump-lead starting terminals.

→ Disconnect the battery and insulate the ground strap so that all contact with a ground carrier is avoided.

→ Wait 1 minute after disconnecting the battery.

→ Only pull off connector on the triggering unit after the waiting time has elapsed.

→ Make sure that no foreign objects are located in front of the airbag unit during installation.

→ Replace damaged parts during removal.

→ Always position airbag units so that the blow-out opening is facing upwards, e.g. crest on driver's airbag.

→ Do not position anything on the airbag units.

→ If removed for an extended period, the airbag units must be stored in a safe place.

— Airbag units must not come into contact with grease, oil, detergents, liquids, or similar substances.

→ Do not expose airbag units to temperatures above 90°.

→ Do not remove the short-circuit spring on the plug-in contacts.

→ Ignition and preparations may only be carried out by skilled staff, supervised by a second responsible person.

→ Before disposal, the airbag unit must be rendered harmless by electrical ignition performed in accordance with all precautionary measures, thereby preventing it from being used incorrectly.

### WM 487919 REMOVING AND INSTALLING TIE ROD (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > PRELIMINARY WORK

Information

Before removing the tie rod, always check the tie rod joints on both sides. If a joint does not meet the test conditions, it must be replaced.

Only if there is no play in the steering can it be set correctly and the operating reliability of the vehicle can thus be guaranteed.

1. Check tie rod joint.

Test conditions: The vehicle must be standing on its wheels in order to check the tie rod joints; vehicles with air suspension must be adjusted to maximum ground clearance.

![](images/daa66741406b419f70caa1c3345c3ea353e0db6fbd39e9d9003ba7cea607aa21.webp)  
Fig 1: Checking Tie Rod Joint

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

1. 1.1. Check that the dust boots, bellows and joints are working perfectly and have no leaks.

2.1.2. Check the left tie rod joint.

Turn the wheels to the right and take hold of the tie-rod ball -1- . Get a second mechanic to turn the steering by moving the steering wheel back and forth slightly.

There must be no play on the joint.

If you detect a certain amount of play that is not caused by the tie rod joint, the axial joint between the steering gear and tie rod is worn.

3.1.3. Check the right tie rod joint.

Turn the wheels to the left and take hold of the tie-rod ball -1- . Get a second mechanic to turn the steering by moving the steering wheel back and forth slightly.

There must be no play on the joint.

If you detect a certain amount of play that is not caused by the tie rod joint, the axial joint between the steering gear and tie rod is worn.

2. Remove tie-rod ball → REMOVING AND INSTALLING TIE-ROD BALL .

3. Remove front underbody panelling → 519219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COVER FOR FRONT UNDERBODY .

### WM 489055 REPLACING POWER-STEERING GEAR (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Raise the vehicle → 4XOOIN LIFTING THE VEHICLE .

2. Remove front wheels — 440519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WHEEL .

### Pay particular attention to the following:

Always use new steering gear fastening screws and a new clamping screw on the universal joint following removal. Clean screw threads and make sure that they remain clean and free of grease.

Always check the bellows and clamps for damage and make sure they are seated securely to prevent water from leaking in.

Connectors must lock with an audible click.

Replace fastening screws that are tightened to a torque angle!

Replace nuts for the steering gear fastening screws!

•Observe specified tightening torques and torque angle.

1. Move steering gear into installation position.

1.1.1. Screw in fastening screws -1- and -2- for the steering gear, but do not tighten them!

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

2. Fit universal joint.

1.2.1. Grease the journal of the input shaft for the steering gear using a non-watersoluble lubricant (e.g. lithium-saponified grease).

2. 2.2. Slide the universal joint -1- to the correct position in the center.

### WM 489055 REPLACING POWER-STEERING GEAR (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

### WM 4XOOIN LIFTING THE VEHICLE (ALL MODELS) > LIFTING THE VEHICLE > LIFTING THE VEHICLE

1. Drive vehicle onto the lifting platform. Pay particular attention to the following:

1. When driving onto a lifting platform, ensure that there is sufficient distance between the lifting platform and the vehicle.   
. If work has to be done in the front footwell, the vehicle should be positioned in such a way that the doors can be opened far enough.

2. On vehicles with air suspension/levelling system: Switch off the levelling system.

1.2.1. Switch on ignition.

2. 2.2. Press and hold the levelling system button until the message >>Levelling system switched off<< appears on the instrument cluster.

![](images/aed746d6b1853e39989cbd021d35a7d127840b7036326dc76bb5c8f81e36f42e.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Levelling System Button

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

WARNING: Vehicle can fall down

1. Risk of squashing or crushing

2. Risk of damage to the vehicle

→ Do not place any solid objects under the raised vehicle.   
→ Ensure that the lifting platform is prevented from lowering.   
→ Remove solid objects before lowering the vehicle.   
→ Raise the vehicle only at the take-up points provided.

3. Raise the vehicle at the four jacking points -1- .

![](images/880a4fe748b7657de47ca9c0a5819ac418aa535939d43514530410b724d8bf87.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Vehicle Jacking Points


### WM 4XOOIN LIFTING THE VEHICLE (ALL MODELS) > SUBSEQUENT WORK > SWITCHING ON THE LEVELLING SYSTEM

1. Lower the vehicle.

2. Switch on ignition.

3. Press and hold the levelling system button until the message >>Levelling system switched on<< appears on the instrument cluster.

Alternatively, the levelling system wil switch on automatically while driving (→ Speed greater than: +7 km/h (4 mph)) .

![](images/1ec86873092c33230c30c9a7f73fe35031a8835c55c85680ecc73ace881c45c6.webp)


### WM 400619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT-AXLE CARRIER (ALL MODELS) > TECHNICAL VALUES

![](images/68c242b97dc9a2898c8cbc4429c220c71f8dbfaacc142fb36d1d9616801d7749.webp)

![](images/324efb7979cb72bb1ee09e229c0a2899c081bc4cd1738de029a36b18ff425656.webp)


### WM 400619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT-AXLE CARRIER (ALL MODELS) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Raise the vehicle → 4XOOIN LIFTING THE VEHICLE .

2. Remove front wheels → 440519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WHEEL .

3. Remove wheel housing liner on both sides of the vehicle → 505619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT WHEEL HOUSING LINER .

4. Remove front underbody panelling → 519219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COVER FOR FRONT UNDERBODY .

5. Remove front-axle support → 400819 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT-AXLE SUPPORT.

6. Unscrew fastening screws -1 and 2- and remove heat shields at the left and right.

![](images/b0edfd14af0eccdb8cd9a295db967ad854504e5c37d2e630f94b081246f395b9.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Front-Axle Carrier Heat Shield

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

7. Remove anti-roll bar — 407719 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT ANTI-ROLL BAR .

8. Remove power-steering gear —→ 489055 REPLACING POWER-STEERING GEAR .

9. Remove front level sensors → 431855 REPLACING FRONT LEVEL SENSOR .

10. Tie up wheel bearing housing on both sides of the vehicle with tension straps (e.g. strapping belts 9454 ) at the mounting saddle. → Tying up wheel bearing housing

![](images/ee2252360c71bb71373dbc5917944f414255a0490349f0104215e98ab055f9bd.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Tension Straps

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

11. Remove lower trailing arm on both sides of the vehicle → 401719 REMOVING AND INSTALLING LOWER TRAILING ARM .

12. Support engine on the body → 1001IN SUPPORTING ENGINE ON THE BODY (ENGINE SAFETY DEVICE) .


### WM 400619 REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT-AXLE CARRIER (ALL MODELS) >REMOVING AND INSTALLING FRONT-AXLE CARRIER > REMOVING FRONT-AXLECARRIER

1. Separate threaded joint -1- .   
2. Swivel out control arm and secure on the body (e.g. using welding wire).

![](images/75f1b559c909ee654e21db6e513731cff65448a502c202e9ff6279de9e258f23.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Lower Control Arm

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

3. Remove strut -2- at the lower lock carrier on both sides.

1.3.1. Unscrew fastening nut -3- .

2.3.2. Unscrew fastening screw -1- .

![](images/74e327ab5a71bee225b481e4c417575b901e62bc7d27349e7ed5a57d191ef73c.webp)  
Fig 2: Identifying Lower Strut Fastening Nut And Screws

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.


### 3.3.3. Remove strut -2- on both sides.

4. Open locking lug -1- with a screwdriver, open housing cover -2- on the right longitudinal member and remove it.

![](images/7d27bea350f7a17faf10812d776af15a8803e5251ffc4662192e1d008e691fe5.webp)  
Fig 3: Identifying Housing Cover And Locking Lug

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

5. Disconnect electric lines on the right longitudinal member.

1.5.1. Unclip headlight vent line -8- at the clip -7- and set it aside.

2. 5.2. Unscrew fastening nut -2- and move ground lines -1 and 6- aside.

### Risk of damage to chassis components

If the front-axle carrier, steering gear or front-axle support is not fitted correctly, never lower the vehicle onto its wheels!   
Supporting the vehicle on the front-axle carrier or on the front-axle support (e.g. using a jack) is not permitted!   
If the vehicle needs to be moved, the front-axle support must be installed using the old bolts and square nuts and must then be tightened to the specified torque without additional torque angle.

1. Installation is performed in reverse order. Observe the specified tightening torques (replace fastening screws!): Front-axle support to front-axle carrier: Step 1 Initial tightening 90 Nm (67 ftlb.) Step 2 Final tightening +90° Front-axle support to front-axle carrier, middle and rear: Step 1 Initial tightening 90 Nm (67 ftlb.) Step 2 Final tightening +135°

Risk of squashing or crushing

The joint on the transmission side and the joint pin on the wheel side of the front axle can be replaced.   
The entire drive shaft must be replaced if the profile shaft of the joint pin is defective.

1. Remove the outer flat joiner on the inner drive shaft boot using pliers Nr.74 and use a slotted screwdriver for support if necessary.

Before fitting the joint, slide all drive shaft boots and flat joiners onto the drive shaft.

Do not confuse the drive shaft boots. They are not identical parts.

### WM 408919 REMOVING AND INSTALLING SHOCK ABSORBER FORKS (ALL MODELS) > REMOVING AND INSTALLING SHOCK ABSORBER FORKS > INSTALLING SHOCK ABSORBER FORK

WARNING: Wheel bearing housing raised incorrectly

Risk of squashing Risk of damage to components → Wear personal protective gear.

→ Do not raise the wheel suspension higher than the normal vehicle position (vehicle resting on wheels).

Information

Al screws and threaded joints on the axle must be tightened in vehicle position. Vehicle position means: vehicle standing on its wheels, or the wheel suspension is raised with a universal vehicle lift. Dimension -1- , from lower edge of wing to center of axle corresponds to vehicle position. The current height can be found in → 4495TW ADJUSTMENT VALUES FOR SUSPENSION ALIGNMENT . Always observe the following points!

![](images/0bc6f253065202f5f28b6030db69e9882e0c7185e694b53d2cc02f161e9d6b92.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Wheel To Wing Lower Edge Dimension (Rear Axle)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

On vehicles with air springs, the respective air spring must be bled using the Porsche System Tester . → 430 1IN BLEEDING AND FILLING THE LEVELLING SYSTEM

Screws and nuts are Geomet-coated and must not be greased.

### WM 420519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR AXLE HOUSING (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Raise the vehicle → 4XOOIN LIFTING THE VEHICLE .

2. Remove wheels — 440519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WHEEL .

3. Remove cover for underbody at the sides → 519319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COVER FOR CENTER UNDERBODY .

4. Remove brake calliper on both sides of the vehicle and suspend it at a suitable position in the wheel housing (do not open the brake hydraulic system!) → 474119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR BRAKE CALLIPER .

5. Remove coil springs/air springs on both sides of the vehicle —→ 427219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR COIL SPRING → 434319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR AIR SPRING .

6. Remove rear silencer → 260119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING EXHAUST SYSTEM .

7. Loosen cardan shaft from rear final drive and secure to the body with a piece of wire —→ 393519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR CARDAN SHAFT .

8. Release final drive from allines → 390119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR FINAL DRIVE .

### WM 420855 REPLACING REAR-AXLE BEARINGS (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > PRELIMINARY WORK

1. Raise the vehicle → 4XOOIN LIFTING THE VEHICLE .

2. Remove wheels — 440519 REMOVING AND INSTALLING WHEEL .

3. Remove cover for underbody at the sides → 519319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING COVER FOR CENTER UNDERBODY . 4. Remove rear coil springs/air springs — 427219 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR COIL SPRING → 434319 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR AIR SPRING .


### WM 420855 REPLACING REAR-AXLE BEARINGS (MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > REPLACING REAR-AXLE BEARINGS

WARNING: Preloaded or pressurized components

Risk of squashing or bruising

→ Do not reach into the danger area.

— Relieve the tension on components before starting work.

→ Secure components to prevent them from loosening suddenly.

CAUTION: Heavy components

Risk of squashing

→ Wear personal protective gear.

→ Get someone to help if necessary.


### Installation position of front bearing

Twist lock -1- is at an angle to the direction of travel. -arrow- indicates direction of travel.

![](images/3904a6397ae0c62ae9bcab08ae742878982c89ba1c08f56cc318a4f5805fe8f0.webp)  
Fig 8: Aligning Twist Lock   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

The following must also be observed:

1. Align bearing with the applied markings before pressing it in.   
2. Press bearing in until the collar is positioned loosely at the bush of the rear axle housing.   
3. The ends of the rubber beads on the bearing must match the markings on the rear axle housing.


### Installation position of front bearing

Twist lock -1- is at an angle to the direction of travel. -arrow- indicates direction of travel.

![](images/fa202fe1dc854a8f96416d577abbe04d925e84a31c82f64abf59d36a2cd347f0.webp)  
Fig 18: Aligning Twist Lock   
Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

The following must also be observed:

1. Align bearing with the applied markings before pressing it in.   
2. Press bearing in until the collar is positioned loosely at the bush of the rear axle housing.   
3. The ends of the rubber beads on the bearing must match the markings on the rear axle housing.

3. Fit wheels → INSTALLING WHEEL .

CAUTION: Wheel carrier raised incorrectly

Risk of squashing Risk of damage to components → Wear personal protective gear.

→ Do not raise the wheel suspension higher than the normal vehicle position (vehicle resting on wheels).

Information

Al screws and threaded joints on the axle must be tightened in vehicle position. Vehicle position means: vehicle standing on its wheels, or the wheel suspension is raised with a universal vehicle lift. Dimension -1- , from lower edge of wing to center of axle corresponds to vehicle position. The current height can be found in → 4495TW ADJUSTMENT VALUES FOR SUSPENSION ALIGNMENT . Always observe the following points!

![](images/9067cc08b2fd776774342b0b516fd1b0487d8f14ff59b2d96dcb91e42b5e710a.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Wheel To Wing Lower Edge Dimension (Rear Axle)

Courtesy of PORSCHE CARS NORTH AMERICA, INC.

On vehicles with air springs, the respective air spring must be bled using the Porsche System Tester . → 430 1IN BLEEDING AND FILLING THE LEVELLING SYSTEM

Screws and nuts are Geomet-coated and must not be greased.

Inner joint (transmission side)


### WM 422137 DISASSEMBLING AND ASSEMBLING REAR DRIVE SHAFT (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > DISASSEMBLING AND ASSEMBLING REAR DRIVE SHAFT > ASSEMBLING REAR DRIVE SHAFT

WARNING: Danger of objects or loads falling down

Risk of squashing or crushing → Secure components to prevent them from falling down.

The drive shaft is assembled in reverse order.

Check all parts to be re-used carefully.

Before fitting the joint, slide all bellows, hose clamps and other clamps onto the drive shaft.   
Use new circlips and ensure that they are seated correctly.

Use a new protective ring (on transmission side). Check that it is fitted correctly.

1. Clamp the joint (use aluminum protective jaws). Carefully slide the new circlip onto the shaft from above.   
2. Press the circlip together as required so that the joint slides over it easily when you tap it with a rubber hammer. Hold the drive shaft and joint pin with both hands and fit the joint pin onto the drive shaft under the workshop press until the pressure increases (this is as far as it can go). Check the pressure gauge! → Contact force: +20 kN Do not exceed the maximum force for pressing in joints (20 kilonewtons/2 tons)!

The procedure for fitting both joints is identical.


### WM 422137 DISASSEMBLING AND ASSEMBLING REAR DRIVE SHAFT (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > SUBSEQUENT WORK

1. Install rear drive shaft → 422119 REMOVING AND INSTALLING REAR DRIVE SHAFT .

WARNING: Whee bearing housing raised incorrectly

Risk of squashing Risk of damage to components → Wear personal protective gear.

→ Do not raise the wheel suspension higher than the normal vehicle position (vehicle resting on wheels).

Information

Al screws and threaded joints on the axle must be tightened in vehicle position. Vehicle position means: vehicle standing on its wheels, or the wheel suspension is raised with a universal vehicle lift. Dimension -1- , from lower edge of wing to center of axle corresponds to vehicle position. The current height can be found in → 4495TW ADJUSTMENT VALUES FOR SUSPENSION ALIGNMENT . 1. Position connecting links -2- on the removed anti-roll bar -3- .

### WM 430115 CALIBRATING THE LEVELLING SYSTEM (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CALIBRATING THE LEVELLING SYSTEM > CHECKING

Calibration must be performed if one or more of the following situations apply:

Control unit was replaced.   
•Level sensors were replaced.   
Vehicle lies to one side after being raised. If ifting platform mode is activated, carry out a test drive (liting platform mode switches off and the vehicle corrects itself). If this does not work, check the system for faults —→ 430149 TROUBLESHOOTING THE LEVELLING SYSTEM and then calibrate the system.

Level sensors are calibrated by determining a correction value (corresponding to the actual height of the vehicle) and storing it permanently in the control unit.


### WM 430115 CALIBRATING THE LEVELLING SYSTEM (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CALIBRATING THE LEVELLING SYSTEM > NOTES ON CALIBRATION

The nominal values for the nominal heights of the level sensors are stored in the control unit. The actual values of the respective axle heights, front left, front right, rear left, rear right, have to be measured manually and then entered using the Porsche System Tester. The actual values must be measured on the front and rear axle, both on the left and right. → Height Measurement Point On Rear Axle ; - Height Measurement Point On Front Axle .

See also: → Conditions For Carrying Out Calibration .


### WM 430115 CALIBRATING THE LEVELLING SYSTEM (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CALIBRATING THE LEVELLING SYSTEM > HEIGHT MEASUREMENT POINT ON REAR AXLE

The distance between the lower edge of the wing and upper edge of the measured-value pickup -X- is measured.

![](images/1cece32758b8d56323ecb1052e0dbad29547e1596d69796fa9ba7d5e1ec49426.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Rear Axle Point Height


### Check the following at the height measuring point on the front axle:

Lower edge of the wing is covered by the front lid.   
Only measure the height on the front axle when the front lid is open.

The distance between the lower edge of the wing and upper edge of the measured-value pickup -X- is measured.

![](images/ce8f233a7775f95466668ec0325dda23418436d383e688993f2a5e53e5edd312.webp)  
Fig 1: Identifying Front Axle Point Height


### WM 430115 CALIBRATING THE LEVELLING SYSTEM (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > CALIBRATING THE LEVELLING SYSTEM > CALIBRATION PROCEDURE

NOTE: Voltage drop

•Risk of irreparable damage to control unit   
Risk of damage to control unit   
Fault entries in the control unit   
•Coding in the control unit is aborted   
• Malfunctions in control unit, even during programming

→ Prior to disconnecting the control unit, switch off ignition and remove ignition key.

→ Ensure that the power supply is not interrupted during programming.

→ Connect a battery charger with a current rating of at least → Nominal value: 40 A to the vehicle battery.

Adhere strictly to the information provided under "Conditions for carrying out calibration"!

Always carry out the "Calibration procedure" step-by-step until calibration is complete!

1. Fit measured-value pickup Quick clamping device WE 1621 on the relevant wheel.

2. PIWis Tester Il 9818 must be connected to the vehicle before starting the Tester. Switch on ignition using original remote control (hand-held transmitter).

3. Apply electric parking brake.

4. Close the doors and tailgate.


### 5. Erase the fault memory.

To do this, connect the Porsche System Tester. Select >>Levelling system/PASM<< >>Fault memory<< >>Erase fault memory<< in the control unit overview.

Follow the instructions on the Porsche System Tester.

6. Perform Height sensor system component test.

Select >>Maintenance/repairs<< >>Height sensor system component test<< in the menu.

Follow the instructions on the Porsche System Tester.

7. Perform height sensor calibration.

Select >>Maintenance/repairs<< >>Height sensor calibration<< in the menu.

Follow the instructions on the Porsche System Tester.


### Sample calculation:

Measured dimension X = 430 mm; measured-value pickup radius = 32.5 mm

X + measured-value pickup radius = height of vehicle body 430 mm + 32.5 mm = 462.5 mm

2.7.2. Enter the determined values in the Porsche System Tester. If an implausible value is entered (actual value is not accepted by Porsche System

Tester), please refer to the information under: "Procedure: Measured actual value is not accepted".


### 8. Complete the diagnostic session (only for steel springs)

Select >>Drive links/checks<< >>Completion of height sensor calibration<< in the menu.

Follow the instructions on the Porsche System Tester.

When calibration is completed successfull, >>Result << >>Function completed << is displayed!

When calibration is complete, the vehicle does not adjust automatically to Normal Level. The height values can only be checked after test-driving the vehicle.


### Example:

The height measurement shows that front left vehicle height is 430 mm and the measured value is not accepted during height sensor calibration.

Actual value: 430 mm; required value: 464 mm

(Actual value + required value)/2 = mean value

(430 mm + 464 mm)/2 = 447 mm

Now enter the value 447 mm for the front left height in the Porsche System Tester.

2. 3.2. Perform Height sensor system component test (vehicle is adjusted to the required value on the affected side of the vehicle).

Select >>Maintenance/repairs<< >>Height sensor system component test<< in the menu.

Follow the instructions on the Porsche System Tester.

3. 1.1.3. Select >>Levelling system/PASM<< >>Drive links/checks<< >>Adjust vehicle level<< in the control unit overview.   
4.1.1.4. Select the value Low level 1 and press [F8] to start. Vehicle adjusts to Low Level.   
5.1.1.5. Once Low Level has been reached, select Normal Level and press [F8] to start. Vehicle now adjusts to Normal Level.

2.1.2. Switch offthe levelling system (switch it back on again when work is complete).

1. 1.2.1. Use PIWis Tester Il 9818 to select >>Levelling system/PASM<< >>Drive links/checks<< >>Activate/deactivate vehicle<< in the control unit overview. 2. 1.2.2. Select the value Deactivate levelling system (permanently) and press [F8] to start. The levelling system is now switched off.

3. 1.3. Compress vehicle at front and rear axles by approximately 25 mm 2-3 times and allow it to spring back freely.

4.1.4. Open the bonnet.

5. 1.5. Fit measured-value pickup Quick clamping device WE 1621 on the relevant wheel.


### Sample calculation:

Measured dimension X = 430 mm; measured-value pickup radius = 32.5 mm

X + measured-value pickup radius = height of vehicle body

430 mm + 32.5 mm = 462.5 mm

7. 1.7. Measure the vehicle height (→ 1.6. ) again after two hours and compare it with the first measurement.

Dimensions and tolerances can be taken from the prescribed vehicle height for vehicles with air suspension. → 4495TW ADJUSTMENT VALUES FOR SUSPENSION ALIGNMENT

If the vehicle is lying at an angle, there is a leak at the wheel suspension with the greatest difference between the first and second measurement.

Use commercially available leak detection spray to check the affected air-spring strut/air spring and the relevant air line one after the other.

If there is no difference after two hours, the vehicle height must be measured again after 24 hours.

The following components must also be checked:

1. Air line connections . Air-spring strut/air spring 3. Valve unit

If the vibration dampers are faulty, oil from the vibration damper may have entered the air supply system. To ensure that the air spring system works perfectly, it is absolutely essential that you clean the system after a fault is found and replace other components.

2. Procedure for repairing the air spring system after a fault is found on the vibration dampers:

1. Screw off the affected line on the air-spring strut/air spring and solenoid valve block. Blow out the line several times until it is clean using compressed air by introducing the compressed air at the end of the line at the solenoid valve block. 3. Check for traces of vibration damper oil in the solenoid valve block. 4. If vibration damper oil has contaminated the valve unit, it must be replaced. 5. Check the internal line from the compressor to the solenoid valve block. 6 If there is oil in the line between the compressor and the pressure accumulator, the line and the pressure accumulator must be replaced. If there is oil in the internal line, the compressor must be replaced.

### WM 4301IN COMPONENT ARRANGEMENT - AIR SUSPENSION (MACAN, MACAN S, MACAN TURBO) > COMPONENT ARRANGEMENT - AIR SUSPENSION > COMPONENT ARRANGEMENT - AIR SUSPENSION

The Macan models feature an optional levelling system with fully supporting air suspension on both axles and an electronically controlled damping system Porsche Active Suspension Management (PASM).

The air suspension with level control makes it possible to actively adapt the ground clearance of the Macan to the current driving situation or to the vehicle load.

Depending on the load, various vehicle ride heights with various suspension characteristics can be achieved by increasing or decreasing the air volume. The amount of air needed for each air-spring strut is determined by means of a control unit and provided via an air supply consisting of a compressor, a

solenoid valve unit and pressure accumulator.
